description: Spacious seafood taverna known for fresh grilled octopus, calamari and saganaki, with a lovely sea-view terrace and very clean facilities. Set slightly outside the main strip, it rewards the short walk with a quieter, more local feel.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About a 10-minute walk from the port/village center, along the coast.
Hours: Opens at 10 AM daily.

name: Mango eats and drinks
description: Friendly little spot for crepes, gyros, wraps and coffee, run by a welcoming owner who greets guests personally. A good stop for breakfast or a light lunch away from the busiest strip.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: On Belousi street in Katakolon village, a short walk inland from the port.

name: Golden Taste Katakolo
description: Beloved dessert and coffee spot on Antheon street known for premium gelato, loukoumades (Greek donuts) and warm, friendly service. A sweet, well-reviewed stop while strolling the port.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: On Antheon street, a short walk from the harbor.

name: Ο Τζίμης /Jimmys
description: Charming village taverna tucked away from the main tourist strip, with leafy greenery and caged songbirds adding to its cozy atmosphere. Popular with cruise crew for classic gyros, souvlaki and Greek salads.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: In Katakolon village, a short walk up from the port past the shops.
Hours: Opens at 10 AM daily.

name: Glyfada Cafe (Glyfada Fish Restaurant)
description: Family-run beachfront fish restaurant about 10 minutes' walk from the tourist strip, offering fresh, homemade seafood at roughly half the price of central Katakolon. Free beach chairs for diners make it a relaxed choice for a beach lunch or dinner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: On Alkyona beach, about a 10-minute walk from the port/village center.
Hours: Opens at 10 AM daily.

name: Cafe Del Mar
description: Casual harbor-front cafe known for crepes, desserts and coffee, with clean facilities and unobstructed port views. A relaxed spot for a light lunch or sweet treat while watching the boats.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Directly on the harbor waterfront in Katakolon.
Hours: Opens at 9 AM daily.

name: cafe meltemi katakolo
description: Hilltop cafe with spectacular panoramic views over the port and cruise ships, reachable via a short uphill walk from the terminal. A favorite for a relaxed coffee break with the best vantage point in town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Uphill from the cruise terminal — allow extra time for the climb; well signed from the port.
Hours: Opens at 10 AM daily.

name: Lime Bar, Katakolo
description: Small beach bar with bean-bag loungers, good cocktails and coffee, right on a small sandy patch of the port beach. A casual daytime hangout that stays open into the evening.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: On the small beach by the port.
Hours: Open until 11 PM.

name: Banana Katakolo
description: Lively beach bar on Alkyona beach with sunbeds, cocktails and a sandy swimming spot, popular with families and cruise passengers looking to cool off. Stays open late into the night.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: On Alkyona beach; a 10-15 minute walk or short taxi/tourist-train ride from the port.
Hours: Open until 3 AM.

name: MeZen Restaurant Corfu
description: Stylish restaurant near the Old Fortress serving refined Mediterranean and Corfiot dishes in a beautiful garden-courtyard setting. Praised for impeccable service and a romantic atmosphere, it's a top pick for a special dinner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended, especially for dinner — reserve via phone or the restaurant's website.
Getting there: Just off Sofokleous Dousmani street, a short walk from the Old Fortress.
Hours: Open until 12:30 AM.

name: Pomo D'Oro Corfu
description: Upscale, stylish restaurant in the heart of Corfu Town known for creative Mediterranean cuisine and an elegant atmosphere. A favorite for a special-occasion dinner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — book ahead, especially for dinner.
Getting there: On Skaramagka street in central Corfu Town.
Hours: Open until 11:30 PM.

name: AgioLi Mediterranean Cuisine
description: Highly rated Mediterranean restaurant on Nikiforou Theotoki street praised for exceptional service, creative dishes, and a lovely setting in the heart of the Old Town. A reliable pick for lunch or dinner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — reserve a table via Google/phone.
Getting there: On Nikiforou Theotoki, central Old Town.
Hours: Open until 12 AM.

name: Ampakas
description: Popular, high-volume restaurant known for generous portions of Greek classics, attentive staff, and great value. One of the most-reviewed spots in Corfu Town for good reason.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in, or order online for takeout.
Getting there: On Velissariou street, central Old Town.
Hours: Open until 12 AM.

name: Rex Restaurant
description: Long-established restaurant just off the Liston with a prime people-watching location, serving elevated Greek and Corfiot dishes. Known for an impressive culinary experience and attentive service, though pricier than average.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — reserve a table.
Getting there: On Kapodistriou street, right by the Liston.
Hours: Open until 11 PM.

name: Corfu Sailing Club Restaurant
description: Waterfront restaurant at the Mandraki marina beneath the Old Fortress walls, serving Mediterranean cuisine with excellent service and fortress/harbor views. A scenic spot for lunch or a sunset dinner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — reserve a table.
Getting there: At Mandraki marina, beside the Old Fortress — a short walk from the Liston/Spianada.
Hours: Open until 12 AM.

name: Spianada Meats & Greens
description: Upscale steak-focused restaurant overlooking the Spianada square, praised for some of the best steak in Corfu along with well-executed sides. A top choice for a memorable dinner in the heart of town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — reserve a table.
Getting there: On Kapodistriou street, facing the Spianada.
Hours: Open until 12 AM.

name: Salto
description: Easygoing bistro near the harbor with a varied seasonal menu, excellent wine list, and outdoor seating with views of Corfu castle and the sunset. A great spot for sharing plates and wine at the edge of the Old Town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; recommended to arrive early for sunset-view seating.
Getting there: On Donzelot street, near the Old Port/harbor edge of the Old Town.
Hours: Open until 11:30 PM.

name: Porta Otturata Corfu
description: Highly acclaimed restaurant near the New Fortress serving beautifully executed Greek and international dishes with top-quality ingredients. Frequently cited as among the best meals in Corfu Town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — order online or call ahead; can order online for takeout too.
Getting there: On Plateia Neou Frouriou, by the New Fortress.
Hours: Open until 12 AM.

name: To Tsipouradiko
description: Beloved local taverna serving traditional Corfiot dishes tapas/meze-style in generous portions with a vibrant, authentic atmosphere. A favorite among both locals and visitors for classic Greek home cooking.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in recommended early; gets busy in the evening.
Getting there: On the corner of Prosalendou and Gida Gonia streets, Old Town.
Hours: Opens at 6:30 PM (evening only).

name: Bougainvillea
description: Traditional Greek restaurant near the town hall square known for classic dishes like moussaka, Greek salad and shrimp saganaki, all fresh and well-prepared. A solid, centrally located choice for authentic Greek fare.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: On Plateia Dimarcheiou (Town Hall Square), Old Town.
Hours: Open until 11 PM.

name: Elia
description: Well-located Greek restaurant serving delicious traditional dishes with excellent service. A dependable choice in the heart of the Old Town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: At the corner of Spirou Arvanitaki and Palaiologou streets.
Hours: Opens at 10 AM daily.

name: Mouragia
description: Authentic Greek taverna with generous portions at prices lower than many Old Town restaurants, praised for excellent, friendly service. A good value option near the Old Port.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: On Arseniou street, along the Old Port/seafront edge of the Old Town.
Hours: Open until 12 AM.

name: Fishalida's Garden
description: Elegant seafood restaurant known for extremely high-quality, beautifully plated fish and seafood in a sophisticated garden ambiance. A top pick for a special seafood dinner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — reserve ahead, especially for dinner.
Getting there: On Vrela Armeni street, Old Town.
Hours: Open until 11 PM.

name: Fishalida
description: Always-busy seafood restaurant known for fresh, creatively prepared fish dishes. A reliably good option for seafood lovers in the Old Town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in recommended early; very popular.
Getting there: On Lochagou Spiridonos Vlaikou street, Old Town.
Hours: Open until 11 PM.

name: Dora Fish Taverna
description: Well-regarded fish taverna in Mandouki serving very fresh fish cooked to perfection. A solid choice for a seafood meal near the port area.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: On Ethnikis Antistaseos street in Mandouki, near the port.
Hours: Open until 12 AM.

name: Poseidonio
description: Small-plates seafood restaurant in Garitsa praised as outstanding compared to other Corfu eateries, with real fresh seafood and excellent service.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; recommended to arrive early.
Getting there: On Alkiviadou Dari street in Garitsa, a short walk from the Old Fortress.
Hours: Open until 11:30 PM.

name: Psaraki
description: Unique seafood restaurant in a great location near the Liston, offering amazing service and a memorable setting for a seafood dinner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — reserve a table.
Getting there: On Kapodistriou street, central Old Town.
Hours: Open until 12 AM.

name: Konoba PustiMeProć
description: A newer, intimate konoba tucked just off the Temple of Jupiter lane, with a chic stone-walled room. The kitchen mixes Dalmatian classics like tuna pašticada with steak tartare, shark, and ribeye, and diners consistently single out the polished, attentive service. It works well for a relaxed long lunch or a romantic dinner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — call +385 21 675 015
Getting there: Inside Diocletian's Palace on Kraj Svetog Ivana, a 2-minute walk west of the Peristyle; about 5 minutes on foot from the Riva.
Hours: Mon–Sat 11:00–24:00; closed Sunday

name: Fig Split
description: A buzzy all-day café-restaurant inside the palace walls with a creative, globally inspired menu. Brunch is the star, especially the French toast, breakfast burritos, and quesadillas, and the jalapeño-blueberry burger is a talked-about oddity. Expect a wait at peak times, but turnover is quick and prices are fair for the Old Town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; queues likely at brunch
Getting there: Dioklecijanova 1, just inside the palace near the Peristyle; about 4 minutes on foot from the Riva.
Hours: Daily 9:00–23:00

name: Konoba Tovar Split
description: A small, newly opened tavern serving honest, generous Dalmatian home cooking. Regulars praise the fresh grilled fish, truffle gnocchi, and sweetbreads, plus a warm, family-style welcome. It is a good antidote to the more polished palace restaurants.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner (small room)
Getting there: Ul. Majstora Jurja 4, in the northern part of the palace near the Golden Gate; about 7 minutes on foot from the Riva.
Hours: Mon–Sat 12:00–24:00; closed Sunday

name: Konoba Korta
description: A lively seafood konoba set on a small square in the palace's residential eastern quarter, with a terrace made for people-watching. The octopus is repeatedly called the best in Croatia by visitors, and the truffle pasta and daily specials are strong value. Service is relaxed and you are never rushed.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — call +385 21 277 455
Getting there: Poljana Grgura Ninskog 3, east side of the palace near the Silver Gate; about 5 minutes on foot from the Riva.
Hours: Daily 8:00–24:00

name: Temple Kitchen seafood & steak
description: A seafood-and-steak restaurant beside the Temple of Jupiter, set slightly back from the busiest lanes. The grilled sea bass, tuna steak, octopus salad, and scampi-and-prawn risotto all earn praise, as do generous sharing platters. It looks touristy from outside but cooks well.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — call +385 95 363 0555
Getting there: Kraj Sv. Ivana 2, next to the Temple of Jupiter; 2 minutes west of the Peristyle.
Hours: Daily 12:00–22:30

name: ZOI
description: Fine dining built into the sea-facing wall of Diocletian's Palace, with a long terrace hovering above the Riva. Expect refined Mediterranean tasting menus, including a vegetarian option, and good wine pairings; it appears in the Michelin Guide. The terrace has no shade, so book for sunset rather than early evening in warm months.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reservation strongly recommended — call +385 99 287 9097
Getting there: Entrance from the Riva side of the palace wall (Obala Hrvatskog narodnog preporoda 23); steps up to the terrace.
Hours: Daily 18:00–23:00 (dinner only)

name: Makarun Split
description: A multi-generational family restaurant hidden inside the palace, with a quiet private terrace away from the crowds. Highlights include salt-crusted sea bass, lobster pasta, and a much-praised octopus salad, with a knowledgeable sommelier guiding Croatian wine picks. It is upscale and calm rather than buzzy.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — call +385 21 725 058
Getting there: Marulićeva ul. 3, western palace lanes; about 4 minutes on foot from the Riva.
Hours: Daily 12:00–24:00

name: Restaurant Nostromo
description: A serious fish restaurant right by the fish market, where the catch of the day is shown raw at the table and filleted after grilling. The kitchen also reworks traditional starters like fish soup and savići, and uses excellent olive oil. A good choice for travelers who want a proper whole-fish dinner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — call +385 95 209 9691
Getting there: Kraj Svete Marije 10, next to the Ribarnica fish market, just west of the palace; about 4 minutes from the Riva.
Hours: Daily 11:00–22:00

name: Bepa
description: A café-restaurant with tables spilling onto Pjaca (People's Square), the elegant medieval square just west of the palace. It does a good brunch, with Italian-style breakfasts and chocolate-orange pancakes, and has decent vegetarian dishes like truffle polenta later in the day. The setting is the draw.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Narodni trg 1 (Pjaca), through the Iron Gate west of the palace; about 4 minutes from the Riva.
Hours: Daily 8:00–24:00

name: Pizzeria Portas
description: A family-friendly pizzeria at the Golden Gate with a terrace under grapevines and air-conditioned rooms inside. Pizzas arrive fast even when busy, and the fresh salads are a step above average. A reliable, reasonably priced choice for groups and kids.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 99 555 5715 for larger groups
Getting there: Ul. Kraj Zlatnih vrata 1, beside the Golden Gate at the palace's north side; about 7 minutes from the Riva.
Hours: Daily 11:00–24:00

name: Pizzaferaj City - Split Old Town
description: A small, cozy pizzeria with a light sourdough-style crust and a good wine list. It suits a casual dinner when you want a break from seafood. Service can slow at peak times.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner (small) — call +385 91 335 1232
Getting there: Ul. Majstora Jurja 8, northern palace near the Golden Gate.
Hours: Daily 12:00–24:00

name: Tradicija Bakery
description: A traditional bakery known for light cinnamon rolls, vanilla custard pastries, cherry pie, and homemade biscuits, nearly all under €3. Go in the morning, since the selection thins and freshness drops by afternoon.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Bosanska ul. 2, a lane just north of Pjaca; about 5 minutes from the Riva.
Hours: Mon–Fri 8:00–20:00; Sat 8:00–17:00; closed Sunday

name: Mr.Pozzetti Desserts
description: A dessert stop specializing in chimney cones baked to order and filled with gelato and toppings. The warm cinnamon-sugar cone with pistachio ice cream is the signature move. It costs a bit more than standard gelato, but it is fresh and fun.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Marulićeva ul. 1, western palace lanes near the Riva.
Hours: Mon–Sat 12:00–23:30; Sun 12:00–22:30

name: Gelateria Emiliana
description: Split's most hyped gelato shop, with inventive flavors such as salted caramel popcorn and blueberry cheesecake. The line can stretch to 20+ minutes in summer, but it moves; there is only outdoor stool seating. Card payment accepted.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Pistura ul. 1, in the lanes north of Pjaca, a short walk from the Riva.
Hours: Daily 10:00–23:30

name: Bokeria Kitchen & Wine
description: One of the Old Town's liveliest dining rooms, inspired by a Barcelona market hall, with a big wine list and Mediterranean plates. Black-ink risotto, tartare, sea bass, and sweet-potato tacos are popular, and the room hums all evening. A strong all-rounder from breakfast to late dinner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — call +385 99 226 0000
Getting there: Domaldova ul. 8, just west of the palace between Pjaca and Marmontova; about 4 minutes from the Riva.
Hours: Mon–Fri 8:00–24:00; Sat–Sun 8:00–01:00

name: SIP27 wine & tapas bar
description: A small, sophisticated wine bar where the sommelier walks guests through Croatian regions and grape varieties. Creative tapas, charcuterie boards, and even a pašticada make it a light dinner option. Ideal for wine-curious travelers.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended in the evening — call +385 91 609 9423
Getting there: Obrov ul. 9, between Marmontova and Pjaca; about 4 minutes from the Riva.
Hours: Mon–Sat 14:00–23:15; Sun 18:00–23:15

name: Zinfandel Food & Wine Bistro
description: A wine bistro in a historic building with a long Croatian wine list and a curated menu of small plates and mains. The Dalmatian meatballs, bacon-wrapped dates with blue cheese, and flat-iron steak stand out, and there is often live acoustic music. Evenings only.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — call +385 21 355 135
Getting there: Marulićeva ul. 2, western palace lanes near the Riva.
Hours: Daily 16:00–24:00

name: Misto Street Food & Bar
description: A tiny street-food bar just off Pjaca doing burgers, fried sardines, a pašticada sandwich, and soparnik, the local Swiss-chard pie. Cheap and quick, though seating is very limited.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Bosanska ul. 11, a few steps north of Pjaca.
Hours: Tue–Sun 10:00–24:00; closed Monday

name: Street food Corner
description: A small Asian-style takeaway counter turning out wok dishes and pad thai at fair prices. Mostly to-go with a few tables, handy for a quick lunch between sights.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Kraj Svete Marije 3, by the fish market west of the palace.
Hours: Daily 10:00–24:00

name: Sandwich & Caffe bar @noon
description: A father-and-son sandwich shop making huge made-to-order sandwiches with produce from the market next door. The mortadella and caprese are favorites, and Aperol spritzes are among the cheapest in town. A great budget lunch near the Silver Gate.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ul. Frane Bulića 2, a side alley near the Silver Gate and the green market.
Hours: Daily 10:00–20:00

name: BARAKOKULA Plant-based
description: A fully plant-based restaurant set in the courtyard of the historic Cindro Palace. Dishes like the creamy 'sexy tofu', truffle pasta, and Geisha rolls win over non-vegans too. Prices sit on the higher side, in line with the Old Town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; book for groups at +385 98 448 476
Getting there: Ul. kralja Petra Krešimira IV 3, inside the palace near the Peristyle.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–23:00; closed Sunday

name: SORA Sushi Bar Split
description: A newly opened, intimate sushi bar with generous, creative rolls and good cocktails. The small room and attentive host make it feel personal. Evenings only.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended (small) — call +385 95 807 1801
Getting there: Obrov ul. 4, between Marmontova and Pjaca.
Hours: Daily 16:00–24:00

name: Temple Sushi & More
description: A stylish, upstairs sushi restaurant with an open kitchen, strong Japanese beer and whisky list, and fresh sashimi. The dragon roll and gyoza get frequent praise. Tables fill after 19:00, so request the second-floor window seats.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended after 19:00 — call +385 99 388 4372
Getting there: Marmontova ul. 3, on the main shopping street west of Pjaca.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:00

name: ADRIATIC sushi • oyster • seafood
description: An upscale seafood and sushi spot on a quiet palace square, combining raw-bar oysters and ceviche with Adriatic seafood pastas and risottos. Staff often share local history and wine context, which makes it a strong special-occasion pick. Pricier than average.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — call +385 99 360 7777
Getting there: Carrarina poljana 4, eastern palace near the Silver Gate.
Hours: Daily 12:00–01:00

name: PULS bar Split
description: A café by day and cocktail bar by night, with a cool vaulted cellar inside the palace that offers relief on hot afternoons. Good coffee and fresh juice in the morning, well-made cocktails and music later.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ulica Andrije Buvine 1, inside Diocletian's Palace near the Riva.
Hours: Sun–Thu 7:00–24:00; Fri–Sat 7:00–01:00

name: Imperial cocktail & champagne bar
description: An elegant little bar that serves coffee and matcha by day and champagne and expertly made cocktails at night. The espresso martini earns particular praise, and complimentary olives arrive with drinks.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Papalićeva ul. 2, eastern palace near the Silver Gate.
Hours: Mon–Thu 8:00–24:00; Fri–Sat 8:00–00:30; Sun 8:30–00:30

name: The Daltonist Craft Bar
description: A craft-beer gastropub brewing its own ales, including a popular lavender beer, plus creative cocktails. It also serves solid breakfasts like shakshuka and bar food such as baked camembert. A fun stop at any hour.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Hrvojeva 10, just inside the Silver Gate area, east side of the palace.
Hours: Wed–Mon 9:00–24:00; closed Tuesday

name: D16 Coffee
description: A cult specialty coffee shop on a narrow palace lane, known for strong espresso drinks and filled croissants. Seating is tight, but there is a separate quiet workspace across the street.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Dominisova ul. 16, central palace lanes.
Hours: Daily 7:00–19:00

name: KaKantun - Specialty coffee and Gin
description: A pretty specialty café serving Brazilian-roast espresso drinks, matcha, house lavender syrup, and excellent pistachio croissants. In the evening it shifts to gin.
mapQuery: KaKantun Specialty coffee and Gin Split
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ul. Dujma Vuškovića, northern palace near the Golden Gate.
Hours: Tue–Sun 8:00–24:00; closed Monday

name: 4 Coffee
description: A tiny takeaway counter that many coffee lovers rate as Split's best flat white and cold brew. There is no seating, so grab and go.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Hrvojeva 9, near the Silver Gate on the palace's east side.
Hours: Mon–Sat 7:00–13:00; closed Sunday

name: Gelateria Riva split
description: A friendly gelato stand at the start of the Riva with generous scoops and rotating flavors like lavender and passion fruit. Ideal for an evening promenade cone.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Obala Hrvatskog narodnog preporoda 20, on the Riva itself.
Hours: Daily 9:00–23:00

name: ST Burek
description: A burek shop featured on 'Somebody Feed Phil', selling big, flaky meat and cheese pies for about €3. Quality reports vary by batch, but it is a cheap, filling local snack with a takeaway window.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Domaldova ul. 13, west of Pjaca.
Hours: Mon–Sat 7:30–23:00; Sun 8:00–23:00

name: Restoran K.užina
description: A refined Croatian restaurant with a quiet courtyard and an excellent six-course tasting menu with wine pairing. Beef tartare, shrimp-and-lemon risotto, and many gluten-free options stand out. Service is polished but unpretentious.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — call +385 91 606 0973
Getting there: Kraj Svete Marije 1, near the fish market just west of the palace.
Hours: Mon 12:00–23:30; Tue–Sat 12:00–24:00; closed Sunday

name: Uje Restaurant
description: An olive-oil-themed restaurant and shop where you can do an 'olive oil journey' tasting before a meal of Dalmatian seafood and vegetable dishes. It is romantic and quietly set in the palace lanes, with a discount at the adjoining oil shop.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — call +385 95 200 8009
Getting there: Dominisova ul. 3, central palace.
Hours: Daily 12:00–24:00

name: Villa Spiza
description: A beloved, tiny market-to-table spot with a handwritten menu that changes daily. You can watch the cook at work, and the fish soup and shrimp pasta are standouts. Service is brisk and there are no reservations, so arrive early.
details:
Reservations / tickets: No reservations — walk-in; arrive early to avoid a queue
Getting there: Ul. Petra Kružića 3, just outside the Golden Gate at the palace's north side.
Hours: Mon 16:30–22:00; Tue–Sat 13:00–22:00; closed Sunday

name: Bajamonti Steak & Pizza
description: A grand-café style restaurant on Prokurative (Republic Square) with steaks, pizzas, and Croatian dishes, plus live music some nights. The menu labels allergens clearly and has vegan breakfast options. The arcaded square views are a highlight.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — call +385 21 341 033
Getting there: Trg Republike 1 (Prokurative), at the west end of the Riva.
Hours: Mon–Sat 8:00–24:00; Sun 9:00–24:00

name: Kruščić Bakery
description: A local artisan bakery with traditional Croatian pastries, breads, and seasonal specialties. Lines form most mornings. Cash only, and it closes early.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (cash only)
Getting there: Obrov ul. 6, between Marmontova and Pjaca.
Hours: Mon–Sat 8:00–14:00; closed Sunday

name: PARADOX Wine & Cheese Bar
description: A wine and cheese bar offering Croatian wine flights with matched cheeses, smoked tuna, prosciutto, and jams. The rooftop terrace has views down to the harbor. Staff are knowledgeable and fun.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for the rooftop — call +385 21 787 778
Getting there: Ul. bana Josipa Jelačića 3, just north of Prokurative.

name: Corto Maltese Freestyle food
description: A quirky restaurant themed around the classic Corto Maltese comic, with walls covered in its pages. The playful, original menu includes seafood pasta, slow-cooked lamb, ceviche, and house pâté with homemade bread. Great atmosphere and music.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — call +385 21 587 201
Getting there: Obrov ul. 7, between Marmontova and Pjaca.
Hours: Daily 9:00–23:30

name: Pasticceria Emiliana
description: The pastry offshoot of Gelateria Emiliana, focused on tiramisù in classic and inventive flavors like pistachio and salted caramel, plus fresh cannoli. A small, cute takeaway counter.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Cosmijeva ul. 1, next to Gelateria Emiliana north of Pjaca.
Hours: Daily 10:00–24:00

name: Tiramisù Bar Split
description: A small shop devoted to tiramisù, with flavors such as lemon, pistachio, and hazelnut alongside the classic. Portions are generous and well balanced, perfect for eating while strolling.
details:

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Obala kneza Domagoja 1, at the top of the port food court by the bus and train stations; about 5 minutes east of the Riva.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:00–21:00; Sun 9:00–17:00

name: Lola Split
description: An open-air restaurant near the port, known for excellent mussels, beef pasta, and lively service with a good playlist. There is no indoor dining, and traffic passes nearby.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — call +385 98 908 3454
Getting there: Ul. Mile Gojsalić 1, near the ferry port and bus station; about 6 minutes east of the Riva.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:30

name: Madre bistro
description: A newer, cozy bistro with homemade pasta, gluten-free options, and Dalmatian touches like soparnik and gnocchi with pašticada. Warm, relaxed, and good value.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — call +385 95 354 5315
Getting there: Ul. kralja Zvonimira 12, near the ferry port; about 8 minutes east of the Riva.
Hours: Tue–Sun 11:00–23:00; closed Monday

name: Restaurant Adriatic
description: An upscale seafood and grill restaurant at the ACI marina on the Sustipan headland, with sweeping views across the harbor to the Old Town. The tuna tartare, beef-cheek risotto, tuna steak, and truffle pasta draw steady praise, along with strong Croatian wine pairings. Book a terrace table for sunset; plan on roughly €70–80 per person with wine.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Strongly recommended for sunset and dinner — call +385 21 398 560
Getting there: About 15 minutes on foot west from the Riva along Trumbićeva obala, then around the ACI marina toward Sustipan; a 5-minute taxi ride.
Hours: Daily 12:00–24:00

name: Restoran Jugo
description: A newer fine-dining restaurant at the ACI marina, reinterpreting traditional, locally grown Dalmatian ingredients with a modern touch. Plating is artful, and the chef often visits tables. Service is polished and the setting calm, which suits a special-occasion dinner away from Old Town crowds.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — call +385 21 399 003
Getting there: Uvala Baluni 2 at the ACI marina, about 15 minutes on foot west of the Riva.

name: Restaurant Zrno Soli
description: An elegant seafood restaurant on the upper floor of the ACI marina building, with a terrace overlooking yachts and the Old Town skyline. White-fish carpaccio, Adriatic fish, and fish soup are highlights. A weekday lunch special that includes water, wine, and coffee is a standout value, and a retractable roof keeps it usable in poor weather.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner and groups — call +385 91 434 3050
Getting there: Uvala Baluni 8, ACI marina; about 15 minutes on foot west of the Riva.
Hours: Sun–Thu 12:00–24:00; Fri–Sat 12:00–01:00

name: Velum
description: A relaxed, slightly hidden seafood and steak restaurant at the ACI marina. It is popular for seafood platters for two, a Dalmatian sharing board, grilled squid, and prawn risotto at mid-range prices. Service is warm, though it can slow when large private events are being set up.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 21 398 439 for groups
Getting there: Uvala Baluni 1, ACI marina; about 15 minutes on foot west of the Riva.
Hours: Mon–Thu 9:00–24:00; Fri–Sat 8:00–24:00; Sun 9:00–24:00

name: Shpizza and Pizza
description: A casual, good-value spot by the Jadran marina known for light-crusted pizzas (the burrata pizza is a favorite), lamb with gnocchi, and fresh salads. It has air-conditioned indoor seating plus a terrace, and works well for lunch after a swim at Zvončac.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 21 399 800 for groups
Getting there: Sustjepanski put 23, by the Jadran marina and Zvončac bay; about 20 minutes on foot west of the Riva.
Hours: Daily 8:00–23:30

name: Jadran Beach Bar
description: A locals' favorite seaside bar at the Jadran swimming club on Zvončac bay, with ladders and stairs straight into the sea and rocks for cliff jumping. It serves drinks, coffee, and croissants only, with no kitchen. Sunbeds rent for about €40 per pair with umbrella in summer, and sunsets are the big draw.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Sustipanski put 5, Zvončac; about 20 minutes on foot west of the Riva. Map pins can misroute — follow the coastal path past the Jadran pool.
Hours: Daily 8:00–22:00

name: Shakerato
description: A tiny, family-run brunch bistro in residential Meje with a short menu of homemade dishes: focaccia, shakshuka, roast-beef and turkey sandwiches on house bread, and steak salad. Creative drinks such as orange-sage soda and lavender iced tea round it out. It is pet-friendly and cash only.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (cash only)
Getting there: Ul. Antuna Mihanovića 37, Meje; about 20 minutes on foot west of the Riva, or a short taxi ride.
Hours: Wed–Sun 10:00–14:00; closed Monday and Tuesday

name: Restaurant Lučica
description: A traditional Croatian restaurant at the Špinut marina on Marjan's quieter north shore, popular with locals. It is known for grilled meat platters, stuffed steaks, homemade pasta, and fish, sometimes with live piano music. Sides and bread are charged separately, so the bill adds up.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended on weekends — call +385 21 386 763
Getting there: Lučica 7, Špinut marina, north side of the Marjan peninsula; about 30 minutes on foot from the Riva or a 10-minute taxi ride. It can also be reached by trail down from the Marjan summit.
Hours: Daily 9:00–23:30

name: Restoran Gusar
description: A refined seafood restaurant beside the water at Špinut, known for extremely fresh fish dressed simply with olive oil and salt. Tables sit right by the sea and service is excellent. It is also a sought-after wedding caterer, so it occasionally closes for private events.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — call +385 21 385 136
Getting there: Spinutska ul. 69, north shore of the Marjan peninsula; about 30 minutes on foot from the Riva or a 10-minute taxi ride.
Hours: Mon 10:00–22:00; Tue–Sun 10:00–23:00

name: Kavana Procaffe
description: A quiet seaside café on the Špinut waterfront with views over the bay to the Kozjak mountains. It offers good coffee, an excellent cake selection, and sandwiches on fresh-baked bread. A peaceful break before or after walking Marjan's northern paths.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Spinutska ul. 67, north shore of the Marjan peninsula, next to Restoran Gusar; about 30 minutes on foot from the Riva or a 10-minute taxi ride.
Hours: Mon–Sat 7:00–24:00; Sun 8:00–24:00

name: Anona
description: Polished modern-Mediterranean kitchen on a lively corner terrace where the Bačvice district meets the ferry port. The menu leans toward raw and lightly cooked seafood like octopus carpaccio, bluefin tuna tataki and oysters, plus truffle pasta and serious dry-aged steaks. Staff give genuinely good Croatian wine guidance, which makes this one of the strongest all-round dinners on this side of town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead for dinner, especially in summer: call +385 91 640 5400.
Getting there: About 5 minutes on foot from the ferry/cruise terminal, on Mile Gojsalić at the Bačvice end of the port.
Hours: Daily 12:00–00:00

name: Soul Kitchen
description: Creative global-Mediterranean restaurant with a leafy, tropical-feeling terrace a short stroll above Bačvice beach. The menu mixes Dalmatian produce with tacos, falafel, tuna and inventive salads, and it is one of the strongest vegetarian- and vegan-friendly kitchens in Split. Service is warm and personal, making it a good choice for mixed-diet groups.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reservations recommended in season: call +385 99 555 5950.
Getting there: Prilaz braće Kaliterna 8, a 2-minute walk uphill from Bačvice beach; about 10 minutes on foot from the port via the underpass by the bus station.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:00

name: Matoni
description: Owner-run Dalmatian restaurant set in a converted stone cellar divided into small, intimate rooms, with a strong local following. The kitchen is known for handmade tagliatelle, tuna pašticada with gnocchi, grilled squid and braised beef shoulder. It delivers near-fine-dining cooking at mid-range prices and feels distinctly un-touristy.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead, particularly Friday–Saturday: call +385 91 608 8333.
Getting there: Prilaz braće Kaliterna 6, just above Bačvice beach; about 10 minutes on foot from the port.
Hours: Tue–Thu 12:00–23:00; Fri–Sat 12:00–23:30; Sun 12:00–22:30; closed Monday

name: V Restaurant & Bar
description: Small, chef-driven restaurant and bar on the Kaliterna lane above Bačvice, focused on refined Mediterranean seafood and pasta. Early diners praise the truffle-and-prosciutto Dalmatian pasta and carefully plated sea bass. Opens from breakfast through dinner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 21 312 704 to reserve for dinner.
Getting there: Prilaz braće Kaliterna 12, just above Bačvice beach.
Hours: Daily 07:00–22:00

name: Median
description: Calm boutique-hotel restaurant with a shaded sea-view terrace at the top of Bačvice. It is good for an unhurried lunch, with steak tagliata, Istrian fuži pasta with steak and truffle, salads and cocktails. Service is attentive, and gluten-free dessert options are available.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in for lunch; call +385 21 399 300 for dinner.
Getting there: Prilaz braće Kaliterna 1, at the top of the steps above Bačvice beach.
Hours: Daily 07:00–23:30

name: Žbirac
description: The cult café-bar on the Bačvice promenade where locals have watched picigin, Split's shallow-water ball game, for decades. It serves drinks and coffee only, with no food, but the beachfront people-watching is the real point. It is the most 'local Split' coffee stop in the zone.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Šetalište Petra Preradovića 5, directly on Bačvice beach; about 10 minutes on foot from the port.
Hours: Listed as open 24 hours

name: Havana Beach Bar
description: Upbeat beach bar right on the Bačvice sand, known for its music, beach parties, well-made cocktails and light bites. It is ideal for a post-swim drink. The staff are a big part of the appeal.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: On the Bačvice beach promenade (Šetalište Bačvice); about 10 minutes on foot from the port.
Hours: Daily 08:00–22:00

name: Bacvice Ice Cream & Cold Drinks
description: Tiny kiosk-style stop steps from the water for creamy ice cream and cold drinks after a swim. It is useful as a quick treat on the beach rather than a sit-down destination.
mapQuery: Bacvice Ice Cream & Cold Drinks Split
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Šetalište Petra Preradovića 5, on the Bačvice promenade.

name: A'E kitchen & wine bar
description: Relaxed kitchen and wine bar on a quiet residential street a few minutes inland from Bačvice. It has an unusually deep list of Croatian wines by the glass and knowledgeable staff for informal tastings. Traditional dishes and breakfast round out an all-day menu.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 91 640 1950 for groups or tastings.
Getting there: Kuzmanićeva 13, about 5 minutes inland from Bačvice beach and 10 minutes from the port.
Hours: Daily 07:00–00:00

name: Missy B. Bistro
description: Cozy book-lined bistro just inland from Bačvice, strong for breakfast, brunch and lunch. French toast and big brunch plates fill the mornings, and fried calamari and pašticada carry lunch. It offers good value and personal service.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ulica Sv. Petra Starog 16, a few minutes north of Bačvice and the bus station.
Hours: Mon–Sat 08:30–16:30; closed Sunday

name: FAST FOOD POPAJ POJISANSKA
description: No-frills local sandwich and grill counter with build-your-own sandwiches, wraps, burgers and ćevapi at very low prices. It is popular with locals and is a reliable, fast budget fuel stop. The menu is self-service style.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Pojišanska 22, about 5 minutes inland from Bačvice/Firule.
Hours: Mon–Sat 09:30–00:00; Sun 13:00–00:00

name: Beach Bar Amazonico
description: Seafront bar between Bačvice and Ovčice with open sea views, cocktails, Croatian beers and casual food such as pizza. It is one of the best sunset spots on this stretch, with friendly staff.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Šetalište Petra Preradovića 2, on the coastal path at the east end of Bačvice; about 12 minutes on foot from the port.
Hours: Daily 09:00–22:00

name: Café Ovčice
description: Easygoing café-bar on Ovčice cove, the quieter pebble-and-concrete beach between Bačvice and Firule. It serves cheap beer, cocktails and simple snacks like salads, with plenty of shade. Sun loungers can be rented here for the day.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Put Firula 4, on the coastal path about 15 minutes on foot from the port.
Hours: Daily 08:00–22:00

name: Cookie Lab
description: Modern dessert bar and specialty-coffee stop near the Firule waterfront. The signature is tiramisu served in a chocolate cup that you finish with a shot of espresso, alongside cakes, cookies and plant-milk coffees. It makes a good mid-walk pause.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Put Firula 1, about 15 minutes on foot from the port along the coast.
Hours: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 08:00–21:00; Wed & Sat 09:00–21:00; closed Sunday

name: Maestro Grill Club Split
description: Upscale grill restaurant with a pine-shaded terrace above Firule, serving premium steaks, tartare, tuna steak and local seafood. It is especially atmospheric for dinner. Staff walk guests through the dishes and wine, and it is one of the few restaurants here with on-site parking.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner: call +385 99 200 0313.
Getting there: Put Firula 6, about 15–20 minutes on foot from the port; on-site parking available.
Hours: Daily 12:00–00:00

name: Nevera Tavern
description: Honest, generous tavern cooking at Firule: whole grilled fish, big grilled prawns, Istrian beef pasta and home-made bread. It feels authentic and unpretentious and is fairly priced for the portions. The warm, characterful service is often singled out.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 21 388 736 for dinner; walk-ins often possible at lunch.
Getting there: Put Firula 17, about 20 minutes on foot from the port.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:00

name: Dvor
description: One of Split's most atmospheric dinners: a garden terrace cascading toward the sea at Firule, with views across to Brač. The cooking is refined Dalmatian, with ceviche, tuna steak, lamb chops and medovnik honey cake, plus a sommelier-led local wine list. Courses with wine pairings are available, and it suits a special-occasion meal or a group.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Strongly recommended, especially for sunset tables: call +385 21 571 513.
Getting there: Put Firula 14, about 20 minutes on foot from the port or a 5-minute taxi.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:00

name: Tennis Bar
description: Firule institution: a big, mostly outdoor bar with sea and Brač views that runs from morning coffee to late-night drinks. Weekends bring DJs and Balkan music and a mixed local crowd. Cocktails are made with fresh citrus at reasonable prices.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Put Firula 18, about 20 minutes on foot from the port.
Hours: Mon, Tue, Thu 07:00–02:00; Wed, Fri, Sat 07:00–03:00; Sun 08:00–02:00

name: Caffe Bar Mythos
description: Simple terrace bar perched at the top of the steps down to Firule beach, with a strong beach view. It serves coffee, beer and basic food like burgers and wings. It is best for a casual sundowner rather than a meal.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Put Firula 18, directly above Firule beach.
Hours: Daily 08:00–00:00

name: Paiz Beach Bar
description: Beachfront cocktail bar at Firule with one of the best open-sea views in the zone and plenty of shade. Cocktails get strong marks, but service is inconsistent. Ask for an itemized bill before paying.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Put Firula 20, at Firule beach.
Hours: Mon–Thu 08:00–00:00; Fri–Sun 08:00–01:00

name: Bottiglia Wine & Deli
description: Elegant upstairs garden-terrace wine bar near Firule beach, run by staff who host genuinely educational Dalmatian wine tastings. It pours an excellent selection of Croatian wines with tapas-style plates, seafood boards and tuna pâté. It is ideal as a pre-dinner stop before Dvor or as a light dinner on its own.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 95 202 0427 to book wine tastings; walk-ins welcome for drinks.
Getting there: Put Firula 37, about 20 minutes on foot from the port.
Hours: Sun–Thu 14:00–00:00; Fri–Sat 14:00–01:00

name: Movi
description: Neighborhood pizzeria-restaurant near Firule turning out crisp wood-fired pizzas, plus pastas and the house olive oil. The playful flowerpot chocolate mousse is a hit with kids. It is reliable and fairly priced.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 21 571 540 for groups.
Getting there: Put Firula 47, about 20–25 minutes on foot from the port.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:00

name: BIBERON Sushi Bar
description: Popular sushi bar on Put Firula with high-quality fish and creative rolls, including truffle specials. It is a good option when travelers want a break from Dalmatian menus. Tables are often reserved, and service can be uneven.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve ahead, as walk-ins are often turned away at peak times: call +385 21 280 448.
Getting there: Put Firula 57, about 25 minutes on foot from the port.
Hours: Daily 12:00–00:00

name: Pimpinella
description: Rustic, locals-first Dalmatian konoba a few streets inland from Firule. It is known for some of the best pašticada in Split, seafood risotto and daily specials, at prices well below the Old Town. It fills quickly, so expect to wait or come back later.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 21 389 606; often full at peak times.
Getting there: Spinčićeva 2A, about 5 minutes inland from Firule beach; 25 minutes on foot or a short taxi from the port.
Hours: Mon–Sat 09:00–00:00; Sun 10:00–17:00

name: Konoba Barkarola
description: Large seaside konoba on the Zenta marina promenade with harbor views and a broad, affordable menu of grilled fish, cuttlefish risotto, ćevapi and meat plates. It has a good wine list. Service quality varies by shift, but the setting and value are solid.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 97 629 1174 for dinner.
Getting there: Šetalište Kalafata 2, Zenta marina; about 25–30 minutes on foot from the port or a 5–7 minute taxi.
Hours: Daily 11:00–00:00

name: Konoba Špurtil
description: Small, family-feel konoba by the Zenta boats, praised for generous shared seafood and meat platters, some of the best grilled squid in town and home-made cheesecake. It has a relaxed, unhurried atmosphere and is a true hidden gem.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 91 621 5030 for dinner.
Getting there: Šetalište Kalafata 2, down at the Zenta marina; about 25–30 minutes on foot from the port.
Hours: Tue–Fri 09:00–23:00; Sat–Sun 12:00–23:00; closed Monday

name: Šalša Pizza & Comfort Food
description: Fun marina-side pizza spot at Zenta serving both thick Chicago-style deep dish and thin New York–style pies, including standout mortadella-pistachio combinations. It has a great view and chill vibe at fair prices, and it is a hit with families and anyone pizza-curious.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 95 200 3310 for larger groups.
Getting there: Šetalište Kalafata 2, Zenta marina.
Hours: Tue–Sat 11:00–00:00; Sun 12:00–00:00; closed Monday

name: Restaurant Nautica
description: Genuinely family-run harborside restaurant at Zenta, good for an honest whole grilled fish, tuna steak, risotto and shared meat platters. It has a warm welcome, accepts cards and has a pretty setting beside the marina.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 95 844 5545 for dinner.
Getting there: Šetalište Kalafata 2, Zenta marina.
Hours: Daily 08:00–23:00

name: Restoran i pizzeria Renato
description: Terrace pizzeria-restaurant overlooking the Zenta boatyard and marina, best known for its shareable 'Grandma' deep-dish pizza. It also serves fried squid and tuna steak. It is casual and good value, but check the bill for an added service charge.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 21 571 271 for groups.
Getting there: Šetalište Kalafata 2, Zenta marina.
Hours: Daily 08:00–23:00

name: Restoran Triton Split
description: Refined seafood restaurant in a seafront hotel at Trstenik, the next bay east of Zenta. Whole fish such as John Dory is filleted tableside, alongside blue-crab salad, scallops, langoustines and an excellent black cuttlefish risotto. It has polished, knowledgeable service and a sea-view terrace.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended: call +385 91 603 4334.
Getting there: Put Trstenika 19, Trstenik; about 35–40 minutes on foot from the port or a 10-minute taxi.
Hours: Daily 12:00–00:00

name: Caffe Bar Bonsai
description: Charming garden café near Trstenik beach run by a welcoming owner who once lived in Japan, which explains the name. It serves cheap, good coffee, iced drinks and plant milks in a leafy, quiet setting. It makes a peaceful break on a walk out to the eastern beaches.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Trstenik 2, a short walk from Trstenik beach; about 35 minutes on foot from the port.
Hours: Daily 07:00–23:00

name: Cafe Cube
description: Low-key waterfront café-bar on Poljud bay frequented by locals, with Croatian prices and a playground right in front. It is a family-friendly spot for coffee or a glass of wine, and kayak tours depart nearby. Drinks are basic and there is no real food menu.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Osmih mediteranskih igara 9, on the Poljud waterfront; about 35 minutes on foot from the port. Parking by the nearby church.
Hours: Mon–Fri 07:00–00:00; Sat–Sun 07:00–01:00

name: Restaurant Poljud
description: Restaurant and event venue on the historic Poljud promenade, near the 16th-century Franciscan monastery. It serves daytime meals and functions mainly as a wedding and catering venue, so it is lunch only. Book ahead in case a private event is on.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call ahead to confirm availability: +385 99 338 6408.
Getting there: Poljudsko šetalište 1, Poljud; about 35 minutes on foot from the port or a 10-minute taxi.
Hours: Mon–Sat 08:00–16:00; closed Sunday

name: Pizzeria & pivnica "ST Spiza"
description: Genuine locals' pizzeria and beer hall by Hajduk Split's Poljud stadium, with a huge menu of pizzas, mixed grill platters, burgers and Mexican-style dishes. It is excellent value with very large portions. The atmosphere comes alive on match days.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 21 380 736 for groups.
Getting there: Ulica Zrinsko Frankopanska 58, next to Poljud stadium; about 30 minutes on foot from the port.
Hours: Mon–Sat 08:00–23:00; closed Sunday

name: blue Coffee
description: Bright, modern café by Poljud stadium with good coffee, friendly staff and plenty of indoor and outdoor seating. It is a handy stop for anyone visiting the stadium or the Hajduk fan shop.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Put Supavla 1, beside Poljud stadium.
Hours: Daily 07:00–23:00 (Fri until 01:00)

name: Garden Bar Marina
description: Neighborhood café-bar near Poljud stadium with a large garden terrace, cheap coffee and a wide beer selection. It fills with singing Hajduk fans after home matches.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ulica Zrinsko Frankopanska 28, near Poljud stadium; about 25–30 minutes on foot from the port.
Hours: Mon–Fri 07:00–23:00; Sat–Sun 08:00–00:00

name: Cafe Sport-Cafe
description: Everyday local coffee bar beside the Poljud pool and sports complex. It is drinks-focused with very limited food, and good coffee at local prices.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Osmih mediteranskih igara 21, by the Poljud pools.
Hours: Mon–Sat 07:00–23:00; closed Sunday

name: Konoba Fortin
description: Family-run konoba at the quiet western end of Trogir's old town and one of the island-town's most loved tables. Grilled fish and squid, fish soup and the classic Dalmatian side of potatoes with Swiss chard are the things to order. Finish with the house carob liqueur.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner; it fills fast. Walk-ins sometimes seated at lunch.
Getting there: Western edge of Trogir old town on Hrvatskih mučenika, near the Kamerlengo fortress end. Trogir is about 27 km west of the Split cruise port, roughly 30–40 min by taxi or Uber, or about 1 hr on city bus 37.
Hours: Mon–Sat 12:00–22:00; closed Sun

name: Queen Teuta restaurant
description: Polished old-town seafood house where you pick your fish from the display and see it weighed before it goes on the grill. Ceviche, beetroot salad and the green risotto get steady praise, and misting fans keep the terrace bearable at midday. Ask the per-kilo fish price before ordering.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner: +385 91 534 6602
Getting there: Matije Gupca 16, in the heart of Trogir old town. About 30–40 min by taxi from the Split cruise port.
Hours: Daily 8:00–23:00

name: ALKA - Fine Food Old Money Style Restaurant
description: Warm, owner-run restaurant near the Kamerlengo end of the old town, with desserts made with the owner's mother. A good-value two-course lunch special runs into mid-afternoon, and the shared meal-for-two is popular at dinner. Service is consistently singled out.
mapQuery: ALKA Fine Food Restaurant Trogir Split
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner: +385 91 202 3639
Getting there: Blaženog Augustina Kažotića 15, southwest corner of Trogir old town. About 30–40 min by taxi from the Split cruise port.
Hours: Daily 10:00–23:30 (Fri to 23:00)

name: Restaurant Kamerlengo
description: Stone courtyard restaurant beside the Kamerlengo fortress, known for whole fresh fish filleted tableside and a generous tomahawk steak. Fish and shrimp soups are standouts. Confirm the per-kilo fish price up front to avoid a surprise bill.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner: +385 21 884 772
Getting there: Vukovarska 2, by Kamerlengo Fortress at the southwest tip of the old town. About 30–40 min by taxi from the Split cruise port.
Hours: Daily 9:00–00:00

name: Casa Don Dino
description: Stylish all-day spot that works for brunch (breakfast wrap, shakshuka) and dinner alike. Tuna tartare, tuna tacos, tuna steak and the house risotto are the signatures, backed by good cocktails. Smaller and newer than the old-town classics.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner: +385 97 705 5560
Getting there: Matije Gupca 14, central Trogir old town next to Queen Teuta. About 30–40 min by taxi from the Split cruise port.
Hours: Daily 8:00–00:00

name: Konoba Toma
description: Busy, mid-priced old-town konoba with a pleasant terrace and staff who handle large groups without a booking. The fish platter for two is the go-to order. Tips cannot be added by card, so carry some euros.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in usually fine; call ahead for big groups: +385 91 781 7142
Getting there: Šubićeva 44, western part of Trogir old town. About 30–40 min by taxi from the Split cruise port.
Hours: Daily 12:00–00:00

name: Konoba Škrapa
