Hours: Tue–Sun 12:00–22:30; closed Mon

name: Strada Restaurant
description: Courtyard-garden restaurant near the sea in Kaštel Gomilica with a polished, almost upscale feel at mid-range prices. Black risotto, shrimp risotto, grilled squid, tuna and sea bass with chard are favourites.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner: +385 95 367 5700
Getting there: Primorska 58, Kaštel Gomilica. About 15–20 min by taxi from the Split cruise port.
Hours: Thu–Tue 9:00–23:00; closed Wed

name: Restoran Spinnaker Marina Kaštela
description: Upscale marina restaurant with a patio over the yachts and beautiful sunsets, a go-to for anniversaries. Sea bass ceviche and seafood starters are highlights.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve for sunset: +385 98 921 4433
Getting there: Obala kralja Tomislava 10a, Marina Kaštela in Kaštel Gomilica. About 15–20 min by taxi from the Split cruise port.
Hours: Wed–Thu 12:00–23:00; Fri–Sun 8:00–23:00; closed Mon–Tue

name: Angolo
description: Straightforward roadside restaurant with well-cooked rib-eye, meat and seafood platters, chicken in gorgonzola and pizza at reasonable prices. Card accepted; it sits on the main road rather than the sea.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; +385 21 222 102
Getting there: Cesta Dr. Franje Tuđmana 396, Kaštel Gomilica. About 15–20 min by taxi from the Split cruise port.
Hours: Daily 8:00–23:00

name: PASTA DALMATA
description: Small family pasta kitchen with homemade pasta and playfully named dishes, closest of this zone's restaurants to Split. Quick, warm and very reasonably priced; a good stop on the Split–Trogir drive.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; +385 21 209 777
Getting there: Putaljski put 1, Kaštel Sućurac, just off the main road. About 15 min by taxi from the Split cruise port.
Hours: Wed–Mon 10:00–23:00; closed Tue

name: Putalj
description: Mountain lodge-restaurant high on Kozjak above Kaštel Sućurac with breathtaking views over the bay, Split and the islands. A short chalkboard menu of the day, soup and dessert, popular with hikers; also has hostel-style rooms.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call ahead: +385 98 131 8481
Getting there: Above Kaštel Sućurac on the Kozjak slope. The access road is rough and a high-clearance vehicle is advised; parking at the top is limited, so many park lower and walk up. Hiking up from Kaštela takes about 2 hours. A true half-day commitment from the Split cruise port.
Hours: Tue–Sun 11:00–20:00; closed Mon

name: Konoba Gurman
description: A hugely popular local konoba on the western edge of Solin, packed with Croatian families for its massive portions and fair prices. Mixed grills, stuffed pork, and traditional stuffed beef are the dishes to order, served in a charming rustic interior. It also sells house-made cakes and wine, and has its own free parking.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Strongly recommended — call +385 21 817 091
Getting there: Kaštelanska ul. 2, west Solin near the Kaštela road; about 20 minutes by taxi or car from Split. A half-day outing best paired with the Salona ruins (about 5 minutes away by car).
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:30–24:00; closed Sunday

name: Street Restaurant 21210
description: A modern, air-conditioned restaurant in central Solin that goes well beyond its 'street food' name. Burgers with quality ingredients, burrata, mixed grills, stuffed turkey, and newer dishes like gnocchi with squid all earn praise. Service is warm, often with a complimentary cherry liqueur.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 21 280 212 for groups
Getting there: Ul. kralja Zvonimira 74, central Solin by the Jadro river; about 20 minutes by car, taxi, or local bus from Split. Combine with Salona as a half-day trip.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:00–23:30; closed Sunday

name: Girasole
description: An established Solin restaurant near the tourist office and the Jadro river, with a garden terrace. Gnocchi with pašticada, rich and red-wine braised, is the standout. Service can be uneven when it is busy, and smoking is permitted in parts of the restaurant.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended on weekends — call +385 21 262 215
Getting there: Ul. kralja Zvonimira 4, central Solin; about 20 minutes by car or local bus from Split.
Hours: Tue–Sun 9:00–24:00; closed Monday

name: River Pizzeria Konoba
description: A riverside pizzeria-konoba on the Jadro where you can watch ducks from the windows. Large, inexpensive pizzas (about €10) and cheap beer are the draw; grilled platters get mixed reviews, so stick to pizza. Staff are accommodating with gluten- and dairy-free requests.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ul. kralja Zvonimira 46, central Solin on the Jadro river; about 20 minutes from Split.
Hours: Daily 10:00–24:00

name: Green Park Restaurant
description: A family restaurant-café by Solin's riverside park serving pizzas, burgers, and steaks in generous portions. It is a handy all-day stop, but smoking is allowed in the main room and service slows when the kitchen is busy.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ul. Grada Vukovara 12, central Solin near the river park; about 20 minutes from Split.
Hours: Mon–Sat 7:00–23:00; Sun 8:00–23:00

name: B Cool Food & Bar
description: A casual food bar beside the Jadro river with towering burgers like the 'Terminator', quesadillas, truffle-cheese fries, and good pizza. It works well for a relaxed lunch or drinks on a hot day by the cool river.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 91 589 7608
Getting there: Ul. kralja Zvonimira 52, central Solin on the Jadro; about 20 minutes from Split.
Hours: Mon–Thu 15:00–24:00; Fri 15:00–01:00; Sat 12:00–01:00; Sun 12:00–24:00

name: Gastro kutak Jadro
description: A friendly grill near the source of the Jadro river, ideal for lunch before or after a cool riverside walk. Trout, steaks, ćevapi, and a chicken platter for two are favorites, and grilled vegetables keep vegetarians happy. Prices are low and it is child-friendly.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 91 611 7625
Getting there: Put Majdana 50, upper Solin near the Jadro spring; about 25 minutes by car from Split. A half-day outing; pair with the Jadro river walk.
Hours: Tue–Sun 9:00–23:00; closed Monday

name: Salona street food
description: A small street-food spot close to the Salona archaeological site, known for big smash burgers, generously topped pizzas, and Italian-style sandwiches. A fast, cheap lunch right after touring the ruins.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ul. Svetog Nikole 16A, a few minutes' walk from the Salona ruins entrance; about 20 minutes from Split.
Hours: Mon–Fri 10:00–23:00; Sat 17:00–23:00; closed Sunday

name: Fast food A je to
description: A friendly neighborhood fast-food counter with stuffed burgers, fresh tuna sandwiches, and tuna salads at local prices. A good quick bite in north Solin.
mapQuery: Fast food A je to Solin
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ul. dr. Martina Žižića 11, north Solin; about 20 minutes from Split.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:00–22:30; Sat 11:00–22:30; closed Sunday

name: Antonio Pizzeria / Konoba
description: A pizzeria-konoba in Mravince on the hillside above Solin, with a quiet street terrace. Pizzas, pašticada, carbonara, and a Dalmatian cold-cut platter are well made, and prices are fair for the Split area. It is busier after 20:00.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 21 219 131 for groups
Getting there: Ul. Braće Radić 1, Mravince, on the eastern side of Solin; about 20 minutes by car from Split.
Hours: Daily 8:00–23:00

name: Perlica
description: Klis's most famous lamb house, roasting whole lambs on the spit at Grlo, the pass below the fortress, with beef or veal under the peka bell also available. Lamb is priced per person, so ask about portion weight before ordering. Some recent reviews report disputes over meat substitutions, so confirm what you are ordering.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended on weekends — call +385 21 240 004
Getting there: Trg Grlo 1, Klis, on the main road just above Klis Fortress; about 25 minutes by car or taxi from Split, or by Promet Split local bus. A half-day trip; pair with Klis Fortress.
Hours: Daily 9:00–22:00

name: Tavern Klis
description: A lunch-only garden tavern in the Klis hamlet of Mihovilovići, tied to an olive-oil and heritage visit with tastings and a gift shop. Food is limited to a few set combinations, mostly traditional pasta and gnocchi, with excellent desserts and lemonade. Best treated as part of a tasting experience rather than a full menu restaurant.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — call +385 99 215 0250
Getting there: Mihovilovići, Klis, about 1 km east of Klis Grlo; about 25 minutes by car from Split. Car or tour recommended; a half-day trip.
Hours: Mon–Sat 11:00–15:30; closed Sunday

name: Belfast Klis
description: A simple café-bar on Klis Megdan square at the foot of the fortress, useful for an espresso, cold drink, or snack before or after the climb or the nearby zipline. Prices are low. Cash only, and smoking is permitted indoors.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (cash only)
Getting there: Trg Mejdan 7, Klis Megdan, directly below Klis Fortress; about 20 minutes by car from Split.
Hours: Daily 7:00–24:00

name: Cafe Oprah
description: A local café near Klis Megdan known for good coffee and a selection of Belgian beers. It serves drinks only, no food.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ul. kneza Trpimira 229, Klis, a short walk below Klis Megdan; about 20 minutes by car from Split.
Hours: Mon–Sat 6:00–23:00; Sun 7:00–23:00

name: Mlin bar Solin
description: A café beside the historic Gašpina mill on the Jadro river, with ducks paddling past and the sound of rushing water. It is a tranquil spot for coffee and light bites while exploring Solin.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ul. Gašpina mlinica 38, Solin, at the restored mills on the Jadro; about 20 minutes from Split.
Hours: Mon–Sat 7:00–23:00; Sun 7:30–23:00

name: Bar Aura
description: A popular café in a converted old mill building with a millstream running alongside and beneath its patio. Good coffee and rakija in a fenced garden that is easy with kids, though it gets crowded on weekends.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ul. Marka Marulića 7, central Solin near Hotel President; about 20 minutes from Split.
Hours: Mon–Sat 6:30–24:00; Sun 7:00–24:00

name: Art Caffe
description: A modern café-bar by the Jadro river park with indoor and outdoor seating, a children's playground, and well-priced signature cocktails. Smoking is permitted inside.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ulica Grada Vukovara 5a, central Solin by the river park; about 20 minutes from Split.
Hours: Daily 7:00–23:00

name: Caffe bar Corte Cafeteria
description: A relaxed local café on Solin's main street, good for coffee and people-watching. Table service can be slow at times.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ul. kralja Zvonimira 50, central Solin; about 20 minutes from Split.
Hours: Daily 7:00–23:00

name: Caffe bar Galerija
description: A legendary neighborhood café in Solin with a cheerful owner, strong coffee, and cheap, ice-cold beer. A genuine slice of local life.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Petra Krešimira IV, east Solin; about 20 minutes from Split.
Hours: Mon–Sat 7:00–22:00; Sun 7:00–15:00

name: Siesta Caffe Bar Solin
description: A small local café near the Salona archaeological area, handy for an espresso before or after touring the ruins. Service is casual, so you may need to order at the bar.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ul. don Frane Bulića 68k, Solin, close to the Salona ruins; about 20 minutes from Split.
Hours: Daily 7:00–23:00

name: Na terenu
description: A café-bar in upper Solin with good coffee, friendly hosts, and a large parking area. It is a convenient stop on the drive up toward Klis.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ul. fra Grge Martića 9, upper Solin on the way to Klis; about 20 minutes by car from Split.
Hours: Daily 8:00–24:00

name: Viadel Slastice
description: A traditional pastry shop selling Croatian cakes and cookies by weight at very low prices. It is good for take-away treats, but some visitors report a 1 kg minimum.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Bunje ul. 62, west Solin near Konoba Gurman; about 20 minutes from Split.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:00–21:00; closed Sunday

name: Slatkarija
description: A small dessert shop on Solin's main street with pancakes and ice cream, praised for friendly service. It has very few reviews so far.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ul. kralja Zvonimira 10, central Solin; about 20 minutes from Split.

name: Dalmatino
description: Hvar Town's most consistently praised dinner, in a stone lane just off the main square. The kitchen is upscale Dalmatian with truffle gnocchi, tuna tartare, fish soup, brodetto and excellent steaks. Service is slick and warm, and a truffle-polenta amuse-bouche with house liqueur sets the tone.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead, as it fills most evenings in season.
Getting there: Hvar Town, 3 minutes from the catamaran stop on the Riva. Split–Hvar Town catamaran takes about 1 hour each way, so with 9 hours ashore this is a full-day commitment; check return sailings before booking.
Hours: Mon–Sat 12:00–00:00; closed Sunday

name: Konoba Elysium
description: Newer seafood konoba on a quiet side street of the old town, run by a young, energetic team. It is known for scampi buzara, Adriatic mussels, prosciutto, truffle pasta and 'poor man's lobster', with good wine pairing advice.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 91 727 8484.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Marije Maričić 17, a few minutes from the Riva. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 12:00–00:00

name: Restaurant Stajun Hvar
description: Polished Mediterranean seafood restaurant with a beautiful dining space and a standout raw bar of scallop carpaccio and crudo. Whole oven-baked sea bass is made for sharing, and lamb chops and Irish ribeye cover meat-eaters. The service is notably knowledgeable.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve: +385 91 915 4479.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Težačka 2, just off the main square. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 12:00–00:00

name: Mediterraneo Dine & Wine
description: Fine-dining restaurant in a historic stone courtyard, where every course is explained tableside. It offers elegant Mediterranean plates and a deep Croatian wine list. A strong choice for a special-occasion dinner if staying overnight on Hvar.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead: +385 91 949 7808.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Braće Bibić 15, steps from the Riva. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 12:00–00:00

name: Val Marina Restaurant
description: Waterfront hotel restaurant on the Fabrika side of the harbor with sunset views across to the Pakleni Islands. The cooking is refined Mediterranean, with seafood platters, grilled octopus and cod, and the welcome prosecco and polished service set it apart. It handles large groups well.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve: +385 21 750 200.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Fabrika, a 5-minute harborside walk west of the Riva. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily breakfast 07:00–11:00; dinner 18:00–23:00 (no lunch service)

name: Aria Restaurant
description: Sea-view terrace restaurant on the Fabrika waterfront with a welcome drink, warm service and fresh-caught seafood. Monkfish, seafood risotto, tuna carpaccio and truffle gnocchi with prosciutto are the dishes guests rave about. It works equally well for a long lunch or sunset dinner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 95 799 8739.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Fabrika 32, 5 minutes west of the Riva. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:00

name: Dva Ribara
description: Relaxed harborside restaurant whose specialty is whole fish such as scorpion fish cooked over wood fire, plus fish soup and seafood platters. It is a reliable waterfront lunch with professional service and good Croatian whites.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 99 868 3576.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Fabrika 31, on the western harbor. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:00

name: Plava Alga
description: Riva restaurant overlooking the yachts, good for classic Dalmatian dishes like grilled sea bass, fish soup and pašticada with homemade gnocchi. It has prime people-watching and friendly service that will debone your fish, and it is right where the catamaran lands.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 21 717 061 for dinner.
Getting there: Hvar Town, on the Riva near the catamaran stop. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 11:45–23:00

name: Restaurant Faria
description: Leafy garden terrace a short walk above the harbor, popular on the way down from the Fortica fortress. It serves grilled scampi and octopus, crispy sea bass, seafood pasta and pizza, with occasional live music and good value for Hvar.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 91 881 3995.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Dr. Mate Miličića 12. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:00

name: Grande Luna
description: Open rooftop-terrace restaurant a couple of minutes off the marina, known for huge, well-priced seafood platters for two, shrimp-and-truffle pasta and fried fish platters. Staff are friendly, and the prices are noticeably fairer than the waterfront.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 21 741 400.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Petra Hektorovića 1, behind the main square. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:00

name: Restaurant Park Hvar
description: Elegant hotel restaurant reached through a lush garden entrance, with a terrace overlooking the town. Menu standouts include octopus, prawn tartare, aged beef, tempura prawns and well-made cocktails.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 21 741 149.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Ul. Sveti Marak 2, by the main square. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily breakfast 07:00–11:00; dinner 18:00–23:00

name: Black Pepper Restaurant
description: Creative fine dining set right on the flower-lined stone stairway leading up to the fortress. The steak tartare, cuttlefish and duck are frequently singled out, and the presentation is meticulous. It is dinner only and fills fast.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve in advance: +385 95 750 9790.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Skaline od Gojave 11, on the steps toward Fortica. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 18:00–00:00 (dinner only)

name: Paradise Garden Hvar
description: Atmospheric garden restaurant with stylish décor and music, popular for celebrations. It serves seafood platters, octopus carpaccio, seafood pots and a signature peach-shaped tiramisu. Reviews on some mains are mixed, but the setting and service are strong.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 95 508 6972.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Dr. Mate Miličića 8. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Sun–Thu 15:00–00:00; closed Friday & Saturday

name: Konoba Menego
description: Rustic, candlelit konoba on the old-town stairs that deliberately serves only traditional Hvar and Dalmatian food, with no pizza and no pasta. It is known for tuna pašticada, handmade gnocchi, octopus carpaccio and homemade cakes. Portions are modest, so plan on several courses.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; arrive early for dinner.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Kroz Grodu 26, in the old town. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Mon–Sat 12:00–14:00 and 18:00–22:30; closed Sunday

name: Fig Hvar
description: Laid-back, globally inspired café-restaurant just above the main square, strongest at breakfast and lunch. It serves flatbreads, Buddha bowls, burritos and chimichurri fries plus local Hvar Brewing beers. It is very vegetarian- and vegan-friendly.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Hvar Town, Ivana Frane Biundovića 3. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 09:00–22:00

name: Code 11
description: Tropical-styled seaside restaurant and lounge a few minutes around the bay from the Riva, with sunbeds by day and sunset dinners by night. It serves salads, pizzas, seafood and a lava-cake dessert at prices more reasonable than central Hvar.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 91 887 1266.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Fulgencija careva 1, a short walk south-east around the harbor. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 10:30–22:30

name: KOGO - Pizza, Pasta & Grill
description: Long-running, fast and friendly all-rounder on St. Stephen's Square, Croatia's largest piazza. It serves thin-crust pizza, pasta, fish and burgers in a prime setting. Many day-tour skippers recommend it as a reliable lunch.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 98 582 531 for groups.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Trg sv. Stjepana 34. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 10:00–00:00

name: BB Club
description: All-day harborfront restaurant at the Riva Marina hotel. It offers an egg-bar brunch, smash burgers, pizza, shawarma and well-made cocktails. It is convenient for groups arriving off the catamaran.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 21 750 100 for groups.
Getting there: Hvar Town, on the Riva steps from the catamaran stop. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 07:00–00:00

name: SEVEN - Pizza & Burgers Hvar
description: Late-night pizza, burger and steak-pasta spot near the harbor that doubles as a bar. It is popular for a post-dinner or post-club bite.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Hvar Town, Fabrika 1. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 18:00–02:00

name: Fast Food Big Bang
description: Family-run budget grill about 8–10 minutes' walk east of the square. It serves huge ćevapi, chicken burgers and salads at a fraction of waterfront prices, and is a great value pick in an expensive town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Hvar Town, Miće Marchija 12, east of the center. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 15:30–22:30

name: kava37
description: Family-run specialty-coffee shop widely considered the best coffee in Hvar Town, even pouring single-origin geisha. It serves excellent cappuccinos with plant milks, fresh juices and light breakfast. It closes mid-afternoon.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Hvar Town, Kroz Burak 37, a block behind the Riva. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 07:00–15:00

name: Nonica Caffe Bar
description: Charming pastry café in an old-town alley with elaborate house-made cakes. The raspberry brownie and the Bella Maria are favorites. It is good for coffee and dessert any time of day.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Hvar Town, Kroz Burak 23. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Mon–Sat 08:00–21:00; Sun 14:30–21:00

name: aROMA Gelato
description: Creamy natural gelato on the Riva, with tiramisu, Madagascar vanilla and dark chocolate as standouts. It is a handy treat while waiting for the return catamaran. Note that the nearby Riva 4 branch rates lower.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Hvar Town, Riva 10. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.

name: ASTIGAMANDE - Gelato & Paradižot Bar
description: Gelato and dessert bar on the main square, named after the traditional paradižot custard. Many visitors rate it the best gelato in town, though a minority report inconsistent service.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Hvar Town, Trg sv. Stjepana 3. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 08:00–00:00

name: Wine Bar Kronjac Hvar
description: Small family-run wine bar in the old town pouring local Hvar wines with cheese and charcuterie boards. The host knows the wines well and explains them.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 91 597 3873 for groups.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Kroz Grodu 22. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Mon–Sat 18:00–00:00; closed Sunday

name: KAVINO
description: Newer alley bar focused on Hvar wines and produce from local farms, with coffee in the morning. It is known for espresso martinis and genuinely warm hosts, and feels authentically local.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Hvar Town, Petra Hektorovića 5. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 08:00–12:00 and 18:00–02:00

name: Vintage Bar Hvar
description: Lively bar-kitchen with creative small plates like bao buns, ćevapi dumplings, sea bass ceviche and polenta fries, plus strong cocktails. It has good vegan options and gets busy at night.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book for dinner: +385 91 489 3377.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Obala Fabrika 4a. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 18:00–02:00

name: Teraca Bar
description: Hidden terrace bar with handmade wooden furniture, vinyl on the turntable and views over the square, cathedral and fortress. It is a classic sunset Aperol spot with a mixed local crowd.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Hvar Town, above the main square. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.

name: Central Park Club, Hvar
description: Popular bar-restaurant near the waterfront with multiple terraces, sandwiches and wraps by day, and live jazz and cocktails by night. The Bloody Mary is a favorite.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Hvar Town, Ul. Sveti Marak 2. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 07:00–02:00

name: Spritz Bar Garip Hvar
description: Small Riva café-bar for spritzes, including the local pelin spritz, with little desserts and free cold tap water. It is a shady people-watching stop. There is no food beyond sweets.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Hvar Town, Riva 2. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 08:00–00:00

name: Beach Club Hvar
description: Full-service beach club on the promenade west of town with sunbeds, easy sea access, a restaurant and attentive service. It suits a slow half-day of swimming and lunch, though the kitchen closes earlier than the bar.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve sunbeds: +385 91 174 1589.
Getting there: Hvar Town, Šetalište Tonija Petrića 3, about 10 minutes' walk west of the Riva. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split.
Hours: Daily 10:00–00:00

name: Calma Beach Bar
description: Tiny rock-perched bar on a calm, pine-shaded cove west of Hvar Town, often visited on boat tours. It serves drinks only, with no food and no menu, and makes a peaceful swim-and-drink stop.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: West coast of Hvar, beyond Hvar Town. Easiest by boat tour or taxi boat; requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split plus onward transport.
Hours: Daily 12:00–21:00

name: Konoba Ringo
description: Family-run seafood konoba in quiet Pribinja cove north of Hvar Town, decorated with fishing nets and hand-carved wood. It serves exceptionally fresh whole fish explained tableside. It is dinner only and a destination meal for overnight guests.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve: +385 91 510 3686.

name: Ristorante Palmizana Meneghello
description: Family-run seafood restaurant set inside the Meneghello botanical garden on Palmižana in the Pakleni Islands. It is known for lobster, langoustines, black risotto and grilled John Dory with generous portions, and is a dreamy long lunch.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 91 478 3111.

name: Zori Timeless Hotel & Restaurant
description: Upscale hotel restaurant above Palmižana bay with a romantic sunset terrace and haute-cuisine leanings. Service gets glowing mentions, but prices are high and some find the food overpriced.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 91 322 2227.
Getting there: Palmižana, Pakleni Islands, about 20–30 minutes by taxi boat from Hvar Town harbor.

name: Max Fast Food
description: Friendly snack bar at the ACI marina on Palmižana serving burgers, pizza and drinks. It is a budget alternative to the island's pricier restaurants.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: ACI Marina Palmižana, Pakleni Islands, reached by taxi boat from Hvar Town.
Hours: Daily 09:00–00:00

name: BioMania Bistro Bol
description: Bol's top-rated restaurant, a plant-based bistro whose creative bowls, burgers and raw desserts win over non-vegans too. It has a great brunch, good coffee and matcha, and free filtered water.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 91 936 2276 for groups.
Getting there: Bol, Rudina 10, near the harbor. Split–Bol catamaran takes about 1 hour with limited daily sailings; check times. Alternatively take the ferry to Supetar and drive or bus about 40 minutes.

name: Argento
description: Sea-view terrace restaurant on Bol's eastern waterfront, a local favorite for sunsets. It serves generous fish platters, tuna steak, shrimp tagliatelle and buzara with warm, professional service.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 91 110 0636.
Getting there: Bol, Hrvatskih Domobrana 83. Requires the 1-hour catamaran from Split or ferry to Supetar plus a 40-minute drive.
Hours: Daily 08:00–22:00

name: Konoba Dinko
description: Small family konoba on the water just east of Bol's center, with simply cooked fresh fish and excellent house white. It has few tables, so expect a queue in season. It is dinner only and best for overnight visitors.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 98 522 479, or arrive early.
Getting there: Bol, Ante Starčevića 1, east end of the waterfront.
Hours: Daily 18:00–00:00 (dinner only)

name: Konoba Gušt
description: Stone-walled tavern in the heart of Bol, best for peka, octopus and generous traditional plates with local wine. It is family-run with professional service.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 91 404 3682.
Getting there: Bol, Ul. Radića Frane 14, near the harbor.
Hours: Daily 16:00–00:00

name: Pumparela Restaurant
description: Marina-side restaurant open from breakfast to late, with very fresh tuna and seafood, homemade bread, and patio heaters for cooler months. It offers good quality at fair prices.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 99 507 1820 for evening tables.
Getting there: Bol, Ul. Bolskih Pomoraca 16, by the marina where the catamaran docks.
Hours: Daily 07:00–00:00

name: Ranc Restaurant
description: Quiet terrace-and-garden restaurant west of the harbor crowds. Dishes include traditional octopus with potatoes, squid-ink risotto, grilled calamari and an excellent seafood platter.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 21 635 635.
Getting there: Bol, Hrvatskih Domobrana 23, about 10 minutes west of the harbor toward Zlatni Rat.

name: Riva - Bol
description: Harborfront bistro under a big shade tree, good for a quick seafood lunch of octopus salad, grilled squid and lamb chops. It is family-friendly and finishes with a house brandy.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 21 635 236.
Getting there: Bol, Ul. Radića Frane 5, on the harbor.

name: Ribarska Kućica
description: 'The Fisherman's Hut', set right at the water's edge in a tucked-away cove east of Bol. It serves fresh fish, octopus salad, mussels and risotto with great house white. Ask for a table by the sea.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 21 635 033.
Getting there: Bol, Ante Starčevića, east of the center along the coast path.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:00

name: Restaurant - Pizzeria Bava Bol
description: Seafront pizzeria-restaurant at the start of the Zlatni Rat promenade, good for wood-oven bread, grilled squid, prawn pasta and pizza at reasonable prices. It can be slow when busy.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 98 193 9097.
Getting there: Bol, Put Zlatnog Rata 2A, at the start of the walk to Zlatni Rat.

name: Caffè Bar Kala
description: Pine-shaded local hangout with a sea view, cold beer and excellent pizzas and homemade lasagna. It has a relaxed, locals-heavy vibe.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Bol, Ul. Hrvatskog preporoda, east side of town.

description: Wood-fired pizzeria a few minutes inland, cheaper than the harbor, with seafood pizza, lasagna and big meat platters. The back room is dark, so sit up front.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 21 582 345.

name: Pizzeria Gogy
description: Roman-style pizza joint known for the best price-to-quality in Bol. It is mainly delivery and takeaway, though the owner will seat you outside.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Order by phone: +385 91 526 6167.

name: Beach Bar NOA
description: Beachfront bar-restaurant on the path to Zlatni Rat, beside the kitesurf area. It serves local wine, shark steak, fresh plates and reggae-soundtracked sundowners.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

name: Cocktail Bar Bolero
description: Open-air lounge under pines beside the Zlatni Rat path, with comfy wicker seating, cicadas, well-made cocktails and desserts. It is a daytime spot and closes early evening.

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

name: Varadero

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

name: Konoba Vinotoka
description: Atmospheric konoba with tables set along a white-stone lane just off the harbor. It is famous for its green pasta with seafood, alongside fish platters, prawn tartare and truffle pasta, and is recommended by locals.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 99 463 1984.

name: KONOBA KETY
description: Waterside konoba on Supetar's harbor with well-cooked tuna steak, beef tartare and salted-caramel pancakes. It has a pleasant atmosphere right by the water.
details:

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 21 672 755.

name: Jure

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

Reservations / tickets: Call +385 98 191 3210.

name: Bunja Restaurant & More
description: Beachfront restaurant at a boutique campsite east of Supetar, serving clam-packed seafood pasta, cuttlefish with fava, tomahawk steak and sharing platters. It is open all day.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 99 169 6175.

name: Agroturizam Hrapoćuša
description: Family farm restaurant among olive groves and vineyards in the stone village of Dol. Lamb or veal peka is slow-cooked for hours, with house wine, cured meats, cheese and the namesake Hrapoćuša cake. It is one of Brač's most memorable meals.

name: Specijal Supetar

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

name: Caffe bar Kiwi
description: Family-run café and ice cream bar steps from the harbor, praised for creamy gelato and coffee in a relaxed, unhurried setting. Check your bill.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

name: Pekara Diana

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

name: Beach bar SPACE FUN
description: Budget-friendly beach bar by Tri Mosta beach for coffee, cocktails and sunsets with upbeat music.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

name: Hotel Osam Rooftop Bar
description: Rooftop cocktail bar with the best sunset panorama over Supetar's town and bay, and free entry. Drinks are mixed in quality, but the view is the draw.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

name: Restaurant Panorama
description: The restaurant at the top of the Dubrovnik cable car, 405 m above the Old Town, with a tiered terrace looking straight down on the walls, Lokrum and the Elaphiti Islands. The Mediterranean menu is solid rather than spectacular; the view is the reason to come. Lunch is breezy and shaded by umbrellas, and sunset dinner, as the city lights come on, is the signature experience.
tags: verify: cable car last descent time
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve online or call +385 20 312 664. Book front-row terrace tables 3–4+ weeks ahead in season, longer for sunset. Walk-ins are sometimes seated, more easily at lunch.
Getting there: Take the Dubrovnik Cable Car from the lower station on Petra Krešimira IV, a 5-min walk uphill from the Old Town's Buža/Ploče side. The cable car is roughly €30 per person return, so for 2+ people a taxi, Uber or Bolt up the Bosanka road is cheaper. Self-drivers can park at the summit, which avoids the after-sunset queue for the cable car down. From the Gruž cruise port, allow about 15 min by taxi to the lower station or about 20–25 min to drive to the summit. Hikers can walk up the rocky switchback trail from the Jadranska road in about 1 hour; wear proper shoes, not sandals.
Hours: Daily 9:00–21:00

name: Konoba Dubrava
description: Rustic, family-style konoba in the village of Bosanka on the Srđ plateau, well known for peka: meat or octopus slow-cooked under an iron bell in the embers. The mixed meat peka, veal and lamb, stuffed pljeskavica and strudel are the orders, in a quiet setting far from Old Town crowds. Dogs are welcome inside and out.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve: +385 95 420 4000. Peka must be ordered at least 3 hours in advance.
Getting there: Bosanka village, on the plateau behind Mount Srđ, about 10–15 min by taxi or car from the Old Town and roughly 20–25 min from the Gruž cruise port. There is no public transport to speak of, so plan a taxi both ways. It can be paired with a drive up to the Srđ summit viewpoint nearby.
Hours: Daily 11:00–00:00

name: Bon Appetit Bistro - Pizzeria
description: A busy all-day bistro on the Gruž harbor promenade with a terrace facing the boats. Seafood spaghetti, seafood risotto, chicken wok, tuna, and burgers are reliable and fairly priced for Dubrovnik. Locals and ferry passengers fill it in the evening, so arrive before 19:00 or book.
details:

name: Bistro Glorijet

name: Porat Restaurant

name: Pekara Mare

Hours: Daily 8:00–24:00

name: Madonna
description: A long-standing family restaurant run by four brothers, with a lovely upper terrace in Lapad. Simple, very fresh grilled sea bass, mussels, squid risotto, and steaks are the draws.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for the terrace — call +385 20 436 253
Getting there: Ul. Mata Vodopića 6, just off the Lapad promenade.
Hours: Daily 11:00–23:30

name: Fish Bar El Pulpo
description: A popular, good-value fish bar in Lapad with a cozy garden. The seafood platter for two (around €58) is the star. Waits for mains can reach an hour on busy nights, so book 2–3 days ahead.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Strongly recommended — call +385 20 294 028
Getting there: Ul. Mata Vodopića 6, off the Lapad promenade.
Hours: Mon–Sat 12:00–23:30; Sun 16:00–23:30

name: Shizuku -Japanese cuisine-
description: A stylish Japanese and Asian restaurant in Lapad with crystal rolls, tempura, green curry, and a good dessert list. It is very popular in the evening, so reserve for 19:00–21:00.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — call +385 20 311 493
Getting there: Ul. Mata Vodopića 2A, Lapad, next to the Grand Hotel Park.
Hours: Tue–Sun 12:00–24:00; closed Monday

name: Trinity Oriental Fusion Lounge
description: A Thai, Japanese, and fusion lounge in Lapad praised for authentic green curry, pad thai, crispy karaage, and generous sushi at fair prices. Book ahead in season; outdoor tables can be sunny early in the evening.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — call +385 20 752 575
Getting there: Ul. Mata Vodopića 2A, Lapad.
Hours: Tue–Sun 12:00–24:00; closed Monday

name: The Food Bar Dubrovnik
description: A relaxed brunch café by a pool in Lapad with a breakfast buffet (about €15 with drinks), granola and chicken bowls, pistachio-mortadella focaccia, and good coffee. A tranquil alternative to the busy promenade.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Ul. Mata Vodopića 4a, Lapad.
Hours: Daily 7:00–21:00

name: Pull Over Restaurant
description: A busy promenade restaurant in Lapad with a wide menu spanning steaks, burgers, gyoza, sushi, and bao, plus good daiquiris. Portions are larger in the evening; payment handling can be fussy.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — call +385 91 177 7767
Getting there: Šetalište kralja Zvonimira 18, Lapad promenade.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:45

name: Caffe&Cocktail Bar Promenada
description: A modern café-bar with a big terrace on the Lapad promenade and a huge cocktail menu. Good for morning coffee or evening drinks, though service can be inattentive when busy.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Šetalište kralja Zvonimira 22, Lapad promenade.
Hours: Daily 9:00–02:00

name: Moritz Eis Gelato Sunset Beach
description: A creative gelato counter at Sunset Beach in Lapad, with rotating natural flavors like dragon fruit-lime and pineapple-mint, plus excellent dark chocolate. Staff happily offer tastes.
mapQuery: Moritz Eis Gelato Sunset Beach Dubrovnik
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Šetalište Nika i Meda Pucića 1, Sunset Beach at the end of the Lapad promenade.
Hours: Daily 11:00–22:00

name: Mango's Kitchen & Bar
description: An upstairs terrace restaurant facing Lapad Bay, perfectly placed for sunset. Pizza, sushi, sea bass, and tuna are good value for the setting, though service can be brisk.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for sunset — call +385 95 904 5799
Getting there: Masarykov put 3, above Lapad Bay beach.
Hours: Daily 9:00–24:00

name: Restaurant More
description: An upscale Mediterranean restaurant at Hotel More with spectacular views over the sea. Generous plates of steak, prawn risotto, and lamb shank are served by polished staff. Pair dinner with a drink in its natural Cave Bar below. Service can be slow at peak times.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Strongly recommended — call +385 20 494 200
Getting there: Ul. kardinala Stepinca 33a, on the coast between Lapad and Babin Kuk.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:00

name: Cave Bar More
description: A one-of-a-kind bar built inside a natural cave with stalactites, reached by elevator through Hotel More, plus a seaside terrace outside. Cocktails and snacks are pricey, but you are paying for an unforgettable setting.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Šetalište Nika i Meda Pucića 13, through Hotel More on the Lapad–Babin Kuk coastal walk.
Hours: Daily 8:00–24:00

name: Belvedere
description: A quiet, affordable restaurant on the hillside above Lapad with city views. Friendly service and solid food make it a good-value lunch away from the crowds.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 20 311 761
Getting there: Ul. Iva Vojnovića 58, upper Lapad (Montovjerna).
Hours: Mon–Sat 12:00–20:00; closed Sunday

name: Pivnica Dubrava
description: A pub-style grill on Babin Kuk's 'Mali Stradun' that is the area's best-rated casual dinner. Juicy burgers, mixed meat platters, and grilled octopus come with fast, friendly service.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 20 448 354
Getting there: Mali Stradun, Babin Kuk; bus 6 from Gruž or the Old Town, or about 10 minutes by taxi from the port.
Hours: Tue–Sun 12:00–23:00; closed Monday

name: Dinner In The Sky Dubrovnik
description: A table for 22 guests hoisted by crane high above Babin Kuk, with views over the sea and Elaphiti islands and a set lunch or dinner served aloft. You pay for the experience and views; the food is secondary.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Advance booking required via the Dinner in the Sky Dubrovnik website or +385 99 348 8820
Getting there: Ul. Iva Dulčića 34, Babin Kuk; about 10 minutes by taxi from Gruž port. Inexpensive parking is nearby. A timed, ticketed experience of roughly 1–2 hours.
Hours: Daily sessions 14:00–22:00

name: Coral Beach Club Dubrovnik
description: An adults-oriented beach club on Babin Kuk with daybeds, a dock for swimming, DJ sets from early afternoon, and a good restaurant. It is ideal for a full beach day; daybeds are bookable ahead.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book daybeds in advance via the club's website or +385 99 323 9430
Getting there: Ul. Ivana pl. Zajca 30, Babin Kuk near Copacabana Beach; about 10 minutes by taxi or bus 6 from Gruž. A full-day outing.

name: La Mar Restaurant
description: A beachfront hotel restaurant on Babin Kuk with fresh, high-quality Mediterranean dishes like grilled octopus and attentive servers. Prices are steep, but the setting by the water is lovely for lunch.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 20 441 109
Getting there: Ul. Iva Dulčića 142, Babin Kuk beach level; access is via the hotel and stairs.
Hours: Mon–Fri 12:00–22:00; closed Saturday and Sunday

name: Tavern Bonaca
description: A family-run seafood tavern on the water at Sustjepan, across the Rijeka Dubrovačka inlet, with sunset views. The fish platter for two, seafood risotto, steak, and famous apple pie are highlights. Dinner only.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — call +385 20 450 000
Getting there: Sustjepanska obala 23, Sustjepan; about 10 minutes by taxi from Gruž port.
Hours: Thu–Tue 17:00–22:30; closed Wednesday

name: Bistro-pizzeria Megi
description: A clean, friendly local bistro in Mokošica with a covered veranda. It serves huge mussels, meat plates that feed four, fresh fish, pizza, and lasagna at fair prices.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended on weekends — call +385 20 871 941
Getting there: Ul. uz Jadransku cestu 33, Mokošica, past the Franjo Tuđman Bridge; about 10 minutes by taxi or local bus from Gruž.
Hours: Daily 8:00–22:30

name: Pizzeria Laus
description: A local favorite in Nova Mokošica for homemade pizza, mixed meat platters, and pasta in big portions at low prices. The upstairs terrace has a nice view; it pairs well with a visit to the Ombla river spring.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 20 451 002
Getting there: Ul. od Izvora 64, Nova Mokošica, up the Rijeka Dubrovačka inlet; about 15 minutes by taxi or local bus from Gruž.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–24:00; closed Sunday

name: Konoba Galijun
description: A hotel konoba in Donje Obuljeno on the Rijeka Dubrovačka inlet, praised for excellent Dalmatian cooking in a picturesque, quiet setting. Service reviews vary.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — call +385 95 333 5335
Getting there: Gorava ul. 41, Donje Obuljeno; about 15 minutes by taxi or bus 1A/1B from Gruž.
Hours: Daily 8:00–10:00 (breakfast) and 17:00–22:00

name: Konoba Knez | Country Home
description: A farm-to-table dinner on a working family farm above Mokošica, with homemade liqueurs, cured meats and cheeses, and slow-cooked veal and lamb peka or steaks you choose yourself. Set menus are generous; drinks are charged separately.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reservation required — call +385 91 311 2029
Getting there: Pobrežje 1, hills above Mokošica; about 15–20 minutes by taxi from Gruž. A full-evening experience; arrange return transport.
Hours: Mon–Wed and Fri–Sat 18:00–23:00; Sun 12:30–17:00; closed Thursday

name: Restaurant Vimbula
description: A riverside hotel restaurant in Komolac on the Ombla, with mountain views and cool river air. Meat plates for two, sea bass, mussels, tuna steak, and bone marrow are highlights; a small cover charge applies.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — call +385 95 530 5318
Getting there: Tenturija ul. 44, Komolac, near ACI Marina Dubrovnik; about 15 minutes by taxi from Gruž.
Hours: Mon and Wed–Sun 11:00–23:00; Tue 15:00–23:00

name: Azzurro Restaurant
description: A family-run restaurant a short walk from ACI Marina in Komolac, popular with sailing crews. Pre-order peka; otherwise veal rack, grilled octopus, and celery soup with prawns are excellent, with large portions.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended; order peka a day ahead — call +385 20 871 991
Getting there: Ul. na Skali 2, Komolac by ACI Marina Dubrovnik; about 15 minutes by taxi from Gruž.
Hours: Daily 8:00–23:00

name: Capitano
description: A relaxed riverside bar-grill near the Ombla spring with local prices, pizza, and cold beer. Cash only; service reports are mixed.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (cash only)
Getting there: Tenturija ul. 96, Komolac, near the Ombla river source; about 15 minutes by taxi from Gruž.
Hours: Daily 8:00–24:00

name: Public Old Town Croatian Bistro
description: Modern Croatian bistro on Prijeko, the quieter lane running parallel to the Stradun. Inventive, beautifully plated dishes like cuttlefish orzo and beef tartare, with knowledgeable servers and a house liqueur to finish. One of the strongest all-round meals inside the walls.
mapQuery: Public Old Town Croatian Bistro Dubrovnik
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 20 747 867 for dinner; walk-ins often work at lunch.
Getting there: Old Town, Prijeko 30. From Gruž cruise port take city bus 1A/1B/3/8 or a ~10-minute taxi to Pile Gate, then walk ~5 minutes; the Old Town is car-free.
Hours: Daily 11:00–22:30

name: Trattoria Carmen
description: Small, always-busy trattoria with shaded tables against the limestone city walls near the Old Port. Known for its octopus, truffle-and-shrimp hand-rolled pasta, seafood platters and homemade gnocchi with beef stew. Expect a queue at peak times.
details:
Reservations / tickets: No phone listed; arrive early or expect a wait.
Getting there: Old Town, Ul. kneza Damjana Jude 10, by the Old Port, about 8 minutes from Pile Gate.
Hours: Tue–Sat 11:00–22:00; Sun 11:00–17:00; closed Monday

name: La Bocca Dubrovnik
description: Intimate side-street restaurant praised for top-quality ingredients, swordfish steak and attentive service. It feels like a discovery away from the Stradun crowds.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; expect a short wait after 20:00.
Getting there: Old Town, Ul. Nikole Božidarevića 10, 4 minutes from Pile Gate.
Hours: Daily 10:00–22:00

name: Gradska kavana Arsenal Restaurant
description: Historic city café-restaurant in the old Republic's galley arsenal, with soaring ceilings, live piano and a terrace over the Old Port. Seafood risotto, octopus tartare and lamb are standouts. It covers everything from breakfast and cake to a polished dinner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book for dinner: +385 20 321 202. Walk-ins may get a time-limited table.
Getting there: Old Town, Pred Dvorom 1, beside the Rector's Palace at the Old Port end of the Stradun.
Hours: Daily 08:00–00:00

name: ARKA Dubrovnik (OLD TOWN)
description: Refined modern restaurant at the foot of the Jesuit Stairs, the Game of Thrones 'walk of shame' steps. It serves tuna tartare, miso black cod, lobster and filet mignon with polished service. One of the Old Town's best settings for a special dinner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve: +385 91 610 2292.
Getting there: Old Town, Uz Jezuite 8, below the Jesuit Stairs.
Hours: Mon 15:00–00:00; Tue 12:00–00:00; Wed–Sat 08:30–00:00; Sun 15:00–00:00

name: Restaurant 360
description: Michelin-starred fine dining set on the city ramparts above the Old Port, with sweeping harbor views. Langoustine, mackerel and lamb courses are paired with a deep wine list. The splurge dinner of a Dubrovnik stay.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve well ahead and request a wall-side table: +385 20 322 222.
Getting there: Old Town, Svetog Dominika 2, on the walls by Ploče Gate.
Hours: Tue–Sun 18:00–00:30; closed Monday

name: Restaurant Dubrovnik
description: Rooftop fine-dining restaurant serving creative tasting menus with matched, mostly local wines. Sea urchin, ravioli and octopus courses get top marks. Dinner only.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve: +385 20 324 810.
Getting there: Old Town, Ul. Marojice Kaboge 5, near the Jesuit Stairs.
Hours: Daily 18:00–00:00

name: Restaurant Marco Polo
description: Michelin-recommended 36-seat restaurant with a small courtyard. The kitchen is creative Dalmatian: crab, monkfish Wellington, roast lamb and duck, oysters and arancini. The service is warm and very knowledgeable.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve: +385 20 323 719.
Getting there: Old Town, Lučarica 6, behind St. Blaise's Church.
Hours: Daily 10:00–00:00

name: Above 5 Rooftop Restaurant
description: Hotel rooftop restaurant with panoramic views over Old Town roofs. The cooking is elevated and inventive, and there is a lighter lunch menu of burgers and sea bass sandwiches. Wine guidance is excellent.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve: +385 20 322 244.
Getting there: Old Town, Od Sigurate 4 (inside Hotel Stari Grad), 3 minutes from Pile Gate.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:00

name: Forty Four Restaurant
description: Tastefully designed courtyard restaurant with a short, focused menu: beef tartare, sea bass with celery purée, and the heritage Dubrovnik skorup cake. Service is notably polished.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 95 862 2411.
Getting there: Old Town, Ul. Miha Pracata 6.
Hours: Daily 11:00–00:00

name: Pavvo
description: Stylish, relaxed restaurant just off Gundulić Square with well-executed black risotto, burrata, monkfish and specials. It pairs friendly, funny service with strong cocktails.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 91 448 8440.
Getting there: Old Town, Ul. Cvijete Zuzorić 1.
Hours: Daily 10:00–23:00

name: Bokar Dubrovnik
description: Quiet corner restaurant at the edge of the Old Town that skips the usual pizza-and-pasta formula. Signature dishes include 'dirty' pljukanci pasta, black Slavonian pork, oysters and creative cocktails, at fair prices.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 20 323 700.
Getting there: Old Town, Zeljarica 7.
Hours: Daily 09:00–23:00

name: Lucin Kantun Dubrovnik
description: Tapas-style small-plates restaurant on a side street off the Stradun. Black risotto, baked octopus, sardines, Dubrovnik-style beef pasta and arancini are favorites. Good value, with drinks served on the steps while you wait.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 20 321 003, or expect a wait in season.
Getting there: Old Town, Od Sigurate 4A, 3 minutes from Pile Gate.
Hours: Daily 11:00–22:30

name: Soul Kitchen Dubrovnik
description: Creative, mostly plant-forward kitchen with large portions: beet and glazed-pear salads, pea pasta, cauliflower and shawarma. It is a welcome change from Old Town seafood menus and suits vegans and pescatarians alike.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book dinner: +385 99 810 5974.
Getting there: Old Town, Od Domina 3, a quiet lane near Pile Gate.
Hours: Daily 11:00–22:00

name: Nishta
description: Long-running fully vegan restaurant on Prijeko. The menu spans vegan ćevapčići and Thai green noodles to curry platters, raw almond gnocchi and raw cheesecake, and it has won over plenty of non-vegans.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Old Town, Prijeko bb.

name: Azur
description: 'CroAsian' fusion in a tucked-away corner near the southern walls. Seafood laksa, curries, tuna tostadas, sushi tacos and fried cauliflower bites stand out, with good-value lunch sets and gluten-free guidance.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book dinner: +385 20 324 806.
Getting there: Old Town, Pobijana 10, below the walls on the south side.
Hours: Daily 12:00–22:00

name: Taj Mahal Old Town
description: Atmospheric Bosnian restaurant, despite the name, serving ćevapi, Bosnian meatballs, dumplings, slow-cooked beef, lamb shank and roasted-pepper meze. It is a hearty, flavorful change of pace.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 20 323 221.
Getting there: Old Town, Ul. Nikole Gučetića 2.
Hours: Daily 11:00–16:00 and 17:30–00:00

name: Zuzori
description: Small Michelin-listed restaurant with a concise menu: shrimp pappardelle, truffle fettuccine, beef risotto, octopus and memorable house bread. Portions are small and still water is pricey.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 20 324 076.
Getting there: Old Town, Ul. Cvijete Zuzorić 2.
Hours: Daily 11:00–23:00

name: Restaurant Kopun
description: Terrace restaurant on the square by the Jesuit Stairs, specializing in the old Dubrovnik dish of capon. It also serves Ston oysters, black risotto, šporki makaruli and rozata custard. Stuffed capon must be ordered a day ahead.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 20 323 969; order stuffed capon 24 hours ahead.
Getting there: Old Town, Poljana Ruđera Boškovića 7.
Hours: Sun–Thu 10:00–22:00; Fri–Sat 10:00–22:30

name: Heritage of Dubrovnik
description: Traditional Dubrovnik cuisine with a menu that explains each dish's history. Octopus salad, stuffed squid, mussels, lamb and Dubrovnik cake are the highlights, served at the calm end of Prijeko.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 20 323 878.
Getting there: Old Town, Prijeko 32.
Hours: Mon–Sat 11:00–21:30; closed Sunday

name: Rozario
description: Cozy restaurant on a medieval lane with quick, friendly service. It is known for steak with fig sauce, black risotto, shrimp risotto, octopus salad and mussels in white sauce.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 99 315 6550.
Getting there: Old Town, Prijeko 1.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:00

name: Konoba Sebastian
description: Family-run konoba above the main bustle, often cited for the best black risotto in town. It also does tuna two ways and tuna tataki. A few reviews flag inconsistent starters.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 95 198 6072.
Getting there: Old Town, Prijeko 11.
Hours: Mon–Sat 11:00–23:00; Sun 16:00–23:00

name: Stara Loza
description: Prijeko restaurant with a lovely rooftop terrace. The Croatian-Mediterranean menu comes with set fish and meat menus. Reviews praise the service and setting more consistently than the food.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Request the rooftop when booking: +385 20 321 145.
Getting there: Old Town, Prijeko 22.
Hours: Daily 08:00–23:00

name: Konoba Nava
description: Unpretentious family-run konoba on a side alley serving home-style Croatian food: fried sardines, octopus salad, whole fish, shrimp risotto and creamy cheesecake.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 20 350 746 for groups.
Getting there: Old Town, Getaldićeva 5, near Pile Gate.
Hours: Daily 09:00–23:00

name: Aquarius Tavern
description: Traditional Dalmatian tavern by the Old Port with a shaded, fan-cooled terrace and air-conditioned basement. Generous seafood platters, mixed grills, grilled sardines and frog legs are at reasonable prices for inside the walls.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 91 526 8790.
Getting there: Old Town, Ul. kneza Damjana Jude 4.
Hours: Daily 11:00–23:00

name: Taverna Pupo
description: Friendly, brother-run tavern known for black risotto, beef-cheek risotto, swordfish and an excellent lava cake. The house white is good value.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 20 323 555.
Getting there: Old Town, Miha Pracata 8.
Hours: Daily 11:00–22:00

name: Fish Restaurant Proto
description: Established, upscale seafood house with a roof terrace just off the Stradun. Offerings include fish of the day with beurre monté, octopus ragù with polenta, a fish tasting menu and truffle croquettes.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve: +385 20 323 234.
Getting there: Old Town, Široka 1, 2 minutes from Pile Gate.
Hours: Daily 11:00–22:00

name: Restaurant & konoba Gavun
description: Casual, friendly spot on atmospheric Široka street serving risotto, pizza, ćevapi and pasta. It opens early and is popular with cruise passengers for a quick, reliable meal.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Old Town, Široka 3, near Pile Gate.
Hours: Daily 07:00–22:30

name: Dionis Mediterranean Cuisine
description: Quiet-alley Mediterranean restaurant with charismatic service. It serves black and seafood risotto, flavorful tuna steak, octopus salad, pizza and lasagna, and food arrives fast.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 97 649 0608.
Getting there: Old Town, Žudioska 3, off the Stradun.
Hours: Daily 08:00–00:00

name: King Richard's Restaurant
description: Terrace restaurant on lively Bunićeva Square below the cathedral. It serves meat platters, tuna steak, bruschetta and burgers. Note that it does not serve tap water.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 95 533 1043.
Getting there: Old Town, Bunićeva poljana 3.
Hours: Daily 08:00–00:00

name: Stradoon
description: Stradun café-bar facing the cathedral end of the main street. It does good breakfasts like eggs Benedict and omelettes with fresh OJ, and creative cocktails at night. Prime people-watching.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Old Town, Stradun 6.
Hours: Daily 07:00–02:00

name: Bota Šare Oyster & Sushi Bar
description: Quirky oyster-and-sushi bar from a Croatian group that farms its own Ston oysters. It serves amberjack carpaccio, spicy tuna, poke and gyoza with a strong local wine list.
mapQuery: Bota Šare Oyster & Sushi Bar Dubrovnik
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve: +385 99 348 0880.
Getting there: Old Town, Peline 4, along the northern walls.
Hours: Daily 11:00–23:00

name: Mediteraneo Sushi and Seafood
description: Low-key corner spot beside the northern Buža gate with fresh local-fish sushi, sashimi, oysters and risotto. Some reviews report inconsistent steaks, so stick to seafood.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 97 707 5243.
Getting there: Old Town, Peline 4.
Hours: Thu–Tue 12:00–22:00; closed Wednesday

name: Bonsai Sushi & Wok
description: Air-conditioned sushi and wok restaurant off the Stradun with generously filled rolls, sashimi, ramen and gyoza. Staff are friendly and will even teach chopsticks.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve: +385 91 608 1508.
Getting there: Old Town, Između Polača 1.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:00

name: Storia
description: Friendly wood-fired pizzeria by the Old Port walls, with the seafood 'Dubrovnik' pizza, excellent garlic bread and pasta. It is a good post-Lokrum-ferry stop.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 20 324 783.
Getting there: Old Town, Ul. kneza Damjana Jude 6, steps from the Lokrum ferry at the Old Port.
Hours: Daily 11:00–22:00

name: PIZZERIA OLIVA
description: Popular pizzeria near St. Blaise's Church with thin, crisp pies and pasta. A takeaway counter sells big slices for about €5, a smart budget lunch.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Old Town, Lučarica 5.
Hours: Daily 10:00–23:00

name: Pizzeria Mama! Dubrovnik
description: Small pizzeria serving light, fluffy-edged pizzas with fresh toppings, for takeaway or dine-in.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Old Town, Luža ulica, by the clock tower end of the Stradun.
Hours: Daily 12:00–22:30

name: Pizzeria Mamma Margherita
description: Casual pizzeria on a quieter street with pizza, lasagna and seafood at prices below most Old Town restaurants.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Old Town, Između Polača 7.
Hours: Daily 11:00–00:00

name: Mea Culpa Pizzeria & Trattoria Dubrovnik
description: Cozy alley trattoria known for its lasagna, including a four-cheese and a vegetarian version, plus pizza and risotto. Heaters and blankets are offered for cooler months, and Dubrovnik Pass holders get a discount.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +385 99 222 1172.
Getting there: Old Town, Za Rokom 3.
Hours: Daily 12:00–22:00

name: Republic Burger House
description: Alley-side burger house famous for its octopus burger and spicy calamari. It has gluten-free buns and prices below the Old Town average. Restrooms are around the block.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Old Town, Široka 4.
Hours: Daily 11:00–23:00

name: Fox Bros smash&street
description: New smash-burger spot with homemade fries, truffle and loaded fries, and milkshakes. The friendly crew handles a busy lane with ease.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Old Town, Prijeko 4.
Hours: Mon–Sat 11:00–23:00; closed Sunday

name: Barba
description: Family-run seafood street-food spot famous for its octopus burger, octopus salad, fried calamari and tempura prawns. Guests sign wooden forks to leave on the wall, and you can eat on the stone steps outside.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Old Town, Boškovićeva 5, off the Stradun.
Hours: Daily 11:00–00:00

name: Holy Burek
description: Busy Old Town burek counter turning out flaky, freshly baked pastry with veal, cheese, spinach or chicken fillings. It is ideal as a fast breakfast or walk-and-eat lunch; go early to beat the queue.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Old Town, Od Puča 22, 3 minutes from Pile Gate.

name: Bakery Mokošica
