Hours: Daily 08:00–20:00

name: Vinarija Dingač "Pasi"
description: Small family winery beside the Dingač tunnel, with tastings of Plavac, Dingač, grappa, liqueurs and olive oil, and a warm, educational welcome.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Potomje 5, Pelješac. About 2 hours' drive from Dubrovnik.
Hours: Mon–Sat 08:00–21:00; Sun 11:00–21:00

name: Milicic Winery
description: Family winery overlooking its vineyards that serves winery dinners and tastings by request only. Call ahead so the owner can prepare.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Advance booking required for food: +385 20 742 015.
Getting there: Potomje, Pelješac. About 2 hours' drive from Dubrovnik.
Hours: Mon–Fri 09:00–18:00; Sat 09:00–15:00; closed Sunday

name: Konoba "Andiamo"
description: Popular beachfront konoba on Orebić's promenade with fast, tasty seafood such as squid with Swiss chard and potatoes and octopus. It hands out pillows so waiting guests can sit on the beach.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reservations recommended: +385 98 983 8614.
Getting there: Orebić, Šetalište Kneza Domagoja 28, at the far end of Pelješac. About 2 hours 15 minutes' drive from Dubrovnik; only practical with an overnight stay.
Hours: Mon, Sat–Sun 12:00–00:00; Tue–Fri 10:00–00:00

name: Old Captains Restaurant
description: Family-run seafood restaurant on the Orebić seafront, known for whole grilled sea bream, perfectly grilled squid, local Pošip wine and a standout mascarpone dessert.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 20 714 488.
Getting there: Orebić, Šetalište Kneza Domagoja 8. About 2 hours 15 minutes' drive from Dubrovnik.
Hours: Tue–Sun 12:00–22:00; closed Monday

name: Guesthouse Mimbelli
description: Seafront guesthouse restaurant in Orebić serving tuna steak, an excellent fish pâté and Korčula truffle pasta, with a breakfast terrace on the beach. Service can be slow at peak times.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 20 713 636.
Getting there: Orebić, Trg Mimbeli 6.
Hours: Daily 08:00–00:00

name: Restaurant & Villa Vrgorac
description: Seafront terrace in Perna, just west of Orebić, with views to Korčula town. It serves meaty black risotto, tender squid and Pošip at fair prices, with a wide menu.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book a seafront table: +385 20 719 152.
Getting there: Perna 24, about 2.5 km west of Orebić.
Hours: Daily 07:00–23:00

name: Restaurant Lavanda
description: Waterfront restaurant at a campsite east of Orebić with fresh fish, tuna steak and local Pošip and Postup wines. A free cart shuttles guests from the parking area.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 20 454 485.
Getting there: Dubravica 34, east of Orebić; park at the campsite and take the free cart down.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:00

name: Fratelli Žuljana
description: Newly opened garden pizzeria in the center of Žuljana with light, well-baked pizzas on a shaded back terrace. Dog-friendly.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Žuljana, Kraj 77, on Pelješac's south coast. About 1 hour 45 minutes' drive from Dubrovnik.
Hours: Daily 18:00–22:00

name: Bistro Ankora
description: Family bistro overlooking Žuljana's beach and harbor with fish, meat and pizza at reasonable prices and good house wine.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 20 756 135.
Getting there: Žuljana, Kraj 51.
Hours: Daily 13:00–22:30

name: MEDITERAN - konoba, caffe bar
description: Garden konoba under a huge walnut tree among lemon and pomegranate trees, near beautiful Vučine beach. It serves grilled local calamari and chicken dishes plus cocktails. Service can be slow.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Žuljana, near Vučine bay.
Hours: Daily 08:00–23:00

name: Konoba Solar
description: Grill-focused konoba where you watch steaks, ribeye, octopus and fish cooked over embers. It has no sea view, but strong local wine. Desserts are pricey.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 98 192 7655.
Getting there: Žuljana, Kraj 49.
Hours: Daily 16:00–23:00

name: Restaurant Riva
description: Harborside Žuljana restaurant with sea-and-mountain views. Grilled calamari, mussels, tuna steak and the owner's home-hunted wild boar are the dishes to order. Service can be slow.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Žuljana harbor.
Hours: Daily 13:00–23:00

name: Restaurant Dubrovnik, Lopud
description: Lopud's upscale harborfront seafood restaurant, known for Adriatic lobster pasta, scampi pasta, house-baked bread and artful desserts. It has a good vegan pasta option. It is expensive, with lobster pasta around €155.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book in season: +385 95 196 6312.
Getting there: Lopud harbor promenade. Jadrolinija ferry from Gruž port (next to the cruise terminal) takes about 50 minutes, or take an Elafiti excursion boat from Gruž or the Old Port. Check return sailings; this is a half-day trip.
Hours: Daily 09:00–01:00

name: La Villa Restaurant
description: Waterside tables in front of a boutique villa on Lopud's harbor. Specialties include salt-baked sea bass, lobster pasta, grilled calamari and truffle scampi pasta, and it has lovely sunset views.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 99 222 5115.
Getting there: Lopud, Iva Kuljevana 33. Ferry from Gruž is about 50 minutes.

name: Restaurant Nikica
description: Relaxed, fairly priced harbor restaurant on Lopud, recommended by cruise crews. Fried calamari and grilled squid are the dishes to order, and it handles gluten-free requests well.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Lopud harbor promenade. Ferry from Gruž is about 50 minutes.
Hours: Daily 11:00–23:00

name: BAROON Wine&more
description: Friendly harborside wine and cocktail bar steps from the Lopud ferry, with prices well below Dubrovnik Old Town. It is ideal while waiting for the boat.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Lopud, Obala Iva Kuljevana 11, by the ferry landing.
Hours: Daily 08:30–00:30

name: Rajski kutak Bindo
description: Peaceful grill restaurant perched above sandy Šunj beach, away from the beach-bar crowds. It serves fresh grilled calamari, mussels and salads with lovely views and warm service.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 95 887 6236.
Getting there: Šunj beach, Lopud, about 20–25 minutes' walk over the hill from the harbor, or take a golf-cart taxi for a fee.
Hours: Sat–Wed 11:00–16:00; closed Thursday & Friday

name: Beach bar fia
description: Laid-back beach bar on Šunj beach with great cocktails, homemade rakija and genuinely friendly staff. It is a perfect day-at-the-beach base.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Šunj beach, Lopud; walk or take a golf-cart taxi from the harbor.
Hours: Mon–Fri 09:00–19:00; Sat–Sun 09:30–19:00

name: Beachbar | šunj
description: Šunj beach bar serving pizzas, bruschetta and cocktails, with free sunbeds when you order. Confirm any sunbed charges up front, as one reviewer reports a surprise fee.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Šunj beach, Lopud.
Hours: Daily 10:00–23:00

name: G Chelo Lounge Bar & Restaurant
description: Terrace restaurant overlooking the cove at Gornje Čelo on Koločep, the closest Elafiti island to Dubrovnik. It serves simple, fresh traditional dishes like whole fish with vegetables, with good wine and sunset cocktails.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 20 414 616.
Getting there: Gornje Čelo, Koločep. Ferry from Gruž port is about 30 minutes, the easiest Elafiti day trip.
Hours: Daily 11:00–23:00

name: Konoba Skerac
description: Family-run Koločep konoba where fish and prawns are cooked on a charcoal grill on the patio. It offers octopus salad, homemade carob and sour-cherry rakija, and serves lunch only.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 91 576 1165.
Getting there: Near Gornje Čelo, Koločep. Ferry from Gruž is about 30 minutes, then a short walk.
Hours: Daily 10:00–16:00

name: Konoba Tauris
description: Sailors' favorite on Šipan with its own garden, homemade olive oil and charcoal grill. It is known for fresh sea bass, a superb octopus starter and lemon cheesecake, with mooring buoys out front.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 98 619 013.
Getting there: Šipanska Luka 96, Šipan. Ferry or catamaran from Gruž is about 1–1.5 hours; check return times, as this is a full-day trip.
Hours: Daily 10:00–00:00

name: Konoba Kod Marka
description: Waterside Šipan konoba with no fixed menu: choose meat or fish and the kitchen guides you. Octopus cakes, grilled prawns and whole sea bass are signatures, with sunset views. Bread is charged separately.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 20 758 007.
Getting there: Šipanska Luka 180, Šipan. Ferry from Gruž is about 1–1.5 hours.
Hours: Daily 11:00–23:30

name: Konoba U Balda
description: Generous, family-run konoba on Šipanska Luka harbor where you pick your fish from the day's catch. It serves homemade desserts, local wine and pelinkovac, and is vegan-friendly.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 98 942 6427.
Getting there: Šipanska Luka, Šipan.
Hours: Daily 08:00–00:00

name: Pizzeria Lukrecija
description: Family pizzeria on Šipanska Luka's waterfront with crisp pizzas, fresh pasta, crêpes and sundaes, and great harbor sunsets. It has been known to stay open into mid-October.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Šipanska Luka, Šipan.
Hours: Daily 07:00–00:00

name: Konoba TriSestre
description: View terrace above Suđurađ harbor on Šipan, next to Hotel Božica. Courgette fritters, swordfish, steak and octopus peka (order ahead) are the highlights.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 98 915 8056; order peka in advance.
Getting there: Suđurađ, Šipan, a short climb from the harbor. Ferry from Gruž to Suđurađ is about 1 hour.
Hours: Daily 13:00–23:00

name: Konavoski Dvori Restaurant
description: Atmospheric restaurant beside old watermills on the Ljuta river, the iconic Konavle valley lunch. It serves river trout, veal, pork ribs, dumplings and peka (order days ahead) to the sound of rushing water.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book, and confirm peka in advance: +385 99 342 0463.
Getting there: Ljuta, Konavle valley. About 40–45 minutes' drive south-east of Dubrovnik; car, taxi or tour needed.
Hours: Daily 11:00–22:00

name: Konoba Vinica Monkovic
description: Family konoba with tables right on the Ljuta river. It is known for pašticada with homemade gnocchi, dry-aged steaks and peka, which requires a 3-hour pre-order. Easy parking.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve river tables; pre-order peka 3+ hours ahead: +385 99 215 2459.
Getting there: Donja Ljuta 44, Gruda. About 45 minutes from Dubrovnik; a taxi round-trip is roughly €40 according to recent diners.
Hours: Tue–Sun 12:00–23:00; closed Monday

name: Kameni Mlin (Stone Mill) - Agrotourism Konavle
description: Family agritourism tasting experience, not a regular restaurant. It includes an olive-mill tour, unlimited home wine, and a hearty country meal with live music and dancing, led by an entertaining host.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead: +385 98 309 820.
Getting there: Bistroće 3, Čilipi. About 25–30 minutes' drive from Dubrovnik, near the airport.

name: Kameni Dvori Tavern
description: Family farm tavern in Lovorno where guests can pick garden ingredients and help prepare dinner. The meal comes with homemade olive oil, wine and creative traditional dishes. It feels like dining with Croatian relatives.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reservation required: +385 98 913 4758.
Getting there: Lovorno 11A, Gruda, Konavle. About 40 minutes from Dubrovnik.
Hours: Listed only Mon 18:00–21:00

name: Konoba Konavoski Komin
description: Garden konoba 500 m up in the hills above Cavtat, with spectacular coastal views on the drive. The gracious elderly owner serves wood-fired local dishes and octopus peka.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +385 91 510 2430.
Getting there: Velji Do 5, above Cavtat. About 35 minutes from Dubrovnik on a narrow, winding mountain road; a car is required, so drive carefully after dark.

name: Điron
description: Village bistro in Gruda with an excellent-value daily menu of soup, main, salad and bread for around €8–12. It also serves schnitzel, veal steak and pizza. Service can be curt.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Gruda 96, Konavle. About 40 minutes from Dubrovnik.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–17:00; closed Sunday

name: Pergola
description: Simple village café in Gruda with mountain views, low prices and friendly staff. It is good for coffee or a beer on a Konavle drive.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Gruda, Konavle, next to Điron.
Hours: Daily 07:00–23:00

name: CRVIK - VINOGRADI I VINARIJA
description: Boutique Konavle winery with personal tastings led by a passionate winemaker, set among beautifully tended vineyards. It caters thoughtfully to allergies.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book tastings: +385 98 192 7797.
Getting there: Kotari 12, Komaji, Čilipi. About 30 minutes from Dubrovnik.

name: La Catedral Pasta Bar
description: A hugely popular pasta bar beside St. Tryphon's Cathedral with rich house pastas, prawn bruschetta, and excellent gluten-free pasta. Lunch is calmer; expect long queues at dinner, and kitchen timing can be slow when packed.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead for dinner — call +382 67 711 711
Getting there: Cathedral Square (Trg Sv. Tripuna), Old Town; about 4 minutes from the Sea Gate.
Hours: Daily 8:00–22:00 (Wed to 22:30)

name: Pescaria Dekaderon
description: A seafood restaurant in a central Old Town courtyard with cooling fans, good beef carpaccio, mussels, tuna tartare and steaks, and a well-loved sous-vide chicken plate. It is gluten-free friendly and great for people-watching.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +382 67 023 918
Getting there: Old Town, between the Square of Arms and the Cathedral; about 3 minutes from the Sea Gate.
Hours: Daily 8:00–22:00

name: Pier65
description: A Turkish-run restaurant on a quiet Old Town square with generous breakfasts, wraps, homemade meatballs, mussels, and seafood risotto, plus homemade sweets. Friendly service, frequent visits from Kotor's famous cats, and no tourist-trap feel.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +382 68 401 587
Getting there: Stari Grad 368, near the Square of Arms; about 3 minutes from the Sea Gate.
Hours: Daily 9:00–21:30

name: The Drunken Sailor
description: A relaxed pub-style seafood bar in the Old Town with tuna tacos, fish burgers, crispy seafood, and cold beer at fair prices. Fast, friendly service; good for a casual meal or drinks.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Stari grad 343, Old Town; about 5 minutes from the Sea Gate.
Hours: Daily 8:00–23:00

name: Old Town Pub Kotor
description: A friendly Old Town pub known for bartenders who craft cocktails to your taste. A lively, welcoming spot for evening drinks.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Old Town near Milk Square; about 5 minutes from the Sea Gate.
Hours: Daily 10:00–01:00

name: Niente Cafe Bar
description: A characterful little café with generous coffees, milkshakes, ice cream, matcha, and krempita (Kotor's custard cake) at good value. Small and warm inside but full of personality.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Stari grad 266, southern Old Town lanes toward the Gurdić Gate.
Hours: Daily 8:30–22:00

name: Marshall's Gelato
description: Widely considered Kotor's best gelato, with flavors that pop. Two scoops cost about €4 and the line moves fast; some visitors return to Kotor just for it.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Stari Grad 359A, just inside the Sea Gate near the Square of Arms.
Hours: Daily 10:00–22:00

name: Perchè Gelateria
description: Homemade gelato with unusual flavors like salty pistachio and fig-walnut, plus fresh cakes, good coffee, and gluten-free cones. Pretty outdoor seating.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Old Town 476, near Milk Square.
Hours: Daily 9:00–23:00

name: Davanti Gelateria & Bistro
description: A charming corner gelateria at the quieter back of the Old Town with very natural strawberry and lemon gelato, sourdough cookies, and a bistro across the lane doing cheap, tasty sandwiches.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Stari Grad 494, near the Škurda (North) Gate.
Hours: Daily 7:00–23:00

name: Moritz Eis
description: An artisanal ice cream shop by the North Gate with fresh fruit flavors such as cherry and mandarin, plus cakes. Scoops are small for the price.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Stari Grad 495, by the Škurda (North) Gate. Note: the Square of Arms branch is rated lower.
Hours: Daily 9:00–22:00

name: Pizzeria Pronto
description: A busy Old Town pizzeria with huge pizzas and slices for about €3.50, a cheap, quick bite. No reservations, so expect a short wait at peak times.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in only
Getting there: Old Town near the Square of Arms; about 3 minutes from the Sea Gate.
Hours: Daily 9:00–01:00

name: Primo Pizza Kotor
description: A takeaway pizza counter with huge €3.50 slices, a budget favorite in pricey Kotor. Seating is very limited.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Old Town 368, near the Square of Arms.

name: CAVE Coffee Specialty
description: A specialty coffee stand just outside the North Gate serving precisely extracted espresso, signature drinks like a crème brûlée latte, oat milk, and beans to buy. Takeaway only.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (cards accepted over €6)
Getting there: Square Mata Petrovića, just outside the Škurda (North) Gate.
Hours: Mon–Sat 7:30–20:00; Sun 8:00–18:00

name: Kordić bakery & pastry shop
description: A local bakery near the North Gate with good-value pastries, pistachio cheesecake, honey cake, krempita, and vegan options. Check freshness on day-old items.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Just north of the Škurda (North) Gate by the river.
Hours: Daily 6:30–22:00

name: Cheese Shop
description: A rustic rest stop partway up the Ladder of Kotor trail, run by a colorful host. It serves cold beer, Turkish coffee, rakija, and goat cheese with prosciutto, with spectacular views over the bay. Cash only; supplies come up by donkey.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (cash only)
Getting there: About 45–60 minutes uphill on the free Ladder of Kotor trail from its start near the Škurda (North) Gate. The old ladder shortcut into San Giovanni Fortress is now sealed, so the fortress is only reached via the paid town-walls route (about €15). Go early to avoid heat. A half-day hike.

name: Marenda Steak House
description: An air-conditioned steakhouse between the bus station and the Old Town with excellent local meat platters, tartare, three-meat soup, and homemade bread. Highly professional service; avoid the pulled-pork burger.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +382 69 340 300
Getting there: Put prvoboraca 232, about 5–8 minutes' walk south of the Old Town toward the bus station.
Hours: Daily 7:00–23:00

name: "Ladovina" Kitchen & Wine Bar
description: An upmarket garden kitchen and wine bar just south of the Old Town, with huge mussel portions, braised beef, tuna fillet, seafood pasta, and good cocktails. Lively and pricier than average.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — call +382 63 422 472
Getting there: Njegoševa 209, a few minutes' walk south of the Old Town near the Gurdić Gate.

name: Restaurant Kafana Porto Turo
description: A family kafana in Njeguši village that smokes its own prosciutto and cheese, also sold vacuum-packed to take home. Ćevapi, Njeguški steak (veal stuffed with local ham and cheese), and calf's liver come in large portions at mountain-village prices. It is quieter when tour coaches are not stopping.
mapQuery: Restaurant Kafana Porto Turo Njeguši Kotor
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +382 68 867 162
Getting there: On the P1 road in Njeguši, about 20 km above Kotor via the 25-hairpin Serpentine road (about 45 minutes by car). A half-day trip by car, taxi, or tour.
Hours: Daily 9:00–21:00

name: Mountain pub Porto
description: A quirky, cozy pub next door to Porto Turo (same family) in Njeguši serving ćevapi, rabbit ragù, chicken, and pasta at prices well below Kotor. A friendly village atmosphere popular with both locals and travelers.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +382 68 867 162
Getting there: P1 road, Njeguši (Kopito), about 45 minutes by car from Kotor via the Serpentine. A half-day trip.
Hours: Daily 9:00–21:00

name: Restoran Konoba kod Radonjica
description: A rustic Njeguši konoba with a stone interior and garden known for tender veal and lamb, excellent local prosciutto, cheese, bread, wine, and honey mead. Check the menu for a 10% service charge, which one diner reported was not clearly shown.
mapQuery: Restoran Konoba kod Radonjica Njeguši Kotor
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +382 41 239 820
Getting there: Kopito, Njeguši, with parking opposite; about 45 minutes by car from Kotor via the Serpentine. A half-day trip.
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:00

name: Konoba Batricevic-Njegusi
description: A peaceful family konoba on the Njeguši plain with a veranda overlooking the fields. The owner often tours guests through the large smokehouse before serving generous prosciutto-and-cheese platters with homemade bread and house wine.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +382 69 560 982
Getting there: Erakovići, just off the P1 in the Njeguši area; about 45 minutes by car from Kotor. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon–Fri and Sun 9:00–18:30; Sat 9:00–21:00

name: Turo Njeguski Prsut I Sir
description: A family producer of Njeguši prosciutto and cheese where hosts explain the curing process among hanging hams, offer tastings with wine and rakija, and sell products to take home. A great authentic stop, not a sit-down restaurant.
mapQuery: Turo Njeguski Prsut I Sir Njeguši Kotor
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +382 68 867 162
Getting there: P1 road, Njeguši; about 45 minutes by car from Kotor. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon–Fri 8:00–14:00; Sat 8:00–12:30; closed Sunday

name: Kod Pera na Bukovicu
description: A historic roadside inn, reportedly among the oldest in Montenegro, with a garden and Lovćen views. The menu is mostly prosciutto, cheese, olives, and bread with ice-cold beer and rakija, a classic road-trip break.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +382 69 055 021
Getting there: On the P1 between Njeguši and Cetinje, on the right when heading toward Kotor; ample parking. About 50 minutes by car from Kotor. A half-day trip.
Hours: Daily 8:40–19:00

name: Restaurant Nevjesta Jadrana
description: A mountainside restaurant on the Serpentine road with breathtaking views over the Bay of Kotor, reachable by car or by continuing up from the Ladder of Kotor hike. Local prosciutto, cheese, and meatballs are good; service ranges from excellent to slow at busy times.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +382 69 697 952
Getting there: On the Kotor–Njeguši Serpentine road (P1) above Kotor; about 20–25 minutes by car, or a strenuous hike up the Ladder of Kotor trail. Closes at 18:00. A half-day trip.
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:00

name: Horizont Bar
description: A drinks-and-snacks bar at one of the most dramatic viewpoints over the entire Bay of Kotor, on the Serpentine road and spectacular at sunset. Drinks are pricey and inconsistently charged, so confirm prices; the viewing terrace is often accessible off-season.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: On the P1 Serpentine road above Kotor; about 20 minutes by car. The road is narrow with tight hairpins, so drive cautiously. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon and Thu–Sun 9:00–20:30; Tue–Wed 9:30–20:30

name: Monte 1350 bar
description: A big mountaintop terrace bar and restaurant at the top of the Kotor Cable Car on Mt. Lovćen, with sweeping views of the bay, DJs or live music, mixed grills, cheese platters, and cocktails. Stay for sunset, but watch the time of the last cable car down.
tags: verify: cable car ticket price and last descent
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +382 69 501 509
Getting there: At the upper station of the Kotor Cable Car (lower station a short taxi ride from the Old Town). Cable car ticket required. A half-day outing.
Hours: Mon and Wed–Sun 9:00–20:00; Tue 10:30–20:00

name: National Restaurant Belveder
description: A traditional Montenegrin restaurant on a ridge outside Cetinje with famous views toward Lake Skadar and the Lovćen valleys. Generous grilled meats, local cheeses, lamb, and vegetarian options come with fast, friendly service and easy parking.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for groups — call +382 67 569 217
Getting there: On the road from Cetinje toward Rijeka Crnojevića, a few km southeast of Cetinje; about 1 hour 10 minutes by car from Kotor. A half-day trip.
Hours: Daily 10:00–22:00

name: Restoran TavèRna
description: One of Cetinje's best restaurants, with veal soup, Montenegro salad, huge mixed grills, and a house meat specialty for two to three, ideally with gorgonzola sauce. Portions are big and the value great.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +382 69 502 503
Getting there: Baja Pivljanina 61, Cetinje; about 1 hour by car from Kotor via the Serpentine and Njeguši. A half-day trip.
Hours: Daily 8:00–23:00

name: Kole Restaurant
description: A popular Cetinje restaurant with indoor and outdoor seating, famous for its specialty meat platter (easily feeds three), generous pastas, and excellent value. Service is quick and friendly.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +382 69 606 660
Getting there: Bulevar Crnogorskih Junaka 12, Cetinje; about 1 hour by car from Kotor. A half-day trip.
Hours: Daily 7:00–23:00

name: Restobar DVOR
description: A covered terrace restaurant on Cetinje's central Court Square between the museums, serving ćevapi, chicken in champignon sauce, seafood risotto, tiramisu, and homemade drinks. Fast service and good vegetarian options, with paid parking nearby.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +382 67 727 822
Getting there: Dvorski Trg, central Cetinje; about 1 hour by car from Kotor. A half-day trip.

name: Room 8
description: An upscale, cozy fusion restaurant in Cetinje with European-leaning dishes such as tuna steak, octopus salad, fresh-mushroom plates, and a must-order chocolate fondant. Attentive service makes it a special-occasion pick.
details:

Getting there: Portonovi Resort promenade, about 45 min from Kotor via ferry. Half-day commitment.
Hours: Daily 8:30–00:00

name: TAPASAKE Montenegro
description: Japanese-Mediterranean restaurant at One&Only Portonovi with wagyu and toro nigiri, crispy duck salad and gyoza, plus sunset and a beach-club DJ that can be loud. Free parking for diners.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve: +382 31 691 001
Getting there: One&Only Portonovi, about 45 min from Kotor via ferry; tell security you are dining. Half-day commitment.
Hours: Daily 19:00–23:00

name: Sabia Restaurant
description: Giorgio Locatelli's Italian restaurant inside One&Only Portonovi, with excellent burrata, seafood risotto and an Italian buffet night with live music. Expensive; family policies vary.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve: +382 31 691 001
Getting there: One&Only Portonovi, Kumbor, about 45 min from Kotor via ferry. Half-day commitment.
Hours: Daily 12:00–16:30 & 18:00–22:00

name: RESTAURANT PELIKAN
description: Skadar Lake's best-known family restaurant and hotel in Virpazar, also running boat tours. Lake carp and trout, house-made wine and a famous tres leches cake.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended: +382 69 038 928
Getting there: Trg Ustanka 34, Virpazar, about 70 km (around 1.5 hrs) from Kotor via Budva and Petrovac. Full or half-day trip, usually combined with a boat tour.
Hours: Daily 8:00–22:00

name: De'Andros Restaurant Virpazar
description: Elegant, cozy restaurant in Virpazar with a strong wine list, melt-in-the-mouth pork ribs, Caesar salad and apple pie, plus outstanding service.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Virpazar, Skadar Lake, about 1.5 hrs from Kotor. Half-day or longer.
Hours: Daily 7:00–23:00

name: Konoba Demidžana
description: Large air-conditioned konoba with a river-view terrace in Virpazar. Fast, generous and affordable: veal soup, vegetable platter, lake fish and focaccia.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; +382 66 133 387
Getting there: Virpazar town square, Skadar Lake, about 1.5 hrs from Kotor. Half-day or longer.
Hours: Daily 8:00–23:00

name: KONOBA "VIRPAZAR" & EXPLORE SKADAR LAKE
description: Friendly konoba that also runs boat tours, with fresh carp salad, Njeguši steak, grilled squid and many vegetarian options.
mapQuery: Konoba Virpazar Explore Skadar Lake Kotor
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; book boat tours: +382 68 588 518
Getting there: Trg Ustanka 10, Virpazar, about 1.5 hrs from Kotor. Half-day or longer.
Hours: Daily 8:00–23:00

name: Boat restaurant Silistria
description: Cozy restaurant on a moored boat in Virpazar serving very fresh trout, fish and potatoes at low prices. Smoking is allowed nearby.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; +382 68 573 686
Getting there: Virpazar waterfront, about 1.5 hrs from Kotor. Half-day or longer.
Hours: Daily 9:00–22:00

name: Garnet winery
description: Intimate boutique winery in Godinje village where the owner hosts tastings of his wines, including an orange wine, and rakija with homemade cheese, meats and bread.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book a tasting: +382 67 355 535
Getting there: Godinje, above Skadar Lake near Virpazar, reached by a narrow village road. About 1.5–1.75 hrs from Kotor. Half-day or longer.

name: Vržina Farm house
description: Family farm stay in Godinje serving huge home-cooked dinners of lake fish, garden produce and their own wine, and offering private boat tours.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Call ahead: +382 67 203 391
Getting there: Godinje, Skadar Lake, on high narrow lanes; parking by the villa. About 1.5–1.75 hrs from Kotor. Half-day or longer.

name: Restoran Savina luka Rijeka Crnojevića
description: River-view restaurant with the best outlook in Rijeka Crnojevića, huge portions and outstanding trout. Blankets are offered on cool evenings.
mapQuery: Restoran Savina luka Rijeka Crnojevića Kotor
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; +382 67 024 933
Getting there: Rijeka Crnojevića, about 60 km (around 1.25 hrs) from Kotor via Cetinje; the final road is steep and winding. Half-day or longer.
Hours: Daily 13:00–21:00

name: Konoba "RIJECKI KRAP"
description: Family konoba with traditional fish dishes such as smoked and marinated carp, grilled eel and goat's cheese, plus hearty breakfasts.
mapQuery: Konoba Riječki Krap Rijeka Crnojevića Kotor
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; +382 67 524 069
Getting there: Rijeka Crnojevića, about 1.25 hrs from Kotor via Cetinje. Half-day or longer.
Hours: Daily 9:00–21:00

name: Konoba Obod
description: Riverside konoba with great value: fish soup, trout, risotto and Podgorica-style popeci, with a pleasant terrace before or after a boat trip.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; +382 67 346 829
Getting there: Village square, Rijeka Crnojevića, about 1.25 hrs from Kotor via Cetinje. Half-day or longer.
Hours: Daily 9:00–22:00

name: Stari Most Restoran
description: Simple restaurant by the old stone bridge serving excellent fresh trout and cheap fish soup, with boat trips leaving right outside.
mapQuery: Stari Most Restoran Rijeka Crnojevića Kotor
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: By the old bridge, Rijeka Crnojevića, about 1.25 hrs from Kotor. Half-day or longer.
Hours: Daily 11:00–19:00

name: Etno Konoba Rijeka
description: Small family konoba overlooking the river and bridge with just-caught trout and carp, chicken skewers and apple pie; English menus and friendly service.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; +382 68 913 130
Getting there: Rijeka Crnojevića, about 1.25 hrs from Kotor. Half-day or longer.
Hours: Daily 10:00–01:00

name: Koliba - Manastira Ostrog Bogetići
description: Traditional restaurant and guesthouse below Ostrog Monastery with a big fireplace, roast lamb, house wine, cheesecake and valley views. Convenient parking.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; +382 69 480 635
Getting there: Bogetići, at the foot of the Ostrog Monastery road, about 100 km (around 2 hrs each way) from Kotor. A full-day trip; tours are common.
Hours: Daily 8:00–22:00

name: Hotel & Restaurant Sokoline - Ostrog
description: Family hotel with a terrace restaurant facing Ostrog Monastery and the mountains, serving traditional and modern Montenegrin food, especially lovely at golden hour.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended: +382 69 011 444
Getting there: Below Ostrog Monastery near Danilovgrad, about 2 hrs from Kotor. Full-day trip.
Hours: Daily 8:00–22:00

name: Gostionica Ostrog Podstijene
description: Old-fashioned family inn under the grapevines on the way to Ostrog. Coal-grilled trout and sausages, local cheese, prosciutto, homemade wine and pomegranate juice at low prices.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; +382 69 997 887
Getting there: Podvraće, on the road to Ostrog Monastery, about 2 hrs from Kotor. Full-day trip.
Hours: Daily 9:00–21:00

name: Na Kamenu Podostroškom (Podostrog Stone Restaurant)
description: Large tour-bus stop restaurant near Ostrog with big portions of lamb and veal. Service reviews are polarised and some report billing errors, so check your bill.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; +382 69 023 480
Getting there: Bogetići, below Ostrog Monastery, about 2 hrs from Kotor. Full-day trip.
Hours: Daily 7:00–23:00

name: Trattoria Rosmarino
description: Terrace restaurant up a steep stair behind Perast's waterfront, with one of the finest sunset views over the Bay of Kotor. Twelve-hour slow-cooked octopus, catch of the day, homemade focaccia and burrata, with knowledgeable wine guidance.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve for sunset: +382 69 559 449
Getting there: Up the stairs behind Perast's waterfront. Perast is about 15 km (20–25 min by taxi) from the Kotor cruise port. The village is car-free, so park in the paid lots at either end; they fill early in season.
Hours: Daily 12:00–23:00

name: Eho Restaurant Perast
description: High-calibre restaurant on the water with a small, carefully executed menu, considered by many the best food in Perast. Fish velouté, beef tartare, inventive mussels, truffle tortellini and excellent desserts and cocktails.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended, especially for sunset tables: +382 67 183 293
Getting there: Perast waterfront, western end. About 20–25 min by taxi from the Kotor cruise port; car-free village with paid parking at the edges.
Hours: Daily 11:00–23:00

name: Restoran Armonia
description: Vine-shaded waterfront restaurant good from breakfast through sunset dinner. Whole grilled sea bream deboned tableside, monkfish with spinach pasta and mixed bruschetta, with local wine recommendations.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for waterside tables at sunset: +382 69 508 555
Getting there: Western end of the Perast waterfront. About 20–25 min by taxi from the Kotor cruise port; car-free village.
Hours: Daily 8:00–23:00 (Wed from 9:00)

name: Perast Pizza Bocalibre
description: Neapolitan-style pizzeria with soft, flavourful crust and front-row tables under the trees facing Our Lady of the Rocks. Vegetarian and vegan options; takeaway works well for the benches along the water.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Perast waterfront, central. About 20–25 min by taxi from the Kotor cruise port; car-free village.
Hours: Daily 10:00–22:00

name: Calletta
description: Waterside focacceria-bar serving fresh focaccia sandwiches, croissants, good coffee by morning and cocktails by evening. Tables on the water or in the alley; the friendliest quick stop in Perast.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Perast waterfront, east of the centre. About 20–25 min by taxi from the Kotor cruise port; car-free village.
Hours: Daily 8:00–22:00

name: Perastino
description: Small takeaway spot for pizza by the slice, whole pizzas and fresh sandwiches such as the mortadella-mozzarella Perastino. Light dough, fast service and fair prices.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Perast 152, western end of the village. About 20–25 min by taxi from the Kotor cruise port; car-free village.
Hours: Daily 8:00–21:00

name: Onogošt
description: Budget grill house in Risan with huge portions of juicy Balkan grilled meat, ćevapi and fresh seafood, plus warm local hospitality. Food can be greasy; not a refined meal.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; +382 69 491 001
Getting there: Risan, about 5 km beyond Perast and roughly 25–30 min by taxi from the Kotor cruise port.
Hours: Daily 8:00–23:00

name: Fast food "Risan"
description: Newly opened, friendly harbour-side canteen in Risan with generous portions, whole roast chicken to take away and soft-serve ice cream, all with a fine bay view. Rating rests on few reviews.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Risan harbour on the E65. About 25–30 min by taxi from the Kotor cruise port.

name: Verige 65
description: Celebrated terrace restaurant at the narrowest point of the bay, where cruise ships pass right in front at night. Fusion menu of sushi, tuna tartare, prawn tacos, octopus and risotto, plus local sparkling wines and a famous date cake. Open year-round.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended, especially for terrace tables at dinner: +382 67 656 575
Getting there: Kostanjica on the E65, across the Verige Strait from Lepetane, about 25–30 min by taxi from the Kotor cruise port (around the inner bay via Perast and Risan). Allow a half-day with the round trip.
Hours: Daily 8:00–00:00

name: Castaña Beach Bar
description: Stylish beach bar on a clear, shallow stretch of Kostanjica shore with live music and simple food like the Montenegro sandwich. Lounger-and-umbrella sets for two run about €40. Cash only.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Kostanjica, on the E65 across the bay from Perast, about 25–30 min by taxi from the Kotor cruise port. Parking on the adjacent field costs about €5.
Hours: Daily 9:00–00:00

name: Ćatovića Mlini
description: Destination seafood restaurant set among old stone watermills with streams running through the garden, often called the best fish restaurant in Boka. Salt-baked fish, sea bass tartare, the seafood platter for two and apple strudel. Yachts can call ahead for a tender pickup.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve: +382 68 333 444
Getting there: Morinj, on the E65 at the head of the inner bay, about 30–35 min by taxi from the Kotor cruise port. A half-day commitment with the round trip.
Hours: Daily 12:00–22:30

name: Tramontana Beach Bar
description: Beachside restaurant in Morinj with generous, well-priced breakfasts, thin-crust pizza, shrimp, pastas and salads, all with sweeping bay views. Staff English is limited but friendly.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; +382 68 737 737
Getting there: Morinj waterfront, about 30–35 min by taxi from the Kotor cruise port. Half-day with the round trip.
Hours: Daily 8:00–01:00

name: Amphora Restaurant
description: Romantic waterfront terrace in Lepetane at the Verige Strait, watching the car ferries cross. Fresh seafood linguine, risotto and good breakfasts, with modest but high-quality portions and fair prices.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; +382 67 160 906
Getting there: Lepetane, by the Lepetane–Kamenari ferry landing, about 25 min by taxi from the Kotor cruise port via Prčanj and Stoliv. Half-day with the round trip.
Hours: Daily 11:00–22:00

name: Bocasa Beach & Restaurant
description: Modern beach club and restaurant at Kamenari, between forested hills and the strait, with wood-fired pizza, slow-cooked veal, fresh fish and occasional live music.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended in season: +382 67 600 973
Getting there: Kamenari, on the Herceg Novi side of the Verige Strait. From Kotor it is about 45 min by road around the bay, or cross on the Lepetane–Kamenari car ferry (a few minutes, runs frequently). A half-day commitment.
Hours: Daily 8:00–23:00

name: Caffè Del Professore Add'a Signora
description: A cozy, characterful trattoria-pizzeria directly across from Castel Nuovo, known for warm, theatrical service and excellent seafood pasta such as spaghetti alle vongole and Spaghetti Santa Lucia. Fried anchovies and octopus salad are good starters, and portions and prices are fair for the location.
mapQuery: Caffè Del Professore Add'a Signora Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — call +39 081 252 8256
Getting there: Via Vittorio Emanuele III 53, opposite Castel Nuovo; about 5 minutes on foot from the Stazione Marittima cruise terminal.
Hours: Mon and Wed–Sun 12:00–23:00; closed Tuesday

name: Stritt Stritt
description: A family-run street-side trattoria tucked behind Piazza Municipio, popular with locals for fresh, unpretentious seafood. Peppered mussels and octopus linguine with capers and olives are standouts, served on an enclosed patio.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +39 081 1991 7711
Getting there: Calata San Marco 44/45, opposite the Municipio metro; about 5 minutes from the cruise terminal.
Hours: Mon–Sat 12:30–15:30 and 19:00–22:30; closed Sunday

name: Osteria da Ciccio e Mery
description: A tiny, antique-filled osteria run by its namesake owners, cooking a short, Italian-only daily menu for locals. Spaghetti with clams, beef carpaccio, walnut pesto, and pasta e patate are excellent, with tiramisù and panna cotta to finish. Mostly lunch only.
mapQuery: Osteria da Ciccio e Mery Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +39 338 904 0011
Getting there: Via San Bartolomeo 46, a few blocks inland from Piazza Municipio; about 8 minutes from the cruise terminal.
Hours: Mon–Fri 11:00–15:00; Sat 11:00–15:00 and 18:30–22:00; closed Sunday

name: La Lazzara Trattoria e Pizzeria
description: A hugely popular trattoria-pizzeria on Piazza Francese with excellent Margherita, good pastas, and standout tiramisù and babà. Friendly, efficient staff handle big crowds; there is no air conditioning, so summer can be warm.
mapQuery: La Lazzara Trattoria e Pizzeria Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended; arrive at opening or call +39 081 551 7854
Getting there: Piazza Francese 9/10, just behind Piazza Municipio; about 5 minutes from the cruise terminal.
Hours: Daily 12:00–15:30 and 19:00–23:30

name: Ristorante e Pizzeria Castel Nuovo
description: A spacious, stylish pizzeria-restaurant near the castle and ferry docks, praised for a well-balanced Margherita and a standout tiramisù. Indoor and outdoor seating; English-speaking staff make it easy for first-timers.
mapQuery: Ristorante e Pizzeria Castel Nuovo Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +39 081 551 5524
Getting there: Piazza Francese 42, by Castel Nuovo; about 5 minutes from the cruise terminal and Molo Beverello ferries.
Hours: Daily 11:00–23:30

name: Gusto Marigliano Pizzeria e ristorante
description: A beautifully tiled underground pizzeria on Via Medina, packed with locals, with soft dough, fresh toppings, excellent pizza fritta, stuffed zucchini flowers, and caprese ravioli. Short waits are worth it.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +39 081 224 2338
Getting there: Via Medina 12; about 7 minutes on foot from the cruise terminal.
Hours: Daily 12:00–15:00 and 18:30–23:30 (Fri to 24:00; Sun lunch to 15:30)

name: Amiro Restaurant
description: A creative, seafood-leaning restaurant on Via Medina with prawn fritters with lemon gel, an inventive mixed-seafood pasta with raw scampi, and an excellent house tiramisù. It also runs fun mixology classes; one recent review flagged inconsistency.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — call +39 081 1863 8222
Getting there: Via Medina 19; about 7 minutes from the cruise terminal.
Hours: Mon–Thu 11:30–23:30; Fri–Sun 11:30–24:00

name: Signora Bettola - Napoli (Medina)
description: A stylish modern trattoria known for an outstanding ziti alla Genovese, meatballs in ragù, eggplant parmigiana, and a theatrical tiramisù. Arrive at 19:30 or book for later dinners.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended after 19:30 — call +39 081 377 8653
Getting there: Via Medina 72; about 8 minutes from the cruise terminal.
Hours: Daily 12:30–15:30 and 19:30–23:30 (Sat–Sun lunch to 16:00; Sat dinner to 24:00)

name: Trattoria Caprese Napoli
description: A small, homey trattoria on Via Medina serving prosciutto pizza, pastas, salads, and good wine by the glass. The indoor room can be hot in summer, and some report an indoor seating surcharge.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +39 081 976 1044
Getting there: Via Medina 55/57; about 7 minutes from the cruise terminal.
Hours: Mon–Tue and Thu–Sun 12:00–15:30 and 19:00–24:00; Wed 9:00–23:30

name: Cento Sapori - Takeaway
description: A tiny, family-run lunch counter on Piazza Municipio serving generous home-style primi, secondi, salads, and sandwiches at local prices, with a few tables facing the square.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Piazza Municipio 25; about 4 minutes from the cruise terminal.
Hours: Mon–Fri 12:00–15:30; Sat 12:00–15:30 and 19:00–24:00; closed Sunday

name: DaMè al Plebiscito
description: A bistro-bar on Piazza Carolina beside Piazza del Plebiscito, good for breakfast, coffee, or an aperitivo with terrace glimpses of the sea and Vesuvius. Service is mostly warm, though one visitor found aperitivo drinks overpriced without snacks.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Piazza Carolina 16, off Piazza del Plebiscito; about 12 minutes on foot from the cruise terminal.
Hours: Daily 7:00–23:00

name: Ristorante Sette Passi a Chiaia
description: A sister-run trattoria on the steps above Piazza del Plebiscito with Neapolitan parmigiana, pasta with clams, and pizza in a charming stairway setting. Reviews are mostly warm, though desserts draw mixed notes.
mapQuery: Ristorante Sette Passi a Chiaia Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +39 081 1963 8163
Getting there: Salita Sant'Anna di Palazzo 25, just uphill from Piazza del Plebiscito.
Hours: Daily 11:00–23:00

name: Mary's Sfogliatella
description: A tiny kiosk at the Via Toledo entrance to Galleria Umberto I, widely hailed for the city's best sfogliatella, served warm with ultra-crisp layers. Stick to the classic riccia; the line moves fast.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Galleria Umberto I 66, at the Via Toledo entrance; about 10 minutes from the cruise terminal.
Hours: Mon and Wed–Sun 8:00–20:30; closed Tuesday

name: Augustus Napoli
description: An old-school pasticceria-bar on Via Toledo with cannoli, cakes, sfogliatelle, and lemon granita, plus a back sitting room. Standing at the bar costs less than table service; service gets mixed reviews.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Via Toledo 147, mid-Via Toledo.
Hours: Daily 7:00–20:30

name: Ceraldi Caffe'
description: An elegant wood-paneled café on Piazza Carità with a creamy Caffè del Nonno (served with a chocolate spoon), babà, fresh pastries, and breakfasts. Croissants sell out by mid-morning.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Piazza Carità 14, upper Via Toledo; Toledo metro nearby.
Hours: Daily 6:30–20:30

name: Mennella Il Gelato
description: A top Neapolitan gelato maker with naturally colored, covered tubs. Milk chocolate, almond, pistachio, and fiordilatte stand out, the line moves quickly, and it stays open late.
mapQuery: Mennella Il Gelato Via Toledo Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Via Toledo 110, upper Via Toledo.
Hours: Mon–Thu 10:30–01:00; Fri 10:30–02:00; Sat 10:00–02:00; Sun 10:00–01:00

name: GROM
description: An entirely gluten-free artisanal gelato chain branch on Via Toledo with gelato properly stored in pozzetti. Pistachio, lemon sorbet, and affogato are highlights, with air conditioning, a restroom, and a few seats.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Via Toledo 206, near Galleria Umberto I.
Hours: Mon–Fri 10:30–23:00; Sat 10:30–24:00; Sun 10:39–23:00

name: Spuzzuliann pe' Tuledo
description: A tiny pizza counter at the top of Via Toledo with excellent, cheap Neapolitan pizza, such as a Margherita for about €4.50 and a great diavola. Mostly takeaway, with only a few stools.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Via Toledo 395, upper Via Toledo near Dante.
Hours: Mon–Fri and Sun 10:30–21:30; Sat 10:30–22:00

name: Da Ciro
description: A small, newer trattoria-pizzeria on Via Toledo offering custom-topped pizzas, a well-praised carbonara, and trattoria dishes at very fair prices, with warm service. Fewer reviews so far than most of this list.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +39 373 900 8043
Getting there: Via Toledo 115, upper Via Toledo.
Hours: Mon–Tue and Thu–Sun lunch from 11:30 (Sun 12:00) and dinner from 19:00; closed Wednesday

name: Ristorante La Porta Accanto Napoli
description: A friendly restaurant on upper Via Toledo for regional staples: pasta e patate, cuoppo fritto (mixed fried bites), Genovese, eggplant parmigiana, and caprese ravioli, with wine and beer on tap. Covered canopy seating.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +39 081 976 3078
Getting there: Via Toledo 365, upper Via Toledo.
Hours: Daily 12:00–15:30 (Sun to 16:00) and 19:00–23:00

name: Trattoria da Nennella
description: Naples' most raucous trattoria, where waiters sing, shout, and dance through fast, cheap set meals of about €13 for a primo plus secondo. The pasta e patate con provola is the must-order; come for the show more than fine cooking.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (queue list)
Getting there: Piazza Carità 22, upper Via Toledo. Put your name on the list at the door, since tables turn in waves.
Hours: Mon–Sat 11:45–15:30 and 18:45–23:30; closed Sunday

name: Pizzeria Attilio's
description: A legendary family pizzeria in the Pignasecca market lane where the owner still delivers pizzas to tables. It is famous for its tomato sauce, star-shaped ricotta-crust pizzas, and the Carnevale. Expect a 20–30 minute wait at peak times.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (give name at door); call +39 081 552 0479
Getting there: Via Pignasecca 17, off upper Via Toledo near Piazza Carità.
Hours: Mon 19:00–23:30; Tue–Sat 12:00–15:30 and 19:00–23:30; closed Sunday

name: Trattoria da Concetta
description: A small, cheerful Quartieri Spagnoli trattoria full of locals, with famous polpette (meatballs), Genovese, spaghetti alla Nerano, gnocchi alla sorrentina, and fried anchovies at about €20 a head. Cramped but vibrant.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — call +39 081 402208
Getting there: Via Speranzella 19, Quartieri Spagnoli, a block above Via Toledo.
Hours: Tue–Fri 12:00–15:30 and 19:00–24:00; Sat 12:00–16:30 and 19:00–24:00; Sun 12:00–16:30; closed Monday

name: Vasceria Locanda Popolare
description: A lively locanda on a Quartieri Spagnoli street serving outstanding pasta e patate, Genovese, beef stew, fish, and steak with warm service. Street-side seating is noisy but full of Neapolitan life.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — call +39 342 067 9522
Getting there: Via Speranzella 141, Quartieri Spagnoli.
Hours: Daily 12:00–16:00 and 19:00–23:00

name: Trattoria Donna Tuttina
description: An authentic little Quartieri Spagnoli trattoria known for fish pasta, gnocchi, fried calamari, and an excellent tiramisù. Most reviews are warm, but a few report billing surprises, so check prices when ordering.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +39 392 761 6945
Getting there: Via Portacarrese a Montecalvario 58, Quartieri Spagnoli.
Hours: Mon–Wed and Fri–Sun 11:30–16:00 and 18:00–23:00; closed Thursday

name: Trattoria Quartieri Spagnoli
description: An affordable, authentic trattoria on a narrow lane with good pizza, mussels, squid, and daily specials like tagliatelle with mussels. Friendly staff, but dinner queues are common.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +39 081 251 2225
Getting there: Vico Santa Maria delle Grazie a Toledo 3, just off Via Toledo.
Hours: Mon and Wed–Sun 12:30–16:00 and 18:30–23:30; closed Tuesday

name: Pizzoteca by Quartieri Spagnoli 1536
description: A friendly pizzeria-bookshop just off Via Toledo with thin, light pizzas such as the Genovese and Margherita, indoor air conditioning, and a feed-those-in-need ethic. Its joke about a 'million-euro pineapple pizza' is part of the charm.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +39 081 1925 2348
Getting there: Vico Lungo del Gelso 85, Quartieri Spagnoli, a few steps from Via Toledo.
Hours: Daily 11:30–23:00

name: Pizzeria 400 Gradi

name: Quirinoli

details:

name: Vigna delle Rose
description: A vineyard restaurant and B&B on the Vesuvius slope offering tours, tastings and multi-course lunches with a wine for each course. The estate olive oil is outstanding and the views are wide open. Often added to Pompeii day excursions with transfers.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Booking recommended; call +39 351 542 4946
Getting there: Via Cifelli 10, Trecase; car, driver or tour transfer.

name: I Setari
description: A family-run fusion restaurant with a garden, a glass wall onto the kitchen and a cocktail program. The owner often gives guests a tour of the building. Some nights have live music, which can get loud in the garden.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended; call +39 376 165 3891
Getting there: Via Carotenuto 20b, Boscotrecase; car or taxi from Pompeii (about 15 min).
Hours: Dinner 18:00–24:00 Mon, Tue, Thu–Sun; Sun also 11:00–15:00; closed Wed

name: Vaisló Food&Wine Lab
description: A young chef's food-and-wine lab set in green foothills on the Vesuvius road. Dishes look simple but carry layered flavor; veal, risotto and fried chicken are favorites, and the chocolate-caramel dessert gets raves. The chef often serves too, so the pace is relaxed.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended; call +39 388 575 5328
Getting there: Via Panoramica 4, Boscotrecase; car or taxi.

name: Ristorante Masseria Del Vesuvio

details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead; call +39 081 635 1607

name: HORTI DOMUS Ristorante Braceria
description: A steakhouse in an elegant modern farmhouse on the Vesuvius slope. Guests tour the grounds, pick their cut, and watch it sliced, weighed and grilled. Meatballs and steaks are the stars, with owner-led hospitality.
mapQuery: HORTI DOMUS Ristorante Braceria Terzigno Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reservation recommended; call +39 081 277 7046

name: Il Capitano del Gusto Ristorante – Pizzeria

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

description: A neighborhood bistro in Boscoreale that surprises visitors who wander in; the setting is plain but the cooking is not. Paccheri with octopus and spaghetti with clams are highlights, and the gluten-free pizza is excellent. English-speaking service.
mapQuery: L'angolo del gusto bistrot Boscoreale Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call +39 389 428 4049
Getting there: Via Passanti Flocco 790, Boscoreale; car or taxi.

name: Pizzeria Oplonti
description: A mostly-takeaway pizzeria on the same street as Villa Poppaea (Oplontis), serving authentic pies at very low prices. They will set up a table if asked. An honest, local-priced dinner.

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

name: Osteria Annunziata – Sentimento Gastronomico
description: A cosy, modern osteria pairing traditional cooking with creative plating and a neat wine list. Prawns and genovese are standouts, and the owners greet regulars with hugs. English menus are limited.

details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended; call +39 392 849 6597

Hours: Tue–Fri 16:30–24:00; Sat–Sun 11:00–24:00; closed Mon

name: Dieci Bistrot
description: A family-run bistro led by a female chef, elevating traditional Campanian cooking. The seafood tasting menu, tender octopus and lemon pasta draw praise. A calm alternative to eating in Pompei itself.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended; call +39 081 748 0180
Getting there: Via Vittorio Veneto 14, Torre Annunziata; short taxi from Pompeii or Oplontis.

details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner; call +39 342 589 7733

name: Casa Caponi

name: Capri Blu Pizzeria & Bistrot – Torre Annunziata
description: A buzzing local pizzeria with an inventive menu, excellent dough and craft beers. The gluten-free pizza is a highlight. It fills up fast, so booking is wise.
mapQuery: Capri Blu Pizzeria Bistrot Torre Annunziata Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reservation recommended; call +39 081 922 6596

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

name: Cordella Ristorante Vineria

name: Ristorante Il Baffo Ai Fornelli

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

name: Vesuvè

details:
Reservations / tickets: Call +39 081 574 3405
Getting there: Via Antonio Gramsci 109/d, Massa di Somma; car required.

name: Lo Sfizio
description: A family trattoria on the lane climbing from Capri town toward Villa Jovis, far enough from the Piazzetta that the day-tripper crush thins out. A natural lunch stop before or after the Villa Jovis walk.

name: Pedro Capri

details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended, especially dinner — +39 339 408 8794

name: Luce Capri

Elegant without stiffness — good for a celebratory lunch or a romantic dinner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — +39 347 839 7976
Getting there: 5 min walk from the Piazzetta toward Via Camerelle.

name: Francuccio

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; book for groups — +39 081 837 8990
Getting there: Directly opposite the Marina Grande ferry docks — no funicular needed.

name: Osteria delle Sirene
description: A red-umbrella terrace on Via Roma, just below the Piazzetta, with one of the better sweeping views over Marina Grande. Pizza, meatballs in tomato and thoughtful cocktails make it an easy, unfussy lunch right after the funicular. Smaller and quieter than the big-name terraces nearby.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; call ahead in peak hours — +39 081 837 0003
Getting there: 2 min walk from the Piazzetta along Via Roma, near the bus terminus.

name: Ristorante Augusto Capri
description: A long-running seafood restaurant on the Marina Grande quay known for that-day fish, oysters and lemon-sauced pasta. Whole fish like scorpionfish are portioned tableside. Note that a service charge is added to the bill.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended at lunch — +39 081 837 0853
Getting there: On Via Cristoforo Colombo at Marina Grande, a short walk from the ferry docks.

name: Magna'cu'mme
description: A casual harbor café-restaurant on the left as you step off the ferry, good for pasta, seafood, lemon pastries and gelato. Ideal for a quick bite while waiting for a return boat. Seating is for table-service customers only.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Marina Grande waterfront, left of the ferry docks.

name: Focaccia Lab Capri (porto)
description: A counter spot at the port turning out focaccia sandwiches, slices and panini at prices rare on Capri. A few seats, but most people take it to go. The smartest budget lunch on the island for a short port day.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Via Cristoforo Colombo 63, Marina Grande — 2 min from the ferries.
Hours: Daily 10:00–19:00

name: La Floridiana Seaview Terrace
description: The hotel terrace restaurant of La Floridiana, perched on Via Occhio Marino with a quiet sweep of sea below. Attentive service, generous plates and good wine pairing make it a calm alternative to the crowded town center. Air-conditioned indoor seating helps on hot days.
mapQuery: La Floridiana Seaview Terrace Capri Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended, especially sunset dinner — +39 081 837 0101
Getting there: About 8 min walk from the Piazzetta via Via Camerelle.
Hours: 8:00–22:00 (Monday until 15:30)

name: Lo Scoglio delle Sirene Capri
description: A seafood restaurant, snack bar and bathing establishment on the rocks at Marina Piccola, Capri's south-side swimming cove. Lunch with your feet near the water, then a sunbed. Prices run high, so check before ordering.

details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for groups — +39 081 837 0221

name: Gennaro Amitrano Capri

details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — +39 347 752 5259

name: Ristorante La Capannina

details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — +39 081 837 0732
Getting there: 2 min walk from the Piazzetta.
Hours: Daily 12:00–15:00 & 19:00–23:30

name: Le Monzù

details:

Getting there: 15 min walk from the Piazzetta along Via Tragara.

name: Belle Epoque Capri

Easy WhatsApp booking and close enough to the port to make a pre-ferry lunch practical.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — WhatsApp/phone +39 366 626 9143
Getting there: Short walk uphill from Marina Grande on Via Marina Grande.

name: Ziqu Terrace Restaurant

details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended — +39 081 837 6630
Getting there: Via Marina Grande 191, a short ride or walk up from the port.

name: La Zagara

Reservations / tickets: Recommended; walk-ins possible right at opening — +39 081 837 2923

name: Da Emilia alla Curtiglia capri

mapQuery: Da Emilia alla curtiglia capri Anacapri Naples

name: Le Arcate

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

description: The two-Michelin-star restaurant of the Capri Palace in Anacapri, with live piano and meticulous service. Tasting menus are expensive (several hundred euros per person with pairings). A special-occasion dinner for travelers staying on the island.

details:
Reservations / tickets: Required — +39 081 978 0560

Sea-bass and lobster pastas are the signatures; the dessert room is famous, though the savory dishes outshine the sweets. Expensive and hard to book — plan well ahead.

Reservations / tickets: Recommended — +39 081 1972 1905

Reservations / tickets: Recommended — +39 081 896 0609

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

Reservations / tickets: Recommended on weekends — +39 081 896 9622

Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — +39 081 896 7367

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

Reservations / tickets: Recommended — +39 081 896 8256

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in / takeaway

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; book dinner — +39 377 830 0499

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in — +39 081 1756 3205

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in — +39 081 277 6954

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in — +39 081 333 4529

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in — +39 081 991203

Reservations / tickets: Recommended — +39 347 680 9473

Reservations / tickets: Recommended on weekends — +39 320 867 2867

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in — +39 081 998448

Reservations / tickets: Required — +39 081 997171

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in — +39 379 186 6032

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in — +39 081 1919 0388

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in — +39 081 976 1469

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in — +39 081 990085

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in — +39 081 904208

name: Ristorante Mustafà Pozzuoli

Reservations / tickets: Recommended — +39 333 259 8804

name: Acropolis of Athens
description: The rocky citadel crowned by the Parthenon, Erechtheion, Propylaea, and Temple of Athena Nike, the defining monument of classical Greece. Expect sweeping views over Athens to the sea; marble paths are slippery and shade is scarce.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Timed-entry ticket required; book the official e-ticket at hhticket.gr well ahead. The 8:00 slot is the least crowded.
Getting there: Main west entrance off Dionysiou Areopagitou (Acropoli or Monastiraki metro). The quieter South Slope entrance by the Acropolis Museum takes you past the Theatre of Dionysus. From Piraeus, about 25 minutes on Metro Line 1 or 30–40 minutes by taxi; plan a half-day.
Hours: Daily 8:00–17:00 (last entry earlier; hours change seasonally)

name: Acropolis Museum
description: A modern glass museum at the foot of the Acropolis holding the original Caryatids and Parthenon frieze, with excavations visible beneath glass floors. The top-floor Parthenon Gallery looks straight up at the temple.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door or online at theacropolismuseum.gr
Getting there: Dionysiou Areopagitou 15, beside Acropoli metro, next to the South Slope entrance.
Hours: Mon 9:00–17:00; Tue–Thu, Sat–Sun 9:00–20:00; Fri 9:00–22:00

name: Theatre of Dionysus Eleuthereus
description: The birthplace of Western theatre on the Acropolis's South Slope, where works by Sophocles and Euripides premiered. Stone seats and marble thrones still line the slope.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Acropolis ticket (hhticket.gr)
Getting there: Inside the Acropolis site, via the South Slope entrance on Dionysiou Areopagitou.
Hours: Daily 8:00–18:00 (seasonal)

name: Odeon of Herodes Atticus
description: A Roman-era stone theatre (AD 161) on the Acropolis's southwest slope, still used for summer concerts and the Athens Festival under the floodlit Parthenon. Outside events it is viewed from above on the Acropolis approach.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Interior only during performances; book Athens Epidaurus Festival tickets at aefestival.gr. The view from the path is free with an Acropolis visit.
Getting there: Dionysiou Areopagitou, on the way to the Acropolis west entrance.

name: Dionysiou Areopagitou
description: A broad, tree-lined pedestrian promenade circling the south and west of the Acropolis, linking the museum, theatres, and Thissio. It is magical at dusk with the lit Parthenon above and street musicians below.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: From Acropoli metro, walk west toward Thissio.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Areopagus Hill
description: A bare marble outcrop just below the Acropolis where Athens' ancient court met and St. Paul preached. It offers free close-up views of the Propylaea and a classic sunset spot.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: A metal staircase just right of the path to the Acropolis west entrance. The rock is polished and very slippery, so wear grippy shoes.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Philopappos Hill
description: The pine-covered Hill of the Muses facing the Acropolis, laced with paths by architect Dimitris Pikionis. It is quieter than Areopagus and has some of the best sunset and night views of the Parthenon.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Main paved path starts opposite the Acropolis on Dionysiou Areopagitou near Agios Dimitrios church. Paths are unlit in places at night.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Philopappos Monument
description: A 2nd-century Roman marble mausoleum crowning Philopappos Hill, with panoramic views from the Acropolis to Piraeus and the Saronic Gulf.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Summit of Philopappos Hill, about a 15–20 minute uphill walk from Dionysiou Areopagitou.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Pnyx
description: The hillside assembly ground where Athenian citizens gathered to vote, often called the birthplace of democracy. Its stone speaker's platform faces the Acropolis, with great views and few crowds.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: West of Philopappos Hill, reached from the Pikionis paths or from Thissio.

description: Rock-cut chambers on Philopappos Hill traditionally (though unprovenly) linked to Socrates' imprisonment. Viewed through bars only, it makes a shaded stop on the hill walk.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: On the lower Philopappos path from Dionysiou Areopagitou.
Hours: Open 24 hours

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: At the foot of Philopappos Hill, opposite the Acropolis.
Hours: Daily 7:00–12:00 and 17:00–20:00

mapQuery: National Observatory of Athens Thissio Visitor Center
details:

Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate or hhticket.gr; included in the combined archaeological ticket

details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Ancient Agora ticket

Reservations / tickets: Included in the Roman Agora ticket

Hours: Daily 8:00–20:00 (follows Roman Agora hours)

name: Holy Church of the Virgin Mary Gorgoepikoos (Little Metropolis)
description: One of the world's smallest cathedrals, a 12th–13th-century chapel built almost entirely of recycled ancient and Byzantine marble reliefs.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Mitropoleos Square 8, beside the Metropolitan Cathedral.
Hours: Daily 10:00–17:00

name: Panagia Kapnikarea Church
description: An 11th-century Byzantine church standing in the middle of busy Ermou shopping street. It is a serene, frescoed refuge amid the crowds.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Kapnikareas Square on Ermou St, between Syntagma and Monastiraki.
Hours: Mon–Sat 11:00–21:15; Sun 7:00–21:15

name: Museum of Greek Folk Musical Instruments "Fivos Anoyanakis"
description: A charming Plaka mansion museum with about 1,200 traditional instruments, most with headphones so you can hear them played. Small, inexpensive, and open late.
mapQuery: Museum of Greek Folk Musical Instruments Athens
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Diogenous 1–3, Plaka, beside the Roman Agora.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:00–20:00; closed Tuesday

name: The Jewish Museum of Greece
description: A moving, well-curated museum tracing 2,300 years of Greek Jewish life, including a restored synagogue interior and Holocaust history.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Nikis 39, between Plaka and Syntagma.

name: Varvakios Central Municipal Market
description: Athens' raw, authentic central market, with cavernous meat and fish halls and spice and olive shops spilling into surrounding streets. Not for the squeamish, but full of local color; go in the morning.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Athinas St, between Monastiraki and Omonia.
Hours: Mon–Fri 7:00–15:30; Sat 7:00–18:00; closed Sunday

name: Technopolis City of Athens
description: A 19th-century gasworks turned cultural complex in Gazi, hosting the Maria Callas museum, exhibitions, festivals, and concerts. Lively on event nights.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Mostly free entry; events ticketed via technopolis-athens.com
Getting there: Pireos 100, Gazi, beside Kerameikos metro.

name: Benaki Museum - Pireos
description: The Benaki's industrial-chic annex for major temporary exhibitions of modern and contemporary art, photography, and design, with a café.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door or benaki.org
Getting there: Pireos 138, a short walk from Kerameikos metro.
Hours: Thu and Sun 10:00–18:00; Fri–Sat 10:00–22:00; closed Monday–Wednesday

name: Syntagma Square
description: The central square of modern Athens, facing the Parliament, with a fountain, cafés, and the start of Ermou shopping street. It is the main transport hub, with metro, tram, and airport bus.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Syntagma metro (Lines 2 and 3); from Piraeus, change at Monastiraki or take the X80 bus.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Monument to the Unknown Soldier
description: A war memorial below Parliament guarded by the kilted Evzones, whose slow, high-stepping changing of the guard happens every hour on the hour. The full ceremonial changing with band is on Sundays at 11:00.
mapQuery: Monument to the Unknown Soldier Athens
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Vasilissis Amalias, Syntagma Square. Arrive 30–60 minutes early on Sundays.
Hours: Open 24 hours; guard changes hourly

name: Hellenic Parliament
description: The former royal palace (1843), now Greece's Parliament, presiding over Syntagma. Most visitors admire the façade and the Evzones ceremony out front.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Exterior only for most visitors
Getting there: Syntagma Square.

name: Zappeion Garden
description: Formal gardens around the neoclassical Zappeion Hall, adjoining the shady National Garden, with fountains, parrots, and a café. A cool green walk from Syntagma to the Panathenaic Stadium.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Vasilissis Olgas 1, south of the National Garden. Gates close at the hours shown.
Hours: Mon–Fri 7:00–19:00; Sat–Sun 7:00–21:00

name: Panathenaic Stadium
description: The only stadium in the world built entirely of marble, site of the first modern Olympics in 1896, with a museum of Olympic torches. An audio guide is included; climb the stands for city views.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate or panathenaicstadium.gr
Getting there: Vasileos Konstantinou Ave; about a 15-minute walk from Syntagma through the National Garden.
Hours: Daily 8:00–17:00 (longer in high summer)

name: Mount Lycabettus
description: Central Athens' highest hill, with a 360° panorama from the Acropolis to the sea, best at sunset. It is a steep walk from Kolonaki or a funicular ride, and the summit is crowded at golden hour.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; funicular tickets at the station
Getting there: Walk up from Kolonaki (about 30 minutes), take a taxi to the upper road, or ride the funicular from Aristippou St (rated lower for value; about €13 return).

name: Holy Church of Saint George of Lycabettus
description: A whitewashed 1870 chapel on Lycabettus's summit with a marble terrace, giant Greek flag, and the city's best 360° view.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Summit of Mount Lycabettus.
Hours: Mon–Sat 11:00–19:00; Sun 7:00–16:15

name: National Archaeological Museum
description: One of the world's great museums of antiquity, home to the Mask of Agamemnon, the Antikythera Mechanism, the Artemision bronze, and vast sculpture galleries. Allow 2–3 hours.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door or hhticket.gr; bags are checked
Getting there: 28is Oktovriou (Patission) 44; about 8 minutes on foot from Victoria or Omonia metro.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:00–20:00; Tue 13:00–20:00 (seasonal)

name: Benaki Museum
description: A mansion museum spanning Greek culture from prehistory to the 20th century, with costumes, jewelry, reconstructed Ottoman-era rooms, and a rooftop café. Free Thursday evenings.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door or benaki.org
Getting there: Koumpari 1 at Vasilissis Sofias, Kolonaki; near Syntagma.
Hours: Mon, Wed, Fri–Sat 10:00–18:00; Thu 10:00–24:00; Sun 10:00–16:00; closed Tuesday

name: Benaki Museum - The Ghika Gallery
description: Painter Nikos Hadjikyriakos-Ghika's former home, now showcasing Greece's '30s Generation of artists and writers, with his preserved studio on the top floors.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Kriezotou 3, just north of Syntagma.
Hours: Thu 12:00–20:00; Fri–Sun 10:00–18:00; closed Monday–Wednesday

name: Museum of Cycladic Art
description: A world-class collection of minimalist Cycladic marble figurines, plus Cypriot and ancient Greek galleries and strong temporary shows.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door or cycladic.gr
Getting there: Neofytou Douka 4, Kolonaki; about 10 minutes on foot from Syntagma or Evangelismos metro.
Hours: Mon, Wed, Fri–Sat 10:00–17:00; Thu 10:00–20:00; Sun 11:00–17:00; closed Tuesday

name: Byzantine & Christian Museum
description: A spacious museum of Byzantine icons, mosaics, frescoes, and daily-life objects in a garden villa, with a lovely café and open-air exhibits.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Vasilissis Sofias 22, near Evangelismos metro.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:30–15:30; closed Tuesday

name: War Museum Athens
description: Greek military history from antiquity to WWII, with detailed dioramas and fighter jets and helicopters parked outside. It is inexpensive and great with kids.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Rizari 2–4, next to the Byzantine Museum.
Hours: Mon–Fri, Sun 9:00–19:00; Sat 9:00–22:00

name: National Gallery - Alexandros Soutsos Museum
description: Greece's renovated national art museum, from post-Byzantine icons and El Greco to modern Greek masters like Parthenis. Signage can be sparse.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door or nationalgallery.gr
Getting there: Vasileos Konstantinou 50, by Evangelismos metro.
Hours: Mon, Thu–Sun 10:00–18:00; Wed 10:00–22:00; closed Tuesday

name: Basil & Elise Goulandris Foundation
description: An elegant private museum with works by Van Gogh, Cézanne, Picasso, Gauguin, and Rodin alongside top Greek modernists. It has a nice café and restaurant.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door or goulandris.gr
Getting there: Eratosthenous 13, Pangrati, near the Panathenaic Stadium.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Thu, Sat–Sun 10:00–18:00; Fri 10:00–20:00; closed Tuesday

name: Numismatic Museum of Athens
description: Ancient coins displayed in Heinrich Schliemann's frescoed neoclassical mansion, the Iliou Melathron by Ernst Ziller, which is itself the attraction.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Panepistimiou 12, a short walk from Syntagma.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:30–15:30; closed Tuesday

name: National Historical Museum - Old Parliament House
description: Greece's first parliament building, now telling the story of modern Greece from the 1821 War of Independence onward through paintings and relics. The grand hall also hosts candlelight concerts.
mapQuery: National Historical Museum Old Parliament Athens
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Stadiou 13, Kolokotroni Square, near Syntagma.
Hours: Tue–Sun 10:00–16:00; closed Monday

name: Academy of Athens
description: Theophil Hansen's dazzling marble neoclassical academy, flanked by statues of Athena and Apollo atop Ionic columns. It is part of the Neoclassical Trilogy with the University and National Library, and beautiful lit at night.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Exterior viewing (free)
Getting there: Panepistimiou 28, between Syntagma and Omonia (Panepistimio metro).

name: Vallianeio Megaron (National Library)
description: Hansen's Doric-temple library building with a grand curved stair, completing the Neoclassical Trilogy. The collection moved to the SNFCC, and the interior reading room has had closures.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Exterior viewing; reading room weekdays
Getting there: Panepistimiou 32, next to the Academy. Take care in the area after dark.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:00–14:00

name: Mikrolimano
description: Piraeus's prettiest little harbor, a horseshoe of sailboats and fishing caïques ringed by seafood tavernas and bars below the Kastella hill. It is lovely at sunset.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Akti Koumoundourou, about 3 km southeast of the cruise terminal (taxi about 10 minutes), or Line 1 to Neo Faliro and a 10-minute walk.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Archaeological Museum of Piraeus
