description: A compact museum holding rare original classical bronzes found in Piraeus, including the Piraeus Apollo, Athena, and Artemis, plus a monumental funerary monument. It is the best culture stop near the port.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door (cash reported)
Getting there: Char. Trikoupi 31, near Zea Marina; about 15 minutes on foot from the port's central gates.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 9:00–17:00; closed Tuesday

name: Church of Agios Nikolaos
description: The blue-domed church of St. Nicholas, patron of sailors, overlooking the main port, with richly painted icons and frescoes inside. Free to visit.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Agiou Nikolaou 2, on the port waterfront near the cruise gates.
Hours: Daily from about 6:00 to 18:00–18:30

name: Municipal Theatre of Piraeus
description: Piraeus's grand 1895 neoclassical theatre with an Italian-style auditorium, staging plays (mostly in Greek), tours, and exhibitions, plus an elegant bar.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Shows and tours via the box office or theatre website
Getting there: Iroon Polytechniou 32, opposite Piraeus metro station.
Hours: Box office Mon, Wed–Fri 10:00–14:00 and 18:00–21:00; Sat 16:00–21:00; Sun 18:00–21:00; closed Tuesday

name: Holy Church of the Prophet Elias (Kastella)
description: A hilltop church crowning Kastella, Piraeus's highest point, with sweeping views over Mikrolimano, the port, and the Saronic Gulf. It is a steep climb.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Idis St, Kastella hill above Mikrolimano.

name: Piraeus Tower
description: Greece's first skyscraper (1972), reborn in 2024 with a shimmering façade facing the port, with shops and a top-floor café with harbor views.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Akti Posidonos 2, opposite the metro and port.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:00–21:00; Sat 9:00–20:00; Sun 11:00–20:00

name: Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center (SNFCC)
description: Renzo Piano's landmark home of the National Opera and Library, set in a lavender-scented park with a canal, free events, and a rooftop Lighthouse with 360° views to the Acropolis. There is an evening fountain show.
mapQuery: Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center Athens
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free entry; opera and events at snfcc.org
Getting there: Leoforos Syngrou 364, Kallithea; about 15 minutes by taxi from Piraeus, or the free shuttle from Syntagma.
Hours: Park daily 6:00–24:00

name: Naval Museum Battleship HS Georgios Averof
description: The world's last surviving armored cruiser (1911), hero of the Balkan Wars, open to explore from bridge to engine rooms. A replica trireme and a submarine are moored nearby.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket on site
Getting there: Trocadero Marina by Flisvos, Palaio Faliro; about 15 minutes by taxi from Piraeus, or the coastal tram.
Hours: Tue–Fri 9:00–14:00; Sat–Sun 10:00–17:00; closed Monday

name: Flisvos Marina
description: A superyacht marina on the Faliro waterfront with promenades, cafés, and restaurants, and sunset over the Saronic Gulf. Next to the Averof and close to the SNFCC.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Palaio Faliro; about 15 minutes by taxi from Piraeus, or the coastal tram.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Vouliagmeni Lake
description: A brackish thermal lake in a collapsed limestone cave beneath a sheer cliff, with mild water year-round, tiny 'pedicure' fish, and a lounge-and-restaurant setup. It is a unique swim on the Riviera.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Paid entry; book sunbeds at lakevouliagmeni.gr on busy days
Getting there: Poseidonos Ave, Vouliagmeni; about 40 minutes by taxi from Piraeus. On-site parking with attendants fills on weekends. A half-day outing.
Hours: Daily 8:30–18:00 (seasonal)

name: Vouliagmeni Coast
description: Vouliagmeni's main organized public beach (Akti Vouliagmenis), with clear water, sunbeds included with entry, changing rooms, a snack bar, and play areas. It is the best-value beach close to Athens.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Paid entry at the gate (higher on weekends)
Getting there: Poseidonos Ave 2, Vouliagmeni; about 40 minutes by taxi from Piraeus, or tram to Glyfada plus bus. A half-day outing.
Hours: Daily 9:00–17:00 (seasonal)

name: Astir Beach
description: The Riviera's glamorous premium beach club on the Astir peninsula, with crystal-clear shallow water and immaculate sand. Sunbeds are expensive and service is reported slow.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Paid sunbeds; book ahead at astir-beach.com
Getting there: Apollonos 40, Vouliagmeni; about 40 minutes by taxi from Piraeus. A half-day outing.
Hours: Daily 8:00–20:00 (seasonal)

name: Temple of Poseidon
description: A 5th-century BC marble temple on a sheer cape above the Aegean, where Byron carved his name. It is the most famous sunset in Attica, reached by a spectacular coastal drive.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate or hhticket.gr
Getting there: Cape Sounion, about 70 km (1 hour 15 minutes or more) from Piraeus along the coast road; by tour, car, or KTEL bus from Athens. A half-day trip.

name: Ancient Theatre of Thorikos
description: One of the oldest theatres in the world, with an unusual elliptical shape and original stones, on a hillside near Lavrio. Free, quiet, and atmospheric at sunset.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Thorikos, just north of Lavrio port; park at the small gate below and walk up (don't follow Google Maps further). About 1 hour 10 minutes from Piraeus. A half-day trip.
Hours: Open access

name: Mineralogical Museum of Lavrion
description: A volunteer-run collection of stunning minerals from the ancient Laurion silver mines that funded Athens' golden age. Tiny, Greek-labeled, and open only brief hours.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Andrea Kordela 6, Lavrio; about 1 hour 10 minutes from Piraeus. A half-day trip.
Hours: Wed, Sat, Sun 10:00–12:00

name: Archaeological Site of Brauron
description: The Sanctuary of Artemis Brauronia in a peaceful marsh setting, with a restored stoa and a fine museum of votive finds. It is just 10 minutes from the airport.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (site and museum sold separately)
Getting there: Vravrona, east Attica; about 50 minutes from Piraeus by car. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:30–15:30; closed Tuesday

name: Tumulus of the Athenians at Marathon
description: The burial mound of the 192 Athenians who fell defeating the Persians in 490 BC, set in a landscaped park on the famous battlefield.
mapQuery: Tumulus of the Athenians Marathon Athens
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate
Getting there: Marathon, northeast Attica; about 1 hour from Piraeus by car. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:30–15:30; closed Tuesday

name: Archaeological Site of Ramnous
description: A remote seaside site with the Temple of Nemesis and a hilltop fortress over the Evia straits, reached by a scenic 1 km walk along an ancient road. Rarely visited and magical.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate; call +30 2294 063477 to confirm opening
Getting there: Near Grammatiko, northeast Attica; about 1 hour 15 minutes from Piraeus by car. Wear good shoes and bring water. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:30–15:15; closed Tuesday

name: Kaisariani Monastery
description: An 11th-century Byzantine monastery in pine woods on Mount Hymettus, with fine frescoes and a spring once sacred to Aphrodite. A peaceful escape just outside the center, with hiking trails.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate
Getting there: Hymettus slopes above Kaisariani; about 20 minutes by taxi from Syntagma, or 45 minutes from Piraeus. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:30–15:00; closed Tuesday

name: Holy Monastery of Daphni
description: A UNESCO-listed 11th-century monastery famed for some of the finest Byzantine mosaics anywhere, including a majestic Christ Pantocrator in the dome. Recently restored.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Iera Odos, Chaidari, on the highway west toward Corinth; about 25 minutes by taxi from Piraeus. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:30–17:00; closed Tuesday

name: Eleusis Archeological Site
description: The sanctuary of Demeter and Persephone where the secret Eleusinian Mysteries were celebrated for over a millennium, with a small museum. It is underrated and uncrowded.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate or hhticket.gr
Getting there: Elefsina, about 30 minutes west of Piraeus by car. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:00–19:00 (seasonal); closed Tuesday

name: Corinth Canal
description: A dramatic 6 km channel slicing through sheer limestone walls between the Aegean and Ionian seas, completed in 1893. Watch from the road bridges, where bungee jumping is also offered.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: About 1 hour west of Piraeus on the Athens–Corinth highway. Use the viewpoint and bridge area off the old national road (Google Maps may route you oddly). A half-day trip.
Hours: Open access

name: Acrocorinth
description: A vast hilltop fortress layered with Greek, Roman, Byzantine, Frankish, Venetian, and Ottoman walls, with huge views over the isthmus. Free and wildflower-strewn in spring.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Above Ancient Corinth, about 1 hour 15 minutes from Piraeus; drive to the top car park, then walk on slippery paths. Usually combined with the Corinth Canal on a half-day or day tour.
Hours: Mon–Thu, Sat–Sun 8:30–15:30; Fri 8:30–12:00

name: Archaeological site of Mycenae
description: Agamemnon's Bronze Age citadel, with the Lion Gate, Cyclopean walls, royal tombs, the Treasury of Atreus, and an on-site museum. There is no shade, so go early.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate or hhticket.gr
Getting there: Mykines, Peloponnese; about 1 hour 45 minutes from Piraeus. A full-day tour, often with Epidaurus.
Hours: Daily 8:30–15:30 (seasonal)

name: Ancient Theatre at the Asklepieion of Epidaurus
description: The best-preserved ancient Greek theatre (4th century BC), famed for acoustics that carry a whisper to the top row, with summer performances in the Athens Epidaurus Festival.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate or hhticket.gr; performances via aefestival.gr
Getting there: Epidavros, Peloponnese; about 2 hours from Piraeus. A full-day tour.
Hours: Daily 8:00–19:00 (seasonal)

name: Palamidi Fortress
description: A Venetian hilltop fortress (1711–1714) above Nafplio, Greece's first capital, reached by the famous 999 steps or by car. Panoramic views over the Argolic Gulf; some bastions are closed.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate
Getting there: Nafplio, Peloponnese; about 2 hours from Piraeus. A full-day trip.
Hours: Daily 8:00–18:00 (seasonal)

name: Delphi Archaeological Site
description: The Sanctuary of Apollo, 'navel of the ancient world', terraced into Mount Parnassus with the Temple of Apollo, theatre, and stadium. Breathtaking mountain views; climb to the top for the stadium.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate or hhticket.gr (combined with the museum)
Getting there: Delphi, about 2 hours 45 minutes from Piraeus. A full-day tour; not realistic on a short port call.
Hours: Daily 8:30–20:00 (seasonal)

name: Delphi Archaeological Museum
description: Home of the bronze Charioteer of Delphi, the Naxian Sphinx, and the Siphnian Treasury friezes, finds from the sanctuary next door.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Combined ticket with the site (hhticket.gr)
Getting there: Beside the Delphi site, about 2 hours 45 minutes from Piraeus. Part of a full-day Delphi tour.
Hours: Daily 8:30–20:00 (seasonal)

name: Temple of Aphaia
description: A remarkably complete Doric temple (c. 500 BC) on a pine-clad hilltop on Aegina island, forming the 'sacred triangle' with the Parthenon and Sounion, with sea views and a small museum.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate
Getting there: Aegina island, about a 40–75 minute ferry from Piraeus, then a 25-minute bus or taxi from Aegina town. A full-day trip.
Hours: Daily 8:00–19:00 (seasonal)

name: Old Venetian Port of Chania
description: The crescent-shaped 14th-century Venetian harbour is the heart of Chania, ringed by pastel townhouses, Ottoman domes and waterfront cafés. Morning is quiet and photogenic; evenings turn lively as restaurants fill along the quay. It is the natural starting point for every Old Town walk.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About 15 min by taxi or KTEL bus from Souda cruise port (approx. 7 km) to the Old Town; walk down to the waterfront.
Hours: Open public waterfront

name: Lighthouse of Chania
description: The slender stone lighthouse, rebuilt by the Egyptians in the 1830s on Venetian foundations, anchors the end of the harbour breakwater. The walk out along the narrow, unshaded mole gives the classic view back over the harbour and the White Mountains. The lighthouse interior is not usually open.
tags: verify: breakwater access (one recent review reports a temporary closure)
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Walk east along the harbour past the Venetian shipyards to the breakwater; about 1.5 km and 20 min from the Old Town each way.

name: Firka Venetian Fortress
description: A Venetian bastion at the western mouth of the harbour, where the Greek flag was raised in 1913 to mark Crete's union with Greece. The ramparts give a panoramic view of the harbour and lighthouse. Part of the complex houses naval exhibits.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: West end of the harbour, beside the Maritime Museum.
Hours: Mon–Fri 8:00–14:00; closed Sat–Sun

name: Maritime Museum of Crete
description: A surprisingly large museum inside the Firka complex, with detailed ship models built on site, naval relics and Battle of Crete material. The courtyard has one of the best harbour and lighthouse views. Entry is about €5.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €5 adults)
Getting there: Akti Kountourioti, west end of the harbour.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:00–16:00; closed Sun

name: Archaeological Museum of Chania
description: A modern, spacious museum covering about 6,000 years of western Crete, from Minoan finds to Roman mosaics. Plan about an hour. Fully accessible, with free parking and a terrace café overlooking the sea.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door or online (about €15)
Getting there: Skra 15, Halepa district, about 2 km east of the Old Town; taxi or 25-min walk.
Hours: Mon & Wed–Sun 8:00–20:00; closed Tue

name: Eleftherios Venizelos House
description: The preserved home of Crete's most important modern statesman, filled with original furniture, documents and the bullet-marked car from an assassination attempt. A free app guide adds depth, and there is a shaded café. Entry about €5.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €5)
Getting there: Plateia Elenas Venizelou, Halepa, near the Archaeological Museum; taxi or 25-min walk from the harbour.
Hours: Tue–Fri 10:30–17:30; Sat–Sun 11:00–16:00; closed Mon

name: Byzantine and Post-Byzantine Collection of Chania
description: A small museum in the restored church of San Salvatore holding frescoes, icons, mosaics and Byzantine coins. A quick, rewarding stop for history lovers.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door
Getting there: Theotokopoulou 78, at the harbour end of Theotokopoulou Street.
Hours: Mon & Wed–Sun 8:30–15:30; closed Tue

name: Folklore Museum of Chania
description: A tiny museum in a traditional house showing Cretan crafts such as weaving, basketry and silk work. A resident embroidery artist often works on site. Entry about €4.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €4)
Getting there: Chalidon 46, inside the passage beside the Catholic church; easy to miss.
Hours: Daily 10:00–17:00

name: Center of Traditional Folk Art and Culture
description: A small free exhibition and shop of handmade Cretan embroidery and needlework, including live silkworms. Photography rules are strictly enforced, so ask before taking pictures.
mapQuery: Center of Traditional Folk Art and Culture Chania
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Skoufon 20, Old Town.
Hours: Daily 10:30–22:30

name: Etz Hayyim Synagogue
description: Crete's only surviving synagogue, restored after the Jewish community was lost in 1944. Staff bring the history to life, and a small museum sits alongside. A quiet, moving stop in the busy Old Town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (donation welcome)
Getting there: Parodos Kondylaki, off Kondylaki Street in the old Jewish quarter.
Hours: Mon–Thu 10:00–16:00; Fri 10:00–15:00; closed Sat–Sun

name: Küçük Hasan Mosque
description: The domed Mosque of the Janissaries, built in 1645, is the most recognizable building on the harbour front. It now hosts art exhibitions, so the interior is open only during shows.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in when open
Getting there: Harbour front, Sourmeli 18.
Hours: Fri–Sat 18:00–22:00 per Google; open during exhibitions

name: Grand Arsenal (Megalo Arsenali)
description: A restored Venetian shipyard on the harbour, now a cultural venue hosting free municipal exhibitions and events. The building itself is a handsome harbour landmark.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; exhibitions usually free
Getting there: East side of the inner harbour.
Hours: Mon–Fri 18:00–23:00 during exhibitions

name: Neoria (Venetian Shipyards)
description: Seven of the original seventeen 16th-century vaulted shipyards survive along the eastern harbour, where Venetian galleys were built and stored. You pass them on the walk to the lighthouse.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Eastern inner harbour, on the way to the breakwater.

name: San Salvador Bastion
description: Part of the Venetian walls guarding the western approach to the harbour, near the Topanas quarter. Good for a short walk around the fortifications; parking nearby is very limited.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Pireos 73, west of the harbour by Firka.

name: Old Chania Market
description: The lanes around the cross-shaped 1913 Municipal Market are packed with small shops selling local products, herbs, crafts and leather goods. Lively and very busy on cruise days.
tags: verify: whether the market hall interior is open (it has been under long-term renovation)
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: South edge of the Old Town at the end of Chalidon Street.

name: Holy Metropolitan Church of the Presentation of the Virgin Mary (Trimartiri)
description: Chania's Orthodox cathedral, with an ornate gilded interior, a carved iconostasis and large chandeliers. Free entry; modest dress is expected.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Plateia Mitropoleos, off Chalidon Street.

name: Holy Catholic Church of the Assumption
description: A serene Franciscan church set back from Chalidon Street through a narrow passage, opposite the Orthodox cathedral. Weekend Mass is held in Greek and English.
mapQuery: Catholic Church of the Assumption Chania
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Chalidon 46, through the arched passage.

name: Church of Saint Nicholas (Splantzia)
description: A large church that was a Venetian monastery, then an Ottoman mosque, and is now Orthodox again. It is the only building in Chania with both a bell tower and a minaret. Free to enter when open.
mapQuery: Church of Saint Nicholas Splantzia Chania
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Splantzia Square, eastern Old Town.

name: Splantzia Square
description: The leafy heart of the old Turkish quarter, shaded by a huge plane tree and lined with meze tavernas and cafés. Atmospheric by day and buzzing in the evening.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Eastern Old Town, about 5 min from the harbour.

name: Koum Kapi Beach
description: A small sandy town beach just east of the Old Town walls, with steps down from the seawall, showers, changing cabins and promenade cafés. Good for a quick swim between sights.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Akti Miaouli, about 10 min walk east of the harbour.

name: Nea Chora Beach
description: The nearest proper sandy beach to the Old Town, sheltered by rocks, with loungers, showers and fish tavernas. Occasionally closed briefly for water-quality reasons.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; loungers for rent
Getting there: Akti Papanikoli, about 10 min walk west of the harbour.

name: Venizelos Graves
description: The hilltop tombs of Eleftherios and Sophoklis Venizelos in a shaded park with the best panoramic view over Chania and the coast. Lovely at sunset, with a small chapel and a café.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Profitis Ilias hill, Akrotiri road, about 10 min by car from the Old Town; limited parking.
Hours: Open site

name: Holy Trinity Tzagarolon Monastery (Agia Triada)
description: A beautifully restored 17th-century Venetian-style monastery set among olive groves and vineyards on Akrotiri. A small museum and a shop sell the monks' own wine, olive oil and honey. Entry about €3; free parking.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €3)
Getting there: Akrotiri peninsula, about 30 min by car from Chania or Souda.
Hours: Mon 8:00–20:00; Tue–Fri 7:00–20:00; Sat–Sun 6:30–20:00

name: Gouverneto Monastery (Virgin of the Angels)
description: A fortress-like 16th-century monastery at the tip of Akrotiri, run by monks who sell handmade skin products. It is also the trailhead for the walk down to Katholiko. Check hours carefully: it closes midday and on Wednesdays and Fridays.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Small entry donation (about €2.50)
Getting there: About 4 km beyond Agia Triada; large free car park. Modest dress required.
Hours: Mon, Tue, Thu 9:00–12:00 & 17:00–19:00; Sat–Sun 5:00–12:00 & 17:00–20:00; closed Wed & Fri

name: Monastery Katholiko
description: The dramatic ruins of an 11th-century monastery carved into a gorge, reached on foot past St John the Hermit's cave, with a small bay below. Allow 30–40 min down and more coming back uphill in full sun.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Trailhead at Gouverneto Monastery car park; stepped, rocky path. Wear proper shoes, bring water, and go early or late in the day.
Hours: Trail open daylight hours

name: Seitan Limania
description: A dramatic cliff-lined cove of turquoise water on Akrotiri, one of Crete's most photographed swimming spots. Reaching it means a steep, hairpin access road and a rocky scramble down. Very little space on the tiny beach and no facilities below.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Akrotiri, about 25 min from Chania. Arrive early; the small car park fills by mid-morning. Sturdy shoes essential.

name: Marathi Beach
description: A calm, family-friendly sandy beach on Souda Bay with clear water, mountain views and good fish tavernas. Close to the cruise port, making it the easiest beach escape on a port day.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; loungers for rent
Getting there: About 20 min by car from Souda port. Parking around €5/day fills by afternoon.

name: Souda Bay Commonwealth War Cemetery
description: An immaculately kept Commonwealth War Graves cemetery on the shore of Souda Bay, holding about 1,500 Allied servicemen from the 1941 Battle of Crete. A quiet, moving place for reflection.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Souda, about 5 min by car from the cruise port; free parking.

name: Archaeological Site of Aptera
description: The hilltop ruins of an ancient city-state overlooking Souda Bay, with a well-preserved Roman theatre, huge vaulted Roman cisterns and good on-site information. Plan about 1.5 hours. Bring water, as there is no café on site.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €10)
Getting there: Megala Chorafia, about 20 min by car from Souda port; free parking.
Hours: Mon & Wed–Sun 8:00–18:30; closed Tue

name: Koules Ottoman Fortress (Izzeddin)
description: A restored Ottoman fortress guarding the entrance to Souda Bay, with a small history exhibition and wide views over Souda Island. Easy to combine with Aptera next door. Cash only.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €2, cash only)
Getting there: Kalami, just below Aptera; free parking.
Hours: Mon & Wed–Sun 9:00–19:30; closed Tue

name: Lake Kournas
description: Crete's only natural freshwater lake, ringed by mountains. You can rent pedal boats (about €10/hour) to see freshwater turtles along the far shore. Tavernas and pottery shops line the edge.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; pedal boats rented on site
Getting there: Near Georgioupoli, about 45 min by car from Chania. Free and paid parking available.

name: Saint Nicholas Chapel (Georgioupoli)
description: A tiny whitewashed chapel perched at the end of a rocky causeway into the sea at Georgioupoli. A favorite photo stop. The causeway is wet, slippery and sharp, so grippy shoes are needed.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Georgioupoli seafront, about 40 min by car from Chania.

name: Georgioupoli Beach
description: A long sandy beach where a cold spring-fed river meets the sea, giving a mix of cool and warm water. Plenty of beach bars offer loungers free with drinks, with lifeguards and showers.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Georgioupoli, about 40 min by car from Chania; plenty of parking.

name: Kalyves Beach
description: A soft, sandy beach in the village of Kalyves with gently sloping water, good for families, plus tavernas and shops behind. Watch for rip currents away from the breakwater end.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Kalyves, about 25 min by car from Souda port; free parking.

name: Agii Apostoli Beach
description: Twin sheltered sandy coves divided by a small headland and chapel, just west of the city. Shallow water, free showers and changing cabins, with a café and rentable loungers.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About 10 min by car or local bus west of Chania; free street parking.

name: Platanias Beach
description: The long beach of Chania's busiest resort, lined with tavernas and water sports. It is exposed to wind, so red flags are common.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Platanias, about 20 min by car west of Chania.

name: Maleme German Military Cemetery
description: A hillside cemetery for more than 4,000 German paratroopers killed in the 1941 Battle of Crete, overlooking the Maleme airfield landing zone. A volunteer-run visitor center explains the battle. The uphill walk is hot, so bring water.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Above Maleme on the old road toward Kissamos, about 25 min by car from Chania.

name: Gonia Monastery (Mother of God Odigitria)
description: A 17th-century seaside monastery at Kolymbari with peaceful courtyards and an excellent museum of Byzantine icons. Entry about €4. Modest dress is required.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €4)
Getting there: Kolymbari, about 35 min by car west of Chania.
Hours: Daily 9:00–19:00

name: Balos Lagoon
area: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
description: Crete's most famous lagoon of white sand and shallow turquoise water at the tip of the Gramvousa peninsula. Reach it by boat from Kissamos port, which usually includes Gramvousa, or by car over a long, rough dirt road followed by a 20–30 min hike down. Crowded midday when the boats arrive.
tags: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
details:
Reservations / tickets: Boat tours from Kissamos should be booked ahead
Getting there: About 1.5 hours by car from Chania to the dirt road, then about 30 min of rough driving. Pay €1 per person at the road entry and about €3–5 for parking. A full-day commitment; realistically only with a tour on a port day.

name: Balos Viewpoint
area: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
description: The classic elevated view over Balos Lagoon, on the footpath down from the car park. Allow about 35 minutes to climb back up in the heat. Wear proper shoes and a hat.
tags: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Short walk from the Balos car park at the end of the dirt road.

name: Gramvousa Beach
area: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
description: A boat-access-only beach on Imeri Gramvousa island with clear water and good snorkeling, usually the first stop on Balos boat trips. It gets crowded quickly when several boats land at once.
tags: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book a Balos-Gramvousa boat tour in advance
Getting there: Boat only, from Kissamos port as part of Balos tours.

name: Gramvousa Fort
area: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
description: A Venetian fortress atop Imeri Gramvousa island, once a pirate stronghold, with sweeping views over Balos. The climb takes about 20 minutes on tall, uneven rocky steps. Grippy shoes are a must.
tags: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included with Balos-Gramvousa boat tours
Getting there: Boat only, from Kissamos port on Balos-Gramvousa tours.

name: Falasarna Beach
area: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
description: A wide, sandy west-facing beach with clear water and some of Crete's best sunsets. It is spacious enough to find room even in summer. Loungers cost about €20–30 per set.
tags: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About 1 hr 15 min by car from Chania via Kissamos; paved road and large parking areas.

name: Archaeological Site of Falasarna
area: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
description: The remains of an ancient harbour city lifted out of the sea by the 365 AD earthquake, with towers, quays and mooring stones still visible. The guard is helpful, and a VR app shows the city as it was.
tags: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: North end of Falasarna; the last stretch is a bumpy dirt road, or park and walk 10 min.
Hours: Fri–Mon 8:30–15:30; closed Tue–Thu

name: Archaeological Museum of Kissamos
area: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
description: A well-presented museum of western Crete finds from the Minoan to Roman eras, highlighted by a restored Roman mosaic floor. Plan about an hour. Entry about €5.
tags: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €5)
Getting there: Stratigou Tzanakaki Square, Kissamos town; about 1 hour by car from Chania.
Hours: Mon & Wed–Sun 8:30–15:30; closed Tue

name: Elafonissi Beach
area: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
description: A protected lagoon of shallow, crystal-clear water with patches of pink sand, linked to an islet you can wade to. Very crowded midday. The scenic drive through gorges and villages is part of the experience.
tags: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; loungers about €20
Getting there: About 2 hours by car from Chania on narrow mountain roads; parking about €3–5. A full day on a port call.

name: Chrysoskalitissa Monastery
area: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
description: A whitewashed clifftop monastery overlooking the Libyan Sea, with a small museum and sweeping views. It pairs naturally with Elafonissi, which is 10 minutes away. Knees must be covered; wraps are provided.
tags: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €2.50)
Getting there: About 1 hr 50 min by car from Chania, near Elafonissi; limited free parking.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–19:30; Sun 7:30–19:30

name: Cave of Agia Sofia
area: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
description: A huge lit cave with stalactites and a small chapel, high above the Topolia Gorge, where griffon vultures often circle. A good stop on the drive to Elafonissi. Expect many steps up from the roadside.
tags: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Topolia Gorge road, about 1 hr 15 min from Chania. The final road is single-lane in places; park at the roadside.
Hours: Daily 8:00–20:00

name: Samaria Gorge (Iron Gates)
description: Europe's most famous gorge hike, 13–16 km from the Omalos plateau down to Agia Roumeli on the south coast. The highlight is the Iron Gates, where the walls narrow to a few metres. It is a full-day, one-way hike ending with a ferry and bus back, so it does not fit a standard 10-hour port call.
tags: verify: season dates, latest entry time, and whether tickets must be bought online
details:
Reservations / tickets: Gorge entry ticket required (about €10)
Getting there: Trailhead at Xyloskalo, Omalos, about 1 hr 15 min from Chania. Exit is by ferry from Agia Roumeli to Sougia or Chora Sfakion, then bus or taxi. Gorge parking is about €5–10, cash. A shortcut version starts from Agia Roumeli.
Hours: Open seasonally

name: Imbros Gorge
description: A shorter, quieter alternative to Samaria: about 8 km downhill through a narrow canyon to Komitades near the south coast, taking 2.5–3.5 hours. Taxis shuttle hikers back to the top. Entry about €5.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Pay at the entrance kiosk (about €5)
Getting there: Trailhead at the far end of Imbros village, about 1 hr 15 min from Chania. Use the official entrance; signs earlier in the village belong to tavernas offering parking. Expect loose stones.
Hours: Daylight hours

name: Aradena Bridge
description: A metal-and-plank bridge spanning the deep Aradena Gorge in Sfakia, also a bungee-jumping site. The winding mountain drive and wild goats are part of the adventure, with a small café on site.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Above Anopoli, about 2 hours by car from Chania via Chora Sfakion; steep, winding road.

name: Chora Sfakion – Sweetwater Beach – Loutro Trail
description: A coastal section of the E4 path past Ilingas and Sweetwater beaches to car-free Loutro, with stunning views over the Libyan Sea. Narrow, exposed and unshaded in places. Many hikers return by boat from Loutro.
mapQuery: Chora Sfakion Sweet Water Beach Loutro hiking trail Chania
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; boat back from Loutro (cash)
Getting there: Trailhead off the road west of Chora Sfakion, about 2 hours by car from Chania; roadside parking. Bring plenty of water.

name: Frangokastello Castle
description: A square 14th-century Venetian fortress on the plain below the Sfakia mountains, with a fine sandy beach beside it. Free entry, though access is limited to the central courtyard.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Frangokastello, about 2 hours by car from Chania.
Hours: Mon & Wed–Sun 10:00–18:00; closed Tue

name: Lissos Gorge Trail
description: A scenic 1–1.5 hour hike from Sougia through a gorge and over the headland to the ancient site of Lissos and a pebble beach. Many hikers return by boat to Sougia.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; boat back about €6 cash
Getting there: Starts at Sougia harbour, about 1 hr 20 min by car from Chania. Bring water and snacks.

name: Botanical Park & Gardens of Crete
description: A large hillside garden of fruit trees, tropical plants, herbs and a lake, built after a 2003 wildfire. Peacocks and donkeys roam the grounds, and a farm-to-table restaurant overlooks the valley. Allow 1.5–2 hours on sloping paths.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the entrance
Getting there: Fournes, on the Omalos road, about 25 min by car from Chania; also reachable by KTEL bus.
Hours: Daily 9:00–20:30

name: Therisos Gorge
description: A dramatic, winding drive through a narrow, plane-shaded gorge from the edge of Chania up to the mountain village of Theriso. It is mainly a driving gorge with few places to stop, so watch for goats and fast drivers.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Starts at Perivolia, about 15 min from Chania; Theriso village is about 30 min.

name: Museum of National Resistance 1941–1945
description: A small, moving museum in Theriso documenting Cretan resistance fighters in World War II through photographs and personal stories. Labels are mostly in Greek. Entry about €1.
mapQuery: Museum of National Resistance Theriso Chania
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (about €1)
Getting there: Theriso village, about 30 min by car from Chania via the Therisos Gorge.

name: Eleftherios Venizelos' Birth House
description: The modest village house where Venizelos was born and spent his summers, now run by his foundation, with illustrated displays on his family and life. A good companion to his Halepa residence and the Theriso drive.
mapQuery: Eleftherios Venizelos Birth House Mournies Chania
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Mournies, about 10 min by car south of Chania.
Hours: Tue–Sat 10:00–13:30; closed Sun–Mon

name: Old Fortress
description: The Venetian sea fortress on its own promontory, cut off from town by a moat, with 1,500 years of layered history and a neoclassical British-era church of St George inside. Climb to the top for sweeping views over the Old Town, Vido Island and the Albanian coast. Allow 1–2 hours; the stone paths are polished and slippery.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €10; card accepted)
Getting there: From the cruise terminal it is ~2 km (25 min walk, or the port shuttle/taxi) to Spianada; the fortress bridge is at the east end of the square.
Hours: Daily 8:00–19:00 (shorter winter hours)

name: Old Fortress Lighthouse
description: The lighthouse crowning the highest point of the Old Fortress, reached by a steep final climb on slick cobbles. It delivers the best 360° panorama in Corfu Town, across to Vido and on clear days Saranda in Albania. Wear grippy shoes and go early to beat the heat.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Old Fortress ticket
Getting there: Inside the Old Fortress — follow the path uphill past the clock tower.
Hours: Daily 8:00–15:00 (summit access)

name: Corfu Byzantine Collection
description: A small gallery of Byzantine and post-Byzantine icons, frescoes and mosaics housed in the right wing of the first building inside the Old Fortress. A quiet, air-cooled stop to add context to the fortress visit.
mapQuery: Corfu Byzantine Collection Old Fortress Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Old Fortress ticket
Getting there: Inside the Old Fortress, first building on the right after the entrance.
Hours: Daily 8:30–15:30

name: New Fortress
description: The 16th-century Venetian fortress on the hill above the Old Port, a maze of tunnels, vaulted passages and British barracks. Less crowded than the Old Fortress, with fine views over the harbor, Old Town and mainland. Takes about an hour.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate
Getting there: Entrance near the Old Port, ~15 min walk from the cruise terminal — the closest major sight to the ship.
Hours: 8:30–15:30; closed Tuesday

name: Spianada Square
description: One of the largest squares in the Balkans, the grassy heart of Corfu Town with a cricket pitch left over from British rule. Shaded paths, the bandstand and cafés make it the natural meeting point between the Old Fortress and the Old Town lanes.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Center of the Old Town, ~25 min walk from the cruise terminal.
Hours: Open public square

name: Liston - Eleftheria Pedestrian Street
description: The arcaded promenade facing Spianada, built under French rule in the style of Paris's Rue de Rivoli. Its cafés are the classic place for a coffee or ginger beer while watching town life. Lively from morning through late evening.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: West edge of Spianada Square.
Hours: Open street; cafés roughly 8:00–late

name: Listón
description: The historic French-built arcade itself, a protected landmark and the most photographed façade in town. Worth seeing at different times of day as locals and visitors trade places under the arches.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Kapodistriou, alongside Spianada.
Hours: Open arcade

name: Maitland Monument
description: An Ionic rotunda in the southern part of Spianada, built in 1821 to honor Sir Thomas Maitland, first British High Commissioner. A shady, quiet corner with views toward the mainland.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: South end of Spianada Square.
Hours: Open public monument

name: Corfu Museum of Asian Art
description: Set in the neoclassical Palace of St Michael & St George, this museum holds an exceptional collection of Chinese, Japanese and wider Asian art over three floors. The palace rooms and the hidden garden terrace behind, overlooking the sea, are reasons in themselves. No elevator.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €10)
Getting there: North end of Spianada Square.
Hours: Daily 8:00–20:00

name: Holy Church of Saint Spyridon
description: Corfu's most important church, home to the relics of the island's patron saint, with the tallest bell tower in the Ionian. The interior glows with silver lamps and a painted ceiling. Modest dress required; no photos inside.
mapQuery: Holy Church of Saint Spyridon Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Agiou Spiridonos, 2 min west of Liston.
Hours: Daily 7:00–20:00

name: Plakada t' Agioú Spiridona Square
description: A small, picturesque square beside St Spyridon lined with cafés and the 17th-century church of Panagia Faneromeni. A pleasant place to sit and watch the Old Town pass.
mapQuery: Plakada t Agiou Spiridona Square Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Next to the Church of Saint Spyridon.
Hours: Open square

name: Casa Parlante Museum
description: A restored 19th-century noble mansion presented as a living home, with guided tours through rooms full of period furnishings, sounds and scents. Guides often finish with a taste of homemade sweets and rose liqueur. One of the most engaging museums in town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €10); guided tour included
Getting there: Nikiforou Theotoki 16, Old Town.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–18:00; closed Sunday

name: Banknote Museum of the Ionian Bank
description: A free museum telling Greek history through its currency, from antiquity to the euro, in four well-labelled rooms. Friendly staff and an elevator. Thirty minutes well spent.
mapQuery: Banknote Museum of the Ionian Bank Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free entry
Getting there: Nikiforou Theotoki 32, near St Spyridon.
Hours: Wed & Fri 9:00–14:00 & 17:30–20:30; Thu 9:00–15:00; Sat–Sun 8:30–15:00; closed Mon–Tue

name: Archaeological Museum of Corfu
description: A compact, air-conditioned museum whose star is the Gorgon pediment from the Temple of Artemis, one of the oldest stone pediments in Greece. Allow about an hour.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €10)
Getting there: Vrela Armeni 1, a short walk south of Spianada along the seafront.
Hours: 8:00–20:00; closed Tuesday

name: V museum Corfu
description: A new interactive museum opened in 2025 with holograms, CGI displays and a 3D cinema film on Corfu's history. Staff guide you through. Good for families.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door or online in busy periods
Getting there: El. Venizelou, along the port road ~10 min walk from Old Town.
Hours: Daily 9:00–17:00

name: Museum of Dionysios Solomos
description: The house where Greece's national poet and author of the national anthem lived and died, with manuscripts, his desk and period paintings. Small but meaningful.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door
Getting there: Arseniou 1, Old Town seafront.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:30–14:00; closed weekends

name: Bell Tower of the Annunziata Holy Church
description: The lone surviving bell tower of a church destroyed in WWII bombing, tied to the Battle of Lepanto. A poignant landmark in a busy Old Town square.
mapQuery: Bell Tower of the Annunziata Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Vrachlioti 56, Old Town.
Hours: Viewed from outside

name: Holy Metropolitan Church of the Virgin Mary Spilaiotissa, Saint Blaise and Saint Theodora Augusta
description: Corfu's cathedral (1577), holding the relics of Byzantine Empress St Theodora. Rich icons and fine acoustics.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Mitropoleos 1, near the Old Port.

name: Municipal Greek-British Cemetery of Corfu
description: A tranquil 19th-century garden cemetery with British graves, Commonwealth war graves and resident tortoises.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Kolokotroni 8, south-west of the Old Town.
Hours: Mon 8:00–13:00; Tue–Fri 9:00–13:00; closed weekends

name: Holy Monastery of Panagia Vlacherna
description: The tiny white monastery on an islet joined to Kanoni by a causeway, with Mouse Island just beyond — Corfu's postcard view. Planes land overhead at the airport runway beside it.
mapQuery: Holy Monastery of Panagia Vlacherna Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Kanoni, ~5 km south of town (taxi 15 min or bus no. 2). Walk down from the Kanoni viewpoint and across the causeway.
Hours: Daily 8:00–23:00

name: Boat Rides to Pontikonisi Island
description: Small boats shuttle from Vlacherna to Mouse Island (Pontikonisi) roughly every 15 minutes, landing beside its Byzantine chapel. A 5-minute ride with planes overhead.
mapQuery: Boat Rides to Pontikonisi Island Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; about €3 round trip, cash only
Getting there: Departs from the Vlacherna causeway jetty.
Hours: Daily 8:30–21:30

name: Kanoni Viewpoint
description: The terrace above Vlacherna and Mouse Island, with the runway at your feet — a classic photo and plane-spotting spot. Cafés nearby; magical before sunset.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: End of the Kanoni peninsula; paid parking (~€8).
Hours: Open viewpoint

name: Pontikonisi Beach
description: A small pebble cove at Perama facing Mouse Island, where planes pass low overhead. Two bars; no changing facilities. A quick swim stop rather than a full beach day.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Perama, across the lagoon from Kanoni.

name: The Achilleion Palace
description: Empress Sisi's palace at Gastouri, with terraced gardens, Achilles statues and sweeping views. The interior is largely closed for restoration — visit for the gardens and views.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate
Getting there: Gastouri, ~10 km south of town (25 min by taxi or tour).
Hours: Daily 8:00–20:00

name: Mon Repos Park
description: Wooded park around the villa where Prince Philip was born, with ancient Palaiopolis ruins, a temple site and a small pebble beach. Free entry and shady trails.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free park entry
Getting there: Analipsi, ~2 km south of Spianada along the seafront (25 min walk).
Hours: Daily 8:00–21:00 (gates lock)

name: Holy Church of the Holy Apostles Jason and Sosipater
description: Corfu's oldest church, built around 1000 AD from ancient stones, with uncovered fresco fragments inside. A quiet gem in Anemomylos.
mapQuery: Holy Apostles Jason and Sosipater Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Anemomylos, ~20 min walk south of Spianada.

name: Church of the Hypapante at Gouvia
area: Gouvia, Dassia & the Northeast Resort Strip
description: A tiny chapel on a spit of land in Gouvia Bay, picture-perfect against the water. Interior opens in the evening only.
mapQuery: Church of the Hypapante Gouvia Corfu
tags: Gouvia, Dassia & the Northeast Resort Strip
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Limni/Gouvia, ~8 km north of town; small parking area.
Hours: Interior daily 17:00–22:00

name: Agios Nikolaos Beach (Dassia)
area: Gouvia, Dassia & the Northeast Resort Strip
description: A quiet, shaded pebble cove with a little seaside chapel. No facilities. Water shoes needed.
tags: Gouvia, Dassia & the Northeast Resort Strip
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Dassia, ~12 km north of town; small parking area.

name: Holy Monastery of the Virgin Mary at Paleokastritsa
description: A 13th-century monastery on a headland above Paleokastritsa's turquoise coves, with a flower-filled courtyard, icon museum and spectacular coastal views. Modest dress required; wraps are lent free.
mapQuery: Holy Monastery of the Virgin Mary Paleokastritsa Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; donation welcome
Getting there: Paleokastritsa, ~25 km (40 min) north-west of town; small free car park near the top, otherwise a steep walk from the beach. A half-day round trip on a port day.
Hours: Daily 6:30–12:45 & 15:00–19:00

name: Angelokastro Byzantine Castle
description: A ruined 13th-century Byzantine castle on a sheer crag above the west coast, one of the most dramatic sites in Corfu. A short, steep climb rewards with views across the island. Little shade; bring water.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €10)
Getting there: Above Krini village, ~6 km north of Paleokastritsa via a narrow road; small car park and roadside parking.
Hours: 10:00–17:30; closed Tuesday

name: Angelo Castro Viewpoint
description: The lookout at the foot of Angelokastro with sweeping coastal views even without entering the castle. A 10-minute walk from parking.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Same access as Angelokastro; narrow road.

name: The Blue Eye Cave
description: A sea cave near Paleokastritsa where sunlight through an underwater opening turns the water an electric blue. Seen on 40–45 minute small-boat tours that also visit other caves.
mapQuery: The Blue Eye Cave Paleokastritsa Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Boat ticket about €15 adult, cash
Getting there: Boat tours depart from Paleokastritsa harbor.
Hours: Boats roughly 9:00–19:00

name: Paleo Sea Travel - Boat trips and boat rentals in Corfu,Paleokastritsa
description: A well-organized operator running cave-and-beach boat trips and sunset cruises from Paleokastritsa, plus self-drive boat rentals. Clean boats and engaging skippers.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book online or at the kiosk — +30 698 008 1780
Getting there: Paleokastritsa harbor.
Hours: Daily 9:00–22:00

name: Observatory of Kaiser Wilhelm II
description: The Kaiser's Throne above Pelekas village, where Wilhelm II came to watch the sunset — a 360° view across the island. Corfu's favorite sunset spot.
mapQuery: Observatory of Kaiser Wilhelm II Pelekas Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Pelekas, ~13 km (25 min) west of town; limited parking at the top, fills near sunset.
Hours: Open viewpoint

name: Glyfada Beach
description: One of Corfu's best sandy beaches, backed by green cliffs, with clear water and water sports.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; sunbeds €20–50
Getting there: Below Pelekas, ~16 km west of town; parking €10 near the beach, free roadside above.

name: Porto Timoni beach
description: A spectacular double beach on a narrow isthmus near Afionas, reachable by a rocky 20–30 minute hike. Arrive early; closed-toe shoes recommended.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Park in Afionas village, then hike down.

name: Kanali tou Erota
description: Canal d'Amour at Sidari: sandstone cliffs sculpted into channels and coves where legend says couples swimming through will marry. Crowded in season.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Sidari, ~37 km (1 hr) north-west of town.

name: Cape Drastis
description: Corfu's northernmost cape, with white clay cliffs and rock islets above turquoise water. A short walk from a small car park; best at sunset.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Near Peroulades; small car park fills fast. Access to the cliff edge may be restricted.

name: CAPE DRASTIS COMPANY BOAT TOURS
description: Short boat trips beneath Cape Drastis to Logas Beach and Canal d'Amour with drop-off swims. The best way to see the cliffs up close.
mapQuery: Cape Drastis Company Boat Tours Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: About €20 per person — +30 693 186 8844
Getting there: Departs below the Cape Drastis car park (~20 min walk down).
Hours: Daily 10:00–20:00

name: Logas the sunset beach
description: A narrow beach beneath towering cliffs at Peroulades, famous for its sunset. Access via broken steps and rocks.
mapQuery: Logas the sunset beach Peroulades Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Peroulades, ~5–10 min drive from Sidari.

name: Bataria Beach
description: A turquoise pebble cove beside Kassiopi castle, with excellent snorkeling.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; sunbeds €15–20
Getting there: 15–20 min walk from Kassiopi; paid parking in town.

name: Kassiopi Byzantine Castle
description: Overgrown ruins of a Byzantine-Angevin fortress above Kassiopi harbor, with shaded paths and sea views.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Kassiopi, ~36 km (1 hr) north of town.
Hours: Open site

name: Kalamionas Beach
description: Kassiopi's village pebble beach, good for snorkeling and sunsets.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Short walk from Kassiopi center.

name: Kerasia beach
description: A pebble cove with clear, calm water and great snorkeling. Free parking.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Off the coast road via a narrow, steep lane.

name: The White House Restaurant
description: The waterfront house in Kalami where Lawrence Durrell lived in the 1930s, now an upscale restaurant on the bay.
mapQuery: The White House Restaurant Kalami Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — +30 2663 091465
Getting there: Kalami Bay, ~30 km north of town; reachable by road or water taxi.

name: Mount Pantokrator
description: Corfu's highest peak, with views over the island to Albania and mainland Greece. Narrow, winding asphalt road; café at the top.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: ~1 hr from town; limited summit parking.

name: Monastery of Pantokrator
description: The monastery on the summit of Mount Pantokrator, with a painted ceiling and gift shop. Free entry.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Summit of Mount Pantokrator.
Hours: Daily 10:00–19:00

name: Old Peritheia
description: An abandoned Venetian-era stone village revived with tavernas and a honey producer.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Off the north coast road via Loutses — take the paved northern route.
Hours: Tavernas roughly 9:30–23:00

name: Museum Kouris
description: A private folk-life museum in Lefkimmi with a personal tour by the owner. Free entry; donations welcome.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free — +30 698 844 7799
Getting there: Lefkimmi, ~45 km (1 hr) south of town.
Hours: Daily 10:00–17:00

name: Issos Beach
description: A long, wild sandy beach backed by dunes near Lake Korission. Free parking.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: ~35 km south-west of town.

name: Arkoudilas Beach
description: A secluded sandy beach near Kavos reached by a rough road — often easier to park and walk 1.5 km.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; sunbeds €5
Getting there: South tip near Kavos.

name: Arkoudilas Path
description: A walking trail over Corfu's southern headland with sea views; rough access road.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: From Kavos/Arkoudilas.

name: Arkoudillas Viewpoint
description: A hilltop lookout over Kanoula Bay, reached by a 30–60 minute walk. Go early in summer.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Park on the main road and walk.

name: Cape Asprokavos
description: Corfu's southernmost cape, reached through forest on a rocky trail.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About 1 hour walk from Kavos.

name: Blue Caves
description: The sea caves on Paxos' west coast with luminous blue water. Corfu day cruises often run 8:30–18:30, past a 16:00 all-aboard.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book a boat trip
Getting there: By boat only.

name: Cave Papanikolis
description: A large sea cave on Paxos with pool-blue water.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book a boat trip
Getting there: By boat only.

name: Ypapanti's Cave
description: A large Paxos sea cave visited by tour boats.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book a boat trip
Getting there: By boat only.

name: Tripitos Arch
description: A natural sea arch on Paxos reached by a short rocky walk. Very little parking at the top.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: South of Gaios, Paxos.

name: Gaios viewpoint
description: A hillside lookout over Gaios harbor, a 10–15 minute uphill walk from the port.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Gaios, Paxos.

name: Paralia Voutoumi
description: Antipaxos' celebrated beach with exceptionally clear water. Crowded with boats midday.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book a boat trip
Getting there: Antipaxos — boat only.

name: Dubrovnik City Walls
description: The near-2 km circuit of medieval walls wrapping the Old Town, with ever-changing views over terracotta roofs, forts and the Adriatic. Allow 1.5–2 hours; there are cafés, free toilets and several exit points along the way.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket about €40 online or at entrances, or use the Dubrovnik Pass, which includes the walls plus Lovrijenac and several museums
Getting there: Main entrance just inside Pile Gate, with further entrances near Ploče Gate and St John's Fort. From Gruž cruise port take city bus 1A, 1B, 3 or 8 to Pile (about 15 min) or a taxi.
Hours: Daily from 8:00 to 18:00 (last entry earlier; hours shorten off-season)

name: Pile Gate
description: The Old Town's grand western entrance, with a drawbridge, a statue of St Blaise and the main city-walls ticket office just inside. Arrive before 10 am to beat cruise crowds.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Western edge of the Old Town; the main bus terminus for routes from Gruž and Lapad.
Hours: Open access

name: Ploče Gate
description: The quieter eastern gate, crossed by a stone bridge beside Fort Revelin, with harbour views and its own walls entrance nearby.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Eastern Old Town by Fort Revelin, near the Banje beach road.
Hours: Open access

name: Buza Gate
description: The small northern gate opening onto the upper Old Town, a less-crowded way in and the closest gate to the cable car.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: North wall of the Old Town, about 5 min below the cable car station.
Hours: Open access

name: Stradun (Stari grad Dubrovnik)
description: Dubrovnik's polished limestone main street linking Pile and Ploče gates, lined with Baroque façades, cafés and side alleys. Magical early morning or after the cruise crowds leave in late afternoon.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Runs straight through the Old Town from Pile Gate.
Hours: Open access

name: Onofrio's Large Fountain
description: Domed 15th-century fountain just inside Pile Gate, still pouring cold, drinkable water from its carved masks. A perfect bottle refill before the walls.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Just inside Pile Gate at the start of Stradun.
Hours: Open access

name: Small Onofrio's Fountain
description: The elegant 1440s little sister of the big fountain on Luža Square, beautifully carved and still flowing with fresh water.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Luža Square at the eastern end of Stradun.
Hours: Open access

name: Franciscan Church and Monastery
description: 14th-century monastery with a peaceful orange-tree cloister, a museum of manuscripts and one of Europe's oldest pharmacies (founded 1317), still trading at the entrance. Shell scars from 1991 are still visible.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door (about €8) or included in the Dubrovnik Pass
Getting there: Just inside Pile Gate on the left.
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:00

name: Sponza Palace
description: Graceful Gothic-Renaissance palace and former customs house on Luža Square, now home to the State Archives, exhibitions and a moving room remembering the defenders of 1991–95.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Courtyard free; exhibitions may charge
Getting there: Luža Square, eastern end of Stradun.
Hours: Mon–Fri 8:15–15:00; Sat 8:15–13:00; closed Sun

name: Rector's Palace
description: Seat of the Ragusan Republic's government, now the Cultural History Museum, with an arcaded courtyard, portraits, a dungeon and an old pharmacy collection. Its stairs appear in Game of Thrones.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door or included in the Dubrovnik Pass
Getting there: Pred Dvorom, beside the Cathedral.
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:00

name: The Cathedral of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary
description: Baroque cathedral rebuilt after the 1667 earthquake, with a Titian altarpiece and a treasury of reliquaries, including St Blaise's.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Church free; treasury small fee
Getting there: Kneza Damjana Jude 1, next to the Rector's Palace. The main façade may be under works; use the side entrance.
Hours: Mon–Sat 8:00–19:00; Sun 11:30–19:00

name: Saint Blaise's Church
description: Baroque church of the city's patron saint on Luža Square, home to a 15th-century silver statue of St Blaise holding a model of Dubrovnik that survived the 1706 fire. Free entry.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Luža Square, opposite Sponza Palace.
Hours: Daily 8:00–12:00 & 16:30–19:00

name: Dominican Monastery
description: Gothic monastery with a lovely cloister and a small museum of religious art, gold work and manuscripts. Part of the church may be under renovation.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door (about €6)
Getting there: Sv. Dominika 4, by Ploče Gate.
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:00

name: Church of St. Ignatius
description: Grand Jesuit Baroque church at the top of the Jesuit Stairs, with an impressive frescoed apse. Free and peaceful.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Poljana Ruđera Boškovića, up the Jesuit Stairs from Gundulić Square.

name: Jesuit Stairs
description: Elegant Baroque staircase modelled on Rome's Spanish Steps, famous as the site of Cersei's walk of shame in Game of Thrones. Quietest early or in the evening.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: From Gundulić Square up to St Ignatius.
Hours: Open access

name: Minčeta Fortress
description: The round tower at the walls' highest northern point, with the best 360-degree view over the Old Town and a Game of Thrones location (House of the Undying). Golden hour is magical.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included with the city walls ticket
Getting there: Northwest corner of the walls; reached on the city walls circuit.
Hours: Accessed during city walls hours

name: Fort Revelin
description: Massive 16th-century fortress guarding Ploče Gate, with harbour views. By night it becomes Culture Club Revelin, a well-known nightclub.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Club entry ticketed on event nights
Getting there: Beside Ploče Gate, eastern Old Town.

name: Bokar Tower
description: 15th-century cliffside round fort guarding Pile Gate, with views to Lovrijenac and open sea; a King's Landing filming spot.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included with the city walls ticket
Getting there: Southwest corner of the walls; part of the city walls circuit.
Hours: Accessed during city walls hours

name: Lovrijenac Fortress
description: Dramatic fortress on a 37 m sea rock outside the walls, 'Dubrovnik's Gibraltar', with superb views back to the Old Town and Red Keep scenes from Game of Thrones. About 200 steps up.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included with the city walls ticket or Dubrovnik Pass; otherwise about €15–17
Getting there: 10 min walk west of Pile Gate via the small Pile harbour.
Hours: Daily 8:00–17:30

name: Old Port of Dubrovnik
description: The walled harbour on the Old Town's east side, departure point for Lokrum ferries, glass-bottom boats, kayak and island tours. Lovely at sunset with a walk out to the breakwater.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Boat tickets at kiosks on the quay
Getting there: Through the Ponta gate from Luža Square, or via Ploče Gate.
Hours: Open access

name: War Photo Limited
description: Powerful gallery of world-class war photojournalism, with a permanent exhibit on the 1990s Yugoslav wars. Sobering, essential context for the city.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door (about €10)
Getting there: Antuninska 6, a side street off Stradun.
Hours: Daily 10:00–16:00

name: Banje Beach
description: The city's closest pebble beach, five minutes past Ploče Gate, with clear water and postcard views of the walls and Lokrum. Loungers belong to the beach club and are pricey.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; loungers via the beach club
Getting there: Frana Supila, about 5 min walk east of Ploče Gate down steps from the road.
Hours: Open access

name: John Latsis Katakolo Port
description: The cruise pier opens directly onto the waterfront of a small fishing village, with tavernas, cafés and gift shops a few steps from the gangway. It is the starting point for the train, buses and taxis to Ancient Olympia, and an easy, low-effort stroll if you stay in town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Walk straight off the ship into the village; the harbor promenade runs along the pier.

name: Museum of Ancient Greek Technology Kostas Kotsanas
description: A small, hands-on museum of working replicas of ancient Greek inventions: automata, clocks, siege engines and puzzles. Staff demonstrate the devices, and it is especially good with kids. Entry is by donation.
mapQuery: Museum of Ancient Greek Technology Kostas Kotsanas, Katakolon
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; donation requested
Getting there: On the main road at the edge of the village, about a 5-minute walk from the pier.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:30–15:30; closed Sunday

name: Agios Andreas Beach
description: A small, pebbly cove beside the ancient site of Feia with clear water that is good for snorkeling. A café-bar above offers sunbeds when you buy drinks; water shoes are recommended.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About 2 km north of the port, roughly an 8-minute taxi ride; access is via steps down from the bar, with a small parking lot.

name: Mercouri Estate
description: A historic family winery and olive estate set in landscaped gardens, with peacocks roaming the grounds. Self-guided visits with generous tastings are inexpensive, and you can buy wine and olive oil on site.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead (+30 2621 041601), especially for groups or weekends
Getting there: In Korakochori, about a 10-minute taxi ride north of Katakolon port.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:00–15:00, Sat 9:00–14:00; closed Sunday

name: Katakolo Lighthouse
description: A historic stone lighthouse on the headland south of the village. It is closed to visitors and hard to see from the road, so treat it as a quick walking detour rather than a destination.
details: Getting there: About 1 km south of the port along the headland road.

name: Archaeological Site of Olympia
description: The UNESCO-listed sanctuary of Zeus and the birthplace of the Olympic Games. You walk among temples, the athletes' training grounds and the original stadium. Allow about 3 hours together with the museum; it is shaded and park-like but hot by midday.
tags: verify: seasonal hours on cruise date
details:
Reservations / tickets: Combined ticket (about €20) for the site and museums; buy online at hhticket.gr to skip the ticket queue
Getting there: About 40 km (40–50 min) from the port by taxi, coach or the seasonal Katakolon–Olympia train. This is a half-day trip; arrive early to beat the cruise crowds.
Hours: Summer approx. 8:00–20:00; winter hours are shorter

name: Archaeological Museum of Olympia
description: One of Greece's great museums. It holds the Temple of Zeus pediment sculptures, Praxiteles' Hermes, the Nike of Paionios, and armor and bronzes from the sanctuary. Seeing it first helps you picture the ruins.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the combined site ticket
Getting there: Next to the archaeological site in Ancient Olympia, 40–50 min from the port. Half-day trip.
Hours: Daily approx. 8:00–20:00 in summer

name: Stadium at Olympia
description: The original Olympic stadium, entered through the vaulted Krypte tunnel. Visitors still run the ancient track between grassy embankments where 45,000 spectators once sat.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the site ticket
Getting there: At the eastern end of the archaeological site. Half-day trip from the port.
Hours: Follows site hours

name: Temple of Zeus
description: The massive base of the temple that once housed Phidias' gold-and-ivory statue of Zeus, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. A single re-erected column shows the original scale.
mapQuery: Temple of Zeus, Ancient Olympia, Katakolon
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the site ticket
Getting there: In the center of the archaeological site. Half-day trip from the port.
Hours: Follows site hours

name: Museum of the History of the Olympic Games of Antiquity
description: A compact, well-labeled museum on the ancient Games themselves: the events, athletes, prizes and rituals, with descriptions in several languages. It is included in the site ticket and easy to fit in.
mapQuery: Museum of the History of the Olympic Games of antiquity, Katakolon
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the combined ticket
Getting there: On Praxiteli Kondyli Street in Ancient Olympia village, a short walk from the site. Half-day trip from the port.
Hours: Daily approx. 8:00–20:00 in summer

name: Archimedes Museum
description: A free, interactive museum of Archimedes' inventions and ancient Greek technology, run by the same team as the Kotsanas museum. Staff demonstrate the exhibits in several languages; it is a great stop for kids.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; donation requested
Getting there: Praxiteli Kondyli 9, in the center of Ancient Olympia village. Half-day trip from the port.
Hours: Daily 10:00–20:00

name: International Olympic Academy
description: The academic home of the Olympic movement. Its grounds hold the stele containing Pierre de Coubertin's heart. It is mainly an educational campus, so public access is limited.
details: Getting there: About 1 km east of the archaeological site, on the road above the Kladeos valley. Half-day trip from the port.

name: Archaeological Museum of Pyrgos
description: A beautifully restored 19th-century market hall displaying finds from across Ilia, from the Stone Age through Mycenaean, Roman and Byzantine times. It is quiet, cool and rarely crowded.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; small entry fee
Getting there: Karaiskaki 10, central Pyrgos, about 13 km (20 min) from the port by taxi or bus.
Hours: Tue–Sun 8:30–15:30; closed Monday

name: Holy Metropolitan Church of Saint Nicholas
description: Pyrgos' imposing cathedral crowns the hill of the old Eparchio above the main square. It is an architectural landmark and an active place of worship.
mapQuery: Holy Metropolitan Church of Saint Nicholas, Pyrgos, Katakolon
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; dress modestly
Getting there: Beside Karagiorga Square in central Pyrgos, about 20 min from the port.

name: Sakis Karagiorgas Square
description: Pyrgos' large central square, ringed by cafés and shops and fitted with play areas. It is the best place to sit with a coffee and watch local life.
details:
Getting there: Central Pyrgos, about 20 min from the port.
Hours: Open public square

name: Milton Iatridis Square
description: A small, leafy square in central Pyrgos, good for a short pause between the museum and the cathedral.
details:
Getting there: Letrinon Street area, central Pyrgos.
Hours: Open public space

name: Apollo Theater
description: An elegant late-19th-century neoclassical theater, said to have been designed by Ernst Ziller, that still hosts plays and films. The facade is the highlight; the interior is dated.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets for performances via the theater (+30 2621 036521)
Getting there: Sillaidopoulou 2, central Pyrgos.

name: Kourouta Beach
description: A long, wide Blue Flag sandy beach with clear Ionian water, lined with beach bars that rent sunbeds and umbrellas. It is a favorite day-trip for cruise families; trash can pile up out of season.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; sunbeds through the beach bars
Getting there: About 25 km north of the port, a 30-min taxi ride; travelers report about €100 round trip. Half-day trip.

name: Monastery of Panagia Fragkavilla
description: An 11th-century Byzantine church on the edge of Amaliada, set within rocky walls and gardens. It is serene and historically important.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; dress modestly
Getting there: About 1.5 km from Amaliada center, 10 min inland from Kourouta. Half-day trip from the port.

name: Church of St. Tryphon Amaliada
description: A large, well-kept church with a lovely garden in the town of Amaliada, which serves Kourouta beach.
mapQuery: Church of St. Tryphon Amaliada, Katakolon
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Agiou Trifonos 18, Amaliada, about 10 min from Kourouta.
Hours: Daily from morning to late evening (Sunday from 7:00)

name: Agios Athanasios Church Amaliada
description: A small chapel on Agios Athanasios Square in central Amaliada, making for a pleasant short stop.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Kapodistriou 8, Amaliada.

name: Moni Agiou Athanasiou
description: A peaceful, centuries-old nunnery near Ampelokampos with a long history dating to the Ottoman era. The nuns welcome visitors warmly.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; modest dress
Getting there: About 10 min north of Kourouta by car. Half-day trip from the port.
Hours: Mon–Fri 7:00–12:00, 17:00–20:00; closed Sat–Sun per listing

name: Kaiafas Lake
area: Further Afield: Kaiafa Lake & Spa Coast
description: A pine-fringed coastal lagoon beside the historic sulfur spa. It is good for a quiet walk and photos; the thermal spa itself rates lower and is often closed.
tags: Further Afield: Kaiafa Lake & Spa Coast
details: Getting there: About 60 km south of the port (1 hr) on the Pyrgos–Kyparissia road. Half-day trip.

name: Caiaphas Beach
area: Further Afield: Kaiafa Lake & Spa Coast
description: A seemingly endless, wild sandy beach backed by dunes and pines, with a café in an old railway station. It is quiet and unorganized.
tags: Further Afield: Kaiafa Lake & Spa Coast
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Next to Kaiafa Lake, about 1 hr from the port; a short walk from parking across the old railway tracks. Half-day trip.

name: Zacharo Beach
area: Further Afield: Kaiafa Lake & Spa Coast
description: A beautiful shallow sandy beach with dunes and pine forest; organized sections offer beach bars in summer.
tags: Further Afield: Kaiafa Lake & Spa Coast
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Zacharo, about 1 hr 10 min south of the port. Half-day trip.

name: Frankish Castle of Chlemoutsi
area: Further Afield: Kaiafa Lake & Spa Coast
description: A superbly restored 13th-century Crusader castle with museum exhibits and 360° rooftop views to the Ionian islands. Allow about an hour.
tags: Further Afield: Kaiafa Lake & Spa Coast
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket about €5 at the gate
Getting there: Kastro, near Kyllini and Loutra Kyllinis spa, about 55 km north of the port (1 hr). Half-day trip.
Hours: 9:00–16:00; closed Tuesday

name: Temple of Apollo Epicurius at Bassae
area: Further Afield: Kaiafa Lake & Spa Coast
description: A UNESCO-listed 5th-century BC temple high in the Arcadian mountains, one of the best-preserved in Greece. It currently stands under a protective tent.
mapQuery: Temple of Apollo Epicurius at Bassae, Katakolon
tags: Further Afield: Kaiafa Lake & Spa Coast
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the site (about €6–10)
Getting there: About 100 km from the port via narrow, winding mountain roads (about 2 hr each way). Realistically a full day, only on a long port call or an overnight stay.
Hours: Daily 8:00–20:00 (site area to 19:30)

name: Kotor Old Town
description: A UNESCO-listed walled medieval town of marble lanes, small squares and Romanesque churches, wedged between the bay and sheer limestone cliffs. It is compact enough to explore on foot in a couple of hours, though easy to lose yourself in. Early morning and evening, after cruise passengers leave, are the most atmospheric times.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: The cruise pier sits directly in front of the Sea Gate; walk straight in.
Hours: Open public town

name: Sea Gate
description: The main 1555 entrance to the Old Town, decorated with carved reliefs and Venetian symbols, directly facing the cruise pier. Very crowded at peak cruise times. The walls are lit green at night.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Straight ahead from the cruise pier.

name: Clock Tower
description: A slightly leaning baroque-Gothic clock tower from 1602 on the Square of Arms, the first sight through the Sea Gate. It is the natural group meeting point in the Old Town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Square of Arms, just inside the Sea Gate.

name: Cathedral of Saint Tryphon
description: Kotor's Romanesque Catholic cathedral, consecrated in 1166, with twin bell towers, a silver ciborium and fresco fragments. The upstairs treasury holds relics, and its balcony looks over the square. Entry about €4.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €4)
Getting there: St Tryphon Square, center of the Old Town.
Hours: Daily 9:00–19:00 (Thu to 18:00)

name: St. Tryphon Square
description: The principal square in front of the cathedral, ringed by palaces and cafés. Lively with street musicians in the evening.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Center of the Old Town.

name: Saint Luke's Church
description: A tiny church from 1195 that once held both Catholic and Orthodox altars and survived every major earthquake. Free entry, with a modestly priced icon shop inside.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: St Luke's Square, Old Town.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:00–19:00; Sat 8:00–19:00; Sun 11:00–19:00

name: Saint Nicholas' Church
description: Kotor's main Serbian Orthodox church, completed in 1909 in pseudo-Byzantine style, with a fine iconostasis. If you are lucky, you may hear priests singing.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: St Luke's Square, Old Town.
Hours: Daily 9:00–20:00
