name: Church of St. Mary Collegiate
description: A Catholic church from 1221, built over a 6th-century basilica, with striking modern bronze doors. It houses the relics of Blessed Ozana of Kotor, and a small museum costs about €4.
mapQuery: Church of St. Mary Collegiate Kotor
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; museum about €4
Getting there: By the North Gate, Old Town.

name: Kotor Maritime Museum
description: A baroque palace museum of the Bay's seafaring past, with ship models, navigation instruments, uniforms and paintings. An audio guide is included in the €6 ticket.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €6, cards accepted)
Getting there: Square of Boka Navy, Old Town.
Hours: Mon–Sat 8:00–18:00; Sun 10:00–16:00

name: Kotor Cats Museum
description: A quirky two-room museum of cat-themed prints, postcards and coins. Entry fees and the well-priced merchandise fund care for Kotor's famous street cats.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (about €1–2)
Getting there: Square of Our Lady of Angels, Old Town.
Hours: Daily 10:00–19:00

name: Cat Park
description: A small public park full of friendly street cats looked after by a local volunteer. Children love it; a nearby shop takes donations.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Just outside the North Gate area.

name: Kotor Town Walls
description: The lower ramparts encircling the Old Town can be walked for free in about 20–25 minutes, with views over the rooftops. The upper walls climbing to the fortress are ticketed.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (lower walls free)
Getting there: Access from the North Gate or the Gurdić Gate area.

name: Kotor Fortress (San Giovanni)
description: The classic Kotor climb: about 1,350 uneven stone steps up the walls past the Church of Our Lady of Health to the fortress ruins, 260 m above town. Plan 1.5–2 hours round trip. There is no shade and no toilets, and cash-only vendors sell water along the way.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket about €15 at the gate machine or online
Getting there: Ticketed entrances inside the Old Town, near the North Gate and behind St Mary's. Go early or late to avoid heat; wear grippy shoes.
Hours: Ticketed approximately 8:00–20:00

name: Ladder of Kotor Trail
description: A free, historic zigzag mule path behind the fortress, climbing past the ruined Church of St George to a small cheese-and-drinks hut with superb bay views. The old window shortcut into the fortress has been bricked up, so this route no longer connects to San Giovanni.
mapQuery: Start of the Ladder of Kotor
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Trailhead just north of the Old Town on the road behind the walls (Špiljari side). Allow about 1.5 hours round trip to the cheese hut; loose gravel underfoot.

name: Dobrota Riva Promenade
description: A peaceful waterfront promenade along the old captains' village of Dobrota, with stone palaces, playgrounds, cafés and swimming spots. An easy walk or bike ride north of the Old Town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Starts about 1.5 km north of the Old Town along the bay road.

name: Church of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary (Prčanj)
description: A huge late-baroque church begun in 1789, with a monumental staircase rising from the shore, the tallest of its kind on the eastern Adriatic. Inside are two gilded altars, the only ones of their kind in the Bay.
mapQuery: Church of the Assumption Prčanj Kotor
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Prčanj, about 15 min by car or bus from Kotor along the bay.
Hours: Mon–Fri 12:00–18:00; Sun 10:15–11:30; closed Sat

name: Old Parish Church of the Birth of the Virgin Mary (Prčanj)
description: A ruined hillside church above Prčanj, reached on a short overgrown trail, with engraved family tombs and wide bay views. The building is in poor repair and may be closed.
mapQuery: Old parish church Birth of the Blessed Virgin Mary Prčanj
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Trail from the top of the road above Prčanj, about 20 min walk. Wear long trousers and sturdy shoes.

name: Stoliv
description: A quiet seaside village with calm swimming spots and a market. It is the start of the old stone path up to the nearly abandoned upper village of Gornji Stoliv.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About 20 min by car or bus from Kotor along the bay road toward Lepetane.

name: Church of St. Elijah (Gornji Stoliv)
description: A 1553 church crowning the old hilltop village of Gornji Stoliv, reached by a 30-minute stone path through mossy woods. Nearby are the ruins of St Anne's church and an old olive mill. The views over the inner bay are exceptional.
mapQuery: Church of St. Elijah Gornji Stoliv
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Path from Donji Stoliv; about 30 min climb.

name: Our Lady of the Rocks
description: A man-made island church off Perast, built on rocks sunk by sailors over centuries. The chapel's painted ceiling and a small museum and gallery are inside. Go early to avoid crowds.
mapQuery: Our Lady of the Rocks Perast
details:
Reservations / tickets: Island entry about €3–5; boats on the spot
Getting there: Short boat ride (about €10) from Perast waterfront; Perast is about 25 min by car from Kotor. Many bay boat tours include it.

name: Island of Saint George
description: The natural twin island to Our Lady of the Rocks, dominated by a cypress-ringed Benedictine monastery. It is usually admired from the water rather than visited.
details: Getting there: Visible from Perast; seen on bay boat tours.

name: Perast Town Museum
description: A restored baroque palace with three floors of maps, portraits, weapons and maritime artifacts explaining Perast's Venetian golden age. There is no elevator.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door
Getting there: Perast waterfront, about 25 min by car from Kotor.
Hours: Tue–Sun 8:00–20:00; closed Mon

name: St. Nicholas Bell Tower (Perast)
description: The tall bell tower beside St Nicholas church, climbed by about 150 narrow steps for the best view over Perast and the two islands. Low ceilings in places.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Pay at the entrance (about €1–2, cash only)
Getting there: Center of Perast.
Hours: Opens around 10:00

name: Kotor Serpentine Viewpoint
description: A pull-off high on the famous 25-hairpin Kotor–Lovćen road, giving the classic bird's-eye view over Kotor and the inner bay. The road is narrow, with tour buses and tight bends, so it is only for confident drivers. Go early.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: About 20 min up the P1 serpentine road from Kotor; limited roadside parking.

name: Kotor Cable Car
description: A modern cable car from the bay up to Lovćen with spectacular panoramas. At the top are a restaurant, an alpine coaster and a Falcon Fly zipline. Buy tickets and a coaster fast-pass online to skip long queues.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Buy tickets online in advance (round trip plus coaster about €90 with fast-pass)
Getting there: Lower station at Kavač, about 10 min by car or taxi from Kotor; large paid car park.

name: Lovćen National Park
description: Montenegro's 'Black Mountain' park rising above the bay, with forest trails, mountain cafés and views from the sea to the interior. It is often noticeably cooler than the coast and can hold snow into April.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Park fee paid at entry (about €3)
Getting there: About 1 hour by car from Kotor via the serpentine road and Njeguši. Park entry about €3 per person.

name: Mausoleum of Petar II Petrović Njegoš
description: The tomb of Montenegro's poet-prince on the summit of Jezerski Vrh, reached by a 461-step tunnel stairway. A circular viewing platform offers one of the Balkans' great 360° views. Bring a layer; it is cold at the top.
mapQuery: Mausoleum of Petar II Petrovic Njegos Kotor
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the base of the steps (about €8 adults, plus park fee)
Getting there: Top of the Lovćen park road; walk up from the car park. Allow about 1 hr 15 min by car from Kotor.
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:00

name: Cetinje Monastery
description: The spiritual heart of Montenegro, holding relics revered as the right hand of John the Baptist and a fragment of the Holy Cross. Monks will sometimes show the treasury if asked. Strict modest dress applies; wraps are provided.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Cetinje old royal capital, about 1 hr 15 min by car from Kotor via Njeguši; paid parking nearby.
Hours: Mon–Fri & Sun 8:00–18:30; Sat 8:00–19:00

name: Museum of King Nikola
description: The royal palace of Montenegro's last king, furnished as it was in the family's day, with weapons, portraits and royal belongings. An audio guide app is included. A combo ticket with the Njegoš Mausoleum saves money; no photos inside.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (combo tickets available)
Getting there: Dvorski Trg, central Cetinje.
Hours: Daily 9:00–17:00 (last entry about 16:00)

name: Njegoš Museum Biljarda
description: The former residence of Petar II Petrović Njegoš, named for the billiard table he hauled up the mountain. It displays his life and work, plus a large relief map of Montenegro.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €5)
Getting there: Central Cetinje, beside Cetinje Monastery.
Hours: Daily 9:00–17:00

name: Lipa Cave
description: Montenegro's first show cave: a guided one-hour walk through large chambers of stalactites, reached by a little road train from the visitor center. It is about 10°C inside, so bring a warm layer. Video recording is not allowed.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Guided tours roughly every 30 min; arrive 30 min early (tickets at the entrance)
Getting there: Lipa, near Cetinje, about 1 hr 20 min by car from Kotor on mountain roads; free parking.
Hours: Daily 10:00–16:00

name: Citadela Budva
description: The Venetian citadel at the seaward tip of Budva's walled Old Town, with a small library, ship models and a rooftop café. Views over the old town and coast are the real reward. Cash only; entry about €6–7.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (cash)
Getting there: Inside Budva Old Town, about 40 min by car from Kotor via the Vrmac tunnel.
Hours: Daily 9:00–24:00

name: Budva Ballerina
description: The 'Dancing Girl' bronze statue on rocks just outside Budva Old Town, tied to a local legend of a dancer waiting for her sailor. The short coastal walk to it offers great sea and old-town views; the gate closes in storms.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Coastal path from Budva Old Town toward Mogren Beach.

name: Sveti Stefan Viewpoint (Highway)
description: The roadside lookout on the main coastal road for the postcard shot of Sveti Stefan islet, the walled former fishing village turned luxury resort. The island itself is closed to non-guests. There is a quick-stop car park and a souvenir kiosk.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: On the E65 coast road above Sveti Stefan, about 50 min by car from Kotor. Parking is limited to about 15 minutes.

name: Sveti Stefan View Point (Čelobrdo)
description: A higher, quieter viewing deck above Sveti Stefan reached by a short, steep road. It looks down on the islet and the coast to the north, and is superb at sunset.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: About 5 min up a narrow switchback road above Sveti Stefan; small gravel car park, then a short path.

name: Sveti Stefan – Miločer Scenic Path
description: A cliffside path linking Sveti Stefan and Miločer (Queen's) beaches, with several photo points over the islet and the sea. There are stairs at both ends.
mapQuery: View Points Scenic Path Green Park Sveti Stefan
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Starts beside Sveti Stefan beach; small roadside parking for 4–5 cars.

name: Naval Heritage Collection Museum
description: A museum in a restored 19th-century sawmill at Porto Montenegro, where you can tour the Yugoslav Cold War submarine P-821 Heroj with a guide. It is hot inside the sub in summer.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door
Getting there: Porto Montenegro, Tivat, about 20 min by car from Kotor.
Hours: Tue–Sat 9:00–17:00; closed Sun–Mon

name: Blue Cave
description: A sea cave on the Luštica peninsula where sunlight turns the water electric blue, visited on speedboat tours of the Bay. Boats may no longer enter, so expect to swim in from outside. Best before the midday rush.
tags: verify: current rules on boats entering the cave
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book a speedboat tour in advance
Getting there: Boat only; tours leave from Kotor, Tivat and Herceg Novi (about 3-hour speedboat circuits).

name: Mamula Fortress
description: A round 19th-century Austro-Hungarian island fortress guarding the mouth of the Bay, and a WWII prison camp. It is now a luxury hotel, so non-guests see it from passing boats unless they book a visit with the hotel.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Island access only with a hotel reservation or arranged visit
Getting there: Bay entrance off the Luštica peninsula; seen on Blue Cave boat tours.

name: Arza Beach
description: A small, clear-water cove on the Luštica peninsula facing Mamula island, beside the ruined Arza fort. Good snorkeling, though yachts sometimes bring loud music. Parking about €5.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About 1 hour by car from Kotor via the Lepetane ferry or Tivat. The last stretch is rocky and bumpy, so low cars should go slowly.

name: Kanli Kula
description: A 16th-century Ottoman fortress, the 'Bloody Tower,' once used as a prison, above Herceg Novi. It now holds a large open-air amphitheatre for summer concerts and films, with sweeping town views. Entry about €4, discounted with a Forte Mare ticket.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €4)
Getting there: Upper Herceg Novi, about 1 hour by car from Kotor or via the Kamenari–Lepetane ferry.
Hours: Daily 9:00–20:00

name: Savina Monastery
description: A peaceful Orthodox monastery complex in green hills above Herceg Novi, with richly decorated churches, a tiered cemetery and bay views. The main church has been under restoration.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Savina, east side of Herceg Novi, about 1 hour by car from Kotor.
Hours: Mon–Sat 8:00–20:00; Sun 8:00–12:00

name: Ostrog Monastery
description: Montenegro's most important pilgrimage site, a white monastery built into a vertical cliff with the relics of St Basil of Ostrog. The approach road is narrow and steep, and lines can last an hour on feast days (around May 12). Strict modest dress applies.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Near Danilovgrad, about 2 to 2.5 hours by car from Kotor each way, a full-day commitment on a port call. A shuttle runs from the lower monastery.

name: Royal Palace of Naples
description: The Bourbon kings' palace on Piazza del Plebiscito, with a grand staircase, gilded royal apartments, a court theater and a hanging garden with views of Vesuvius. Well labeled in English, with a free audio guide; allow about 1.5 hours.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €15; terrace/garden add-on about €2) or online
Getting there: Piazza del Plebiscito 1 — about a 15-min walk from the cruise terminal (Molo Angioino).
Hours: 9:00–20:00; closed Wednesday

name: Teatro di San Carlo
description: Europe's oldest continuously active opera house (1737), with a breathtaking red-and-gold horseshoe auditorium. Take a daytime guided tour or catch an evening opera or ballet.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Guided tours bookable on teatrosancarlo.it or at the box office; performance tickets online
Getting there: Via San Carlo 98, beside the Royal Palace — 12-min walk from the port.
Hours: Tours daily 10:00–18:00 (subject to rehearsals); performances in the evening

name: Galleria Umberto I
description: A soaring 1890s iron-and-glass shopping arcade with a dramatic dome and marble mosaic floors. Free to wander, with cafés and a few shops; best for architecture and photos.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Via San Carlo / Via Toledo, opposite Teatro San Carlo — 10-min walk from the port.
Hours: Open public passage

name: Castel Nuovo (Maschio Angioino)
description: A massive 13th-century Angevin castle with a white Renaissance triumphal arch, the Palatine Chapel, Roman remains under a glass floor and a civic art museum. Parts are sometimes closed for events or works.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (small fee)
Getting there: Piazza Municipio — 5-min walk from the cruise terminal.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:00–17:30; closed Sunday

name: Piazza del Plebiscito
description: Naples' grand ceremonial square, framed by the Royal Palace and the Pantheon-like church of San Francesco di Paola. Open, free and the natural starting point for exploring the Spanish Quarter and Via Toledo.
details:
Getting there: 15-min walk from the port.
Hours: Open public square

name: Naples Underground (Quartieri Spagnoli)
description: A guided tour through Greco-Roman aqueducts and cisterns later used as WWII air-raid shelters, run by the volunteers who cleared them. Highly rated guides add a little light adventure; not ideal for claustrophobia.
mapQuery: Naples Underground Vico Sant'Anna di Palazzo
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead online; timed guided tours in English
Getting there: Vico Sant'Anna di Palazzo 52, Spanish Quarter — 15-min walk from the port.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:30–16:30, Sat–Sun 9:30–18:00 (last tours)

name: Murale Diego Armando Maradona
description: The famous shrine-like mural of Maradona deep in the Spanish Quarter, surrounded by flags, tributes and memorabilia stalls. Crowded and chaotic, but a vivid slice of Neapolitan passion.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Via Emanuele De Deo 46 — uphill from Via Toledo, about 20-min walk from the port.
Hours: Open street location

name: Gallerie d'Italia Napoli
description: Intesa Sanpaolo's museum in a restored bank palazzo on Via Toledo, spanning Greek vases, Caravaggio's last painting (The Martyrdom of Saint Ursula) and strong temporary shows. Good café on the ground floor.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €8; free under 26)
Getting there: Via Toledo 177 — 12-min walk from the port.
Hours: Tue–Fri 10:00–19:00, Sat–Sun 10:00–20:00; closed Monday

name: Sansevero Chapel Museum
description: A small Baroque chapel holding Sammartino's Veiled Christ, a marble sculpture so fine it looks like translucent fabric, plus the eerie 'anatomical machines' in the crypt. Many visitors call it the single best thing in Naples. No photos allowed.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book timed tickets online well in advance — it sells out
Getting there: Via Francesco de Sanctis 19/21, off Spaccanapoli — 20-min walk from the port.
Hours: 9:00–19:00; closed Tuesday

name: Naples Cathedral (Duomo)
description: The 13th-century cathedral of San Gennaro, layered with Gothic, Baroque and neo-Gothic work. Free to enter, it houses the saint's relics and connects to the treasure chapel and an early-Christian baptistery.
mapQuery: Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta Naples Duomo
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free entry; dress modestly
Getting there: Via Duomo 147 — 25-min walk or short taxi ride from the port.
Hours: Daily 8:30–19:30

name: Royal Chapel of the Treasure of San Gennaro
description: A dazzling Baroque chapel inside the Duomo, rich with silver busts, marble and frescoes, which keeps the vials of San Gennaro's blood that liquefies three times a year.
mapQuery: Royal Chapel of the Treasure of San Gennaro Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Inside Naples Cathedral, Via Duomo.
Hours: Daily ~8:30–13:00 & 14:30–18:30 (Sun afternoon from 16:00)

name: Museum of the Treasure of San Gennaro
description: A collection of jewels, silver and gifts from popes and kings to Naples' patron saint, including the famous mitre set with thousands of gems. An audio guide is included.
mapQuery: Museum of the Treasure of San Gennaro Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the museum (about €12)
Getting there: Via Duomo 149, next to the cathedral.
Hours: Daily 9:30–18:00

name: Baptistery of San Giovanni in Fonte
description: The oldest baptistery in the Western world (4th century), entered through the Duomo, with remarkable early-Christian mosaics in its dome.
mapQuery: Battistero di San Giovanni in Fonte Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Small fee at the cathedral
Getting there: Inside Naples Cathedral.

name: Complesso Monumentale San Lorenzo Maggiore
description: A Gothic Franciscan church and museum built over the excavated Greco-Roman market of ancient Neapolis, with streets, shops and a treasury you walk through underground. Take the guided tour.
mapQuery: Complesso Monumentale San Lorenzo Maggiore Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €9; guided tour about €2 extra)
Getting there: Piazza San Gaetano 316, Via dei Tribunali.
Hours: Daily 9:30–17:30

name: Napoli Sotterranea (Underground Naples)
description: The classic guided tour 40 m below the old city: Greek quarries, Roman cisterns, WWII shelters and a narrow candle-lit passage, plus a hidden Roman theater above ground. Physical, with many steps.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the entrance (about €15, cash) or online; tours in English run regularly
Getting there: Piazza San Gaetano 68, Via dei Tribunali.
Hours: Mon–Fri 10:00–18:00, Sat–Sun 9:30–18:00

name: Via San Gregorio Armeno
description: The famous 'Christmas Alley', lined year-round with artisan workshops carving nativity scenes and figurines, including footballers, politicians and celebrities.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Off Via dei Tribunali, between Spaccanapoli and San Lorenzo.
Hours: Shops roughly 10:00–19:00

name: Spaccanapoli
description: The arrow-straight ancient street that 'splits Naples' through the UNESCO historic center, packed with churches, pastry shops, pizzerias and street life. Watch for scooters.
details:
Getting there: Runs from Piazza del Gesù Nuovo to Via Duomo — 20-min walk from the port.
Hours: Open street

name: Church of the Gesù Nuovo
description: Behind a severe diamond-studded stone facade lies one of Naples' most opulent Baroque interiors, with frescoes, marble and gold, plus the shrine of St. Giuseppe Moscati. Free.
mapQuery: Church of the Gesù Nuovo Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free; dress modestly
Getting there: Piazza del Gesù Nuovo 2.
Hours: Daily 8:00–12:45, 16:00–19:00

name: Complesso Monumentale di Santa Chiara
description: A 14th-century monastery whose cloister is covered with hand-painted majolica-tile benches and columns among citrus trees, with a museum and Roman bath ruins. A serene escape from the old city's chaos.
mapQuery: Complesso Monumentale di Santa Chiara Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the entrance (about €7) for the cloister and museum
Getting there: Via Santa Chiara 49/c, opposite Gesù Nuovo.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:30–17:00, Sun 10:00–14:00

name: Basilica of Santa Chiara
description: The vast, austere Gothic church of the Poor Clares, rebuilt after WWII bombing, holding Angevin royal tombs. Free entry, separate from the cloister ticket.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Piazza del Gesù Nuovo 18.
Hours: Daily ~8:00–12:45, 16:30–20:00

name: National Archaeological Museum of Naples (MANN)
description: One of the world's great antiquities museums: Pompeii and Herculaneum frescoes and mosaics (including the Alexander Mosaic), the Farnese marbles and the Secret Cabinet. Ideal before or after Pompeii; allow 2–4 hours.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door or online (about €20)
Getting there: Piazza Museo 19 — Museo (Line 1) metro; 15 min from the port by metro.
Hours: 9:00–18:30; closed Tuesday

name: Pio Monte della Misericordia
description: A historic charity's chapel and picture gallery, home to Caravaggio's Seven Works of Mercy in the setting it was painted for. Calm and rarely crowded.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €10)
Getting there: Via dei Tribunali 253, near the Duomo.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–18:00, Sun 9:00–14:30

name: Catacombs of San Gennaro
description: Vast, two-level early-Christian catacombs with frescoes and the saint's original tomb, guided by young people from the Sanità neighborhood. The ticket includes the San Gaudioso catacombs.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book timed guided tours online at catacombedinapoli.it
Getting there: Via Capodimonte 13, beside the Basilica of Madre del Buon Consiglio — taxi or bus 168/178 from the center (15 min).
Hours: 9:30–17:00 (last tour); closed Wednesday

name: Catacombs of San Gaudioso
description: Beneath the Basilica of Santa Maria della Sanità, these catacombs reveal unusual 17th-century burial customs, with skulls set into frescoed walls. Included with the San Gennaro ticket.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Combined ticket online
Getting there: Via Sanità 123, Rione Sanità — 10-min walk from the San Gennaro catacombs.
Hours: 9:30–17:00; closed Wednesday

name: Cimitero delle Fontanelle
description: A vast tuff-rock ossuary holding thousands of skulls once 'adopted' by locals in a remarkable popular cult. Visits are now guided and capped in numbers.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book free/low-cost timed slots on the official website; download the audio app
Getting there: Via Fontanelle 80, upper Sanità — taxi recommended.
Hours: 10:00–17:15; closed Wednesday

name: Capodimonte Museum and Royal Park
description: A Bourbon hilltop palace holding a world-class collection with Caravaggio, Titian, Raphael, Botticelli and Masaccio, set in a huge historic park with city views. Uncrowded.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door or online; park entry is free
Getting there: Via Lucio Amelio 2 / Via Miano — 20 min by taxi or Shuttle Capodimonte from Piazza Trieste e Trento. Plan a half-day with the catacombs.
Hours: Museum 8:30–19:30, closed Wednesday; park opens ~7:00 and closes around dusk

name: Porta Nolana Fish Market
description: A loud, authentic morning street market of fresh seafood, live shellfish and produce under the 15th-century Porta Nolana gate. Try a 2-euro oyster on the spot.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Via Cesare Carmignano, near Napoli Centrale and Circumvesuviana Porta Nolana.
Hours: Tue–Sat 8:00–14:00, Sun 9:00–13:00; closed Monday

name: Castel dell'Ovo
description: Naples' oldest castle, sitting on a tiny island linked to the waterfront at Borgo Marinari, with fishing boats and restaurants around it. Recent visitors report the interior closed for renovation; the exterior and harbor walk remain lovely, especially at night.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free when open
Getting there: Via Eldorado 3, Santa Lucia waterfront — 20-min walk along the seafront from the port.

name: Lungomare Caracciolo
description: Naples' pedestrian seafront promenade running from Castel dell'Ovo to Mergellina, with Vesuvius across the bay. Best at sunset or in the evening passeggiata.
details:
Getting there: Via Francesco Caracciolo, Chiaia — starts 20-min walk from the port.
Hours: Open public promenade

name: Castel Sant'Elmo
description: A star-shaped fortress atop the Vomero hill with the best 360° panorama of Naples, the bay, Capri and Vesuvius from its ramparts. Inexpensive.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €5)
Getting there: Via Tito Angelini 20/A — take the Funicolare Centrale (from Augusteo) or Montesanto funicular, then a 10-min walk.
Hours: Daily 8:30–18:30

name: Certosa e Museo di San Martino
description: A sumptuous Carthusian monastery below Castel Sant'Elmo, with a marble-inlaid Baroque church, serene cloisters, the spectacular Cuciniello nativity scene and terraces over the bay.
mapQuery: Certosa e Museo di San Martino Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €6)
Getting there: Largo San Martino 5, Vomero — Montesanto funicular to Morghen, 5-min walk.
Hours: 8:30–17:30; closed Tuesday

name: Museo Pignatelli
description: A neoclassical aristocratic villa on Riviera di Chiaia with period salons, porcelain, a carriage museum and a garden. Quiet, and sometimes paired with art exhibitions.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door
Getting there: Riviera di Chiaia 200.
Hours: 9:30–16:00; closed Tuesday

name: Naples Aquarium (Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn)
description: One of Europe's oldest aquariums (1874), inside the Villa Comunale gardens. Small but charming, with Bay of Naples marine life; best for kids.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €10)
Getting there: Villa Comunale, Chiaia seafront.
Hours: Tue–Sun 9:00–17:00; closed Monday

name: Parco Virgiliano
description: A clifftop park at the tip of Posillipo with sweeping views over Nisida, Capri, the Phlegraean Fields and Vesuvius. Simple but scenic.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Viale Virgilio, Posillipo — bus 140 then a 20-min walk, or taxi (25 min from the port).
Hours: Daily 7:00–20:00 (gates locked outside these hours)

name: Mercato della Pignasecca
description: Naples' oldest street market, a lively tangle of fish, produce, fried street food and household stalls around Piazza Pignasecca. Busiest in the morning.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Piazza Pignasecca, off Via Toledo near Montesanto.
Hours: Mornings to early afternoon

name: Archaeological Park of Pompeii
description: The vast Roman city buried by Vesuvius in AD 79, with houses, frescoes, the Forum, theaters, baths and plaster casts of victims. Plan at least 3–5 hours, wear good shoes, and bring water and a hat, since shade is scarce.
tags: verify: seasonal closing and last entry on date
details:
Reservations / tickets: Buy nominative timed tickets in advance on the official Pompeii site; daily visitor caps apply
Getting there: About 25 km from the port. Circumvesuviana from Porta Nolana or Garibaldi to Pompei Scavi (~40 min), or private transfer. A half-day minimum.
Hours: 9:00–19:00 in high season (shorter from November; last entry earlier)

name: Basilica of Pompeii (Roman)
description: One of the oldest surviving Roman basilicas (2nd century BC), the city's law court and business hub beside the Forum. Its colonnade gives a real sense of scale.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Pompeii ticket
Getting there: Inside the Pompeii archaeological park, near the Porta Marina entrance.
Hours: Follows park hours

name: Archaeological Park of Herculaneum
description: A smaller, astonishingly preserved Roman town with two-story houses, wooden beams, colorful frescoes and mosaics, and the boathouses where victims' skeletons were found. Easier to see in 2–3 hours than Pompeii.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site or online
Getting there: Corso Resina 187, Ercolano — Circumvesuviana to Ercolano Scavi (~20 min), then a 10-min walk downhill. A half-day.
Hours: Daily 8:30–19:30 in season (shorter in winter)

name: Vesuvius National Park – Gran Cono Crater Path
description: A steep 30–45-minute gravel walk to the rim of the volcano that destroyed Pompeii, with guided commentary at the crater and huge bay views. Wear sturdy shoes and bring layers.
tags: verify: last entry for travel month
details:
Reservations / tickets: Timed online ticket required in advance (no sales at the gate); book via the official Vesuvius site; pre-book parking if driving
Getting there: Shuttle buses from Ercolano or Pompeii (EAV/Busvia del Vesuvio) or car to the Quota 1000 parking, then shuttle or walk 2.5 km to the gate. A half-day.
Hours: Opens 9:00; last entry varies by month (about 15:00–18:00); closes in bad weather or high winds

name: Villa Poppaea (Oplontis)
description: A palatial seaside villa believed to belong to Nero's wife Poppaea, with some of the finest frescoes in the Vesuvian area. It is almost crowd-free and takes about 30–45 minutes.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Pompeii Plus/Greater Pompeii ticket or sold on site
Getting there: Via Sepolcri, Torre Annunziata — Circumvesuviana to Torre Annunziata, 5-min walk; or the Pompeii Artebus shuttle. A half-day with Pompeii.
Hours: 9:00–18:00; closed Tuesday

name: Villa San Marco (Stabiae)
description: A luxurious Roman villa on the Castellammare ridge with a pool courtyard, mosaics and frescoes, and Vesuvius views. Quiet, and free with the Greater Pompeii ticket.
mapQuery: Scavi di Stabia Villa San Marco
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free or included in Greater Pompeii ticket
Getting there: Passeggiata Archeologica, Castellammare di Stabia — bus or taxi from Castellammare station. A half-day.
Hours: 9:00–18:00; closed Tuesday

name: Villa Arianna (Stabiae)
description: A sister villa to San Marco with frescoes and mosaics, bath rooms, and big views over the bay. Often near-empty.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free entry
Getting there: Strada Varano 1, Castellammare di Stabia. A half-day.
Hours: 9:00–18:00; closed Tuesday

name: Pontifical Shrine of Our Lady of the Rosary of Pompei
description: The grand modern basilica in Pompei town, a major pilgrimage site with a gilded interior, mosaics and a bell tower lift. Pair it with the ruins.
mapQuery: Santuario Beata Vergine del Santo Rosario di Pompei
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free; dress modestly
Getting there: Piazza Bartolo Longo, Pompei — 10-min walk from the excavations' amphitheater gate; cheap parking on site.
Hours: Mon–Fri 6:30–14:00 & 15:00–20:00; Sat 6:30–20:00; Sun 5:30–21:00

name: Villa Rufolo
description: A 13th-century villa in Ravello with tiered flower gardens and towers that inspired Wagner, plus one of the Amalfi Coast's most famous views. It hosts the Ravello Festival concerts in summer.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €8)
Getting there: Piazza Duomo, Ravello — about 2 hr from Naples by road, or ferry to Amalfi then bus. A full half-day+.
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:30

name: Villa Cimbrone – Terrace of Infinity
description: The romantic gardens of Villa Cimbrone end at the Terrace of Infinity, a balcony of marble busts suspended over the sea. Many visitors call it Ravello's highlight.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €7–10)
Getting there: Via Santa Chiara 26 — 10–15-min walk from Ravello's square. A half-day+.
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:30 (to sunset seasonally)

name: Amalfi Cathedral (Duomo di Sant'Andrea)
description: Amalfi's striped Arab-Norman cathedral at the top of a grand staircase, with the Cloister of Paradise, a museum and the crypt holding St. Andrew's relics.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Small fee for the cloister/museum/crypt route; cathedral free during worship
Getting there: Piazza Duomo, Amalfi — ferry from Naples seasonal (~1h45–2h) or road. A half-day+.
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:30

name: Church of Santa Maria Assunta, Positano
description: The majolica-domed church that anchors every Positano photo, steps from the beach, with a Byzantine icon of the Black Madonna inside.
mapQuery: Chiesa di Santa Maria Assunta Positano
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Piazza Flavio Gioia, Positano. A half-day+.
Hours: Daily 9:30–12:30, 16:00–20:00

name: Path of the Gods (Sentiero degli Dei)
description: The Amalfi Coast's legendary clifftop hike from Bomerano (Agerola) to Nocelle above Positano, about 7–8 km and 2.5–3.5 hours, mostly downhill. The optional 1,700 steps down to Positano are hard on knees.
mapQuery: Path of the Gods Agerola Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free; no permit needed
Getting there: Trailhead at Piazza Paolo Capasso, Bomerano (Agerola) — SITA bus from Amalfi. Finish in Nocelle and take the local bus (cash) to Positano. Realistically a full day.
Hours: Open trail — start by midmorning and avoid midday heat

name: Bagni della Regina Giovanna
description: Roman villa ruins around a natural rock pool with turquoise water on the Capo di Sorrento headland, popular for swimming and cliff jumping. Rocky — wear water shoes.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Traversa Punta Capo, Sorrento — EAV bus toward Massa Lubrense to the Capo stop, then a steep 10–15-min path down. A half-day.
Hours: Open site; arrive early in summer as it fills

name: Villa Comunale di Sorrento
description: Sorrento's clifftop public garden and terrace with a sweeping view of the bay and Vesuvius, the town's classic sunset spot. A lift (about €1.50) drops to the marina.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Via San Francesco, Sorrento — 3-min walk from Piazza Tasso; ferry from Naples ~45 min. A half-day.
Hours: Daily 7:30–22:30

name: Vallone dei Mulini
description: A deep, fern-choked gorge in the center of Sorrento with the ruins of an abandoned medieval mill. Viewed from the railing only, as it is private.
details:
Getting there: Via Fuorimura 1, beside Piazza Tasso.
Hours: Street viewpoint

name: Fiordo di Furore
description: A dramatic narrow inlet under a high road bridge, with a tiny pebble beach and old fishermen's houses. Parking is almost nonexistent, and the beach is sometimes closed for rockfall risk.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Via Marina di Praia, Furore — SITA bus stop 'Fiordo di Furore' between Positano and Amalfi; stairs down from the bridge. A half-day+.

name: Grotta dello Smeraldo
description: A sea cave near Conca dei Marini where light filtering underwater turns the water emerald green, visited on short rowboat tours.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Pay at the entrance (about €10)
Getting there: Via Smeraldo 33, Conca dei Marini — elevator down from the coast road, or by boat from Amalfi. A half-day+.
Hours: Daily 10:00–16:30 (weather permitting)

name: Gardens of Augustus, Capri
description: Small terraced gardens with the island's most famous views over the Faraglioni rocks and the zigzag Via Krupp. Allow about 30 minutes.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Small fee via ticket machine/QR at the entrance
Getting there: Via Matteotti 2, Capri town — 10-min walk from the Piazzetta; ferry/hydrofoil from Naples ~50 min. A half-day+.
Hours: Daily 9:00–20:00 in summer (shorter in winter)

name: Belvedere di Tragara
description: Capri's classic viewpoint facing the Faraglioni stacks, at the end of a lovely villa-lined walk from town. Continue on the Pizzolungo path for more.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: End of Via Tragara — 20–30-min walk from the Piazzetta. A half-day+.
Hours: Open viewpoint

name: Pizzolungo Path
description: A spectacular coastal walk on Capri's quiet east side from the Arco Naturale past the Grotta di Matermania to the Tragara belvedere. It involves several hundred steps.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Via del Pizzolungo, Capri — allow 1–1.5 hours as a loop from the Piazzetta. A half-day+.
Hours: Open trail — daylight only

name: Villa San Michele, Anacapri
description: Swedish doctor Axel Munthe's villa and award-winning gardens filled with antiquities, with the famous sphinx gazing over the Bay of Naples.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €12)
Getting there: Via Axel Munthe 34, Anacapri — bus or taxi from Capri's Marina Grande. A half-day+.
Hours: Daily 9:00–17:00 (varies seasonally)

name: Monte Solaro Chairlift
description: A 13-minute single-seat chairlift from Anacapri to the island's highest point (589 m) for breathtaking views of Capri, the Faraglioni and the coast. Go early to beat queues.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the base station (about €14 return)
Getting there: Via Caposcuro 10, Anacapri. A half-day+.
Hours: Daily 9:30–17:30 (weather permitting; shorter in winter)

name: Aragonese Castle, Ischia
description: A medieval citadel on a rock islet linked to Ischia Ponte, with convents, churches, gardens and terraces with superb views. Allow 1.5–2 hours; an elevator is available.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the entrance (about €15)
Getting there: Ischia Ponte — ferry/hydrofoil from Naples to Ischia Porto (~1 hr), then bus or taxi. A full day.
Hours: Daily 9:00–17:30 (later in summer)

name: Marina di Corricella, Procida
description: Procida's pastel fishing harbor, the setting of Il Postino, with stacked colorful houses, boats and waterfront trattorias. A quiet, authentic island escape.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Via Marina di Corricella — ferry from Naples to Procida (~40–60 min), then 15-min walk. A half-day+.
Hours: Open harbor

name: Royal Palace of Caserta
description: The colossal UNESCO Bourbon palace often called Italy's Versailles, with 1,200 rooms, a grand staircase and a 3-km cascade-filled park. Allow most of a day; shuttles and bikes run through the gardens.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate or online at reggiadicaserta.cultura.gov.it
Getting there: Piazza Carlo di Borbone, Caserta — regional train from Napoli Centrale (~40–60 min); palace opposite the station. A full day.
Hours: 8:30–19:30; closed Tuesday (park closes earlier in winter)

name: Flavian Amphitheatre, Pozzuoli
description: Italy's third-largest Roman amphitheater, with exceptionally well-preserved underground passages and animal cages you can walk through. Inexpensive and uncrowded.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €5) or Phlegraean Fields pass
Getting there: Corso Nicola Terracciano 75, Pozzuoli — Metro Line 2 or Cumana to Pozzuoli (~30 min). A half-day.
Hours: 9:00–16:40; closed Tuesday

name: Underwater Archaeological Park of Baia
description: A sunken Roman resort town of villas, mosaic floors and statues, now a marine protected area visited by glass-bottom boat, snorkeling or diving. Seasonal and weather-dependent.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book boat, snorkel or dive tours with authorized operators in advance
Getting there: Via Lucullo 94, Bacoli — Cumana train to Baia/Lucrino, then a short walk. A half-day.
Hours: Daily 9:00–19:00 (tours weather-dependent)

name: Archaeological Park of Paestum
description: Three magnificent Greek Doric temples from the 6th–5th century BC, among the best preserved anywhere, plus a museum of painted tombs including the Tomb of the Diver.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate or online
Getting there: Via Magna Graecia 919, Capaccio Paestum — direct train from Napoli Centrale (~1h20–1h40) to Paestum station, then 10-min walk. A full day.
Hours: Daily 8:30–19:30

name: Forte Michelangelo
description: The massive 16th-century papal fortress guarding Civitavecchia's harbor, begun under Pope Julius II with Michelangelo credited for the upper tower. Today it houses port offices, so you admire it from outside — the waterfront walk around its bastions is the best free sight in town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Exterior only
Getting there: At the harbor entrance, ~10 min walk from the cruise shuttle drop-off at Largo della Pace.

name: Cattedrale di San Francesco d'Assisi
description: Civitavecchia's Baroque cathedral, with ornate altars and a statue of St John Bosco outside. A calm, easy stop within walking distance of the port shuttle.
mapQuery: Cattedrale di San Francesco d'Assisi Civitavecchia Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Piazza Vittorio Emanuele, ~10 min walk from the port gate.

name: Promenade Civitavecchia
description: The palm-lined seafront promenade along Viale Garibaldi with Mediterranean gardens, small rocky beaches and sea views. A pleasant, low-effort stroll for travelers staying near the ship.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Viale Garibaldi, 5–15 min walk south of the port.
Hours: Open promenade

name: la macchina del Tempo
description: A small immersive virtual-reality experience recreating pre-war Civitavecchia, about 90% of which was destroyed in WWII bombing. Visitors don VR visors to meet 19th-century characters and walk lost streets. About an hour.
mapQuery: la macchina del Tempo Civitavecchia Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead — +39 347 270 9089
Getting there: Via Piave 1, near the port.

name: Museo del Mare
description: A small maritime museum by the port with naval history and local archaeology.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Calata Principe Tommaso 20, by the old harbor.
Hours: Daily 9:00–13:00

name: The Taurine Baths
description: Extensive ruins of Roman thermal baths outside Civitavecchia, some of the best preserved in Lazio, often almost empty. Not walkable — the road lacks sidewalks.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site (about €5; guided ~€8)
Getting there: ~5 km inland; taxi or the hop-on bus. Line B buses are infrequent.

name: Monumento Naturale La Frasca
description: A wild coastal nature reserve north of town with a pine forest trail along a rocky shoreline. No facilities.
mapQuery: Monumento Naturale La Frasca Civitavecchia Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: ~8 km north of the port by car; park before the pedestrian section.

name: Necropolis of Tarquinia
description: The UNESCO Monterozzi necropolis with painted Etruscan tombs (7th–2nd century BC), viewed through glass. The closest world-class site to the port.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site; combined ticket with the museum
Getting there: Tarquinia is ~20 min north by train or car; the necropolis is ~1.5 km from the old town.
Hours: 9:00–19:30; closed Monday

name: National Archaeological Museum of Tarquinia
description: Housed in the 15th-century Palazzo Vitelleschi, home to the famous terracotta Winged Horses. Labels mostly Italian.
mapQuery: National Archaeological Museum of Tarquinia Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site
Getting there: Piazza Cavour, Tarquinia old town.
Hours: 9:00–19:30; closed Monday

name: Necropolis Banditaccia
description: The UNESCO Etruscan city of the dead at Cerveteri, with mound tombs you can walk into.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site
Getting there: Cerveteri, ~40 min drive from Civitavecchia.
Hours: 9:00–19:30; closed Monday

name: Santa Severa Castle
description: A seaside medieval castle with a 9th-century tower on the site of the Etruscan port of Pyrgi. Much of the courtyard is free; museums about €8.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Museum tickets on site
Getting there: SS1 km 52, ~25 min drive south of Civitavecchia.
Hours: Tue–Fri 9:00–18:00; Sat–Sun 10:00–19:00; closed Monday

name: Castello Odescalchi di Santa Marinella
description: A seafront castle above Santa Marinella's marina, used as an event venue. Admire from outside.
mapQuery: Castello Odescalchi di Santa Marinella Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Exterior only
Getting there: Viale Roma 11, Santa Marinella — ~15 min by train.

name: Orsini-Odescalchi Castle
description: A 15th-century castle above Lake Bracciano with frescoed halls, armor and sweeping views.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site (about €10)
Getting there: Bracciano, ~45 min drive.
Hours: Mon–Fri 10:00–18:00; Sat–Sun 10:00–19:00

name: Ostia Antica
description: Ancient Rome's port city with streets, theater, baths, apartments and mosaics, far less crowded than Pompeii.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site or online
Getting there: ~1h drive from Civitavecchia; from Rome take Roma–Lido train from Piramide (~25 min).
Hours: 8:30–15:30; closed Monday

name: Villa d'Este
description: Tivoli's UNESCO Renaissance villa with hundreds of fountains and terraced gardens.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site or online
Getting there: Tivoli — train from Tiburtina (~1h). From Civitavecchia ~1h45; full-day.
Hours: Mon 14:00–17:30; Tue–Sun 8:30–17:30

name: Villa Adriana
description: Hadrian's vast villa complex outside Tivoli — UNESCO; allow half a day.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site or online
Getting there: ~5 km below Tivoli; taxi or bus.
Hours: Daily 8:15–15:45

name: Villa Gregoriana
description: A FAI-run gorge park in Tivoli with waterfalls, caves and Roman temples. Many stairs.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets online (FAI) or on site
Getting there: Largo Sant'Angelo, Tivoli.
Hours: Daily 9:30–17:30

name: Aniene Falls in Villa Gregoriana
description: A viewpoint on the Great Waterfall across the valley. The road has no sidewalk — view from inside Villa Gregoriana instead.
mapQuery: Aniene Falls Villa Gregoriana Tivoli Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: SP31a, Tivoli — not pedestrian-safe.

name: Parco Regionale dell'Appia Antica
description: The ancient Appian Way, lined with tombs and ruins; best by rented bike or golf-cart tour. Few facilities.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Bus 118 from Circo Massimo; bikes near the visitor center.
Hours: Open road

name: Catacombe di San Callisto
description: Rome's best-known Christian catacombs, visited on 45-minute guided tours. No photos.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book timed tour online (about €10)
Getting there: Via Appia Antica 110 — bus 118.
Hours: 9:30–12:00 & 14:00–16:30; closed Wednesday

name: Catacombs of Saint Sebastian
description: Guided catacomb tours beneath the Basilica of San Sebastiano.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site
Getting there: Via Appia Antica 136 — bus 118.
Hours: 9:15–17:15; closed Monday

name: Basilica of St Sebastian Outside the Walls
description: One of Rome's seven pilgrimage churches, with a Bernini bust of Christ.
mapQuery: Basilica of St Sebastian Outside the Walls Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Via Appia Antica 136.
Hours: Daily 8:30–18:00

name: Mausoleum of Cecilia Metella
description: A monumental 1st-century BC tomb on the Appian Way with a VR experience.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site
Getting there: Via Appia Antica 161.
Hours: 9:00–18:00; closed Monday

name: Circus of Maxentius
description: Ruins of a 4th-century chariot-racing circus and mausoleum. Free entry.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Via Appia Antica 153.
Hours: Tue–Fri 10:00–16:00; Sat–Sun 10:00–19:00; closed Monday

name: The Park of the Aqueducts
description: A park of towering Roman aqueduct arches — magical at sunset.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Metro A to Giulio Agricola or Subaugusta.
Hours: Open park

name: Palazzo dei Papi di Viterbo
description: The medieval Papal Palace, site of the first conclave. Ticket includes cathedral and audio guide.
mapQuery: Palazzo dei Papi di Viterbo Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site (about €10)
Getting there: Viterbo, ~1h by car or train.
Hours: 10:00–19:00 (Thu to 18:00)

name: Colosseum

details:
Reservations / tickets: Timed tickets required — book on the official Colosseum site well ahead
Getting there: From Civitavecchia: train to Roma Termini (~1h20), then Metro B to Colosseo. A Rome day from the port is a full day.
Hours: Daily from 8:30; closing varies by season

name: Roman Forum
description: The political and religious heart of ancient Rome. Uneven paving; bring water.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Colosseum combined ticket
Getting there: Entrance on Via della Salara Vecchia or via the Colosseum side.
Hours: Daily from 9:00; closing varies by season

name: Palatine Hill
description: Legendary birthplace of Rome and site of imperial palaces, with gardens and views over the Forum.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Colosseum combined ticket
Getting there: Via di San Gregorio 30.
Hours: Daily from 9:00

name: Arch of Constantine
description: The largest surviving Roman triumphal arch (AD 315), beside the Colosseum. Free to view.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Piazza del Colosseo.
Hours: Open site

name: Domus Aurea
description: Nero's buried Golden House, visited on guided tours with VR reconstructions.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book guided tour in advance
Getting there: Viale della Domus Aurea.
Hours: Fri–Sun 9:30–17:00

name: Circus Maximus
description: The grassy outline of ancient Rome's great chariot stadium. No shade.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free park
Getting there: Metro B Circo Massimo.

name: Baths of Caracalla
description: Colossal 3rd-century bath complex with mosaics, uncrowded.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site or online
Getting there: Viale delle Terme di Caracalla.
Hours: 9:00–18:00; closed Monday

name: Mouth of Truth
description: The marble mask made famous by Roman Holiday, in the portico of Santa Maria in Cosmedin.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Piazza della Bocca della Verità.
Hours: Daily 9:30–17:50

name: Capitoline Museums
description: The world's oldest public museum, with the Capitoline Wolf and original Marcus Aurelius.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site or online
Getting there: Piazza del Campidoglio.
Hours: Daily 9:30–19:30

name: Piazza del Campidoglio
description: Michelangelo's square atop the Capitoline. Walk behind the town hall for a Forum overlook.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Up the Cordonata ramp from Piazza Venezia.
Hours: Open square

name: Monument to Victor Emmanuel II
description: The white marble Altare della Patria. A glass elevator to the top terrace gives a 360° panorama.
mapQuery: Monument to Victor Emmanuel II Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free monument; elevator ticketed
Getting there: Piazza Venezia.
Hours: Daily 9:30–19:30

name: Mercati di Traiano Museo dei Fori Imperiali
description: Trajan's Markets, often called the world's first shopping mall.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site
Getting there: Via Quattro Novembre 94.
Hours: Daily 9:30–19:30

name: Theatre of Marcellus
description: An Augustan theater (13 BC) with apartments on top. Free to view.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Via del Teatro di Marcello.
Hours: Daily 9:00–19:00

name: Basilica of San Clemente
description: Three layers: 12th-century basilica over a 4th-century church over a Mithraic temple.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Timed tickets for the excavations
Getting there: Piazza di San Clemente.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:00–12:30 & 14:00–18:00; Sun 12:00–18:00

name: Basilica of San Pietro in Vincoli.
description: Home to Michelangelo's Moses and the chains of St Peter. Free.
mapQuery: Basilica of San Pietro in Vincoli Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Piazza di San Pietro in Vincoli.
Hours: Mon–Sat 7:30–12:20 & 15:00–18:50; Sun 9:00–12:00 & 15:00–18:50

name: Papal Basilica of Saint Mary Major
description: One of four papal basilicas, with 5th-century mosaics and a gilded ceiling. Dress code.
mapQuery: Papal Basilica of Saint Mary Major Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Piazza di Santa Maria Maggiore.
Hours: Daily 7:00–18:30

name: Basilica of San Giovanni in Laterano
description: The Pope's cathedral, ranked above St Peter's.
mapQuery: Basilica of San Giovanni in Laterano Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Metro A San Giovanni.
Hours: Daily 7:00–18:30

name: Pontificio Santuario della Scala Santa
description: 28 steps believed to be from Pilate's palace, climbed on the knees. No photos.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Opposite San Giovanni in Laterano.
Hours: 6:00–13:30 & 15:00–18:00 (Sun from 7:00)

name: The Orange Trees Garden
description: A terrace garden on the Aventine with a sunset view to St Peter's.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Piazza Pietro d'Illiria.
Hours: Daily 7:00–18:00 (gates lock)

name: Keyhole of the Order of Malta
description: The keyhole perfectly framing St Peter's dome; queues can top an hour midday.
mapQuery: Keyhole of the Order of Malta Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Piazza dei Cavalieri di Malta.
Hours: Open site

name: National Roman Museum, Baths of Diocletian
description: Vast imperial bath ruins near Termini; on the 4-museum pass.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site
Getting there: Viale Enrico de Nicola 78.
Hours: 9:00–19:00; closed Monday

name: National Roman Museum - Palazzo Massimo alle Terme
description: Home of the bronze Boxer at Rest and Livia's frescoes.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site
Getting there: Largo di Villa Peretti 2.
Hours: 9:00–19:00; closed Monday

name: Museo Nazionale Romano, Aula Ottagona
description: An octagonal hall from the Baths of Diocletian, exhibiting recovered antiquities.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site
Getting there: Via Giuseppe Romita 8.
Hours: 9:00–18:00; closed Monday

name: Saint Peter's Basilica
description: Christendom's largest church: Michelangelo's Pietà, Bernini's baldacchino, and a climbable dome. Dress code.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free entry; dome climb ticketed
Getting there: Train to Roma San Pietro (~1h).
Hours: Daily 7:00–19:10

name: Vatican Museums
description: Papal collections ending in the Sistine Chapel; allow 3–5 hours.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Timed tickets — book on the official Vatican Museums site
Getting there: Viale Vaticano entrance.
Hours: Mon–Sat 8:00–20:00; closed Sunday

name: Sistine Chapel
description: Michelangelo's ceiling and Last Judgment. Reached only through the Vatican Museums.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in Vatican Museums ticket
Getting there: Inside the Vatican Museums.
Hours: Mon–Sat 8:00–20:00; closed Sunday

name: Castel Sant'Angelo
description: Hadrian's mausoleum turned papal fortress, with a rooftop terrace.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book timed tickets ahead
Getting there: Lungotevere Castello 50.
Hours: 9:00–19:30; closed Monday

name: Ponte Sant'Angelo
description: Hadrian's bridge lined with Bernini's angels.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Between Castel Sant'Angelo and the Centro Storico.
Hours: Open

name: Basilica of Santa Maria in Trastevere
description: One of Rome's oldest churches, with glowing 12th–13th century mosaics.
mapQuery: Basilica of Santa Maria in Trastevere Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere.
Hours: Daily 7:30–20:30

name: Janiculum Hill
description: Rome's best free panorama, especially at sunset.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Bus 115 from Trastevere, or walk up from Via Garibaldi.
Hours: Open

name: Villa Farnesina
description: A Renaissance villa with Raphael's frescoes and citrus gardens.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site
Getting there: Via della Lungara 230.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:00–13:15; closed Sunday

name: Pantheon
description: Hadrian's temple (c. AD 126), still the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome, its 9-meter oculus open to the sky. Now a church and resting place of Raphael and Italy's kings. Modest dress required.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticketed entry (about €5); book online to skip the queue
Getting there: Piazza della Rotonda — ~15 min walk from Piazza Venezia. A Rome day from Civitavecchia is a full day (train ~1h20 each way).
Hours: Daily 9:00–19:00

name: Trevi Fountain
description: Rome's grandest Baroque fountain, 26 meters high and nearly 50 wide. Toss a coin to ensure a return.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; access to the basin edge may be managed
Getting there: Piazza di Trevi, ~10 min walk from the Pantheon or Spanish Steps.
Hours: Basin access 9:00–22:00 (Mon & Fri from 11:30); fountain viewable anytime

name: Spanish Steps
description: The 18th-century staircase from Piazza di Spagna to Trinità dei Monti, with city views from the top. Sitting on the steps is prohibited.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Metro A Spagna.
Hours: Open

name: Piazza di Spagna
description: The elegant square at the foot of the Spanish Steps with Bernini's Barcaccia fountain and luxury shopping on Via Condotti.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Metro A Spagna.
Hours: Open square

name: Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi
description: Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers at the center of Piazza Navona, crowned by an Egyptian obelisk. Beware street scammers.
mapQuery: Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi Piazza Navona Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Piazza Navona.
Hours: Open

name: Galleria Borghese
description: Bernini's sculptures and Caravaggio's paintings in Cardinal Scipione Borghese's villa. Strict two-hour timed slots.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Advance booking required; sells out weeks ahead
Getting there: Inside Villa Borghese park.
Hours: 9:00–19:00; closed Monday

name: Villa Borghese
description: Rome's central park, with a boating lake and bike rentals.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Enter from Piazza del Popolo or top of the Spanish Steps.
Hours: Open park

name: Terrazza del Pincio
description: The terrace above Piazza del Popolo, a classic sunset viewpoint.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Walk up from Piazza del Popolo.
Hours: Open

name: Ara Pacis Museum
description: Augustus's Altar of Peace in a modern glass pavilion. Temporary exhibitions often add a surcharge.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site
Getting there: Lungotevere in Augusta.
Hours: Daily 9:30–19:30

name: Mausoleum of Augustus
description: The massive circular tomb of Rome's first emperor; interior visits by booked tour.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book via the city 060608 site
Getting there: Piazza Augusto Imperatore.

name: Museo e Cripta dei Cappuccini
description: The Capuchin bone crypt decorated with remains of thousands of friars. Audio guide included; modest dress.
mapQuery: Museo e Cripta dei Cappuccini Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site or official website
Getting there: Via Vittorio Veneto 27.
Hours: Daily 9:30–12:30 & 14:30–17:30

name: Gallerie Nazionali di Arte Antica - Palazzo Barberini
description: A Baroque palace housing Caravaggio's Judith and Raphael's La Fornarina, beneath Pietro da Cortona's ceiling.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site or online
Getting there: Via delle Quattro Fontane 13.
Hours: 10:00–19:00; closed Monday

name: Piazza Barberini
description: A busy square centered on Bernini's Triton Fountain.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Metro A Barberini.
Hours: Open

name: Church of Saint Louis of the French
description: France's national church in Rome, holding Caravaggio's three St Matthew paintings. Free.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Between the Pantheon and Piazza Navona.
Hours: 9:30–12:45 & 14:30–18:30

name: Chiesa di Sant'Ignazio di Loyola
description: A Jesuit church with Andrea Pozzo's trompe-l'oeil ceiling and fake dome.
mapQuery: Chiesa di Sant'Ignazio di Loyola Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Piazza Sant'Ignazio.
Hours: Daily 9:00–23:30

name: Largo di Torre Argentina
description: Republican temples near the site of Caesar's assassination, plus a cat sanctuary.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free street view; walkway ticketed
Getting there: Via di San Nicola de' Cesarini.
Hours: Walkways 9:30–19:00

name: Campo de' Fiori
description: A morning market square that turns into a lively evening hangout.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Between Piazza Navona and the river.
Hours: Market roughly 7:00–14:00

name: Museo Nazionale Romano, Palazzo Altemps
description: A quiet Renaissance palace of classical sculpture; on the 4-museum pass.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site
Getting there: Piazza di Sant'Apollinare 46.
Hours: 9:00–19:00 (Fri to 22:00); closed Monday

name: Galleria Doria Pamphilj
description: A princely private gallery with Velázquez's Innocent X and Caravaggios.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site
Getting there: Via del Corso 305.
Hours: Mon–Tue & Thu 9:00–19:00; Fri–Sun 10:00–20:00; closed Wednesday

name: The Secret Apartment - Floridi Doria Pamphilj
description: Preserved 19th-century family apartments inside Palazzo Doria Pamphilj. Separate ticket.
mapQuery: The Secret Apartment Doria Pamphilj Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Separate ticket
Getting there: Via del Corso 305 — through the courtyard past Caffè Doria.
Hours: Mon–Tue & Thu 10:00–19:00; Wed 12:30–18:30; Fri–Sun 10:00–20:00

name: Palazzo Pamphili
description: The Pamphilj palace on Piazza Navona, now the Brazilian Embassy, with a frescoed gallery.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead
Getting there: Piazza Navona 14.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:00–18:00; closed weekends

name: Quirinal Palace
description: The Italian president's residence, with a hilltop square. Interior tours by booking.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Interior tours booked online
Getting there: Piazza del Quirinale.

name: Palazzo Massimo alle Colonne
description: Peruzzi's curved Renaissance facade, viewed from outside.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Exterior only
Getting there: Corso Vittorio Emanuele II 141.

name: Theotokopoulos Main Square
description: Fira's central square and the island's main hub, surrounded by shops, cafés and the KTEL bus station that serves every village. It is the natural starting point for orienting yourself, catching buses or walking up to the caldera-edge paths.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Top of Fira. From the Old Port tender dock, take the cable car (about €10 each way; queues of 1–1.5 hours when several ships are in), walk the roughly 580 steps or ride a donkey, then walk about 5 min inland.

name: Panoramic View Fira
description: The classic cliff-edge lookout beside the upper cable-car station, with whitewashed Fira tumbling down to the caldera and the volcano islands offshore. The walkway is lined with cafés for lingering over the view.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Next to the upper cable-car station in Fira.
Hours: Open access

name: Three Bells of Fira
description: The postcard blue-domed Catholic church with its three-bell tower perched over the caldera between Fira and Firostefani. The church is lovely, but the real draw is the photo from the viewpoint just above it.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About 15 min walk north of central Fira along the caldera path toward Firostefani.
Hours: Daily 9:00–21:00

name: Three Bells of Fira Viewpoint
description: The exact spot to frame the Three Bells church and its blue dome against the caldera. It gets busy at sunset, so arrive 20–30 min early or go first thing in the morning.
mapQuery: Three Bells of Fira Viewpoint Santorini
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Firostefani, just above the church. Walkable from Fira, or drive and park nearby.
Hours: Open access

name: Sunset Fira
description: A small square with benches in front of the Three Bells area, a calmer alternative to Oia for watching the sun sink over the caldera.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Fira–Firostefani caldera path, about 15 min walk north of the cable car.
Hours: Open access

name: Metropolitan Church of the Presentation of the Lord
description: Fira's grand Orthodox cathedral, its white bell towers visible all along the cliffs, with a frescoed interior and a peaceful courtyard overlooking the caldera. Free entry; donations welcome.
mapQuery: Metropolitan Church of the Presentation of the Lord Santorini
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; modest dress
Getting there: Ipapantis street, southern Fira, a few minutes from the cable car.

name: Cathedral St. John the Baptist
description: The peach-and-cream Catholic cathedral with a clock tower in Fira's quiet Catholic quarter, a tranquil, colourful contrast to the cliff-edge crowds.
mapQuery: Cathedral St. John the Baptist Fira Santorini
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Agiou Ioannou, Fira's Catholic quarter, about 5 min from the cable car.
Hours: Daily 9:00–21:00

name: Museum of Prehistoric Thera
description: Small, rewarding museum housing the vivid 3,600-year-old frescoes and finds from Akrotiri, including the famous fleet fresco. Ideal before or after visiting the site itself.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Next to the Metropolitan Cathedral, central Fira.
Hours: Wed–Mon 8:30–15:30; closed Tue

name: Megaro Gizi
description: Restored 17th-century Venetian mansion in the Catholic quarter housing old photos, engravings and manuscripts on Santorini's history. A quiet half-hour away from the crowds for about €3.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door (about €3)
Getting there: 25is Martiou, opposite the Catholic cathedral in Fira.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–16:00; closed Sun

name: Santorini Old Harbor
description: The tender port at the foot of Fira's cliffs, with tavernas and boats to the volcano, Thirasia and Oia. Most cruise passengers arrive here; plan the climb up and back with care on busy ship days.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; cable car tickets on site
Getting there: Below Fira. Reach the top via cable car (about €10 each way, roughly 3 min ride; queues can reach 1.5 hours), about 580 steps shared with donkeys, or a donkey ride (about €10).
Hours: Cable car daily about 6:30–22:40

name: Skaros Rock
description: Dramatic rocky headland off Imerovigli where a medieval fortress once stood, reached by a short but steep trail with a tiny chapel tucked on the far side. Spectacular caldera views; the climb back up is punishing in the heat.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Imerovigli, about 30 min walk north of Fira along the caldera path. Wear sturdy shoes and carry water.
Hours: Open access; avoid midday heat

name: Fira to Oia Walk
description: The famous roughly 10 km caldera-rim trail from Fira through Firostefani and Imerovigli to Oia, with constant views and a few steep, exposed climbs in the second half. Allow 3–5 hours.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Starts at Fira and follows the cliff path north. Start early for the heat, wear grippy shoes and carry plenty of water, as services thin out mid-route. A half-day commitment; return by bus or taxi.
Hours: Open access

name: Castle of Oia
description: Ruined Byzantine-Venetian castle at Oia's western tip and the island's most famous sunset perch, with roughly 270-degree views over the caldera and town. Free; arrive very early or well before sunset.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Western end of Oia's main path. Oia is about 25–30 min from Fira by bus or taxi, or by boat from the Old Port to Ammoudi.
Hours: Open access

name: Views of Santorini & Caldera
description: Oia's sunset lookout near the castle, where the cliffside whitewash and windmills glow at dusk. Stairs from here lead down toward Ammoudi Bay.
mapQuery: Views of Santorini & Caldera Oia Santorini
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Beside the Castle of Oia.
Hours: Open access

name: 3 Domes Viewpoint
description: The best-known angle on Oia's cluster of blue domes against the Aegean. Expect a polite queue for photos most of the day; visit early morning to avoid it.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Off Oia's main marble path, near the blue-domed churches.
Hours: Open access

name: Blue Domed Church Santorini
description: Oia's iconic blue-domed churches, the image that defines Santorini. Best seen before 7 am, before the crowds and cruise groups arrive.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Central Oia, near the 3 Domes Viewpoint.

name: The Virgin Mary of the Akathist Hymn Church
description: Graceful blue-domed church on Oia's main path with classic Cycladic lines and a lively square opposite. No photos inside.
mapQuery: Virgin Mary of the Akathist Hymn Church Oia Santorini
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; no photography inside
Getting there: On Oia's main pedestrian street.

name: Windmills of Oia
description: Restored windmills, now holiday rentals, at Oia's quieter western end, with great sunset viewpoints and fewer crowds than the castle.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About 8 min walk from the Oia sunset parking area, below the castle.
Hours: Open access

name: Maritime Museum of Santorini
description: Hidden gem in a captain's mansion telling Oia's seafaring history, with ship models, navigation instruments and a working periscope in the garden. The friendly staff often give personal tours.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Back lanes of Oia, a few minutes from the main path.
Hours: Daily 10:00–18:00

name: Ammoudi Bay
description: Tiny fishing harbour below Oia with seafood tavernas at the water's edge, red cliffs and rocky swimming spots, plus boats to Thirasia. There is no real beach, but it is beautiful at sunset.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Roughly 300 steps down from Oia (sturdy shoes; avoid riding donkeys), or drive down. Parking is about €10 including a golf-cart shuttle; boats also run here from Fira's Old Port.
Hours: Open access

name: Oia to Fira Hike (Start)
description: The Oia trailhead of the caldera-rim hike to Fira, about 10 km of rocky, gravelly path with steep sections and big views. Allow around 3–4 hours.
mapQuery: Oia to Fira Hike Start Santorini
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: East edge of Oia on the Fira road. Start early, wear proper shoes and carry water; facilities are sparse. A half-day commitment.
Hours: Open access

name: Nea Kameni
description: The young, still-active volcanic island in the middle of the caldera, where a 30–45 min walk over black lava fields leads to steaming craters and sweeping views back to the cliffs. Bring good shoes, water and sun protection; there are no restrooms.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book a volcano or caldera cruise; a separate island entry fee is paid on site
Getting there: Boat only, from Fira's Old Port or Athinios, typically as part of a caldera cruise. A half-day commitment.

name: Nea Kameni Hot Springs
description: Sulphur-tinted waters off the volcano that are a few degrees warmer than the sea, reached by swimming from your boat. It is only mildly warm and cold outside summer, and the sulphur can stain light swimsuits.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included on most volcano and hot-spring cruises
Getting there: Boat only, as a stop on volcano cruises from Fira's Old Port. A half-day commitment.

name: Therasia
description: Santorini's quiet sister island across the caldera: unspoiled villages, fish tavernas and a slower, authentic Greek feel, with sunset views back toward Oia.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Boat ticket; check return times
Getting there: Small boats from Ammoudi Bay below Oia, or as a stop on caldera cruises. A half-day commitment or more.

name: Castle of Pyrgos Kallistis
description: Ruined Venetian kastro crowning the hilltop village of Pyrgos, reached through a maze of quiet lanes, with some of the best 360-degree views on the island. Free; there are few signs, so follow those to the hilltop café.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Pyrgos village, about 15 min by taxi or bus from Fira. Park at the village edge and walk up 10–15 min of steps.
Hours: Daily 7:00–20:00

name: Monastery of Prophet Elias of Thira
description: Hilltop monastery on Santorini's highest point, about 560 m, with panoramic views over the whole island and a shop selling local liqueurs. A marked path also runs from here to Ancient Thera.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; modest dress
Getting there: Narrow winding road above Pyrgos, best by car or taxi; parking at the top.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:00–17:00; closed Sun

name: Santorini Wine Museum
description: The Koutsoyannopoulos family's wine museum in a cave about 8 m underground, tracing Santorini winemaking with machinery and dioramas, ending with a tasting and food pairing.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket including tasting at the door
Getting there: Vothonas, about 10 min by car or taxi from Fira.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:30–19:00; Sun 10:00–19:00

name: Santo Wines
description: The island's cooperative winery, with a huge caldera-view terrace for flights of Assyrtiko and Vinsanto paired with snacks. The sunset slot is a classic, and it also serves dinner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Reserve for sunset
Getting there: Between Pyrgos and Megalochori, about 10 min by car from Fira; large car park.
Hours: Daily 9:00–20:30

name: Venetsanos Winery
description: Historic 1947 gravity-flow winery cut into the caldera cliff, with tours, tastings and a terrace for sunset over the volcano.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book tours and tastings
Getting there: Caldera edge above Megalochori and the Athinios port road, about 15 min from Fira.
Hours: Daily 11:00–20:00

name: Art Space Art Gallery - Winery - Museum
description: Santorini's smallest winery, set in old canava caves that double as a contemporary art gallery, run by the same family for five generations. Natural wines and a superb Vinsanto on guided tastings.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tours and tastings (about €25)
Getting there: Exo Gonia, near Kamari, about 15 min from Fira.
Hours: Daily 10:00–19:00

name: Lost Atlantis Experience - Interactive Museum
description: Family-friendly interactive museum on the Atlantis legend and Santorini's eruption, with guided stations and a 9D cinema.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Megalochori, about 15 min from Fira.
Hours: Daily 10:00–19:00

name: Venetian Castle of Emporio
description: Medieval fortified quarter of Emporio, the island's largest village, with tightly packed houses, bougainvillea-draped lanes and the church of Agios Spyridon.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Emporio village, south-central Santorini, about 20 min from Fira. Look up the castle quarter (Kasteli) before you go; the lanes are a maze.

name: Panagia Episkopi
description: One of the oldest churches on the island, an 11th-century Byzantine church with vaulted domes and rare icons, set amid fields below Mesa Vouno.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Near Mesa Gonia, about 15 min from Fira by car.

name: Agios Charalambos
description: Exo Gonia's grand church, among the island's largest, unusual for its tiled roof and broad steps rather than the typical blue dome. Rating rests on few reviews.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Exo Gonia village, about 15 min from Fira.

name: Akrotiri
description: Bronze Age town buried by the eruption around 1600 BC, preserved under a vast roof with multi-storey houses and streets, often called a 'Minoan Pompeii'. An audio guide or guide brings it to life.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket on site or online (about €20)
Getting there: Southwest Santorini, about 25 min by bus or taxi from Fira. A half-day commitment with travel.
Hours: Mon & Thu 8:30–15:30; Tue, Wed, Sat & Sun 8:00–19:00; Fri 8:00–18:30

name: Akrotiri Lighthouse
description: Lighthouse at the island's southwestern tip with a less-crowded sunset over the caldera and open Aegean. The tower is closed to visitors, but you can walk to the rocky point.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
