description: Diocletian launched the last great persecution of Christians, including Domnius, bishop of Salona. Centuries later his own mausoleum was turned into the Cathedral of St. Domnius, which locals see as history's neat revenge. Look for the black granite sphinx on the Peristyle, one of several Diocletian brought from Egypt.
mapQuery: The persecutor's tomb became a saint's cathedral Split

name: Klapa: the sound of Dalmatia
description: Klapa is unaccompanied harmony singing by small groups of men or women, often about the sea, love and home. It is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage. The domed Vestibule's acoustics make it the classic place to hear it, and buying the group's CD is the customary thank-you.
mapQuery: Klapa: the sound of Dalmatia Split

name: Fjaka and 'pomalo'
description: Dalmatians have a word, fjaka, for a pleasant, sun-drugged state of doing nothing, and a motto, pomalo, meaning 'take it easy'. A single coffee on the Riva can last two hours, and that is the point. Don't expect to be rushed, and don't rush anyone else.

name: Hajduk is a religion
description: Hajduk Split, founded in 1911, is the city's football club, and its supporters, the Torcida, founded in 1950, call themselves Europe's oldest organized fan group. Hajduk graffiti covers walls across the city, and support for the club is a core part of local identity.

name: Picigin, a game invented on Bačvice
description: Picigin is Split's own beach game. Players stand in ankle-deep water and keep a small ball in the air with acrobatic dives, never letting it touch the water. It was born on Bačvice beach in the early 1900s, and locals play year-round, including a famous New Year's Day game.
mapQuery: Picigin, a game invented on Bačvice Split

name: Gregory of Nin and a Croatian language in church
description: The giant bronze of Bishop Gregory of Nin outside the Golden Gate is by sculptor Ivan Meštrović. It honors the 10th-century bishop who championed the use of the Croatian language and Glagolitic script in the liturgy, which made him a national symbol. Rubbing his big toe is said to bring luck and a return to Split.
mapQuery: Gregory of Nin and a Croatian language in church Split

name: Venice, Vienna, Belgrade, then independence
description: Split was Venetian from 1420 to 1797, then Austrian, then part of Yugoslavia, until Croatia declared independence in 1991. You can read those layers in the architecture: Roman walls, Venetian Gothic windows, Austro-Hungarian Prokurative arcades and socialist-era blocks beyond the center.
mapQuery: Venice, Vienna, Belgrade, then independence Split

name: Marjan is the city's lungs
description: The forested Marjan peninsula has been protected parkland since the early 20th century, and its stepped paths, hermitages and tiny chapels are a daily refuge for locals. Joining Splićani on the climb to the Vidilica terrace is the easiest way to feel the city's rhythm.
mapQuery: Marjan is the city's lungs Split

name: Acropolis of Athens
description: The sacred citadel of ancient Athens, crowned by the 5th-century BC Parthenon, Erechtheion, Propylaea, and Temple of Athena Nike, the defining monument of classical Greece. The marble paths are slippery and shade is scarce, so go at opening.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Timed-entry ticket required; book well ahead on the official site hhticket.gr
Getting there: Main west entrance off Dionysiou Areopagitou (Acropoli or Monastiraki metro); the South Slope entrance by the Acropolis Museum is usually quieter. From Piraeus, about 25 minutes on Metro Line 1 or 30–40 minutes by taxi. Plan a half-day.
Hours: Daily 8:00–17:00 (hours change seasonally; last entry earlier)

name: Parthenon
description: Pericles' Doric temple to Athena (447–432 BC), the masterpiece of classical architecture and symbol of Western civilization. Long-running restoration scaffolding is part of the view.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Acropolis timed ticket (hhticket.gr)
Getting there: On the Acropolis summit, inside the paid site.
Hours: Follows Acropolis hours

name: Erechtheion
description: An asymmetrical Ionic temple (421–406 BC) sacred to Athena and Poseidon, famed for its Porch of the Caryatids. Five originals are in the Acropolis Museum and one is in the British Museum.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Acropolis ticket
Getting there: North side of the Acropolis summit.
Hours: Follows Acropolis hours

name: Propylaea
description: Mnesikles' monumental gateway to the Acropolis (437–432 BC), through which every visitor still passes. It already offers sweeping views over Athens.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Acropolis ticket
Getting there: West entrance of the Acropolis.
Hours: Follows Acropolis hours

name: Temple of Athena Nike
description: A jewel-box Ionic temple (c. 420 BC) to Athena as goddess of victory, perched on a bastion beside the Propylaea.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Acropolis ticket
Getting there: Beside the Propylaea at the Acropolis entrance.
Hours: Follows Acropolis hours

name: South Slope of the Acropolis of Athens
description: The southern flank of the Acropolis, with the Theatre of Dionysus, the Asklepieion sanctuary, and the Stoa of Eumenes, ending at the Odeon of Herodes Atticus. Entering here builds up to the summit.
mapQuery: South Slope of the Acropolis Athens
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Acropolis ticket
Getting there: Entrance on Dionysiou Areopagitou near Acropoli metro and the Acropolis Museum.
Hours: Daily 8:00–19:00 (seasonal)

name: Theatre of Dionysus Eleuthereus
description: The world's first theatre, where Aeschylus, Sophocles, Euripides, and Aristophanes premiered their plays. Marble front-row thrones for priests still survive.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Acropolis ticket
Getting there: South Slope of the Acropolis.
Hours: Daily 8:00–18:00 (seasonal)

name: Odeon of Herodes Atticus
description: A Roman stone theatre (AD 161) on the Acropolis slope, still used for summer concerts and drama under the floodlit Parthenon. Outside performances it is viewed from the Acropolis approach.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Interior during performances only; tickets via aefestival.gr
Getting there: Dionysiou Areopagitou, below the Acropolis west entrance.

name: Acropolis Museum
description: A modern museum displaying the original sculptures of the Acropolis, including the Caryatids and Parthenon frieze, above glass-floored excavations of an ancient neighborhood. The top floor faces the Parthenon.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door or theacropolismuseum.gr
Getting there: Dionysiou Areopagitou 15, at Acropoli metro.
Hours: Mon 9:00–17:00; Tue–Thu, Sat–Sun 9:00–20:00; Fri 9:00–22:00

name: Areopagus Hill
description: The 'Hill of Ares', seat of Athens' ancient high court and where St. Paul delivered his sermon to the Athenians (Acts 17), with free views of the Propylaea. The rock is polished slick.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Metal stairs to the right of the path to the Acropolis west entrance.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Pnyx
description: The hillside assembly place where Athenian citizens debated and voted, the birthplace of democracy. Pericles and Demosthenes spoke from its rock-cut platform facing the Acropolis.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: West of Philopappos Hill, via the Pikionis paths or from Thissio.

name: Themistoclean Ancient Wall
description: Surviving sections of the walls hastily built in 479 BC under Themistocles from reused column drums and sculpture after the Persian sack. They once linked Athens to Piraeus, with sunset views of the Acropolis.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Dim. Eginitou, on the Hill of the Nymphs and Pnyx area near Thissio. Wear grippy shoes.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Philopappos Monument
description: The marble mausoleum (AD 114–116) of Gaius Julius Antiochus Philopappos, exiled prince of Commagene and Athenian benefactor, atop the Hill of the Muses. Panoramic views to the sea.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Summit of Philopappos Hill, about a 15–20 minute walk up from Dionysiou Areopagitou. Paths are partly unlit at night.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Prison of Socrates
description: Rock-cut chambers on Philopappos Hill traditionally linked to Socrates' imprisonment before his execution in 399 BC. The link is unproven, the chambers are barred, and it is a quiet stop.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Lower Philopappos path from Dionysiou Areopagitou.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: St Demetrios Loumbardiaris
description: A 9th-century chapel built from ancient spolia, named for a 1658 'miracle' when lightning blew up an Ottoman cannon (lumbarda) aimed at it. It has 18th-century frescoes and Pikionis stonework.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Foot of Philopappos Hill, opposite the Acropolis.
Hours: Daily 7:00–12:00 and 17:00–20:00

name: Ancient Agora of Athens

details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate or hhticket.gr (combined ticket valid)
Getting there: Main entrance on Adrianou St near Monastiraki metro.
Hours: Daily 8:00–19:30 (seasonal)

name: Temple of Hephaestus
description: The best-preserved ancient Greek temple in the world (c. 449–445 BC), still roofed, on a knoll above the Agora. It survived by serving as a church for centuries.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Ancient Agora ticket
Getting there: Inside the Ancient Agora site.
Hours: Follows Agora hours

name: Stoa of Attalos - Museum of the Ancient Agora
description: A faithful 1950s reconstruction of King Attalos II's 2nd-century BC colonnade, showing what a working stoa looked like. It houses the Agora museum, with artifacts of Athenian democracy such as ostraka and voting tokens.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Ancient Agora ticket
Getting there: Inside the Ancient Agora, east side.
Hours: Daily 8:00–18:30 (seasonal)

name: Roman Forum of Athens (Roman Agora)
description: The marketplace funded by Julius Caesar and Augustus, with the Gate of Athena Archegetis and the Ottoman Fethiye Mosque. Much is visible from the surrounding lanes.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate (combined ticket valid)
Getting there: Polignotou 3, between Monastiraki and Plaka.
Hours: Daily 8:00–18:30 (seasonal)

name: Horologion of Andronikos Cyrrhestes (Tower of the Winds)
description: A 1st-century BC marble octagon that worked as water clock, sundial, and weathervane, with the eight wind gods carved on its faces. It is antiquity's best-preserved scientific building.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Roman Agora ticket
Getting there: Inside the Roman Agora.
Hours: Follows Roman Agora hours

name: Hadrian's Library
description: Emperor Hadrian's AD 132 cultural complex of reading rooms, lecture halls, and gardens holding some 17,000 scrolls, with a Corinthian façade on Monastiraki Square.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate (combined ticket valid)
Getting there: Areos 3, off Monastiraki Square.
Hours: Daily 8:00–20:00 (seasonal)

name: Kerameikos Archaeological Site

details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate (combined ticket valid)
Getting there: Ermou 148, near Thissio and Kerameikos metro.
Hours: Daily 8:00–19:00 (seasonal)

name: Temple of Olympian Zeus
description: The largest temple of ancient Greece, begun in the 6th century BC and finished by Hadrian 650 years later, with 15 colossal Corinthian columns still standing. Partly under scaffolding.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate or hhticket.gr
Getting there: Vasilissis Olgas entrance by Hadrian's Arch, about 10 minutes on foot from Syntagma.

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Vasilissis Amalias 50.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Zappeio Roman Baths

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (viewed from above)
Getting there: Vasilissis Amalias, by the Zappeion and opposite the Temple of Olympian Zeus.
Hours: Daily 8:00–20:00

Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Epimenidou 3, Plaka.
Hours: Open 24 hours

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)

Hours: Daily 10:00–17:00

details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Mitropoleos Square, between Syntagma and Monastiraki.

name: Plato's Academy Park
description: The site of Plato's Academy (387 BC), the Western world's first institution of higher learning, now a local park with excavated foundations and a small digital museum.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)

Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate or panathenaicstadium.gr

details:
Reservations / tickets: Exterior only for most visitors

Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door

Reservations / tickets: Exterior viewing (free)

Reservations / tickets: Exterior viewing; reading room weekdays

details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door

Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:30–15:30; closed Tuesday

details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door or hhticket.gr
Getting there: 28is Oktovriou (Patission) 44, near Victoria metro.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:00–20:00; Tue 13:00–20:00 (seasonal)

name: Byzantine & Christian Museum

details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Vasilissis Sofias 22, near Evangelismos metro.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:30–15:30; closed Tuesday

name: Archaeological Museum of Piraeus
description: A museum of rare original classical bronzes found in Piraeus (the Piraeus Apollo, Athena, and Artemis), plus finds from the ancient naval port. It connects to the Theatre of Zea.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door (cash reported)
Getting there: Char. Trikoupi 31, near Zea Marina; about 15 minutes on foot from the port's central gates.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 9:00–17:00; closed Tuesday

name: Ancient Athenian Theatre of Zea at Piraeus
description: A Hellenistic theatre (2nd century BC) beside the Zea harbor, once the home of Athens' war-galley sheds. It is viewable from Filellinon St or via the museum.
mapQuery: Ancient Theatre of Zea Piraeus Athens
details:
Reservations / tickets: Best viewed with a museum ticket
Getting there: Beside the Archaeological Museum of Piraeus, about 10 minutes from Piraeus metro.

name: Eetionian Gate of the Ancient Walls of Piraeus
description: Twin round towers of the main gate in the Themistoclean walls of the ancient port, the best surviving piece of the fortifications that linked Piraeus to Athens. Modern ships make the backdrop.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; opening is irregular, so call the Piraeus museum (+30 21 0452 1598) first
Getting there: Kanari St, Kastraki area by the port's western side; taxi recommended.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:00–15:30; closed Saturday–Sunday

name: Themistocles Tomb
description: A seaside monument at the mouth of the harbor traditionally marking the tomb of Themistocles, founder of the Athenian navy and victor of Salamis. It is modestly kept, with a walking and cycling path.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Peiraiki shore at Drapetsona, at the harbor entrance; taxi from the port.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Church of Agios Nikolaos
description: The landmark church of St. Nicholas, patron of sailors, on the port waterfront, with a richly painted interior.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Agiou Nikolaou 2, beside the cruise gates.
Hours: Daily from about 6:00 to 18:00–18:30

name: Municipal Theatre of Piraeus
description: An 1895 neoclassical theatre modeled on Paris's Opéra-Comique, symbol of Piraeus's 19th-century boom. Tours, exhibitions, and plays run here.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Box office or theatre website
Getting there: Iroon Polytechniou 32, opposite Piraeus metro.
Hours: Box office Mon, Wed–Fri 10:00–14:00 and 18:00–21:00; Sat 16:00–21:00; Sun 18:00–21:00; closed Tuesday

name: Naval Museum Battleship HS Georgios Averof
description: The world's last surviving armored cruiser (1911), Greece's flagship in the Balkan Wars victories at Elli and Lemnos. A replica trireme Olympias is moored nearby.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket on site
Getting there: Trocadero Marina, Palaio Faliro; about 15 minutes by taxi from Piraeus.
Hours: Tue–Fri 9:00–14:00; Sat–Sun 10:00–17:00; closed Monday

name: Temple of Apollo Zoster
description: Foundations of a 6th-century BC temple where Leto was said to have loosened her girdle (zoster) before giving birth to Apollo. It now sits inside the Astir Beach club.
mapQuery: Temple of Apollo Zoster Vouliagmeni Athens
details:
Reservations / tickets: Via Astir Beach entry
Getting there: Apollonos 16, Vouliagmeni; about 40 minutes by taxi from Piraeus. Visible through a viewing window, but close access means paying beach-club entry. A half-day outing.

name: Temple of Poseidon
description: A Doric temple (c. 440 BC) on a sheer cape, the last sight of home for ancient Athenian sailors, with Lord Byron's name carved into a column. It is the most famous sunset in Attica.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate or hhticket.gr
Getting there: Cape Sounion, about 70 km (1 hour 15 minutes or more) from Piraeus by the coast road; tours, car, or KTEL bus. A half-day trip.

name: Archaeological Site of Silver Mines at Drymos of Lavreotike
description: Remains of the ancient Laurion silver mines and ore-washeries whose wealth built Themistocles' fleet that won at Salamis. A free open-access trail runs near Agia Triada church.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Fenced site by appointment (+30 2292 022817); trail walk-in (free)
Getting there: Near Sounion in the Lavreotiki park. The fenced site needs an appointment; the marked trail from Agia Triada is open. A half-day trip.

name: Ancient Theatre of Thorikos
description: Among the oldest theatres in the world (6th–5th century BC), with an unusual elliptical shape and original stones, on a quiet hillside above Lavrio. Free.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Thorikos, just north of Lavrio port; park at the small gate below and walk up. About 1 hour 10 minutes from Piraeus. A half-day trip.
Hours: Open access

name: Archaeological Museum of Lavrion
description: A small museum with finds from Thorikos, the ancient mines, the Agrileza quarries, and sculptures from the Sounion temples.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Lavrio town, about 1 hour 10 minutes from Piraeus. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:30–15:30; closed Tuesday

name: Lavrion Technological and Cultural Park
description: The restored 19th-century French mining and metallurgy works that revived Laurion's ancient silver industry, now an industrial-heritage park with exhibitions.
mapQuery: Lavrion Technological and Cultural Park Athens
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Lavrio, about 1 hour 10 minutes from Piraeus. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon–Fri 8:00–16:00; Sat–Sun 9:00–17:00

name: Archaeological Site of Brauron
description: The Sanctuary of Artemis Brauronia, where young Athenian girls served the goddess as 'little bears', with a restored stoa and a fine museum of votives.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (site and museum sold separately)
Getting there: Vravrona, east Attica; about 50 minutes from Piraeus. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:30–15:30; closed Tuesday

name: Tumulus of the Athenians at Marathon
description: The burial mound of the 192 Athenians killed defeating the Persians at Marathon in 490 BC, the battle that inspired the marathon run.
mapQuery: Tumulus of the Athenians Marathon Athens
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate
Getting there: Marathon plain, about 1 hour from Piraeus. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:30–15:30; closed Tuesday

name: Archaeological Site of Ramnous
description: A remote coastal sanctuary of Nemesis and an Athenian garrison fortress over the Evia straits, reached by an ancient road lined with tomb remains.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate; call +30 2294 063477 to confirm opening
Getting there: Near Grammatiko, about 1 hour 15 minutes from Piraeus. A 1 km walk on uneven paths; bring water. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:30–15:15; closed Tuesday

name: Archaeological Site of Amphiaraeion of Oropos
description: A healing sanctuary and oracle of the hero Amphiaraos in a wooded ravine, with a theatre, an incubation stoa, and a temple. It is little visited.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate (cash)
Getting there: Near Kalamos, north Attica; about 1 hour 15 minutes from Piraeus. Cash only. A half-day trip.
Hours: Daily 8:30–15:30

name: Kaisariani Monastery
description: An 11th-century Byzantine monastery on Mount Hymettus with 17th-century frescoes and an ancient spring sacred to Aphrodite.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate
Getting there: Above Kaisariani, about 20 minutes by taxi from Syntagma or 45 minutes from Piraeus. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:30–15:00; closed Tuesday

name: Holy Monastery of Daphni
description: A UNESCO-listed 11th-century monastery with some of the finest Byzantine mosaics anywhere, including the Christ Pantocrator dome, on the Sacred Way to Eleusis.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Iera Odos, Chaidari; about 25 minutes by taxi from Piraeus. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:30–17:00; closed Tuesday

name: Eleusis Archeological Site
description: The sanctuary of Demeter and Persephone, home for nearly 2,000 years of the secret Eleusinian Mysteries, with a museum.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate or hhticket.gr
Getting there: Elefsina, about 30 minutes west of Piraeus by car. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 8:00–19:00 (seasonal); closed Tuesday

name: Corinth Canal
description: A 1893 canal cut through 80 m limestone walls, realizing a dream attempted since Periander and Nero. The ancient diolkos ship-road survives nearby.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: About 1 hour west of Piraeus; viewpoints at the old-road bridges. A half-day trip.
Hours: Open access

name: Archaeological Museum of Ancient Corinth
description: The museum and excavated Roman city of Corinth, with the Temple of Apollo and the Bema where St. Paul stood trial. A key biblical site.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate (site and museum)
Getting there: Archea Korinthos, about 1 hour 15 minutes from Piraeus. A half-day or full-day trip, often with Acrocorinth.
Hours: Daily 8:00–19:00 (seasonal)

name: Acrocorinth
description: A massive mountain fortress layered with Greek, Byzantine, Frankish, Venetian, and Ottoman walls, and the site of the ancient Temple of Aphrodite. Free.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Above Ancient Corinth; drive to the top car park, then walk on slippery paths. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon–Thu, Sat–Sun 8:30–15:30; Fri 8:30–12:00

name: Archaeological site of Nemea
description: The site of the Panhellenic Nemean Games, with the partly re-erected Temple of Zeus, a museum, and an ancient stadium with its athletes' tunnel (same ticket).
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate (includes stadium)
Getting there: Nemea, about 1 hour 30 minutes from Piraeus. A full-day trip, often with Mycenae.
Hours: Daily 8:00–20:00 (seasonal)

name: Archaeological site of Mycenae
description: Agamemnon's Bronze Age citadel, with the Lion Gate, Cyclopean walls, Grave Circle A, the Treasury of Atreus, and a museum. It is the heart of the Homeric world.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate or hhticket.gr
Getting there: Mykines, about 1 hour 45 minutes from Piraeus. A full-day tour. No shade.
Hours: Daily 8:30–15:30 (seasonal)

name: Mycenean Acropolis of Tiryns
description: A UNESCO-listed Mycenaean citadel ('Tiryns of the mighty walls'), with colossal Cyclopean ramparts and corbelled galleries. It is quiet and close to Nafplio, though signage is minimal.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate
Getting there: On the Argos–Nafplio road, about 1 hour 50 minutes from Piraeus. A full-day trip.
Hours: Daily 8:30–15:30 (seasonal)

name: Ancient Theatre at the Asklepieion of Epidaurus
description: The best-preserved ancient theatre in Greece (4th century BC), famed for perfect acoustics, within the healing sanctuary of Asklepios. Summer festival performances are held here.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate or hhticket.gr; performances via aefestival.gr
Getting there: Epidavros, about 2 hours from Piraeus. A full-day trip.
Hours: Daily 8:00–19:00 (seasonal)

name: Palamidi Fortress
description: A Venetian Baroque fortress (1711–1714) above Nafplio, the first capital of modern Greece, where hero Theodoros Kolokotronis was imprisoned. Reached by 999 steps or by car.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate
Getting there: Nafplio, about 2 hours from Piraeus. A full-day trip.
Hours: Daily 8:00–18:00 (seasonal)

name: Delphi Archaeological Site
description: The Sanctuary of Apollo and seat of the Oracle, the 'navel of the world', with the temple, treasuries, theatre, and stadium terraced into Mount Parnassus.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate or hhticket.gr (combined with the museum)
Getting there: Delphi, about 2 hours 45 minutes from Piraeus. A full-day tour.
Hours: Daily 8:30–20:00 (seasonal)

name: Delphi Archaeological Museum
description: Treasures of the sanctuary, including the bronze Charioteer of Delphi, the Naxian Sphinx, and the Siphnian Treasury friezes.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Combined ticket with the site
Getting there: Beside the Delphi site. Part of a full-day Delphi tour.
Hours: Daily 8:30–20:00 (seasonal)

name: Temple of Aphaia
description: A remarkably complete late-Archaic Doric temple (c. 500 BC) on Aegina, forming the 'sacred triangle' with the Parthenon and Sounion. Its pediment sculptures are in Munich.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate
Getting there: Aegina island: ferry from Piraeus (40–75 minutes), then a 25-minute bus or taxi. A full-day trip.
Hours: Daily 8:00–19:00 (seasonal)

name: Old Venetian Port of Chania
description: The 14th-century Venetian harbour is the historic core of Chania, layered with Venetian, Ottoman and Egyptian-era buildings around a crescent quay. Walking it end to end takes you past the shipyards, the Mosque of the Janissaries, the Firka bastion and the lighthouse mole. Best in the quiet early morning or at sunset.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About 15 min by taxi or KTEL bus from Souda cruise port (approx. 7 km) to the Old Town; walk down to the water.
Hours: Open public waterfront

name: Lighthouse of Chania
description: A 16th-century Venetian lighthouse rebuilt in minaret-like form during the Egyptian administration of the 1830s, standing at the end of the harbour breakwater. The 1.5 km walk out gives the definitive view back over the Old Town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Walk east around the harbour past the Neoria to the mole; about 20 min each way, with no shade.

name: Firka Venetian Fortress
description: A late-16th-century bastion guarding the harbour mouth, used by the Ottomans as barracks and a prison. The Greek flag was raised here in 1913 to mark union with Greece. The ramparts offer a fine harbour panorama.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: West end of the harbour, next to the Maritime Museum.
Hours: Mon–Fri 8:00–14:00; closed Sat–Sun

name: Küçük Hasan Mosque (Mosque of the Janissaries)
description: Built in 1645 right after the Ottoman conquest, this is the oldest Ottoman building on Crete and the harbour's signature domed silhouette. It now serves as an exhibition hall; the mihrab and Quranic inscriptions are still visible inside.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in when an exhibition is on (free)
Getting there: On the harbour front at Sourmeli 18.
Hours: Fri–Sat 18:00–22:00 per Google; open during exhibitions

name: Grand Arsenal (Megalo Arsenali)
description: The largest of the Venetian shipyard buildings, restored as a municipal cultural center for free exhibitions. Its arcaded façade is one of the harbour's finest Venetian structures.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; exhibitions usually free
Getting there: East side of the inner harbour.
Hours: Mon–Fri 18:00–23:00 during exhibitions

name: Neoria (Venetian Shipyards)
description: Seven of the seventeen vaulted shipyards built by Venice in the 16th century survive along the eastern harbour, where galleys were built and stored over winter. They are best seen on the walk to the lighthouse.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Eastern inner harbour.

name: Porta Sabbionara
description: The 'Sand Gate,' a surviving Venetian gate and bastion at the northeast corner of the old fortifications. A free short film on the Old Town's history plays nearby, and the bastion top gives coastal views toward the White Mountains.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Akti Miaouli, at the east end of the harbour toward Koum Kapi.

name: San Salvador Bastion
description: A Venetian bastion of the western walls guarding the harbour approach, near the Topanas quarter. Pleasant for a short walk around the old fortifications; parking nearby is very limited.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Pireos 73, west of the harbour by Firka.

name: West Venetian Walls
description: A long, well-preserved stretch of the 16th-century Venetian land walls and moat along the western edge of the Old Town. It is mostly an open green space and quiet compared with the harbour.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Meletiou Piga area, between the Old Town and Nea Chora.

name: Kastelli Archaeological Site
description: Open excavations on Kastelli hill revealing ancient Kydonia, one of Minoan Crete's major cities, uncovered after WWII bombing. Many star finds in the Archaeological Museum came from here, and signboards explain the layers.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (viewed from the street)
Getting there: Kanevarou 34, on the hill just behind the harbour.

name: Byzantine Walls of Chania (Sifaka)
description: Remnants of the Byzantine-era defensive walls that once ringed Kastelli hill, showing repairs from several periods. A quick, atmospheric stop in the Sifaka lanes.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Sifaka 41, Kastelli quarter.

name: Byzantine Walls of Chania (Rianou)
description: A second surviving stretch of the Byzantine fortifications woven into the modern buildings of the Kastelli quarter, now a favorite spot of local cats. Small but evocative.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Rianou 6, Kastelli quarter.

name: Ahmet Ağa Minaret
description: One of the few surviving Ottoman minarets in Chania; its mosque has disappeared. It can only be viewed from outside but remains a landmark of the old Turkish quarter.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (exterior only)
Getting there: Chatzimichali Ntaliani 32, Splantzia area.

name: Church of Saint Nicholas (Splantzia)
description: Founded as a Venetian Dominican monastery church, converted into the Sultan Ibrahim mosque, and returned to Orthodoxy in 1918. It is the only building in Chania with both a bell tower and a minaret. The plane tree in the square outside is linked to the 1821 hanging of the bishop.
mapQuery: Church of Saint Nicholas Splantzia Chania
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Splantzia Square, eastern Old Town.

name: Etz Hayyim Synagogue
description: A former Venetian church that became the synagogue of Chania's Romaniote Jewish community, which was lost in 1944. Restored in the 1990s, it is Crete's only surviving synagogue, with a mikveh and memorial.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (donation welcome)
Getting there: Parodos Kondylaki, in the old Jewish quarter.
Hours: Mon–Thu 10:00–16:00; Fri 10:00–15:00; closed Sat–Sun

name: Holy Metropolitan Church of the Presentation of the Virgin Mary (Trimartiri)
description: Chania's 19th-century Orthodox cathedral, built on the site of an older church that the Ottomans used as a soap factory. Inside are a gilded iconostasis and rich iconography. Free entry; modest dress is expected.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Plateia Mitropoleos, off Chalidon Street.

name: Holy Catholic Church of the Assumption
description: A Franciscan church hidden behind Chalidon Street, reached through a passage. It reflects Chania's long Catholic presence from the Venetian era.
mapQuery: Catholic Church of the Assumption Chania
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Chalidon 46, through the arched passage.

name: Old Chania Market
description: The cross-shaped Municipal Market of 1913, built over part of the Venetian walls and modeled on Marseille's market, with lively shopping lanes around it. A landmark of early-20th-century Chania.
tags: verify: whether the market hall interior is open after renovation
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: South edge of the Old Town at the end of Chalidon Street.

name: Archaeological Museum of Chania
description: A modern museum presenting about 6,000 years of western Cretan history, from Minoan Kydonia to Roman mosaics. The galleries are spacious and fully accessible, with a sea-view café. Plan about an hour.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door or online (about €15)
Getting there: Skra 15, Halepa, about 2 km east of the Old Town; taxi or 25-min walk. Free parking.
Hours: Mon & Wed–Sun 8:00–20:00; closed Tue

name: Byzantine and Post-Byzantine Collection of Chania
description: Housed in the restored Venetian church of San Salvatore, with icons of the Cretan School, frescoes, mosaic floors and coins from Constantine to Justinian.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door
Getting there: Theotokopoulou 78, near Firka.
Hours: Mon & Wed–Sun 8:30–15:30; closed Tue

name: Maritime Museum of Crete
description: A museum of Crete's naval history from the Bronze Age to WWII, set in the Firka complex. Ship models are built on site, and the courtyard frames the lighthouse. Entry about €5.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €5)
Getting there: Akti Kountourioti, west end of the harbour.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:00–16:00; closed Sun

name: Eleftherios Venizelos House
description: The preserved Halepa residence of Greece's great modern statesman, with original furnishings, documents and the bullet-riddled car from an assassination attempt. An excellent free app guide accompanies the visit.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €5)
Getting there: Plateia Elenas Venizelou, Halepa; taxi or 25-min walk from the harbour.
Hours: Tue–Fri 10:30–17:30; Sat–Sun 11:00–16:00; closed Mon

name: Souda Bay Commonwealth War Cemetery
description: An immaculately kept Commonwealth War Graves cemetery on the shore of Souda Bay, with about 1,500 graves from the 1941 Battle of Crete, many of them unnamed. A quiet, deeply moving place for reflection.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Souda, about 5 min by car from the cruise port; free parking.

name: Venizelos Graves
description: The hilltop tombs of Eleftherios Venizelos and his son Sophoklis on Profitis Ilias, where Cretan rebels raised the Greek flag in 1897. A shaded park and chapel sit beside the tombs, with sweeping views over Chania. Superb at sunset.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Akrotiri road, about 10 min by car from the Old Town; limited parking.

name: Holy Trinity Tzagarolon Monastery (Agia Triada)
description: A 17th-century monastery founded by the Venetian-Cretan Tzagarolos brothers, with a Renaissance-style church façade and a small museum. The monks produce wine, oil and honey for sale. Entry about €3.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €3)
Getting there: Akrotiri, about 30 min by car from Chania or Souda; free parking.
Hours: Mon 8:00–20:00; Tue–Fri 7:00–20:00; Sat–Sun 6:30–20:00

name: Gouverneto Monastery (Virgin of the Angels)
description: A fortress-like 16th-century monastery, among the oldest on Crete, with corner towers and a church decorated with carved faces. It is the trailhead for the walk down to Katholiko, and hours are restricted.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Small donation (about €2.50)
Getting there: About 4 km beyond Agia Triada; large free car park. Modest dress required.
Hours: Mon, Tue, Thu 9:00–12:00 & 17:00–19:00; Sat–Sun 5:00–12:00 & 17:00–20:00; closed Wed & Fri

name: Monastery Katholiko
description: Ruins of one of Crete's earliest monasteries, associated with St John the Hermit, carved into a gorge above a tiny bay. The descent passes the saint's cave and an ancient bridge. Allow 30–40 min down and a hot climb back.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Trailhead at Gouverneto Monastery car park; stepped, rocky path. Wear proper shoes, bring water, and avoid midday.
Hours: Trail open daylight hours

name: Chrysopigi Monastery
description: A mid-16th-century convent founded in the last century of Venetian rule, now a working community of nuns known for its icon workshop and warm welcome. Peaceful courtyards are just minutes from the city.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About 3 km southeast of central Chania, near the Souda road; short taxi ride.
Hours: Daily 8:00–12:00 & 15:30–18:00

name: Archaeological Site of Aptera
description: An ancient city-state inhabited from Minoan to Byzantine times, with a restored Roman theatre, giant Roman cisterns, a Doric temple and a Byzantine monastery. It overlooks Souda Bay. Plan about 1.5 hours and bring water.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €10)
Getting there: Megala Chorafia, about 20 min by car from Souda port; free parking.
Hours: Mon & Wed–Sun 8:00–18:30; closed Tue

name: Koules Ottoman Fortress (Izzeddin)
description: An 1870s Ottoman fortress built to control the mouth of Souda Bay, later used as a prison. It now has a small history exhibition and views of Souda Island. Easily combined with Aptera; cash only.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €2, cash only)
Getting there: Kalami, just below Aptera; free parking.
Hours: Mon & Wed–Sun 9:00–19:30; closed Tue

name: Memorial of the Battle of Galatas
description: A Greek and New Zealand memorial to the May 1941 fighting on 'Pink Hill' at Galatas during the Battle of Crete. A small local war museum across the square is run by enthusiastic volunteers.
mapQuery: Memorial of the Battle of Galatas Chania
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Galatas village square, about 15 min by car west of Chania.

name: Maleme German Military Cemetery
description: The resting place of more than 4,000 German paratroopers killed in the 1941 airborne invasion, overlooking the Maleme airfield they attacked. A volunteer-run visitor center explains the battle. The walk up is hot, so bring water.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Above Maleme on the old road toward Kissamos, about 25 min by car from Chania.

name: Gonia Monastery (Mother of God Odigitria)
description: Founded in 1618 and rebuilt after Ottoman raids, this seaside monastery still bears cannonball scars. Its museum holds one of Crete's finest collections of post-Byzantine icons. Entry about €4; modest dress required.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €4)
Getting there: Kolymbari, about 35 min by car west of Chania.
Hours: Daily 9:00–19:00

name: Gramvousa Fort
area: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
description: A 1580s Venetian fortress atop Imeri Gramvousa island that held out against the Ottomans until 1692. It later became a notorious pirate base during the Greek War of Independence. The steep 20-minute climb rewards you with views over Balos.
tags: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included with Balos-Gramvousa boat tours (book ahead)
Getting there: Boat only, from Kissamos port on Balos-Gramvousa tours. A full-day trip on a port call.

name: Archaeological Site of Falasarna
area: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
description: The remains of a Hellenistic port city whose harbour was lifted about 6.5 m out of the sea by the 365 AD earthquake. Towers, quays and mooring stones are still visible, and a VR app shows the city as it was.
tags: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: North end of Falasarna, about 1 hr 15 min by car from Chania. The last stretch is a bumpy dirt road; you can park and walk 10 min.
Hours: Fri–Mon 8:30–15:30; closed Tue–Thu

name: Acropolis of Polyrrinia
area: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
description: The hilltop acropolis of an ancient city-state founded around the 8th century BC, with walls, cisterns and aqueducts still in use. A chapel was built partly from inscribed ancient stones. Views over the Kissamos gulf are spectacular.
tags: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Polyrrinia village above Kissamos, about 1 hr 10 min by car from Chania. The final road is narrow and steep; park in the village and climb on foot.

name: Archaeological Museum of Kissamos
area: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
description: Housed in the Venetian governor's palace, this museum displays finds from ancient Kissamos, Polyrrinia and Falasarna. A restored Roman mosaic floor is the highlight. Entry about €5.
tags: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €5)
Getting there: Stratigou Tzanakaki Square, Kissamos; about 1 hour by car from Chania.
Hours: Mon & Wed–Sun 8:30–15:30; closed Tue

name: Chrysoskalitissa Monastery
area: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
description: A clifftop convent of the 'Golden Step,' named for a legendary golden stair, with a small Byzantine museum and a secret-school room from the Ottoman era. It overlooks the Libyan Sea near Elafonissi. Knees must be covered.
tags: The Far West: Kissamos, Balos & Falasarna
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €2.50)
Getting there: About 1 hr 50 min by car from Chania, 10 min from Elafonissi; limited free parking.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–19:30; Sun 7:30–19:30

name: Frangokastello Castle
description: A square Venetian fortress built in 1371–74 to control Sfakia and deter pirates. It was the site of an 1828 battle whose ghostly 'Drosoulites' are said to appear at dawn in late May. Free, with access to the central courtyard only.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Frangokastello, about 2 hours by car from Chania.
Hours: Mon & Wed–Sun 10:00–18:00; closed Tue

name: Ancient Lissos (via Lissos Gorge Trail)
description: A hike from Sougia through a gorge and over the headland to the ruins of ancient Lissos, a Greco-Roman healing sanctuary of Asklepios with mosaic floors. Hikers often return by boat.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; boat back to Sougia about €6 cash
Getting there: Trail starts at Sougia harbour, about 1 hr 20 min by car from Chania; allow 1–1.5 hours each way. Bring water.

name: Eleftherios Venizelos' Birth House
description: The modest family house in Mournies where Venizelos was born in 1864, now run by his foundation with illustrated displays on his early life. It complements his Halepa residence.
mapQuery: Eleftherios Venizelos Birth House Mournies Chania
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Mournies, about 10 min by car south of Chania.
Hours: Tue–Sat 10:00–13:30; closed Sun–Mon

name: Museum of National Resistance 1941–1945
description: A small museum in Theriso, the village that served as headquarters of Venizelos' 1905 revolt. It documents the Cretan resistance during WWII through photographs and personal stories. Labels are mostly in Greek; entry about €1.
mapQuery: Museum of National Resistance Theriso Chania
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (about €1)
Getting there: Theriso village, about 30 min by car from Chania via the Therisos Gorge.

name: Old Fortress
description: The Venetian sea fortress on its own promontory, separated from town by a moat, layering Byzantine, Venetian and British history over 1,500 years. Climb past the clock tower for views over the Old Town, Vido Island and Albania. Stone paths are polished and slippery.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €10; card accepted)
Getting there: ~2 km (25 min walk, port shuttle or taxi) from the cruise terminal; bridge at the east end of Spianada.
Hours: Daily 8:00–19:00 (shorter winter hours)

name: Old Fortress Lighthouse
description: The lighthouse on the Old Fortress summit, reached by a steep final climb on slick cobbles, with the best 360° panorama in town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Old Fortress ticket
Getting there: Inside the Old Fortress.
Hours: Daily 8:00–15:00 (summit access)

name: Saint George's Church
description: A Doric-temple-style church built in 1840 inside the Old Fortress for the British garrison, Orthodox since 1865. Simple inside but striking against the sea.
mapQuery: Saint George's Church Old Fortress Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Old Fortress ticket
Getting there: Inside the Old Fortress, on its northern side.
Hours: Daily 8:00–20:00

name: Corfu Byzantine Collection
description: Byzantine and post-Byzantine icons and mosaics in the first building inside the Old Fortress.
mapQuery: Corfu Byzantine Collection Old Fortress Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Old Fortress ticket
Getting there: Inside the Old Fortress, right wing of the first building.
Hours: Daily 8:30–15:30

name: New Fortress
description: The 16th-century Venetian fortress above the Old Port, with tunnels, vaults and British barracks. Quieter than the Old Fortress and closest to the ship.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate
Getting there: ~15 min walk from the cruise terminal.
Hours: 8:30–15:30; closed Tuesday

name: Spianada Square
description: The vast square between the Old Town and Old Fortress, laid out as a Venetian firing ground and still home to a British-era cricket pitch.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Center of the Old Town.
Hours: Open square

name: Listón
description: The arcaded promenade built under French rule (1807–14) on the model of Paris's Rue de Rivoli.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: West side of Spianada.
Hours: Open arcade

name: Maitland Monument
description: An Ionic rotunda (1821) honoring Sir Thomas Maitland, first British High Commissioner.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: South end of Spianada.
Hours: Open

name: Corfu Museum of Asian Art
description: Housed in the neoclassical Palace of St Michael & St George, built in 1819 as the British High Commissioner's residence. Asian art over three floors; sea-view garden behind. No elevator.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €10)
Getting there: North end of Spianada.
Hours: Daily 8:00–20:00

name: Archaeological Museum of Corfu
description: Home of the archaic Gorgon pediment from the Temple of Artemis, one of the oldest stone pediments in Greece.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €10)
Getting there: Vrela Armeni 1, south of Spianada.
Hours: 8:00–20:00; closed Tuesday

name: Byzantine Museum of Antivouniotissa
description: A 15th-century church above the seafront walls, now a museum of Ionian icons and vestments.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €5)
Getting there: Arseniou 25 — climb the steps from the seafront. No parking nearby.
Hours: 8:30–15:00; closed Tuesday

name: Serbian Museum of Corfu
description: Tells the WWI story of some 150,000 Serbian soldiers and civilians who found refuge on Corfu in 1916. Free entry.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free; donations welcome
Getting there: Moustoxidi 19, Old Town.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:00–14:00; closed Sunday

name: Museum of Dionysios Solomos
description: The house of Greece's national poet and author of the national anthem, with manuscripts and his desk.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door
Getting there: Arseniou 1, Old Town seafront.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:30–14:00; closed weekends

name: Casa Parlante Museum
description: A 19th-century noble mansion presented as a living home on guided tours.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €10)
Getting there: Nikiforou Theotoki 16.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–18:00; closed Sunday

name: Banknote Museum of the Ionian Bank
description: Greek history told through its currency, free, in the Ionian Bank's historic building.
mapQuery: Banknote Museum of the Ionian Bank Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Nikiforou Theotoki 32.
Hours: Wed & Fri 9:00–14:00 & 17:30–20:30; Thu 9:00–15:00; Sat–Sun 8:30–15:00; closed Mon–Tue

name: V museum Corfu
description: A new (2025) interactive museum of Corfu's history with holograms and a 3D film.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door
Getting there: El. Venizelou, along the port road.
Hours: Daily 9:00–17:00

name: Holy Church of Saint Spyridon
description: The 16th-century church holding the relics of Corfu's patron saint, with the island's tallest bell tower. No photos inside.
mapQuery: Holy Church of Saint Spyridon Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Agiou Spiridonos.
Hours: Daily 7:00–20:00

name: Holy Metropolitan Church of the Virgin Mary Spilaiotissa, Saint Blaise and Saint Theodora Augusta
description: Corfu's Orthodox cathedral (1577), holding the relics of Empress St Theodora.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Mitropoleos 1, near the Old Port.

name: Catholic Metropolitan Church of Saints Jacob and Christopher (Domos)
description: Corfu's Catholic cathedral, founded in Venetian times on Town Hall Square.
mapQuery: Catholic Cathedral Saints Jacob and Christopher Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Town Hall Square (Plateia Dimarchiou).
Hours: Daily 10:00–22:00

name: Old Town Hall of Corfu (San Giacomo Theatre)
description: A 17th-century Venetian loggia that became Greece's first opera house.
mapQuery: Old Town Hall San Giacomo Theatre Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Exterior
Getting there: Town Hall Square.

name: Bell Tower of the Annunziata Holy Church
description: The lone surviving tower of a church destroyed in 1943, linked to Lepanto veterans.
mapQuery: Bell Tower of the Annunziata Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Vrachlioti 56.
Hours: Viewed from outside

name: Jewish Synagogue of Corfu
description: The surviving synagogue of Corfu's once-large Jewish community, deported in 1944. Free.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Velissariou 24.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–16:00; closed Sunday

name: Municipal Greek-British Cemetery of Corfu
description: A 19th-century garden cemetery with British and Commonwealth graves.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Kolokotroni 8.
Hours: Mon 8:00–13:00; Tue–Fri 9:00–13:00; closed weekends

name: Capodistrias Museum - Centre for Capodistrian Studies
description: The summer estate of Ioannis Kapodistrias, first Governor of Greece, with gardens and café.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door
Getting there: Evropouli, ~6 km west of town; taxi or bus.
Hours: Tue–Sat 10:00–16:00; closed Sun–Mon

name: Mon Repos Park
description: The wooded estate around the 1828 villa where Prince Philip was born, laid over the ruins of ancient Palaiopolis, the original city of Corfu. Free trails lead to temple remains and a small pebble beach.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free park entry
Getting there: Analipsi, ~2 km south of Spianada along the seafront (25 min walk or taxi).
Hours: Daily 8:00–21:00 (gates lock)

name: Ancient Greek Doric Temple of Kardaki
description: The best-preserved ancient temple remains on Corfu, a 6th-century BC Doric temple of unknown dedication hidden in Mon Repos park. Free, signposted, about 10 minutes' walk from the park gate.
mapQuery: Ancient Greek Doric Temple of Kardaki Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Inside Mon Repos Park — enter only via the main park gate.
Hours: Daily 8:00–21:00 (park hours)

name: Holy Church of the Holy Apostles Jason and Sosipater
description: Corfu's oldest church and most important Middle Byzantine monument, built around 1000 AD from ancient stones, with uncovered fresco fragments.
mapQuery: Holy Apostles Jason and Sosipater Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Anemomylos, ~20 min walk south of Spianada.

name: Holy Monastery of Panagia Vlacherna
description: The 17th-century white monastery on an islet joined to Kanoni by a causeway, facing Mouse Island and its Byzantine chapel.
mapQuery: Holy Monastery of Panagia Vlacherna Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Kanoni, ~5 km south of town (taxi 15 min or bus no. 2).
Hours: Daily 8:00–23:00

name: The Achilleion Palace
description: Empress Sisi's 1890s palace, later Kaiser Wilhelm II's, with Achilles statues and terraced gardens. Interior largely closed for restoration.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate
Getting there: Gastouri, ~10 km south of town (25 min by taxi or tour).
Hours: Daily 8:00–20:00

name: Church of the Hypapante at Gouvia
area: Gouvia, Dassia & the Northeast Resort Strip
description: A tiny chapel on a spit in Gouvia Bay with carved wooden icons of the apostles. Interior opens evenings.
mapQuery: Church of the Hypapante Gouvia Corfu
tags: Gouvia, Dassia & the Northeast Resort Strip
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Limni/Gouvia, ~8 km north of town; small parking area.
Hours: Interior daily 17:00–22:00

name: Holy Monastery of the Virgin Mary at Paleokastritsa
description: A monastery founded in 1225 on a headland above Paleokastritsa, with a small museum of icons and sea finds. Modest dress; wraps lent free.
mapQuery: Holy Monastery of the Virgin Mary Paleokastritsa Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free; donation welcome
Getting there: ~25 km (40 min) north-west of town; small free car park near the top.
Hours: Daily 6:30–12:45 & 15:00–19:00

name: Angelokastro Byzantine Castle
description: A 13th-century Byzantine castle on a sheer crag that never fell to Ottoman sieges. Short steep climb; little shade.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €10)
Getting there: Above Krini, ~6 km north of Paleokastritsa via a narrow road.
Hours: 10:00–17:30; closed Tuesday

name: Observatory of Kaiser Wilhelm II
description: The Kaiser's Throne lookout above Pelekas, where Wilhelm II watched sunsets; 360° views.
mapQuery: Observatory of Kaiser Wilhelm II Pelekas Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Pelekas, ~13 km west of town; limited parking fills near sunset.
Hours: Open viewpoint

name: Kassiopi Byzantine Castle
description: Overgrown ruins of a Byzantine-Angevin fortress above Kassiopi harbor, free, with shaded paths.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Kassiopi, ~36 km (1 hr) north of town.
Hours: Open site

name: Church of the Panagia Kassopitra
description: Kassiopi's historic church, built over an ancient temple of Zeus. Free.
mapQuery: Church of the Panagia Kassopitra Kassiopi Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Kassiopi village, below the castle.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–14:00; Sun 8:00–11:00

name: Old Peritheia
description: A Venetian-era stone village on Pantokrator's slopes, abandoned and now revived with tavernas.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Via Loutses; take the paved northern route.
Hours: Tavernas roughly 9:30–23:00

name: Monastery of Pantokrator
description: The monastery atop Corfu's highest peak, with a painted ceiling. Free.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Summit of Mount Pantokrator; limited parking.
Hours: Daily 10:00–19:00

name: The White House Restaurant
description: Lawrence Durrell's 1930s home on Kalami Bay, now a restaurant.
mapQuery: The White House Restaurant Kalami Corfu
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended for dinner — +30 2663 091465
Getting there: Kalami Bay, ~30 km north of town.

name: Museum Kouris
description: A private folk-life museum in Lefkimmi with a personal owner-led tour. Free.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free — +30 698 844 7799
Getting there: Lefkimmi, ~45 km (1 hr) south of town.
Hours: Daily 10:00–17:00

name: Agios Nikolaos Castle
description: A ruined Venetian fortress on the islet guarding Gaios harbor on Paxos. Visitor access is restricted.
details: Getting there: Paxos, ~1 hr by boat from Corfu; islet reached only by private boat.

name: Dubrovnik City Walls
description: Medieval walls (mostly 12th–17th century) running nearly 2 km around the Old Town, among the best-preserved fortifications in Europe and the core of the UNESCO site. The full loop takes 1.5–2 hours, with views over terracotta roofs, forts and sea, plus cafés and free toilets along the way.
details:
Reservations / tickets: About €40 standalone, or the Dubrovnik Pass (similar price) which adds Lovrijenac, the Rector's Palace and more. Book online to skip queues.
Getting there: Main entrance inside Pile Gate; others near Ploče Gate and St John's Fortress. From Gruž cruise port, take bus 1A/1B/3/8 or a taxi to Pile (about 15 min).
Hours: Daily from 8:00; closing 17:30–19:30 depending on season

name: Pile Gate
description: The 15th-century main western gate, with a stone bridge, a former drawbridge and a statue of St Blaise, the city's patron, above the arch. The classic entry onto the Stradun.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Bus terminus at Pile, about 15 min from Gruž port.
Hours: Open access

name: Ploče Gate
description: The eastern gate complex, with a 13th-century inner gate, Gothic quatrefoil openings and a bridge to Fort Revelin. Quieter than Pile, with harbour views.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: East side of the Old Town.
Hours: Open access

name: Buža Gate
description: The small northern gate opened in the land walls in 1907, a quiet shortcut from the upper Old Town to the cable car.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Top of the northern Old Town lanes.
Hours: Open access

name: Stradun (Stari grad Dubrovnik)
description: The limestone main street, rebuilt in uniform Baroque style after the 1667 earthquake and polished smooth by centuries of footsteps. Magical early morning and after the cruise crowds leave.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Runs from Pile Gate to Luža Square.
Hours: Open access

name: Onofrio's Large Fountain
description: Domed 1438 fountain by Onofrio della Cava, the end point of an aqueduct that still brings cold, drinkable spring water through 16 carved masks.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Just inside Pile Gate.
Hours: Open access

name: Small Onofrio's Fountain
description: Elegant 1442 companion fountain on Luža Square, delicately carved and still flowing with fresh water.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Luža Square, by the Sponza Palace.
Hours: Open access

name: Clock Tower of Dubrovnik
description: 31 m bell tower from 1444 on Luža Square, with a moon-phase dial and bronze 'jacks' striking the hours. Rebuilt in 1929; lovely lit at night.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Luža Square, end of the Stradun.
Hours: Open access

name: Orlando's Column
description: 1418 statue of the knight Roland, symbol of the Ragusan Republic's freedom, where decrees were proclaimed and cloth was measured by the 51.2 cm 'Ragusan cubit' at its base. May be under restoration.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Luža Square, in front of St Blaise's Church.
Hours: Open access

name: Franciscan Church and Monastery
description: 14th-century monastery with a Romanesque cloister and one of Europe's oldest working pharmacies (since 1317). Shell damage from 6 December 1991 is still visible.
details:
Reservations / tickets: About €8, or included in the Dubrovnik Pass
Getting there: Just inside Pile Gate.
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:00

name: Sponza Palace
description: Gothic-Renaissance former customs house and mint, one of few buildings to survive the 1667 earthquake, now holding the State Archives and a memorial room to the city's 1991–95 defenders.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Courtyard free; small fee for some exhibits
Getting there: Luža Square.
Hours: Mon–Fri 8:15–15:00; Sat 8:15–13:00; closed Sun

name: Rector's Palace
description: Gothic-Renaissance seat of the Ragusan Republic's rector, now the Cultural History Museum, with period rooms, a dungeon and an arcaded courtyard and stairs familiar from Game of Thrones.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket on site or Dubrovnik Pass
Getting there: Pred Dvorom, beside the Cathedral.
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:00

name: The Cathedral of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary
description: Baroque cathedral built 1672–1713 on the site of earlier basilicas, with a Titian polyptych and a treasury holding St Blaise's reliquaries.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free; small fee for the treasury
Getting there: Between the Rector's Palace and the Old Port. Use the side entrance if the facade is scaffolded.
Hours: Mon–Sat 8:00–19:00; Sun 11:30–19:00

name: Saint Blaise's Church
description: Baroque church (1706–15) of the city's patron, holding a 15th-century gilt-silver statue of St Blaise with a model of pre-earthquake Dubrovnik. Free.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Luža Square.
Hours: Daily 8:00–12:00 & 16:30–19:00

name: Dominican Monastery
description: 14th–15th-century Gothic monastery with a graceful cloister and a museum of Ragusan religious art, goldwork and manuscripts. The church may be under renovation.
details:
Reservations / tickets: About €6
Getting there: Ulica Svetog Dominika, by Ploče Gate.
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:00

name: Church of St. Ignatius
description: Jesuit Baroque church completed in 1725, with illusionistic apse frescoes, set at the top of the Jesuit Stairs. Free.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Top of the Jesuit Stairs from Gundulić Square.

name: Jesuit Stairs
description: 1738 Baroque stairway inspired by Rome's Spanish Steps, famous from Cersei's walk of shame in Game of Thrones. Quietest early or after 17:00.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Gundulić Square up to St Ignatius.
Hours: Open access

name: Monument of Ivan Gundulić
description: Statue of Dubrovnik's great Baroque poet on Gundulić Square, with reliefs of scenes from his epic 'Osman'. A morning produce and craft market fills the square around it.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Gundulić Square, behind the Rector's Palace.
Hours: Open access; market Mon–Sat 7:00–18:00

name: Serbian Orthodox Church of the Annunciation
description: Neo-Byzantine church from 1877, damaged in the 1991 siege and restored in 2009, with a richly decorated iconostasis. An icon shop and small museum sit next door.
mapQuery: Serbian Orthodox Church of the Annunciation Dubrovnik
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Ulica od Puča 8, near Pile Gate.
Hours: Daily 8:00–18:00

name: Fort Lovrijenac
description: 11th-century-origin fortress on a 37 m sea rock outside the walls, the 'Gibraltar of Dubrovnik', whose motto above the gate declares freedom is not to be sold. Red Keep in Game of Thrones; about 200 steps.
details:
Reservations / tickets: About €15–17; included with the City Walls ticket and Dubrovnik Pass
Getting there: 10 min walk west of Pile Gate.
Hours: Daily 8:00–17:30

name: Fort Minčeta
description: Round 15th-century tower by Michelozzo and Juraj Dalmatinac at the walls' highest point, with the best view over the whole Old Town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included with City Walls ticket
Getting there: North-west corner of the walls circuit.
Hours: Follows walls hours

name: Fort Bokar
description: 15th-century casemated bastion by Michelozzo, guarding Pile Gate from the cliff edge, one of the oldest preserved of its kind in Europe.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included with City Walls ticket
Getting there: South-west corner of the walls circuit.
Hours: Follows walls hours

name: Fort Revelin
description: Massive 16th-century fortress built against a Venetian threat to guard the land approach to Ploče. It now hosts exhibitions and the Culture Club Revelin nightclub.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Exterior free; tickets for exhibits and the club
Getting there: Just outside Ploče Gate.

name: Old Port of Dubrovnik
description: The Republic's walled harbour, guarded by St John's Fortress and once home to its arsenal, now busy with fishing boats and ferries to Lokrum and Cavtat.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; boat tickets dockside
Getting there: Through Ploče or the Ponte Gate.
Hours: Open access

name: Lazareti
description: Chain of 17th-century quarantine buildings outside Ploče where Ragusa isolated incoming traders, a pioneering public-health system against plague. It now hosts an exhibition, cultural events and concerts.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Small entry fee; discount with Dubrovnik Pass
Getting there: Frana Supila 8, about 3 min walk east of Ploče Gate.

name: War Photo Limited
description: Gallery of conflict photojournalism with a permanent exhibit on the 1990s Yugoslav wars and the siege of Dubrovnik. Sobering and essential context.
details:
Reservations / tickets: About €10
Getting there: Antuninska street off the Stradun.
Hours: Daily 10:00–16:00

name: Homeland War Museum
description: Inside Fort Imperial, built by Napoleon's forces in 1806–12 and held by a handful of defenders throughout the 1991–92 siege, with photos, footage and weaponry. Rooftop views are spectacular.
details:
Reservations / tickets: About €5
Getting there: Top of Mount Srđ by cable car (about €30 return), or about 45 min up the zigzag trail.
Hours: Daily 8:30–22:00

name: Benedictine Monastery of St. Mary
description: Ruined Benedictine monastery on Lokrum, founded in 1023, later remodelled by Archduke Maximilian of Habsburg. It holds exhibits on the island's history and legends, a cloister garden and the Game of Thrones Iron Throne.
mapQuery: Benedictine Monastery of St. Mary Lokrum Dubrovnik
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in Lokrum entry (about €27–30 with boat)
Getting there: Short walk from the Lokrum ferry landing. Ferries about 15 min from the Old Port, seasonal; no overnight stays, so check the last boat.

name: Fort Royal
description: Star fort built by the French in 1806 and expanded by the Austrians on Lokrum's summit, with panoramic views over the island and Old Town after a 15–20 min rocky climb.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in Lokrum entry
Getting there: Lokrum island, uphill from the ferry landing.
Hours: Daily 9:00–19:00

name: Lokrum Quarantine Station (Lazaret)
description: Walls of an unfinished 1627 quarantine complex begun to isolate the sick from plague, now enclosing a quiet olive grove on Lokrum's far side. Little remains, but the history is striking.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in Lokrum entry
Getting there: Lokrum, beyond Fort Royal on the island trail.

name: Petar Sorkočević Summerhouse
description: 16th-century Renaissance summer villa of a Ragusan noble family on the Lapad waterfront, a fine example of the ljetnikovac country-house tradition outside the walls. It now houses an institute, so access is limited.
details: Getting there: Lapadska obala 4, a 10 min walk from Gruž cruise port along the bay.

name: Mausoleum of the Račić Family
description: Ivan Meštrović's 1920s white-stone mausoleum on the hill above Cavtat, a masterpiece of carved symbolism.
details:
Reservations / tickets: About €4
Getting there: Cavtat, about 30 min by bus 10 or car, or about 45 min by water taxi from the Old Port; a short uphill walk. Roughly a half-day commitment.

name: Bukovac House Museum
description: Birthplace of Vlaho Bukovac, Croatia's great 19th-century painter, with his works, original furniture and murals he painted on the walls as a youth, including the Blue Room.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket on site; included in the Dubrovnik Pass (7-day)
Getting there: Bukovčeva 5, a few steps from Cavtat's harbour.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–18:00; Sun 10:00–14:00

name: Church of Our Lady of the Snows
description: Church of Cavtat's 15th-century Franciscan monastery on the harbour, with a herb-planted cloister, a historic organ and Renaissance altarpieces.
mapQuery: Church of Our Lady of the Snows Cavtat
details:
Reservations / tickets: Small fee for the cloister
Getting there: End of Cavtat's harbourfront by the Rat peninsula.
Hours: Daily 7:00–21:00

name: Sokol Grad
description: Fortress grafted onto a rock spur in the Konavle hills, a key Ragusan border stronghold, now with a small museum and sweeping valley views. Many steps.
details:
Reservations / tickets: About €10 adults, €5 children
Getting there: Dunave, Konavle, about 50 min by car; no practical bus. A half-day commitment.
Hours: Daily 8:00–19:00 (seasonal)

name: Konavle County Museum
description: Folk heritage museum with Konavle's famous embroidery, costumes and silk-making traditions, best paired with the Sunday Čilipi folklore show.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket on site
Getting there: Čilipi, about 35 min by car, or Sunday bus 99 from Cavtat. A half-day commitment.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:00–17:00; Sun 9:00–13:00

name: Trsteno Arboretum
description: Renaissance garden of the Gučetić noble family, laid out around 1494, with a Baroque Neptune fountain, old olive mill and aqueduct; the Red Keep gardens in Game of Thrones.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate; cash only
Getting there: Trsteno, about 25 min by car or bus 12/15 north of Dubrovnik. A small car park at the upper entrance. A half-day commitment.
Hours: Daily 7:00–19:00 (shorter in winter)

name: Walls of Ston
description: Begun in 1333 to protect the Republic's precious salt pans, these 5.5 km walls are Europe's longest fortification system after Hadrian's Wall. A steep, rewarding climb.
details:
Reservations / tickets: About €10
Getting there: Ston, about 1 hr by car. Entrances in Ston and Mali Ston. Go early in summer. A half-day commitment.
Hours: Daily 8:00–17:30 (seasonal)

name: Solana Ston
description: Salt pans worked since Roman times and the source of Ragusa's wealth, still harvested by hand. A short film explains the centuries-old process.
details:
Reservations / tickets: About €5
Getting there: Entrance of Ston town.
Hours: Daily 8:00–20:00

name: Old Town Kotor
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: UNESCO-listed walled medieval and Venetian town at the head of the Bay of Kotor, a maze of squares, palaces and churches beneath the mountain.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Usually by day tour
Getting there: Montenegro, about 2–2.5 hrs each way with a border crossing (passport). A full-day trip.
Hours: Open access

name: Saint Nicholas' Church Perast
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: Perast's parish church with a 55 m bell tower from 1691 that can be climbed for bay views, Baroque altars and a small treasury.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Small fee for the tower
Getting there: Perast waterfront, Bay of Kotor.

name: Old Bridge Mostar
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: 1566 Ottoman bridge by Mimar Hayruddin, destroyed in 1993 and rebuilt with original techniques in 2004. Divers still leap from it into the Neretva. UNESCO-listed.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Usually by day tour
Getting there: Bosnia and Herzegovina, about 2.5–3 hrs each way with border crossings (passport). A full-day trip.
Hours: Open access

name: Mostar Old Town
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: Ottoman bazaar quarter (Kujundžiluk) of cobbled lanes, coppersmiths, mosques and riverside cafés around the bridge. Best before tour groups arrive.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Around Stari Most.
Hours: Open access

name: Old Bridge Museum
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: Museum in the Tara Tower and archaeological levels below, covering the bridge's history, destruction and reconstruction, with framed views from the tower.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: About €10
Getting there: East end of the Old Bridge.
Hours: Daily 8:00–16:00

name: Halebija Tower
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: 17th-century Ottoman guard tower on the bridge's west bank, once a prison and lookout, now home to the bridge divers' club.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: West end of the Old Bridge.
Hours: Open access

name: Koski Mehmed Pasha Mosque
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: 1617–18 Ottoman mosque restored after the war; its minaret, up about 86 narrow steps, gives the famous view of the Old Bridge. Modest dress; closed to visitors at prayer times.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: About 10 KM entry, 15 KM with minaret
Getting there: Mala Tepa, a few steps north of the bridge.
Hours: Daily 9:00–20:30 (except prayer times)

name: Kajtaz House
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: Mostar's oldest Ottoman family house, owned by the same family for over 400 years, with original furnishings and a walled garden, shown personally by the family.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: About €5 or 10 KM, cash only
Getting there: Gaše Ilića, a 5 min walk from the Old Bridge.
Hours: Mon–Fri 10:30–17:00; Sat–Sun 10:00–17:00

name: Blagaj Tekke
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: 16th-century dervish lodge built against a sheer cliff at the source of the Buna River, an atmospheric Ottoman spiritual site.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Small entrance fee; parking fee in the village
Getting there: Blagaj, about 20–30 min from Mostar; usually combined with Mostar tours.
Hours: Daily 8:30–20:30

name: Počitelj Fortress
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: Hillside Ottoman fortified village above the Neretva, with the Gavrankapetan tower, a 16th-century mosque, hammam and free wandering with valley views.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Near Čapljina, about 30 min south of Mostar; steep, uneven paths.
Hours: Open access

name: Počitelj Clocktower (Sahat-kula)
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: Ottoman clock tower high above Počitelj village, worth the climb for valley vistas even though the tower itself is closed.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Upper Počitelj, above the mosque.
Hours: Open access

name: Korčula Town Gate
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: Grand stepped Land Gate and Revelin tower leading into Korčula's medieval walled town, laid out in a fish-bone street plan to tame the winds.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Catamaran ticket
Getting there: Korčula, about 2–2.5 hrs by catamaran from Dubrovnik. A full-day trip.
Hours: Open access

name: Saint Mark's Cathedral
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: 15th-century Gothic-Renaissance cathedral with a whimsical carved portal and a tight bell-tower climb to 360-degree views.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: About €3; bell tower about €5 extra
Getting there: Main square, Korčula Old Town.

name: Korčula City Fortifications
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: Venetian-era walls and round towers ringing Korčula's peninsula, including the Great Governor's Tower on the waterfront.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Around Korčula Old Town.
Hours: Open access

name: Kanavelić Tower
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: Semi-circular 1480s defensive tower (Barbarigo) at the northern corner of Korčula's walls, the start of the walk along the ramparts.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: North tip of Korčula Old Town.

name: Marko Polo Centar
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: Exhibition and film on Marco Polo, whom local tradition says was born on Korčula, with a lookout toward the cathedral. Reviews are mixed on content.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket on site
Getting there: Ulica Depolo, Korčula Old Town.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:00–15:00; closed Sat–Sun

name: Saint Mary's Island
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: Islet in Mljet's Great Lake with a 12th-century Benedictine monastery and church, reached by the national park boat.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in Mljet park ticket (about €20)
Getting there: Mljet National Park, about 1.5–2 hrs by catamaran from Dubrovnik. A full-day trip.

name: Roman Palace Polače
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: Substantial ruins of a 5th-century late-Roman palace at Polače harbour on Mljet, among the largest Roman remains on the Croatian islands.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Polače, Mljet National Park, beside the harbour road.
Hours: Open access

name: Archaeological Site of Olympia
description: The UNESCO-listed sanctuary of Zeus where the Olympic Games began in 776 BC. You walk among temples, treasuries, the athletes' gymnasium and palaestra, and the original stadium. Allow about 3 hours together with the museum; there is shade, but midday is hot.
tags: verify: seasonal hours on cruise date
details:
Reservations / tickets: Combined ticket (about €20) for the site and museums; buy online at hhticket.gr to skip the ticket queue
Getting there: About 40 km (40–50 min) from the port by taxi, coach or the seasonal Katakolon–Olympia train. This is a half-day trip; arrive early to beat the cruise crowds.
Hours: Summer approx. 8:00–20:00; shorter winter hours from November

name: Archaeological Museum of Olympia
