description: One of Greece's finest museums. Highlights include the Temple of Zeus pediments, Praxiteles' Hermes, the Nike of Paionios, and the helmets and bronzes dedicated at the sanctuary. Visit it before the ruins to help picture what once stood there.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the combined site ticket
Getting there: Next to the archaeological site in Ancient Olympia. Half-day trip from the port.
Hours: Daily approx. 8:00–20:00 in summer

name: Temple of Zeus
description: The massive platform of the 5th-century BC temple that housed Phidias' gold-and-ivory Zeus, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Fallen column drums lie where earthquakes dropped them, and a single re-erected column shows the original scale.
mapQuery: Temple of Zeus, Ancient Olympia, Katakolon
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the site ticket
Getting there: In the center of the Altis, the sacred precinct of the archaeological site. Half-day trip.
Hours: Follows site hours

name: Temple of Hera
description: One of the oldest monumental Doric temples in Greece, built around 600 BC. The Olympic flame is still lit at the altar in front of it for every modern Games.
mapQuery: Temple of Hera, Ancient Olympia, Katakolon
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the site ticket
Getting there: Northern edge of the Altis, inside the archaeological site. Half-day trip.
Hours: Follows site hours

name: Philippeion
description: An elegant circular Ionic memorial begun by Philip II of Macedon after Chaeronea (338 BC) and completed by Alexander the Great. Several columns have been re-erected, and it is the only round building in the sanctuary.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the site ticket
Getting there: Beside the Temple of Hera, inside the archaeological site. Half-day trip.
Hours: Follows site hours

name: Stadium at Olympia
description: The original Olympic stadium, entered through the vaulted Krypte tunnel the athletes used. Its stone start and finish lines survive, and visitors still race the 192-meter track.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the site ticket
Getting there: Eastern end of the archaeological site. Half-day trip.
Hours: Follows site hours

name: Museum of the History of the Olympic Games of Antiquity
description: A neoclassical building (the old museum) devoted to the ancient Games and their events, athletes, prizes and rituals, with clear multilingual displays. It is included in the site ticket.
mapQuery: Museum of the History of the Olympic Games of antiquity, Katakolon
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the combined ticket
Getting there: Praxiteli Kondyli 4, Ancient Olympia village — short walk from the site. Half-day trip.
Hours: Daily approx. 8:00–20:00 in summer

name: Archimedes Museum
description: A free, hands-on museum of working reconstructions of Archimedes' inventions and other ancient Greek technology, demonstrated by staff in several languages. It is a hit with families.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; donation requested
Getting there: Praxiteli Kondyli 9, center of Ancient Olympia village. Half-day trip.
Hours: Daily 10:00–20:00

name: International Olympic Academy
description: The academic heart of the modern Olympic movement, founded in 1961. Its grounds hold the marble stele containing Pierre de Coubertin's heart. It is primarily an educational campus, so public access is limited.
tags: verify: public access to Coubertin stele
details: Getting there: About 1 km east of the archaeological site. Half-day trip.

name: Museum of Ancient Greek Technology Kostas Kotsanas
description: Working replicas of ancient Greek inventions: automata, the Antikythera mechanism, clocks and siege engines, demonstrated by enthusiastic staff. It is the best historical stop if you stay in port.
mapQuery: Museum of Ancient Greek Technology Kostas Kotsanas, Katakolon
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; donation requested
Getting there: On the main road at the edge of the village, about a 5-minute walk from the pier.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:30–15:30; closed Sunday

name: Katakolo Lighthouse
description: A historic 19th-century stone lighthouse on the headland south of the village. It is closed to visitors and only partly visible from the road, so treat it as a quick walking detour.
details: Getting there: About 1 km south of the port along the headland road.

name: Archaeological Museum of Pyrgos
description: Housed in Pyrgos' restored 19th-century municipal market hall, it traces Ilia's history from the Stone Age through Mycenaean, Roman and Byzantine times. Rare finds include a Mycenaean writing stylus. It is quiet and uncrowded.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; small entry fee
Getting there: Karaiskaki 10, central Pyrgos — about 20 min from the port by taxi or bus.
Hours: Tue–Sun 8:30–15:30; closed Monday

name: Holy Metropolitan Church of Saint Nicholas
description: Pyrgos' imposing historic cathedral, dominating the hill of the old Eparchio above the main square. It is an architectural landmark of the town.
mapQuery: Holy Metropolitan Church of Saint Nicholas, Pyrgos, Katakolon
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; dress modestly
Getting there: Beside Karagiorga Square, central Pyrgos.

name: Apollo Theater
description: A neoclassical 1880s theater, said to have been designed by Ernst Ziller and modeled on Paris's Opéra-Comique, that still stages plays and films. The facade is the main draw; the interior is dated.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Performance tickets via the theater (+30 2621 036521)
Getting there: Sillaidopoulou 2, central Pyrgos.

name: Archaeological Site of Ancient Elis
description: The ruins of the city-state that organized the ancient Olympic Games, where athletes trained for a month before competing. You can see the theater, agora and gymnasium remains across a large, quiet site that is still being excavated.
mapQuery: Archaeological Site of Ancient Elis, Katakolon
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the site or combined with the museum
Getting there: Ilida, about 15 km northeast of Amaliada/Kourouta — 40 min from the port by car. Half-day trip.
Hours: Daily 8:30–16:00

name: Archaeological Museum of Ancient Elis
description: A bright modern museum at the foot of the Elis acropolis, with finds from prehistoric tools to Roman statues, plus mammoth remains found locally. Visit it first to make sense of the site.
mapQuery: Archaeological Museum of Ancient Elis, Katakolon
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the museum (about €4)
Getting there: About a 5-minute drive from the archaeological site; disabled parking with lift. Half-day trip.
Hours: Daily 8:30–15:30

name: Monastery of Panagia Fragkavilla
description: A Byzantine church traditionally dated to the 11th century, set within rocky walls and gardens on the edge of Amaliada. It is one of the region's most important medieval monuments.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; dress modestly
Getting there: About 1.5 km from Amaliada center, 10 min inland from Kourouta beach. Half-day trip.

name: Moni Agiou Athanasiou
description: A centuries-old monastery, now a nunnery, near Ampelokampos, whose history runs back before Ottoman rule, including a massacre of its monks and its 19th-century refounding. The welcome is peaceful and warm.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; modest dress
Getting there: About 10 min north of Kourouta by car. Half-day trip.
Hours: Mon–Fri 7:00–12:00, 17:00–20:00; closed Sat–Sun per listing

name: Frankish Castle of Chlemoutsi
area: Further Afield: Kaiafa Lake & Spa Coast
description: A 13th-century Crusader fortress built by the Villehardouin princes of Achaea, superbly restored with museum exhibits on Frankish Greece and 360° rooftop views to Zakynthos.
tags: Further Afield: Kaiafa Lake & Spa Coast
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket about €5 at the gate
Getting there: Kastro, near Kyllini and the Loutra Kyllinis spa coast — about 55 km north of the port (1 hr). Half-day trip.
Hours: 9:00–16:00; closed Tuesday

name: Temple of Apollo Epicurius at Bassae
area: Further Afield: Kaiafa Lake & Spa Coast
description: A UNESCO World Heritage 5th-century BC temple set at 1,130 m in the Arcadian mountains, attributed to Iktinos (architect of the Parthenon) and among the best-preserved in Greece. It currently stands under a protective tent.
mapQuery: Temple of Apollo Epicurius at Bassae, Katakolon
tags: Further Afield: Kaiafa Lake & Spa Coast
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the site (about €6–10)
Getting there: About 100 km from the port via narrow, winding mountain roads (about 2 hr each way). Only realistic on a long port call or an overnight stay.
Hours: Daily 8:00–20:00 (site area to 19:30)

name: Cathedral of Saint Tryphon
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: Consecrated in 1166 and rebuilt after the 1667 and 1979 earthquakes, Kotor's Romanesque cathedral is one of the oldest in the Adriatic. It holds a silver altar, a carved ciborium, fresco fragments and a treasury of relics upstairs, whose balcony overlooks the square. Entry about €4.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €4)
Getting there: St Tryphon Square, center of the Old Town; about 5 min walk from the cruise pier via the Sea Gate.
Hours: Daily 9:00–19:00 (Thu to 18:00)

name: Saint Luke's Church
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: Built in 1195 under Stefan Nemanja, this small Romanesque-Byzantine church survived every major earthquake. For two centuries it held both Catholic and Orthodox altars, a symbol of Kotor's religious coexistence. Free entry.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: St Luke's Square, Old Town.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:00–19:00; Sat 8:00–19:00; Sun 11:00–19:00

name: Saint Nicholas' Church
description: The Serbian Orthodox church of 1902–1909, built after its predecessor burned on Christmas Eve 1896, with twin domed bell towers and a fine iconostasis. It anchors the Orthodox side of St Luke's Square.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: St Luke's Square, Old Town.
Hours: Daily 9:00–20:00

name: Church of St. Mary Collegiate
description: Built in 1221 on the site of a 6th-century basilica, this church holds the incorrupt body of Blessed Ozana of Kotor. It is known for its 20th-century bronze relief doors and remnants of 16th-century frescoes. A small museum costs about €4.
mapQuery: Church of St. Mary Collegiate Kotor
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; museum about €4
Getting there: By the River (North) Gate, Old Town.

name: Sea Gate
description: The main gate of the Old Town, built in 1555 under Venetian rule, with relief carvings including the winged lion of St Mark and a later inscription commemorating 1944 liberation. It faces the cruise pier.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Directly in front of the cruise pier.

name: River Gate (North Gate)
description: A 16th-century Venetian gate beside the Škurda River, commemorating Kotor's resistance to the 1539 Ottoman siege by Barbarossa. Its stone bridge over the clear spring river is especially atmospheric at night.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: North end of the Old Town by the Škurda River.

name: Gurdić Bastion & Gate
description: The southern bastion and gate of the town walls, the only gate with a drawbridge, fronted by a spring-fed pool. It has the most distinctive curved design of Kotor's three gates.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: South end of the Old Town, near the bus station.

name: Clock Tower
description: A slightly leaning 1602 clock tower on the Square of Arms. In front stands a stone pillory where offenders were once displayed. It is the first landmark through the Sea Gate.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Square of Arms, just inside the Sea Gate.

name: Kotor Town Walls
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: About 4.5 km of fortifications built from the 9th to the 19th century, mostly under Venice, enclosing the town and climbing the cliff. They are a core part of the UNESCO listing. The lower ramparts can be walked free in about 20 minutes.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (lower walls free)
Getting there: Access near the North and Gurdić gates.

name: Kotor Fortress (San Giovanni)
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: The fortress of St John crowning the walls 260 m above town, reached by about 1,350 uneven steps. It was occupied from Illyrian and Byzantine times through the Austro-Hungarian era. Plan 1.5–2 hours round trip; there is no shade or toilets.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket about €15 at the gate machine or online
Getting there: Ticketed entrances in the Old Town near the North Gate and behind St Mary's. Go early or late; grippy shoes.
Hours: Ticketed approximately 8:00–20:00

name: Church of Our Lady of Remedy
description: A small Renaissance chapel halfway up the fortress walls, built by survivors of a 16th-century plague. It is the natural rest point on the climb, with views over the rooftops. Reached within the ticketed fortress route.
mapQuery: Church of Our Lady of Remedy Kotor
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the fortress ticket (about €15)
Getting there: Partway up the San Giovanni stairway.

name: Ladder of Kotor
description: A historic Austro-Hungarian-era mule track zigzagging up the mountain behind the fortress, once the main trade route between Kotor and Cetinje. It is free to hike. The old window shortcut into the fortress is now sealed.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Trailhead north of the Old Town on the road behind the walls. Allow about 1.5 hours round trip to the cheese-and-drinks hut; loose gravel.

name: St. Juraj Church (Ladder of Kotor)
description: A small church among village ruins on the Ladder of Kotor, set on a hillside with goats grazing and big bay views. It is the main historic stop on the free trail.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: About 30–40 min up the Ladder of Kotor from the trailhead.

name: Pima Palace
description: A baroque palace of the Pima noble family, rebuilt after the 1667 earthquake, with notable stone balconies. It is seen from outside only; the gates are locked.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Exterior only
Getting there: Flour Square, Old Town.

name: Drago Palace
description: A Gothic-Renaissance palace of the Drago family beside the cathedral square, with ornate window carvings. It is one of the finest aristocratic façades in Kotor.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Exterior only
Getting there: By St Tryphon Square, Old Town.

name: Buća Palace
description: The 14th-century palace of the powerful Buća merchant family, one of the oldest noble houses in Kotor. It now houses a restaurant, so it is best admired from outside.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Exterior only
Getting there: Near St Tryphon Square, Old Town.

name: Kotor Maritime Museum
description: Set in the baroque Grgurina Palace, the museum traces the Boka Navy brotherhood and centuries of Bay seafaring through ship models, portraits, weapons and instruments. An audio guide is included in the €6 ticket.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €6, cards accepted)
Getting there: Square of Boka Navy, Old Town.
Hours: Mon–Sat 8:00–18:00; Sun 10:00–16:00

name: Church of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary (Prčanj)
description: A vast late-baroque church begun in 1789 to plans by Venetian architect Bernardino Maccaruzzi and completed only in 1909. Its grand staircase from the shore is the tallest of its kind on the eastern Adriatic.
mapQuery: Church of the Assumption Prčanj Kotor
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Prčanj, about 15 min by car or bus from Kotor along the bay.
Hours: Mon–Fri 12:00–18:00; Sun 10:15–11:30; closed Sat

name: Old Parish Church of the Birth of the Virgin Mary (Prčanj)
description: The ruined former parish church on the hill above Prčanj, with engraved tombs of the village's captain families and faded wall paintings. It is reached by a short overgrown trail and is in poor repair.
mapQuery: Old parish church Birth of the Blessed Virgin Mary Prčanj
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Trail from the top of the road above Prčanj, about 20 min. Long trousers and sturdy shoes recommended.

name: Church of St. Elijah (Gornji Stoliv)
description: A 1553 church at the top of the old hill village of Gornji Stoliv, beside the ruins of 12th–13th-century St Anne's, an old olive mill and a cistern. Local families are helping restore it.
mapQuery: Church of St. Elijah Gornji Stoliv
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About 30 min climb on a stone path from Donji Stoliv, about 20 min by car from Kotor.

name: Our Lady of the Rocks
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: An artificial island built from the 15th century by sailors sinking ships and rocks on a reef. Each July 22 the custom is still marked with the Fašinada boat procession. The baroque church holds 68 paintings by Tripo Kokolja and a famous embroidery made with the artist's own hair.
mapQuery: Our Lady of the Rocks Perast
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Island entry about €3–5; boats on the spot
Getting there: Boat from Perast waterfront (about €10); Perast is about 25 min by car from Kotor.

name: Island of Saint George
description: A natural island off Perast with a 12th-century Benedictine monastery and a cemetery of Perast's old sea captains among the cypresses. It is usually seen from the water.
details: Getting there: Visible from Perast; seen on bay boat tours.

name: Perast Town Museum (Bujović Palace)
description: Housed in the Bujović Palace of 1694, Perast's finest baroque building, the museum covers the town's Venetian maritime golden age with maps, portraits, weapons and naval relics.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door
Getting there: Perast waterfront.
Hours: Tue–Sun 8:00–20:00; closed Mon

name: St. Nicholas Bell Tower (Perast)
description: The 55 m bell tower of St Nicholas church, the tallest in the Bay, climbed by about 150 narrow steps. It offers the best view of Perast's palaces and the two islands.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Pay at the entrance (about €1–2, cash only)
Getting there: Center of Perast.
Hours: Opens around 10:00

name: Mausoleum of Petar II Petrović Njegoš
description: The 1974 Meštrović-designed tomb of Montenegro's prince-bishop and poet, set on the 1,657 m summit of Jezerski Vrh. It is reached by a 461-step tunnel stairway and offers a 360° view across the country. Bring a layer; it is far cooler than the coast.
mapQuery: Mausoleum of Petar II Petrovic Njegos Kotor
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the base (about €8) plus park entry (about €3)
Getting there: Top of the Lovćen park road, about 1 hr 15 min by car from Kotor via the serpentine road. Walk up from the car park.
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:00

name: Cetinje Monastery
description: Founded in 1484 and rebuilt in 1701 after Ottoman destruction, this was the seat of Montenegro's prince-bishops. It keeps relics revered as the hand of John the Baptist and a fragment of the Holy Cross, plus a rich treasury. Strict modest dress applies; wraps are provided.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Central Cetinje, about 1 hr 15 min by car from Kotor via Njeguši; paid parking nearby.
Hours: Mon–Fri & Sun 8:00–18:30; Sat 8:00–19:00

name: Museum of King Nikola
description: The 1867 palace of King Nikola I, Montenegro's only king, furnished as in the royal family's time, with weapons, portraits and royal belongings. Audio guide app included; no photos inside. Combo tickets with the Njegoš Mausoleum save money.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (combo tickets available)
Getting there: Dvorski Trg, central Cetinje.
Hours: Daily 9:00–17:00 (last entry about 16:00)

name: Njegoš Museum Biljarda
description: The 1838 residence of Petar II Petrović Njegoš, nicknamed for the billiard table he had carried up the mountains. It documents his rule and poetry, and its grounds hold a large 1917 relief map of Montenegro.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €5)
Getting there: Central Cetinje, beside the monastery.
Hours: Daily 9:00–17:00

name: Castle Church (Ćipur)
description: A small 1886 court chapel built by King Nikola on the ruins of Ivan Crnojević's 15th-century monastery. In 1989 the remains of King Nikola and Queen Milena were reburied here. Often locked but photogenic.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Central Cetinje, near the monastery.

name: Vlaška Church
description: A 1450 church, the oldest in Cetinje, whose fence was made from the barrels of captured Ottoman rifles. It is surrounded by an old cemetery. Free to enter.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Baja Pivljanina street, Cetinje.

name: Orlov Krš (Eagle Ridge)
description: A hilltop above Cetinje Monastery holding the 1896 mausoleum of Bishop Danilo, founder of the Petrović-Njegoš dynasty. It offers sweeping sunset views over the old royal capital. The steep paved path takes 20–30 minutes.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Path up from behind Cetinje Monastery.

name: Citadela Budva
description: The 19th-century Austrian-era citadel built on medieval foundations at the tip of Budva's walled Old Town, one of the Adriatic's oldest settlements. Inside are a small library, ship models and a rooftop café with broad views. Cash only.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €6–7, cash)
Getting there: Budva Old Town, about 40 min by car from Kotor via the Vrmac tunnel.
Hours: Daily 9:00–24:00

name: Holy Trinity Church (Budva)
description: An 1804 Orthodox church in Budva Old Town, striped in pink and cream stone, with a gilded carved iconostasis and frescoes. Free to enter.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Near the citadel, Budva Old Town.
Hours: Mon–Fri 8:30–21:00; Sat–Sun 8:00–21:00

name: Podmaine Monastery
description: A 15th-century monastery in the hills above Budva, once the summer residence of Montenegrin prince-bishops including Njegoš. It has fine frescoes, a garden and a peaceful atmosphere far from the beach crowds.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Uphill above Budva, about 45 min by car from Kotor or a 20-min walk from Budva center.
Hours: Daily 7:00–20:00

name: Naval Heritage Collection Museum
description: A museum in the restored 19th-century Austro-Hungarian Arsenal sawmill at Tivat, now part of Porto Montenegro. The highlight is a guided tour of the 1968 Yugoslav submarine P-821 Heroj.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door
Getting there: Porto Montenegro, Tivat, about 20 min by car from Kotor.
Hours: Tue–Sat 9:00–17:00; closed Sun–Mon

name: PI Museum & Gallery Tivat (Buća-Luković Summer House)
description: A 16th-century fortified summer residence of the Kotor noble Buća family, with a small museum on local history and a WWII naval incident, plus an art gallery. Staff give enthusiastic guided tours.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Trg od kulture 2, central Tivat.
Hours: Tue–Fri 9:00–21:00; Sat–Sun 10:00–21:00; closed Mon

name: Mamula Fortress
description: A round 1853 Austro-Hungarian fortress on an islet at the mouth of the Bay, used as a WWII internment camp. It is now a luxury hotel, so non-guests usually view it from passing boats.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Island access only with a hotel reservation or arranged visit
Getting there: Bay entrance off Luštica; seen on Blue Cave boat tours.

name: Forte Mare
description: A seaside fortress founded by Bosnian King Tvrtko I in the 14th century and rebuilt by Ottomans, Venetians and Austrians. It has passageways, terraces and bay views, and hosts summer film screenings. Save your ticket for a discount at Kanli Kula.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €4)
Getting there: Herceg Novi waterfront, about 1 hour by car from Kotor or via the Kamenari–Lepetane ferry.
Hours: Daily 9:00–20:00

name: Kanli Kula
description: The 'Bloody Tower,' a 16th-century Ottoman fortress used as a prison, high above Herceg Novi. Its open-air amphitheatre now hosts summer concerts. It offers the best panorama of the town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €4)
Getting there: Upper Herceg Novi.
Hours: Daily 9:00–20:00

name: Herceg Novi Clock Tower
description: An Ottoman-era 1667 clock tower that served as the main gate of Herceg Novi's old town. It now frames Nikola Đurković Square and its cafés.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Herceg Novi Old Town, up the steps from the waterfront.

name: Fort Citadela (Herceg Novi)
description: Ruins of a seaside fortress beside Forte Mare, partly collapsed in the 1979 earthquake. It adds harbour views and a short history film.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the entrance (about €5)
Getting there: Herceg Novi waterfront promenade, next to Forte Mare.

name: Savina Monastery
description: A Serbian Orthodox monastery complex with churches dating from the 11th to 18th centuries, a treasury and a tiered cemetery overlooking the bay. The main church has been under restoration.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Savina, east of Herceg Novi, about 1 hour by car from Kotor.
Hours: Mon–Sat 8:00–20:00; Sun 8:00–12:00

name: Ostrog Monastery
description: A 17th-century monastery built into a vertical cliff, holding the relics of St Basil of Ostrog and drawing pilgrims of all faiths. The upper monastery's cave chapels are covered in frescoes. Expect long queues around the May 12 feast day.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Near Danilovgrad, about 2 to 2.5 hours by car from Kotor each way, a full day on a port call. The final road is narrow and steep; a shuttle runs from the lower monastery.

name: Royal Palace of Naples
description: Built from 1600 for the Spanish viceroys and later home to the Bourbon kings, the palace has a monumental staircase, gilded royal apartments, a court theater and a hanging garden facing Vesuvius. It is well signed in English and has a free audio guide.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €15, plus about €2 for the terrace and garden) or online
Getting there: Piazza del Plebiscito 1, about a 15-min walk from the cruise terminal.
Hours: 9:00–20:00; closed Wednesday

name: Teatro di San Carlo
description: Founded in 1737, it is the oldest continuously active opera house in Europe and the model for many that followed. Its red-and-gold auditorium can be seen on a daytime guided tour or at an evening performance.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tours bookable on teatrosancarlo.it or at the box office; performance tickets online
Getting there: Via San Carlo 98, a 12-min walk from the port.
Hours: Tours daily 10:00–18:00, subject to rehearsals

name: Castel Nuovo (Maschio Angioino)
description: This 13th-century Angevin fortress was rebuilt by Alfonso of Aragon, who added a white Renaissance triumphal arch. Inside are the Palatine Chapel, a civic museum and Roman remains under a glass floor.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (small fee)
Getting there: Piazza Municipio, a 5-min walk from the cruise terminal.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:00–17:30; closed Sunday

name: Piazza del Plebiscito
description: Naples' grand ceremonial square, named for the 1860 plebiscite that joined Naples to unified Italy. It is framed by the Royal Palace and the colonnaded Basilica of San Francesco di Paola.
details:
Getting there: About a 15-min walk from the port.
Hours: Open public square

name: Basilica di San Francesco di Paola
description: A neoclassical church modeled on Rome's Pantheon and commissioned by the restored Bourbon king Ferdinand I in 1816. A sweeping Doric colonnade embraces the square, and the domed interior is free to enter.
mapQuery: Basilica di San Francesco di Paola Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: West side of Piazza del Plebiscito.
Hours: Daily 8:30–13:00, 16:00–19:00

name: Galleria Umberto I
description: An 1887–90 iron-and-glass arcade built during the city's post-cholera renewal, with a soaring cross-shaped dome and zodiac mosaic floors. It is free to wander.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Via San Carlo / Via Toledo, opposite Teatro San Carlo.
Hours: Open public passage

name: Galleria Borbonica
description: King Ferdinand II commissioned this 1850s tunnel as a royal escape route between the palace and the barracks, cutting through 16th-century cisterns. It was later a WWII air-raid shelter and a car impound, and is now explored on guided tours (an adventure route is also offered).
details:
Reservations / tickets: Guided tours only; book online at galleriaborbonica.com
Getting there: Main entrance at Parcheggio Morelli (Via Domenico Morelli 61, Chiaia); second entrance at Vico del Grottone 3, near Piazza del Plebiscito.
Hours: Fri–Sun 10:00–17:00 (fixed tour times); closed Mon–Thu

name: Naples Underground (Quartieri Spagnoli)
description: A guided descent into Greco-Roman aqueducts and cisterns that sheltered Neapolitans in WWII, led by the volunteers who cleared the debris. It is lively and informative.
mapQuery: Naples Underground Vico Sant'Anna di Palazzo
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book timed tours online
Getting there: Vico Sant'Anna di Palazzo 52, about a 15-min walk from the port.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:30–16:30, Sat–Sun 9:30–18:00

name: Sansevero Chapel Museum
description: The 18th-century chapel of the alchemist Prince Raimondo di Sangro holds Sammartino's Veiled Christ, the Baroque masterpiece Disillusion and the mysterious anatomical machines in the crypt. Photography is not allowed.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book timed tickets online well ahead, as it sells out
Getting there: Via Francesco de Sanctis 19/21, about a 20-min walk from the port.
Hours: 9:00–19:00; closed Tuesday

name: Naples Cathedral (Duomo)
description: This 13th-century Angevin cathedral incorporates the 4th-century Basilica of Santa Restituta. It is the seat of the cult of San Gennaro, whose blood is said to liquefy three times a year.
mapQuery: Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta Naples Duomo
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free; dress modestly
Getting there: Via Duomo 147, about a 25-min walk or short taxi from the port.
Hours: Daily 8:30–19:30

name: Royal Chapel of the Treasure of San Gennaro
description: Vowed by the city during the 1527 plague, this opulent Baroque chapel has frescoes by Domenichino and Lanfranco and silver busts of the patron saints. It also guards the vials of San Gennaro's blood.
mapQuery: Royal Chapel of the Treasure of San Gennaro Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Inside Naples Cathedral.
Hours: Daily ~8:30–13:00 & 14:30–18:30 (Sun afternoon from 16:00)

name: Museum of the Treasure of San Gennaro
description: Seven centuries of gifts to the patron saint from popes, kings and emperors, including the jewel-encrusted mitre and necklace. An audio guide is included.
mapQuery: Museum of the Treasure of San Gennaro Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the museum (about €12)
Getting there: Via Duomo 149.
Hours: Daily 9:30–18:00

name: Baptistery of San Giovanni in Fonte
description: Dating from the late 4th century, it is regarded as the oldest baptistery in the Western world. Its dome preserves rare early-Christian mosaics.
mapQuery: Battistero di San Giovanni in Fonte Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Small fee at the cathedral
Getting there: Inside Naples Cathedral.

name: Complesso Monumentale San Lorenzo Maggiore
description: A Gothic Franciscan basilica, where Boccaccio is said to have first seen his Fiammetta, built over the excavated Roman macellum (market) of Neapolis. You can walk ancient streets and shops below it.
mapQuery: Complesso Monumentale San Lorenzo Maggiore Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €9; guided tour about €2 extra)
Getting there: Piazza San Gaetano 316, Via dei Tribunali.
Hours: Daily 9:30–17:30

name: Napoli Sotterranea
description: A 40 m descent into Greek tuff quarries, Roman aqueducts and cisterns and WWII shelters beneath the old city, including a narrow candle-lit passage. The tour includes a visit to the hidden Roman theater.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the entrance (about €15, cash) or online; regular English tours
Getting there: Piazza San Gaetano 68, Via dei Tribunali.
Hours: Mon–Fri 10:00–18:00, Sat–Sun 9:30–18:00

name: Roman Theatre of Neapolis
description: The theater where Nero performed now lies hidden within later houses, and it is entered through a traditional basso apartment via a trapdoor under a bed. The visit is part of the Napoli Sotterranea tour.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Visited with the Napoli Sotterranea ticket
Getting there: Via dell'Anticaglia / Piazza San Gaetano 68.
Hours: Daily 10:00–18:00 (with tours)

name: Church of San Domenico Maggiore
description: A 13th-century Dominican church where Thomas Aquinas taught, with Aragonese royal coffins in the sacristy and a richly gilded interior. The guided tour of the hidden spaces is well worth it.
mapQuery: Church of San Domenico Maggiore Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Church free; guided tour for a small fee
Getting there: Piazza San Domenico Maggiore 8a, off Spaccanapoli; entrance up the side steps.
Hours: Daily 10:00–18:00

name: Purgatorio ad Arco
description: A 17th-century church with bronze skulls on its facade and an underground hypogeum. There Neapolitans tended anonymous skulls in the cult of the 'pezzentelle' souls, and photos are not allowed below.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €7)
Getting there: Via dei Tribunali 39.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–17:00, Sun 10:00–14:00

name: Church of the Gesù Nuovo
description: A 15th-century palace facade of diamond-point stone, later converted into a Jesuit church with one of Naples' most lavish Baroque interiors. It also holds the shrine of St. Giuseppe Moscati.
mapQuery: Church of the Gesù Nuovo Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free; dress modestly
Getting there: Piazza del Gesù Nuovo 2.
Hours: Daily 8:00–12:45, 16:00–19:00

name: Complesso Monumentale di Santa Chiara
description: A Franciscan monastery founded in 1310 by Robert of Anjou and Queen Sancia. Its cloister is covered in 18th-century hand-painted majolica, and the complex includes a museum and Roman bath ruins.
mapQuery: Complesso Monumentale di Santa Chiara Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the entrance (about €7)
Getting there: Via Santa Chiara 49/c.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:30–17:00, Sun 10:00–14:00

name: Basilica of Santa Chiara
description: The vast Gothic church of the Poor Clares and burial place of the Angevin and Bourbon royals. It was rebuilt after being gutted by 1943 Allied bombing and is free to enter.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Piazza del Gesù Nuovo 18.
Hours: Daily ~8:00–12:45, 16:30–20:00

name: Spaccanapoli
description: The ancient Greek decumanus that slices straight through the UNESCO historic center. It is lined with churches, palazzi and shrines over 2,500 years of continuous street life.
details:
Getting there: Runs from Piazza del Gesù Nuovo to Via Duomo.
Hours: Open street

name: Via San Gregorio Armeno
description: A street of artisan workshops continuing the 18th-century Neapolitan presepe (nativity) craft, beside the convent of San Gregorio Armeno.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Off Via dei Tribunali.
Hours: Shops roughly 10:00–19:00

name: National Archaeological Museum of Naples (MANN)
description: A world-class collection of Pompeii and Herculaneum frescoes and mosaics, including the Alexander Mosaic, alongside the Farnese marbles and the Secret Cabinet. Allow 2–4 hours.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door or online (about €20)
Getting there: Piazza Museo 19, Museo metro (Line 1).
Hours: 9:00–18:30; closed Tuesday

name: Pio Monte della Misericordia
description: A charitable confraternity founded in 1602 and still active today. Its chapel holds Caravaggio's Seven Works of Mercy in its original setting, and upstairs is a historic picture gallery.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €10)
Getting there: Via dei Tribunali 253.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–18:00, Sun 9:00–14:30

name: Catacombs of San Gennaro
description: Southern Italy's largest catacombs (2nd–10th century), on two levels, with early-Christian frescoes and San Gennaro's first tomb. They are guided by young people from the Sanità neighborhood.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book timed tours at catacombedinapoli.it (combined with San Gaudioso)
Getting there: Via Capodimonte 13, by taxi or bus from the center (15 min).
Hours: 9:30–17:00; closed Wednesday

name: Catacombs of San Gaudioso
description: Catacombs beneath Santa Maria della Sanità that reveal the 17th-century practice of drying corpses and setting skulls into frescoed walls.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Combined ticket online
Getting there: Via Sanità 123.
Hours: 9:30–17:00; closed Wednesday

name: Cimitero delle Fontanelle
description: A former tuff quarry that became the ossuary for victims of the 1656 plague and the 1836 cholera. It later gave rise to a popular cult of 'adopting' skulls.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book timed slots on the official website
Getting there: Via Fontanelle 80; taxi recommended.
Hours: 10:00–17:15; closed Wednesday

name: Capodimonte Museum and Royal Park
description: The Bourbon hunting palace built from 1738 to house the Farnese collection, with royal apartments and masterpieces by Caravaggio, Titian and Masaccio. It sits in a 134-hectare historic park.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door or online; park free
Getting there: Via Lucio Amelio 2, by taxi or Shuttle Capodimonte. Plan a half-day with the catacombs.
Hours: Museum 8:30–19:30, closed Wednesday; park opens ~7:00 and closes around dusk

name: Porta Capuana
description: A 1484 Aragonese Renaissance gate by Giuliano da Maiano, flanked by towers of the old city walls next to Castel Capuano. The surroundings are scruffy.
details:
Getting there: Piazza San Francesco a Capuana, a 10-min walk from Napoli Centrale.
Hours: Open street monument

name: Castel dell'Ovo
description: The city's oldest castle, on the islet where Greek settlers founded Parthenope and later the site of Lucullus' villa. Legend says it stands on an egg hidden by Virgil. Recent visitors report the interior closed for renovation.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free when open
Getting there: Via Eldorado 3, Borgo Marinari, a 20-min seafront walk from the port.

name: Castel Sant'Elmo
description: A 16th-century star-shaped Spanish fortress crowning Vomero, long used as a prison. Its ramparts have the best panoramic views over Naples and the bay.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €5)
Getting there: Via Tito Angelini 20/A; Funicolare Centrale or Montesanto funicular, then a 10-min walk.
Hours: Daily 8:30–18:30

name: Certosa e Museo di San Martino
description: A Carthusian monastery founded in 1325 and remade in Baroque marble, with a lavish church, monumental cloisters and the famous Cuciniello presepe. Its terraces look over the bay.
mapQuery: Certosa e Museo di San Martino Naples
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door (about €6)
Getting there: Largo San Martino 5; Montesanto funicular to Morghen.
Hours: 8:30–17:30; closed Tuesday

name: Museo Pignatelli
description: An 1826 neoclassical villa built for the Acton family and later owned by the Rothschilds and Pignatelli, with period salons, porcelain and a carriage museum set in gardens.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the door
Getting there: Riviera di Chiaia 200.
Hours: 9:30–16:00; closed Tuesday

name: Parco Vergiliano a Piedigrotta (Virgil's Tomb)
description: A terraced park holding the Roman columbarium traditionally revered as Virgil's tomb and the tomb of the poet Leopardi. It sits beside the entrance to the Roman Crypta Neapolitana tunnel, which is currently closed.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Salita della Grotta 20, Mergellina, a 5-min walk from Mergellina station.
Hours: Mon & Thu–Sun 9:30–15:00, Wed 14:00–19:00; closed Tuesday (gates locked outside these hours)

name: Parco Archeologico del Pausilypon & Grotta di Seiano
description: A 770 m Roman tunnel through the Posillipo cliff leads to the ruins of the 1st-century BC seaside villa of Vedius Pollio, with a theater, odeon and stunning views of Nisida.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Guided visits only; book in advance online or by phone (+39 081 240 3235)
Getting there: Discesa Coroglio 36, Posillipo, by taxi or bus (about 30 min from the center). Half-day.
Hours: Tue–Fri morning tours; Sat–Sun tours about 9:00–12:15; closed Monday

name: Archaeological Park of Pompeii
description: The Roman city frozen by Vesuvius in AD 79, with its forum, temples, baths, theaters, villas, brothels and plaster casts of victims. It is one of the world's most important archaeological sites. Plan 3–5 hours, wear good shoes and bring water, since shade is scarce.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Buy nominative timed tickets in advance on the official Pompeii site; daily visitor caps apply
Getting there: About 25 km from the port. Take the Circumvesuviana from Porta Nolana or Garibaldi to Pompei Scavi (~40 min) or a private transfer. Half-day minimum.
Hours: 9:00–19:00 in high season (shorter from November)

name: Villa of the Mysteries
description: A grand suburban villa outside Pompeii's walls, famous for a near-complete cycle of red-ground frescoes thought to depict a Dionysian initiation rite. It is among the finest surviving ancient paintings.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Pompeii ticket
Getting there: Via Villa dei Misteri 2, at the far western edge of the site — a long walk via the Necropolis or a short trip from the Porta Marina side. Half-day.
Hours: Follows park hours

name: Basilica of Pompeii (Roman)
description: Built in the 2nd century BC, it is one of the oldest surviving Roman basilicas. It served as Pompeii's law court and business hall, and its colonnaded nave and tribunal still convey its scale.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Pompeii ticket
Getting there: Beside the Forum, near the Porta Marina entrance.
Hours: Follows park hours

name: Archaeological Park of Herculaneum
description: Buried under 20 m of volcanic material, this smaller Roman town survived better than Pompeii, with upper floors, carbonized wood, vivid frescoes and the boathouses where hundreds of skeletons were found. It is compact enough to see in 2–3 hours.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site or online
Getting there: Corso Resina 187, Ercolano — Circumvesuviana to Ercolano Scavi (~20 min), then a 10-min walk. Half-day.
Hours: Daily 8:30–19:30 in season (shorter in winter)

name: Villa Poppaea (Oplontis)
description: A sumptuous seaside villa attributed to Nero's wife Poppaea Sabina, with some of the finest Second Style frescoes anywhere and almost no crowds.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Greater Pompeii ticket or on site
Getting there: Via Sepolcri, Torre Annunziata — 5 min from the Circumvesuviana station. Pair with Pompeii for a half-day.
Hours: 9:00–18:00; closed Tuesday

name: Villa San Marco (Stabiae)
description: One of the largest villas of ancient Stabiae, the resort town where Pliny the Elder died during the eruption. It has a peristyle pool, mosaics, frescoes and Vesuvius views.
mapQuery: Scavi di Stabia Villa San Marco
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free or included in the Greater Pompeii ticket
Getting there: Passeggiata Archeologica, Castellammare di Stabia. Half-day.
Hours: 9:00–18:00; closed Tuesday

name: Villa Arianna (Stabiae)
description: A Roman villa named for its fresco of Ariadne abandoned by Theseus, with baths, gardens and bay views. Entry is free and it is often near-empty.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Strada Varano 1, Castellammare di Stabia. Half-day.
Hours: 9:00–18:00; closed Tuesday

name: Pontifical Shrine of Our Lady of the Rosary of Pompei
description: A basilica founded in 1876 by Blessed Bartolo Longo that grew modern Pompei around it. Its gilded interior holds a revered Madonna icon, and a bell tower lift gives views.
mapQuery: Santuario Beata Vergine del Santo Rosario di Pompei
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free; dress modestly
Getting there: Piazza Bartolo Longo, Pompei — 10 min from the excavations' amphitheater gate.
Hours: Mon–Fri 6:30–14:00 & 15:00–20:00; Sat 6:30–20:00; Sun 5:30–21:00

name: Villa Rufolo
description: A 13th-century palace of Ravello's merchant Rufolo family, with Arab-Norman cloisters, towers and terraced gardens that inspired Wagner's Parsifal. It hosts the Ravello Festival.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the gate (about €8)
Getting there: Piazza Duomo, Ravello — about 2 hours by road, or ferry to Amalfi then bus. Half-day+.
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:30

name: Villa Cimbrone

Reservations / tickets: Tickets on site
Getting there: Via della Lungara 230.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:00–13:15

name: Akrotiri
description: Bronze Age town buried by the great eruption around 1600 BC, preserved under a vast protective roof with streets, multi-storey houses, storage jars and frescoes. Often called the 'Minoan Pompeii' and linked to Atlantis legends; an audio guide or guide brings it to life.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate or online (about €20); audio guides available
Getting there: Southwest Santorini, about 25 min by KTEL bus or taxi from Fira. With the cable-car climb from the tender port, plan a half-day.
Hours: Mon & Thu 8:30–15:30; Tue, Wed, Sat & Sun 8:00–19:00; Fri 8:00–18:30

name: Ancient Thera
description: Ruins of the Hellenistic, Roman and early Byzantine city on the Mesa Vouno ridge 360 m above Kamari and Perissa, including temples, agora, theatre and houses, with sweeping views both ways. There is no shade, few signs and no restrooms, so bring water.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the site (about €10)
Getting there: Hairpin road from Kamari to a small car park (experienced drivers only; tour shuttles run in season), or a 45 min hike up from Perissa in proper shoes. Half-day commitment.
Hours: Thu–Tue 8:30–15:00; closed Wed

name: Museum of Prehistoric Thera
description: Compact museum holding Akrotiri's 3,600-year-old frescoes, pottery and finds, including the famous fleet fresco. The best companion to the Akrotiri site.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Central Fira beside the Metropolitan Cathedral, about 5 min from the upper cable-car station.
Hours: Wed–Mon 8:30–15:30; closed Tue

name: Megaro Gizi
description: Restored 17th-century Venetian mansion in Fira's Catholic quarter displaying engravings, maps, manuscripts and old photographs of Santorini, including the 1956 earthquake. A quiet, inexpensive half-hour.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door (about €3)
Getting there: 25is Martiou, opposite the Catholic Cathedral of St John the Baptist, Fira.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–16:00; closed Sun

name: Emmanuel A. Lignos Santorini Folklore Museum
description: Private museum in a restored 19th-century cave house showing traditional island life, with a canava (winery), workshops, a chapel and a pumice mine tunnel. Guided tours run about an hour for around €5.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door (about €5), guided visit included
Getting there: Kontochori, a 10 min walk north-east of Fira's central bus station.

name: Metropolitan Church of the Presentation of the Lord
description: Fira's Orthodox cathedral, rebuilt after the 1956 earthquake, with whitewashed bell towers, frescoes by local painter Christoforos Asimis and a caldera-view courtyard. Free entry; donations welcome.
mapQuery: Metropolitan Church of the Presentation of the Lord Santorini
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; modest dress
Getting there: Ipapantis, southern Fira, a few minutes from the cable car.

name: Cathedral St. John the Baptist
description: Peach-and-cream Catholic cathedral with a clock tower, the heart of Fira's Venetian-era Catholic quarter. Peaceful and colourful, and a counterpoint to the Orthodox churches.
mapQuery: Cathedral St. John the Baptist Fira Santorini
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Agiou Ioannou, Fira Catholic quarter, about 5 min from the cable car.
Hours: Daily 9:00–21:00

name: Three Bells of Fira
description: The Catholic Church of the Dormition, with its blue dome and three-bell tower perched on the caldera edge in Firostefani, Santorini's most photographed church.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About 15 min walk north of Fira on the caldera path.
Hours: Daily 9:00–21:00

name: Skaros Rock
description: Headland off Imerovigli that held Skaros Castle, the island's medieval Venetian capital, abandoned after earthquakes in the 1800s. A short, steep trail leads past the ruins to the tiny Theoskepasti chapel with huge caldera views.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Imerovigli, about 30 min walk north of Fira. Steep steps back up; wear sturdy shoes, carry water and avoid midday heat.
Hours: Open access

name: Saint Nikolaos Holy Convent
description: Large working convent on the caldera edge at Imerovigli, founded by Venetian-era families in the 1600s and moved here in 1815. Best viewed from the caldera path, and visitable in the mornings.
mapQuery: Saint Nikolaos Holy Convent Imerovigli Santorini
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; modest dress
Getting there: Imerovigli, on the caldera footpath between Firostefani and Skaros.
Hours: Daily 8:00–12:00

name: Castle of Oia
description: Ruins of Agios Nikolaos castle, a Byzantine-Venetian lookout at Oia's western tip, now the island's most famous sunset perch. Free, with a little church tucked below the walls.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Far west end of Oia's main path. Oia is about 25–30 min by bus or taxi from Fira, or by boat from Fira Old Port to Ammoudi.
Hours: Open access

name: Maritime Museum of Santorini
description: 19th-century captain's mansion telling Oia's seafaring history through ship models, figureheads, nautical instruments and a working wartime periscope in the garden. Staff often give personal introductions.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Back lanes of Oia, a few minutes from the main path.
Hours: Daily 10:00–18:00

name: Windmills of Oia
description: Restored traditional windmills, now rentals, at Oia's quieter western end, remnants of the island's milling past and a fine sunset viewpoint.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About 8 min walk from the Oia sunset parking area, below the castle.
Hours: Open access

name: The Virgin Mary of the Akathist Hymn Church
description: Oia's main Orthodox church, a classic Cycladic white-and-blue landmark on the marble main path with a lively square opposite. No photos inside.
mapQuery: Virgin Mary of the Akathist Hymn Church Oia Santorini
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; no photography inside
Getting there: Main pedestrian street, central Oia.

name: Blue Domed Church Santorini
description: The cluster of blue-domed churches (Anastasi and Agios Spyridon) that defines Oia's skyline. Visit before 7:00 to beat the crowds.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Central Oia, near the 3 Domes Viewpoint.

name: Church of Agios Nikolaos (Oia)
description: Grey-stone church with a blue dome near the castle end of Oia, one of the village's most-photographed and traditionally built churches.
mapQuery: Church of Agios Nikolaos Oia Santorini
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Western Oia, on the path toward the castle.

name: Church of Agios Georgios (Oia)
description: Sand-coloured church with a blue dome at the eastern end of Oia's main path, fronted by a quiet square with benches. Calmer than the central churches; usually closed inside.
mapQuery: Church of Agios Georgios Oia Santorini
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: East end of Oia's main street, near the bus stop.

name: Nea Kameni
description: The young volcanic island in the caldera, built by eruptions from 197 BC to 1950, with a 30–45 min trail over lava flows to active steaming craters. It shows the force that shaped Santorini's history.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book a volcano cruise; island entry fee paid on site
Getting there: Boat only, from Fira Old Port or Athinios, usually on a volcano or caldera cruise. Half-day commitment; good shoes and water, no restrooms.

name: Iera Moni Kimisis Theotokou
description: Uninhabited hilltop monastery on Thirasia's south-eastern tip, with three-sided views over the caldera, Santorini and the Aegean, the scene of a big island festival every 15 August.
mapQuery: Iera Moni Kimisis Theotokou Thirasia Santorini
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; open grounds
Getting there: Thirasia: boat from Ammoudi (Oia) or on caldera cruises, then about a 2 km dirt-road walk from Manolas village. Half-day commitment or more.

name: Castle of Pyrgos Kallistis
description: Ruined Venetian kastro crowning Pyrgos, once the island's capital, reached through a maze of medieval lanes with some of the best 360-degree views on Santorini. Free; follow the signs to the hilltop café.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Pyrgos village, about 15 min by bus or taxi from Fira. Park at the village edge and walk 10–15 min uphill.
Hours: Daily 7:00–20:00

name: Church of the Dormition of the Theotokos (Pyrgos)
description: Church within Pyrgos's old castle quarter. The Theotokaki church nearby is among the island's oldest Byzantine chapels, set amid quiet lanes and craft shops.
mapQuery: Church of the Dormition of the Theotokos Pyrgos Santorini
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Inside the Pyrgos castle quarter, near the summit.

name: Monastery of Prophet Elias of Thira
description: 18th-century monastery on the island's highest peak (about 565 m), once a centre of learning, with a small shop and panoramic views over the whole island.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; modest dress
Getting there: Winding road above Pyrgos; by car or taxi, parking at the top. A marked path continues to Ancient Thera.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:00–17:00; closed Sun

name: Panagia Episkopi
description: Late-11th-century Byzantine church founded by Emperor Alexios I Komnenos, one of Santorini's oldest, with rare icons and frescoes in a quiet rural setting below Mesa Vouno.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Near Mesa Gonia, about 15 min by car from Fira.

name: Venetian Castle of Emporio
description: Fortified medieval quarter (Kasteli) of Emporio, the island's largest village, with tightly packed houses forming defensive walls, bougainvillea-draped lanes and the church of Agios Spyridon.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Emporio, about 20 min from Fira. Research the castle quarter first; the lanes are a maze.

name: Agios Charalambos
description: Exo Gonia's grand church, rebuilt in the mid-20th century after earthquake damage, among the island's largest and unusual for its tiled roof and wide stairway. The rating rests on few reviews.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Exo Gonia village, about 15 min from Fira.

name: Santorini Wine Museum
description: Koutsoyannopoulos family museum in a cave about 8 m underground, tracing Santorini's 3,500-year winemaking heritage with historic machinery and dioramas, ending with a tasting.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket with tasting at the door
Getting there: Vothonas, about 10 min by car from Fira.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:30–19:00; Sun 10:00–19:00

name: Castle of Akrotiri
description: Hilltop remains of La Ponta Venetian castle above Akrotiri village, badly damaged in the 1956 earthquake, with a small family café and views across the caldera.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Akrotiri village, about 25 min from Fira. Small cars can drive near the top; otherwise park in the village and walk up.

name: Akrotiri Lighthouse
description: Lighthouse from 1892 at the island's southwestern tip, one of Greece's oldest. The tower is closed to visitors, but the headland gives a quieter sunset over the caldera.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: End of the Akrotiri road, about 30 min from Fira. Parking is scarce, so leave the car 1–2 min before and walk. Strong winds.
Hours: Open access

name: Tomato Industrial Museum, D. Nomikos
description: A 1945 tomato-paste factory preserved as an industrial-heritage museum, telling the story of pre-tourism Santorini, with audio guide, tasting and a souvenir can.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door (about €12)
Getting there: Vlychada, south coast, about 25 min from Fira; free parking nearby.
Hours: Tue–Sun 10:00–18:00; closed Mon

name: Diocletian's Palace
description: The colossal retirement palace built by Roman Emperor Diocletian around AD 295–305, one of the best-preserved Roman palaces in the world and a UNESCO site. Medieval Split grew inside its walls, so Roman columns, Romanesque houses, and Venetian palaces now share the same lanes.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free); individual monuments are ticketed
Getting there: Directly behind the Riva, a 5–10 minute walk from the cruise and ferry port; enter by the Brass (Bronze) Gate from the waterfront.
Hours: Open 24 hours (public streets)

name: Saint Domnius' Cathedral
description: Diocletian's octagonal mausoleum, converted in the 7th century into a cathedral for St. Domnius, a bishop martyred under Diocletian. It is one of the oldest cathedrals still in use, with 13th-century carved walnut doors by Andrija Buvina and a rich treasury.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Tickets at the office opposite the bell tower; several combo options cover the crypt, treasury, tower, and baptistery
Getting there: On the Peristyle at the center of the palace.
Hours: Mon–Sat 8:00–20:00; closed to tourists Sunday (seasonal)

name: Saint Domnius Bell Tower
description: A 57 m Romanesque-Gothic campanile built from the 13th to 16th centuries, rebuilt in the early 1900s, and the city's defining landmark. The climb is steep and narrow, with see-through metal steps near the top and 360° views at the summit.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the cathedral ticket office
Getting there: On the Peristyle beside the cathedral.
Hours: Mon–Sat 8:15–15:30; Sun 13:00–17:30 (seasonal)

name: Vestibul
description: The domed, round antechamber to Diocletian's private apartments, now open to the sky through its oculus. Its acoustics are famous, and klapa a cappella groups often perform here.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Just south of the Peristyle.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Diocletian's Cellars
description: The vaulted Roman substructures that held up the emperor's apartments, later used as Split's rubbish dump, which is why they survived nearly intact. They are the best place to grasp the palace's original floor plan and were a Game of Thrones filming location.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket for the side halls at the entrance
Getting there: Enter through the Brass Gate from the Riva; the central hall is a free passage and the side halls are ticketed.
Hours: Daily 8:30–20:00 (seasonal)

name: Brass Gate (Porta Aenea)
description: The palace's modest southern sea gate, where the emperor once arrived by boat straight into the cellars. Today it is the main entrance from the Riva and was partly under restoration in 2026.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Obala Hrvatskog narodnog preporoda 22, midway along the Riva.
Hours: Daily 8:30–22:00

name: Split Golden Gate
description: The palace's ceremonial north gate (AD 305), the main imperial entrance on the road to the provincial capital Salona. It is framed by arcaded niches that once held statues.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: North side of the palace, beside the Gregory of Nin statue.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Eastern (Silver) Gate
description: The palace's east gate on the old road to Epetium (Stobreč), heavily restored after Allied bombing in WWII. It now opens onto the Green Market.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: East wall of the palace, beside the Green Market.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Iron Gate
description: The best-preserved palace gate, in continuous use for 17 centuries, with a tiny early-medieval church above it and a Renaissance clock tower with a 24-hour dial.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: West side of the palace, opening onto People's Square.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Gregory of Nin Statue
description: Ivan Meštrović's 1929 bronze of the 10th-century bishop who defied Rome to defend Old Church Slavonic liturgy, a symbol of Croatian identity. Rubbing the polished big toe is said to bring luck.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Outside the Golden Gate.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: People's Square (Pjaca)
description: The medieval civic center that grew just outside the palace walls, with the 15th-century Gothic Old Town Hall and Venetian-era palaces around it.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: West of the palace, through the Iron Gate.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Radić Brothers Square (Fruit Square)
description: A square dominated by the 15th-century Venetian octagonal tower, part of a castle built against Split's rebels, and the Baroque Milesi Palace. Meštrović's statue of Marko Marulić, father of Croatian literature, stands in the center.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Just west of the palace, off the Riva.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Republic Square (Prokurative)
description: A 19th-century neo-Renaissance square modeled on Venice's Procuratie and opening to the harbor, built during Split's Austro-Hungarian era.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: West end of the Riva.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Church and Convent of St. Francis
description: A Franciscan church and 13th-century cloister on the site of the early-Christian church of St. Felix. It holds the tombs of poet Marko Marulić and statesman Ante Trumbić.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Trg Franje Tuđmana 1, at the west end of the Riva.

name: Split City Museum
description: Split's history from Roman times through the Middle Ages, displayed in the 15th-century Gothic Papalić Palace by Juraj Dalmatinac. Highlights include Diocletian coins, medieval sculpture, and a multimedia study of the cathedral doors.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Papalićeva 1, inside the palace near the Golden Gate.
Hours: Tue–Sun 9:00–20:00; closed Monday (seasonal)

name: Split Ethnographic Museum
description: Traditional Dalmatian costume, jewelry, and weapons in palace-era rooms, including the remains of the church of St. Andrew de Fenestris. The rooftop terrace overlooks the Peristyle.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Iza Vestibula 4, by the Vestibule.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:00–17:00; Sat 10:00–14:00; closed Sunday

name: Split Synagogue
description: A 16th-century synagogue built into the palace's west wall, one of the oldest functioning in Europe and still used by Split's small Jewish community.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (donation)
Getting there: Židovski prolaz 1, off People's Square.
Hours: Mon–Fri 10:00–14:00; closed Saturday–Sunday

name: Archaeological Museum in Split
description: Croatia's oldest museum (1820), holding finds from Roman Salona and early-Christian Dalmatia, with a large garden lapidarium of sarcophagi and inscriptions. Many labels are in Croatian only.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door; combo ticket with Salona available
Getting there: Zrinsko-Frankopanska 25, about a 15-minute walk north of the palace.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:00–14:00 and 15:00–20:00; Sat 9:00–14:00; closed Sunday

name: Tvrđava Gripe (Gripe Fortress)
description: A 17th-century Venetian bastion fortress built after Ottoman threats to Split, now home to the Croatian Maritime Museum's naval and WWII collections. Peacocks roam the grounds.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the museum (low fee)
Getting there: Glagoljaška 18, on the hill about a 10-minute walk east of the palace.

name: Croatian National Theater in Split
description: An 1893 neo-Renaissance theater, once among the largest in southeastern Europe, which still stages opera, ballet, and drama and anchors the Split Summer Festival.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Box office or hnk-split.hr
Getting there: Trg Gaje Bulata 1, about 5 minutes north of the palace.
Hours: Box office Mon–Fri 9:00–21:00

name: Church of St. Nicholas
description: A simple Romanesque church commissioned in 1219 on Marjan's first peak, one of several medieval hermit churches on the hill. It is usually closed.
mapQuery: Church of St Nicholas Marjan Split
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: A few minutes uphill from the Vidilica viewpoint via the Marjan stairs from Varoš.

name: Old Jewish cemetery
description: A Jewish cemetery founded in 1573 on Marjan's slope, among the oldest in Europe, with weathered headstones from the 16th to 20th centuries.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Next to the Vidilica café; the entrance is just right of the restaurant.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Sustipan
description: A clifftop peninsula that was home to an early-medieval Benedictine monastery and later Split's 19th-century city cemetery, now a peaceful pine park with harbor views.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Sustipanski put, a 15-minute walk southwest of the Riva past the ACI marina.
Hours: Daily 6:00–23:00

name: Meštrović Gallery
description: The 1930s seaside villa that sculptor Ivan Meštrović designed for himself, displaying his marble and bronze works in the house and gardens. The ticket includes the Kaštilac chapel nearby.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Šetalište Ivana Meštrovića 46, about 25 minutes on foot west of the Riva, or a short taxi ride.
Hours: Tue–Sun 8:00–18:00; closed Monday (seasonal)

name: Meštrovićeve Crikvine - Kaštilac
description: A 16th-century fortified summer residence of the Capogrosso family, restored by Meštrović, whose chapel holds his carved wooden panels of the life of Christ.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Meštrović Gallery ticket
Getting there: Šetalište Ivana Meštrovića 39, a 200 m walk west of the gallery.
Hours: Tue–Sun 8:00–18:00; closed Monday

name: Salona Archaeological Site
description: The ruins of Salona, capital of Roman Dalmatia, a city of some 60,000 people and Diocletian's birthplace, destroyed by Avars and Slavs in the 7th century. Its refugees founded medieval Split inside the palace; walls, basilicas, baths, and necropolises survive, with 3D reconstructions via QR codes.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the main entrance; combo ticket with Split's Archaeological Museum
Getting there: Solin, about 6 km north of Split; bus 1 to the main entrance (20–30 minutes). Allow 2 hours plus travel, so it is a half-day trip; there is little shade, so bring water.
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:00 (seasonal)

name: Manastirine Monasteries
description: An early-Christian cemetery and basilica complex at Salona built around the tombs of martyrs, including St. Domnius, with sarcophagi and column remains. It is the most impressive excavated area of Salona.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Salona ticket
Getting there: Next to the Salona main entrance and Tusculum, Solin. A half-day trip from Split.
Hours: Mon–Fri 7:00–18:00; Sat 8:00–18:00; Sun 9:00–13:00

name: Tusculum, Salona
description: The 1898 villa of archaeologist Don Frane Bulić, the father of Salona's excavations, built with Roman fragments set into its walls. It now holds a small museum and café.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Salona ticket
Getting there: At the Salona main entrance, Solin. A half-day trip from Split.
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:00

name: Amphitheatre Solin
description: Salona's 2nd-century amphitheatre, which once seated about 18,000 spectators and where Christians were martyred under Diocletian. It is the highlight of the Salona site.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included in the Salona ticket
Getting there: West end of Salona at Put Salone. The west entrance (Para House) is a closer start, a half-day trip from Split.
Hours: Mon–Fri 7:00–18:00; Sat 8:00–18:00; Sun 9:00–13:00

name: Diocletian Aqueduct
description: Surviving arches of the 9 km Roman aqueduct that carried water from the Jadro spring to Diocletian's Palace, partly restored and still in use. The arches stand among modern houses.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Along the D8 between Split and Solin, about 15 minutes by car.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Klis Fortress
description: A strategic stronghold commanding the pass above Split for 2,000 years: an Illyrian fort, seat of Croatian kings, and the site of a heroic Uskok defense before falling to the Ottomans in 1537. It appeared as Meereen in Game of Thrones.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate
Getting there: Klis, about 12 km northeast of Split; 25 minutes by car or bus 22/34/35/36. The small car park fills fast, so use the overflow lot below the village and walk up the steep lane. A half-day trip.
Hours: Daily 9:00–19:00 (seasonal)

name: Trogir Old Town
description: A UNESCO-listed island town founded by Greek colonists as Tragurion, whose Romanesque, Gothic, and Renaissance fabric is among the best preserved in central Europe.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: About 27 km west of Split; 30–50 minutes by bus 37 or the summer boat from the Riva. A half-day trip.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: North Old Town Gate (Land Gate)
description: Trogir's 17th-century Baroque Land Gate, topped by a 15th-century statue of patron St. John of Trogir, with the town museum just behind it.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: At the bridge from the mainland, Trogir. A half-day trip from Split.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: St. Lawrence's Cathedral
description: A Romanesque-Gothic cathedral begun in 1213, famous for Master Radovan's 1240 portal with Adam and Eve and Nikola Firentinac's Renaissance chapel of St. John. The bell tower has fine views.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket required; shoulders must be covered
Getting there: Trg Ivana Pavla II, Trogir; buy tickets across the square. A half-day trip from Split.
Hours: Daily 8:00–16:00 (seasonal)

name: City Loggia Trogir
description: A 15th-century loggia that served as Trogir's court of justice, with a relief by Nikola Firentinac and a later Meštrović work.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Trg Ivana Pavla II, opposite the cathedral. A half-day trip from Split.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: South Gate (Sea Gate)
description: Trogir's Renaissance Sea Gate (1537), studded with iron, beside surviving 13th-century walls and a small lodge where late arrivals once waited.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Obala bana Berislavića, Trogir. A half-day trip from Split.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Kamerlengo Castle
description: A 15th-century Venetian fortress, named for the Venetian chamberlain who governed Trogir, with ramparts and a tower over the marina. Summer concerts are held in the courtyard.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate
Getting there: West tip of Trogir. A half-day trip from Split.
Hours: Daily 9:00–22:00 (seasonal)

name: Kaštilac (Kaštel Gomilica)
description: A 16th-century fortified islet castle built by Benedictine nuns as refuge from Ottoman raids. It is one of the Kaštela castles and appeared as Braavos in Game of Thrones, with residents still living inside.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in (free)
Getting there: Kaštel Gomilica, about 20 minutes by car or bus west of Split; paid marina parking is about 10 minutes away on foot. A half-day trip.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Kaštela City Museum (Vitturi Castle)
description: A 1487 seaside castle of the Vitturi family, now the Kaštela town museum, telling the story of the seven anti-Ottoman castles and the tragic lovers Miljenko and Dobrila.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Brce 1, Kaštel Lukšić, about 25 minutes west of Split. A half-day trip.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:00–20:00; Sat 9:00–13:00; closed Sunday

name: Kaštel Rušinac (Miljenko's Castle)
description: The small castle of Miljenko Rušinac from Kaštela's 17th-century tragic love story, with a medieval garden that hosts summer tastings and concerts.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; events via the Mastrinka society
Getting there: Šetalište Miljenka i Dobrile, Kaštel Lukšić; a short walk from Vitturi Castle. A half-day trip.

name: Španjola Fortress (Hvar Fortica)
description: A 16th-century Venetian hilltop fortress above Hvar Town, with dungeons and a small museum, built where earlier Illyrian and medieval forts stood. The views over the harbor and Pakleni Islands are superb.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the gate
Getting there: About a 15–20 minute walk up from Hvar Town square; Hvar is roughly 1 hour by catamaran from Split. A full-day trip, so check return sailings.
Hours: Daily 9:00–20:00 (seasonal)

name: Saint Stephen's Cathedral
description: Hvar's 16th–17th-century Renaissance-Baroque cathedral, with a four-story bell tower and marble altars. A small entry fee applies and photos are not allowed.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Small entry fee
Getting there: At the head of St. Stephen's Square, Hvar Town. A full-day trip from Split.
Hours: Daily 9:00–12:30 and 16:30–19:30

name: St. Stephen's Square (Pjaca)
description: Dalmatia's largest square, laid out in the 15th century over a filled-in inlet. It is framed by the cathedral, the Venetian Arsenal, and Renaissance façades.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Hvar Town center, about 1 hour by catamaran from Split. A full-day trip.
Hours: Open 24 hours

name: Fortress of Petar Hektorović (Tvrdalj)
description: The 16th-century fortified summer house of Renaissance poet Petar Hektorović in Stari Grad, with a seawater fishpond, gardens, and Latin and Croatian inscriptions. It is a tranquil gem; pay in cash.
mapQuery: Tvrdalj Petar Hektorovic Stari Grad Hvar
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door (cash)
Getting there: Stari Grad, Hvar: about 2 hours by car ferry from Split, or by catamaran to Hvar Town plus a 20-minute bus. A full-day trip.
Hours: Daily 10:00–13:00 and 16:00–18:00

name: Blaca Hermitage
description: A monastery built into a Brač cliff by Glagolitic priests fleeing the Ottomans in 1551, preserved with its library, astronomical observatory, and furnishings. Visits are by guided tour.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Guided tour at the site (cash reported)
Getting there: About a 2 km rocky hike (30–45 minutes) down from the road-end car park, or up from Blaca bay by boat; bring water. A full-day trip from Split.
Hours: Tue–Sun 9:00–15:00; closed Monday

name: Muzej otoka Brača (Brač Island Museum)
description: Brač's island museum in the Radojković tower in Škrip, the island's oldest village, set amid Illyrian walls and a Roman mausoleum. A knowledgeable curator often guides visitors in the mornings.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at the door
Getting there: Škrip, central Brač: ferry from Split to Supetar (about 50 minutes), then about 15 minutes by car. A full-day trip.
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:00–19:00; Sun 10:00–13:00 and 15:00–19:00

name: Olive oil museum
description: A family olive press in Škrip turned into a museum of Brač's centuries-old olive-oil heritage, with guided tours that end in a generous local tasting.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; tasting options at the site
Getting there: Put Ploča 5, Škrip, Brač: ferry to Supetar, then about 15 minutes by car. A full-day trip.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–18:00; Sun 10:00–15:00

name: Old Venetian Port of Chania
description: Flat, scenic stroll around the 14th-century Venetian harbour, past the Mosque of the Janissaries, the arsenali and the waterfront tavernas toward the Egyptian-style lighthouse. Loveliest early morning or at sunset; a good gentle option on a short port day.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About 2–3 km loop on flat paving, around 1 hour. From Souda cruise port it is about 7 km by taxi or bus to Chania Market. The breakwater out to the lighthouse has recently been closed for works.
Hours: Open access

name: Firka Venetian Fortress
description: Late-16th-century Venetian bastion at the western end of the harbour, housing the Maritime Museum. Its ramparts give a panorama of the harbour and lighthouse, and it makes a natural turnaround point on a harbour walk.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; Maritime Museum has a separate ticket
Getting there: Western tip of the harbour; about 0.5 km flat walk from the harbour centre, 15–30 min with a look around. From Souda port, about 7 km by taxi or bus.
Hours: Fortress grounds Mon–Fri 8:00–14:00; closed Sat–Sun

name: Byzantine Walls of Chania
description: Excavated sections of the Byzantine and Minoan-era walls on Kastelli hill above the harbour, an easy add-on loop through the oldest quarter of the old town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Sifaka 41, Kastelli hill. Short climb of about 30 m from the harbour, under 1 km and 20–30 min.
Hours: Open access

name: West Venetian Walls
description: Well-preserved stretch of the massive 16th-century Venetian land walls and moat on the west side of the old town, walked on the way to Nea Chora beach.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Meletiou Piga 2. About a 1 km flat walk along the walls toward Nea Chora, 20–30 min.
Hours: Open access

name: Virgin of the Angels Monastery (Gouverneto)
description: Fortress-like 16th-century working monastery on the Akrotiri peninsula and the trailhead for the descent to the Katholiko ruins and the sea. The courtyard is worth a look when open; dress modestly.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Monastery about €2.50 donation
Getting there: About 20 km (35 min) by car from Chania or Souda; large free car park. The Katholiko trail starts behind the monastery.
Hours: Mon, Tue & Thu 9:00–12:00 & 17:00–19:00; Sat–Sun 5:00–12:00 & 17:00–20:00; closed Wed & Fri

name: Monastery Katholiko
