description: A zigzag trail marked with Stations of the Cross climbing about an hour to the summit of Srđ, with views over the Old Town all the way. Loose stones and little shade on the upper half, so go early.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Trailhead on Jadranska cesta above the Old Town; take a taxi or bus to the trailhead. Do not follow the walking route along the highway, which has no sidewalk.
Hours: Open access

name: Homeland War Museum
description: Housed in Fort Imperial, the Napoleonic fortress defenders held during the 1991–92 siege, it tells the story of the war through film, photographs and relics. The rooftop view is spectacular.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: At the top of Srđ, next to the cable car upper station.
Hours: Daily 8:30–22:00

name: Dead Sea (Lokrum)
description: A small saltwater lake on Lokrum connected to the sea through underground fissures, calm and buoyant even on rough days. Good for a gentle swim, with a bar above.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Lokrum boat ticket includes island entry (around €27–30)
Getting there: Boat from the Old Port (~15 minutes); 10-minute walk from the landing.
Hours: Daily 9:00–17:00 (lake)

name: Hidden Cove, Lokrum
description: A natural rock arch near the Dead Sea where the cove opens to the sea, framing passing boats. Tricky to find but shaded and perfect for a picnic.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Lokrum entry ticket
Getting there: Near the Dead Sea lake; turn right at the bench at the top and look for steps down.
Hours: Follows Lokrum boat schedule

name: Lokrum Rocks
description: Flat rock platforms on Lokrum's southern shore with ladders into deep water and showers nearby. A beautiful wild swimming spot.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Lokrum entry ticket
Getting there: South side of Lokrum, near the Dead Sea.
Hours: Follows Lokrum boat schedule

name: Buža na Lokrumu
description: A hidden sea cave reached by scrambling down rocks near the Dead Sea, a spectacular photo spot. Footing is tricky, so take care.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Lokrum entry ticket
Getting there: Near the Dead Sea on Lokrum, behind the stone wall.
Hours: Daily 8:00–20:00

name: Benedictine Monastery, Lokrum
description: The ruined medieval monastery and cloister at the heart of Lokrum, later converted into a residence by Archduke Maximilian of Habsburg, with peacocks in the gardens. Local legend tells of a curse on the island by departing monks.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Lokrum entry ticket
Getting there: Centre of Lokrum, 5 minutes from the landing.
Hours: Follows Lokrum boat schedule

name: Fort Royal, Lokrum
description: A star-shaped fort built by the French on Lokrum's highest point, reached by a pine-shaded path. Climb the top for a 360-degree view.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Lokrum entry ticket
Getting there: Uphill from the Lokrum landing, about 20 minutes.
Hours: Follows Lokrum boat schedule

name: Bukovac House Museum
description: The family home of painter Vlaho Bukovac, Croatia's great portraitist, with his works and his own painted murals in the house. A delight hidden steps from Cavtat's harbour.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; included with Dubrovnik Pass
Getting there: Bukovčeva 5, Cavtat; boat from Dubrovnik Old Port or 30 minutes by bus.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–18:00; Sun 10:00–14:00

name: Mausoleum of the Račić Family
description: A domed white-stone mausoleum by sculptor Ivan Meštrović on the hilltop cemetery of Cavtat. The views over the bays are lovely.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Small entry fee
Getting there: Top of the Rat peninsula in Cavtat.

name: Beach Rat, Cavtat
description: A rocky beach along the pine-shaded promenade around the Rat peninsula, with clear deep water, sunbed rental, kiosk and a nearby restaurant. Quieter than Cavtat town beach.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free; sunbeds charged
Getting there: Follow the promenade around Rat peninsula from Cavtat harbour.

name: Beach Kamen Mali
description: Rocky terraces with sunbeds on the far side of the Rat peninsula, with shade and good swimming. A small bar serves drinks.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Along the Rat peninsula path in Cavtat.

name: Beach Bar Little Star
description: A rustic multilevel bar built over the rocks at Kamen Mali, serving drinks while the sun sets over the sea. A perfect end to a day in Cavtat.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Kamen Mali, Rat peninsula, Cavtat.
Hours: Daily 11:00–22:00

name: Mlini Harbour
description: A small village harbour with restaurants, a church and water taxis to Dubrovnik and Cavtat. Pleasant evenings with live music.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Mlini, between Dubrovnik and Cavtat.

name: Soline Beach
description: A tiny pebble cove at the bottom of around 250 steps near Mlini, with showers and small rocks for jumping. Quiet because of the climb.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Soline, near Mlini; steep steps down.

name: Val di Breno
description: A beach club and restaurant in Srebreno serving sushi and fusion dishes. Sunbed packages include food and drinks.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book via +385 99 166 4383
Getting there: Šetalište dr. Franja Tuđmana 41, Srebreno.
Hours: Daily 8:00–23:30

name: Pasjača Beach
description: A dramatic pebble beach under towering cliffs in Konavle, reached via a steep path cut into the rock. Waves can be strong; water shoes recommended.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Popovići, Konavle; ~40 minutes' drive from Dubrovnik, then a steep walk.

name: Sokol Grad
description: A medieval fortress perched on a rock above the Konavle valley, guarding the old border with Bosnia. Small museum and sweeping views.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Paid entry on site
Getting there: Dunave, Konavle; ~50 minutes' drive from Dubrovnik.
Hours: Daily 8:00–19:00

name: Kojan Koral
description: A family-run riding stable offering horseback and buggy tours through the Konavle hills. Rides end with fruit and local wine.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead via +385 99 300 5001
Getting there: Gruda, Konavle; pickups available from Dubrovnik.

name: Malvasija Karaman Winery
description: A family winery reviving Dubrovnik Malvasija, served with homemade food and views over Konavle. Intimate and personal.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead
Getting there: Pridvorje, Konavle; ~45 minutes from Dubrovnik.
Hours: Mon–Sat 13:00–18:00; closed Sun

name: OPG Pero Šiša
description: A centuries-old family farm offering wine, olive oil, liqueurs and homemade sweets. Close to the airport.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead via +385 98 383 042
Getting there: Gruda, Konavle.
Hours: Mon–Fri 16:00–21:00; Sat–Sun 10:00–21:00

name: Crvik Winery
description: A small vineyard with tastings led by a passionate winemaker. Personal and relaxed.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead
Getting there: Komaji, Konavle.

name: Winery Botaro
description: A family vineyard with homemade cheese, cured meats and grappa. Weekend tastings only.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead
Getting there: Drvenik, Konavle.
Hours: Sat 12:00–16:00; Sun 12:30–16:30

name: Agrotourism & Winery Brajković
description: A 300-year-old stone house now a family winery producing wine and rare olive oil. Hosts share stories of the 1991 conflict.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Zastolje, Konavle.
Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–18:00; closed Sun

name: Cadmos Village
description: An eco adventure park with treetop ziplines, a treehouse and restaurant in the Konavle woods. Great for families.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead via +385 91 112 9200
Getting there: Komaji, Konavle.

name: Kameni Mlin
description: An agrotourism restaurant in an old watermill in Konavle serving traditional dishes. Countryside escape.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended
Getting there: Konavle valley.

name: AR Atelier Silk Embroidery
description: A workshop preserving Konavle silk embroidery. Visitors can see the craft and buy pieces.
details: Getting there: Konavle.

name: Mikki's Croatian Kitchen
description: A hands-on cooking class making traditional Croatian dishes. Friendly and immersive.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead
Getting there: Konavle area.

name: Konavle County Museum
description: A museum of Konavle costumes, embroidery and rural life. Small but rich.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Čilipi, Konavle.

name: Walls of Ston
description: Medieval walls stretching some 5 km across the hills between Ston and Mali Ston, built to protect the Republic's salt pans. Walk the short circuit or the full route.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at any entrance
Getting there: Ston, about 1 hour from Dubrovnik.
Hours: Daily 8:00–17:30

name: Mali Ston Oysters
description: Boat trips out to the oyster beds in Mali Ston bay, where oysters and mussels are pulled from the water and eaten on the spot.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead via +385 91 369 6981
Getting there: Mali Ston harbour.
Hours: Daily 9:00–20:00

name: Kapetanova Kuća
description: A classic waterfront restaurant in Mali Ston famous for oysters, black risotto and the local Ston cake made with pasta.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended
Getting there: Obala dr. Ante Starčevića 9, Mali Ston.
Hours: Daily 11:00–23:00

name: Bota Šare Mali Ston
description: An oyster bar and restaurant in Mali Ston harbour offering seafood platters and pontoon oyster tastings.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Recommended
Getting there: Mali Ston harbour.
Hours: Daily 9:00–23:00

name: Three Green Caves
description: Sea caves on Koločep with luminous green water, where confident swimmers can explore narrow passages.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Boat tour
Getting there: Boat tour from Dubrovnik.

name: Blue Cave, Koločep
description: A sea cave you swim into to see the water glow blue. Afternoon light is best.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Boat tour
Getting there: Boat tour from Dubrovnik.

name: Koločep
description: A tiny car-free island of pine woods and olive groves, the closest Elafiti island to Dubrovnik.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ferry ticket
Getting there: Ferry from Gruž.

name: Kalamota Beach House
description: A small beach hotel and bar on Koločep with a calm sandy swimming area. Relaxed island lunch stop.
details: Getting there: Gornje Čelo, Koločep.

name: Beach Lopud
description: A sandy beach by Lopud's harbour with calm, shallow water and restaurants nearby.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Ferry from Gruž to Lopud.

name: Šipan
description: The largest Elafiti island, with Renaissance summer villas, olive groves and quiet harbours.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ferry ticket
Getting there: Ferry from Gruž.

name: Trsteno Arboretum
description: A Renaissance garden laid out by the Gučetić family, with a baroque fountain and plane trees.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticket at entrance
Getting there: Trsteno, ~25 minutes north of Dubrovnik.

name: Edivo Wine Bar
description: A winery that ages wine underwater in the sea, with tastings in Drače on Pelješac.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead
Getting there: Drače, Pelješac.

name: Saints Hills Vinaria
description: A modern Pelješac winery with tastings of Plavac Mali.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead
Getting there: Pelješac peninsula.

name: St Luke's Church, Kotor
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: A small 12th-century church in Kotor's old town once shared by Catholic and Orthodox worshippers.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Kotor old town; full-day trip with border crossing.

name: Kajtaz House
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: An Ottoman-era family house in Mostar preserved with its original furnishings.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Paid entry
Getting there: Mostar; full-day trip with border crossing.

name: Blagaj Tekke
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: A dervish house built at the spring of the Buna river beneath a cliff.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Paid entry
Getting there: Blagaj, near Mostar.

name: Počitelj Fortress
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: A fortified Ottoman village climbing a hillside above the Neretva river.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Počitelj, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

name: Halebija Tower
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: A tower beside Mostar's Old Bridge offering close views of the bridge.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Paid entry
Getting there: Mostar Old Town.

name: Villa Korta Katarina
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: A Pelješac winery producing Plavac Mali and Pošip with elegant tastings.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book ahead
Getting there: Orebić, Pelješac.

name: Korčula Town Gate
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: The Land Gate of Korčula's walled old town.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Korčula; full day by road and ferry.

name: St Mary's Island, Mljet
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: A Benedictine monastery on an islet in Mljet National Park's saltwater lake.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: National Park ticket
Getting there: Mljet; full-day catamaran trip.

name: Roman Palace, Polače
area: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
description: Ruins of a late Roman palace by the harbour of Polače on Mljet.
tags: Further Afield: Kotor, Mostar & the Far Islands
details:
Reservations / tickets: Free
Getting there: Polače, Mljet.

name: The Orange Trees Garden (Giardino degli Aranci)
description: A walled garden of bitter-orange trees on top of the Aventine Hill, built over the ramparts of the Savelli family's medieval fortress. Its terrace looks out over the Tiber to the dome of St Peter's. Romans come here for the sunset, so it is busiest in the hour before dusk.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Aventine Hill, a 10–12 min uphill walk from Circo Massimo metro (Line B).
Hours: Daily 7:00–18:00; closing time moves with the seasons, roughly at sunset

name: Giardino di Sant'Alessio
description: A narrow, pine-shaded terrace tucked between the convents of Santa Sabina and Sant'Alessio, with the same rooftop panorama as the Orange Garden and a fraction of the people. It makes a good alternative to queuing at the Knights of Malta keyhole a few steps away.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Via di Sant'Alessio on the Aventine, 2 min from the Orange Garden.
Hours: Daily 7:00–19:00

name: Basilica of Saint Sabina
description: A 5th-century basilica that escaped later Baroque remodeling, so its interior shows what an early Christian church looked like. Its carved cypress doors date to around 430 AD, and one panel carries one of the oldest surviving images of the Crucifixion. The windows are glazed with thin selenite rather than glass, which gives the light its milky quality.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free; modest dress
Getting there: Piazza Pietro d'Illiria, beside the Orange Garden.
Hours: Tue–Sat 8:00–19:00; Sun–Mon 12:00–19:00

name: Roseto Comunale di Roma
description: The city's rose garden, set on the slope of the Aventine directly across from the Circus Maximus, with about 1,100 varieties. One side holds the permanent collection and the other the entries in the annual Premio Roma competition held in May.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Entrance on Clivo dei Publicii, opposite Circo Massimo.
Hours: Spring only: 2026 season ran 11 April–14 June, daily 8:30–19:30; closed the rest of the year

name: Non-Catholic Cemetery
description: A peaceful cemetery set against the Aurelian Walls and the Pyramid of Cestius, where John Keats and Percy Bysshe Shelley are buried along with Antonio Gramsci and writer Andrea Camilleri. It is run largely by volunteers, and a colony of cats lives among the graves.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; suggested donation of about €5
Getting there: Via Caio Cestio 6, Testaccio — 5 min walk from Piramide metro (Line B).
Hours: Mon–Sat 9:00–17:00; Sun 9:00–13:00

name: Centrale Montemartini
description: Rome's first public power station, opened in 1912, now houses part of the Capitoline Museums' collection of ancient sculpture. Marble gods and emperors stand beside giant diesel engines and turbines, and the museum is rarely crowded. A papal railway carriage is also on display.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticketed at the door (about €11); no booking needed
Getting there: Via Ostiense 106 — 10 min walk from Garbatella or Piramide metro (Line B).
Hours: Tue–Sun 9:00–19:00; closed Monday

name: Basilica di Santo Stefano Rotondo al Celio
description: A 5th-century round church, one of the oldest in Rome, now the national church of Hungary. Its walls are lined with 16th-century frescoes depicting 34 martyrdoms in unflinching detail, which may be too graphic for young children.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Via di Santo Stefano Rotondo 7, Celio — 10 min walk from the Colosseum.
Hours: Tue–Sun 10:00–13:00 & 15:30–18:30; closed Monday

name: Basilica e Monastero Santi Quattro Coronati
description: A fortified medieval monastery on the Celio that looks more like a castle than a church, with an original Cosmatesque marble floor and a 13th-century cloister. The Chapel of San Silvestro's frescoes are among the finest medieval paintings in Rome. Augustinian nuns still live here.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; small fee for the cloister and chapel
Getting there: Via dei Santi Quattro 20 — 10 min uphill walk from the Colosseum.
Hours: Church daily 6:30–12:45 & 15:15–19:30 (Sun closes 12:00 in the morning)

name: Basilica of Saints John and Paul on the Caelian Hill
description: A basilica founded in the 4th century over the house of two Roman martyrs. Its interior is famous for dozens of crystal chandeliers, which is why it is a favorite for Roman weddings. Below it lie the excavated Case Romane del Celio.
mapQuery: Basilica Santi Giovanni e Paolo Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Piazza dei Santi Giovanni e Paolo — 8 min walk from the Colosseum.
Hours: Daily 8:30–12:45 & 14:00–17:00

name: Villa Celimontana
description: A quiet public park on the Celio, a short walk from the Colosseum, with an Egyptian obelisk and shaded paths. It hosts an open-air jazz festival in summer.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Main gate on Via della Navicella 12.
Hours: Daily 7:00–20:00

name: Basilica of San Pietro in Vincoli
description: An unassuming basilica that holds Michelangelo's Moses, carved for the tomb of Pope Julius II, and the chains said to have bound Saint Peter. It is free to enter. Arrive at opening for the quietest visit.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Piazza di San Pietro in Vincoli — 5 min walk from Cavour metro (Line B).
Hours: Mon–Sat 7:15–12:20 & 15:00–18:50; Sun 9:00–12:00 & 15:00–18:50

name: Santa Prassede
description: A small 9th-century basilica just behind Santa Maria Maggiore, hidden behind a plain doorway. Inside is a dazzling set of gold mosaics, especially in the Chapel of San Zeno. Bring coins for the light boxes.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Via di Santa Prassede 9a, 2 min from Santa Maria Maggiore.

name: National Roman Museum – Palazzo Massimo alle Terme
description: One of the world's great collections of ancient Roman art, yet usually quiet. Highlights include the bronze Boxer at Rest, the frescoed garden room from the Villa of Livia, and a large coin collection. The ticket also covers three other National Roman Museum sites for a week.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticketed at the door (about €15 combined); no booking needed
Getting there: Largo di Villa Peretti 2, opposite Termini station.
Hours: Tue–Sun 9:00–19:00; closed Monday

name: Galleria Colonna
description: The private Baroque palace of the Colonna family, who still live here, with a Great Hall that rivals Versailles. The final scene of Roman Holiday was filmed in this hall, and a cannonball from the 1849 siege is still lodged in the marble stairs.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book online in advance at galleriacolonna.it; guided tours available
Getting there: Via della Pilotta 17, near Piazza Venezia and Trevi.
Hours: Fri–Sat 9:30–13:00 only

name: Galleria Spada
description: A cardinal's palace with a small but rich collection of Baroque paintings, including works by Artemisia and Orazio Gentileschi. The real draw is Borromini's forced-perspective colonnade in the courtyard, which looks 37 meters long but is about 8 meters.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticketed at the door; free on the first Sunday of the month
Getting there: Piazza Capo di Ferro 13, 3 min from Campo de' Fiori.
Hours: Wed–Mon 8:30–19:30; Tue 16:30–19:30

name: Church of Saint Louis of the French (San Luigi dei Francesi)
description: France's national church in Rome, home to three Caravaggio masterpieces on the life of Saint Matthew in the Contarelli Chapel. The painted light matches the light falling from the chapel window. Free entry.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free; coins for the chapel lights
Getting there: Piazza di San Luigi de' Francesi, between the Pantheon and Piazza Navona.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:30–12:45 & 14:30–18:30; Sat 9:30–12:00 & 14:30–18:30; Sun 12:00–12:45 & 14:30–18:30

name: St. Ivo alla Sapienza
description: Borromini's Baroque masterpiece, with a spiraling lantern visible across the skyline. The arcaded courtyard of the old university can be visited at any reasonable hour.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Corso del Rinascimento 40, near Piazza Navona.
Hours: Interior traditionally opens only Sunday mornings

name: Cloister of Bramante (Chiostro del Bramante)
description: Bramante's first Roman work, a Renaissance cloister now hosting rotating exhibitions. The upstairs café is free to enter and looks onto a window into Raphael's Sibyls in Santa Maria della Pace.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Exhibition ticketed; café walk-in
Getting there: Arco della Pace 5, 2 min from Piazza Navona.
Hours: Mon–Thu & Sun 10:00–19:00; Fri–Sat 10:00–20:00

name: Biblioteca Angelica
description: Founded in 1604, one of Europe's first public libraries, with a reading room lined in carved wood and holding some 200,000 volumes. It is a working library, so visit quietly.
tags: verify: visitor access to the reading room
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; ID may be requested
Getting there: Piazza di Sant'Agostino 8, near Piazza Navona.
Hours: Mon–Fri 9:00–13:30; closed weekends

name: Napoleonic Museum
description: A house museum in Palazzo Primoli devoted to five generations of the Bonaparte family in Rome, with portraits, furniture and personal objects. Free and rarely busy.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Piazza di Ponte Umberto I, by the Tiber near Piazza Navona.
Hours: Tue–Sun 10:00–18:00; closed Monday

name: Church of Santa Maria della Vittoria
description: A small Baroque church holding Bernini's Ecstasy of Saint Teresa in the Cornaro Chapel, one of the most theatrical sculptures in Rome.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Via Venti Settembre 17 — 5 min from Repubblica metro (Line A).
Hours: Mon–Sat 7:00–12:00 & 16:00–18:00; Sun 9:00–12:00 & 16:00–18:00

name: Parish Basilica of Santa Maria del Popolo
description: Two Caravaggios, a Raphael-designed chapel and Bernini sculpture packed into one church on Piazza del Popolo. It featured in Angels & Demons.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Piazza del Popolo 12 — by Flaminio metro (Line A).
Hours: Mon–Sat 8:30–9:45, 10:30–12:00 & 16:00–18:00; Sun 16:30–18:00

name: Terrazza del Pincio
description: A balustraded terrace above Piazza del Popolo with one of the city's classic views across to St Peter's, especially at sunset.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Climb the ramps from Piazza del Popolo or walk from the top of the Spanish Steps.

name: Fountain of the Frogs – Quartiere Coppedè
description: The centerpiece of the Coppedè quarter, a fairy-tale enclave of Art Nouveau and neo-Gothic buildings designed by Gino Coppedè in the 1920s. The Beatles reportedly jumped into the fountain in 1965.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Piazza Mincio, northeast of Villa Borghese — about 20 min by taxi from the center; tram 3 or 19 nearby.

name: I Villini delle Fate
description: The 'Fairy Villas' of the Coppedè quarter, covered in frescoes, mosaics and tributes to Florence, Venice and Rome.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Private residences; view from the street
Getting there: Piazza Mincio, Coppedè quarter.

name: Palazzo del Ragno
description: The 'Spider Palace' in the Coppedè quarter, with a giant spider on its façade and Assyrian-Babylonian motifs.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Private residence; view from the street
Getting there: Piazza Mincio 4.

name: Casina delle Civette
description: The 'House of the Owls' in Villa Torlonia park, a whimsical Art Nouveau folly famous for its stained glass.
mapQuery: Casina delle Civette Villa Torlonia Rome
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticketed
Getting there: Villa Torlonia, Via Nomentana 70; tickets sold at a separate building about 300 m away.
Hours: Tue–Sun 9:00–19:00; closed Monday

name: Mausoleo di Santa Costanza
description: A 4th-century round mausoleum built for Constantine's daughter, with some of the oldest surviving Christian-era mosaics in the ambulatory vault. Often empty; pair with the catacombs of Sant'Agnese next door.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Mausoleum free; catacombs by guided tour only (cash)
Getting there: Via Nomentana 349 — 10 min walk from Sant'Agnese/Annibaliano metro (Line B1).
Hours: Daily 9:00–18:00

name: Tempietto del Bramante
description: Bramante's small round temple, built on the traditional site of Saint Peter's crucifixion, is a High Renaissance landmark. Entry is free through the Spanish Academy, and you will likely have it almost to yourself.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Piazza di San Pietro in Montorio, on the Janiculum above Trastevere — steep 10 min walk.
Hours: Tue–Sun 10:00–18:00; closed Monday

name: Fontana dell'Acqua Paola
description: A monumental 17th-century fountain on the Janiculum, built for Pope Paul V, facing a terrace with sweeping views of Rome. Romans call it 'il Fontanone'.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Via Garibaldi, uphill from Trastevere; 3 min from the Tempietto.
Hours: Outdoor; accessible at all hours

name: Santa Cecilia in Trastevere
description: A tranquil basilica on the quiet side of Trastevere with Maderno's moving statue of the saint and a crypt over Roman houses. Pietro Cavallini's 13th-century Last Judgment fresco is in the nuns' choir.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; small fees for the crypt and Cavallini fresco
Getting there: Piazza di Santa Cecilia 22, Trastevere.
Hours: Daily 10:00–12:30 & 16:30–18:30

name: Villa Doria Pamphili
description: Rome's largest landscaped park, with umbrella pines, villas and long walking loops.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Main entrance Via di San Pancrazio, above Trastevere; bus or taxi.
Hours: Daily 7:00–20:00 (closes at dusk in winter); some fountains closed for restoration

name: Lungomare Civitavecchiese
description: Civitavecchia's seafront promenade, with pebble beaches, cafés and a short pier walk.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: Lungomare Thaon de Revel; 10–15 min walk from the port shuttle drop-off.

name: Echo Point
description: A small viewpoint on the seafront with views of the harbor.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; free
Getting there: Viale Garibaldi 14, on the seafront.

name: Belvedere su Civita di Bagnoregio
description: The classic viewpoint over Civita di Bagnoregio, a hilltop village on an eroding tuff outcrop reached by a single footbridge.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Viewpoint free
Getting there: Bagnoregio, about 1h45 by car from Civitavecchia — a full-day trip.

name: Il Ponte di Civita
description: The steep pedestrian bridge into Civita di Bagnoregio.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Entry fee (about €5) at the bridge
Getting there: From the Bagnoregio parking area; steep walk.

name: Anfiteatro romano di Sutri
description: A Roman amphitheater carved entirely from volcanic tuff.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticketed (about €5)
Getting there: Via Cassia, Sutri — about 1h by car from Civitavecchia.
Hours: Tue–Sun 10:00–18:30; closed Monday

name: Tolfa
description: A hill town in the Tolfa Mountains with a ruined fortress and views to the sea.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in
Getting there: About 30 min by car inland from Civitavecchia.

name: Vulci Archaeological and Natural Park
description: Etruscan and Roman ruins set in open countryside with a waterfall.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Ticketed (about €10)
Getting there: Montalto di Castro, about 50 min by car north of Civitavecchia.
Hours: Daily 9:00–19:00

name: Trevignano lungolago
description: The lakeside promenade of Trevignano Romano on Lake Bracciano.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; paid parking
Getting there: About 1h by car from Civitavecchia.

name: Parco Regionale dell'Appia Antica
description: The ancient Appian Way and its regional park, lined with tombs, catacombs and aqueducts.
tags: verify: gate hours for park sections
details:
Reservations / tickets: Walk-in; bike and golf-cart rentals nearby
Getting there: Visitor point at Via Appia Antica 42; bus 118 or taxi.

name: Castello di Giulio II
description: A Renaissance castle built in 1483 by the future Pope Julius II, included with the Ostia Antica ticket.
mapQuery: Castello di Giulio II Ostia Antica
details:
Reservations / tickets: Included with the Ostia Antica ticket
Getting there: Piazza della Rocca, Ostia Antica borgo.
Hours: Tue–Sun 13:30–19:00; closed Monday

name: Palazzo Pontificio – Castel Gandolfo
description: The papal summer palace above Lake Albano, now a museum.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Book through the Vatican Museums website
Getting there: Castel Gandolfo — train from Roma Termini (about 40 min).
Hours: Mon–Sat 8:00–20:00; closed Sunday

name: Giardino di Ninfa
description: A romantic garden grown among the ruins of a medieval town.
details:
Reservations / tickets: Guided tours only; book ahead at giardinodininfa.eu
Getting there: Cisterna di Latina, about 1h15 by car from Rome.
Hours: Seasonal weekends only (shown Sat–Sun 9:00–16:30)
